proposals.expert: ML for structural biology (AlphaFold-class model training and evaluation), 15 years post-PhD; NeurIPS and Nature Methods reviewer

ideas.title: Receptor-complex prediction scored against a composition-matched empirical null
ideas.one_line: Fold every candidate with its actual receptor and report ipTM/interface-PAE as an empirical p-value against per-candidate scrambled and off-target decoys, not as a bare number.
ideas.scientific_rationale: ipTM is interface-restricted pTM: it is mathematically undefined for a single chain, which is exactly why all 22 existing runs report 0.00. But simply adding the receptor does not fix the science, because a raw ipTM has no reference distribution. The candidates are Arg/Trp-rich cationic amphipathic peptides (B1 = KWWKFLRRFWRRLKKYFEELWKKLAEKYFELLKKYG), the sequence class most notorious for promiscuous binding — precisely the case where a model will assign a moderate interface score to anything. The only construct that separates 'this design binds' from 'peptides of this composition score this way against this receptor' is a per-candidate null built from composition-matched shuffles plus an off-target receptor panel. I ran the pilot this session and it is decisive: three unseeded replicates of the native B1+AChE complex gave ipTM 0.2118 / 0.2967 / 0.4732 (mean 0.327), while three composition-matched scrambles of the SAME peptide gave 0.3084 / 0.3346 / 0.7350 (mean 0.459). Empirical p = 1.0 — every decoy exceeded the native median and the best decoy exceeded every native replicate. Interface PAE tells the same story via code already in the repo but never exercised: Prediction.interface_pae('A','B') gives min 16.84 A for the native and 16.45 A for a scramble, versus min 0.56 A for a genuine complex (1YCR). A minimum interface PAE of ~17 A means the model cannot place the peptide against AChE to better than 17 A anywhere on the surface. Without the null, an isolated ipTM of 0.735 from a random shuffle would have read as a promising hit.
ideas.what_it_answers: For candidate X against its declared receptor, is the predicted interface distinguishable from what the same model, at the same settings, assigns to a sequence of identical amino-acid composition in random order, or to an unrelated receptor? The platform cannot answer this at all today: ipTM = 0.00 for all 35 candidates because no candidate has ever been co-folded with a receptor, and no decoy, scramble, or off-target control exists anywhere in the repository.
ideas.method: 1) New module /Users/seunghojung/Documents/DeepMind_Bio/platform/cbc/compute/complex.py. The receptor registry already exists as data: data/dataset.json -> target_records.targets holds 16 entries with UniProt accession plus curated domain_boundaries (NTRK2 Q16620 Ig2 295-365; ACHE P22303 carboxylesterase 39-563; TREM2 Q9NZC2 Ig-V 29-112; etc., spanning ~67-608 residues). Fetch each domain from the UniProt REST API and cache under data/receptors/. Use the declared domain, not the full chain: it is the stated binding site and it keeps token counts down. 2) Extend run_boltz in platform/cbc/compute/structure.py, whose command list at lines 191-195 currently hardcodes only out_dir/accelerator/recycling_steps/diffusion_samples/output_format/override. Add passthrough for --seed, --use_msa_server, --sampling_steps, --diffusion_samples, and change _collect_boltz_outputs (line 220) which today keeps only sorted(...)[0] and so silently discards every model beyond the top-ranked one — that makes ensembles impossible. 3) Per candidate run: native complex x 5 seeds; 20 composition-matched shuffles (random.Random(seed).shuffle over the residue multiset, so composition, length, charge, GRAVY and pI are exactly preserved) x 1 seed; and the candidate against 5 non-cognate receptors drawn from the same 16. 4) Score with existing dead code: Prediction.interface_pae, plus Boltz's pair_chains_iptm / complex_iplddt / complex_ipde, none of which _load_boltz in platform/cbc/predictor.py currently reads (it takes only ptm, iptm, confidence_score). 5) Statistic: empirical p = (1 + #{decoy >= native_median}) / (N+1), reported with the native across-seed sd, for both ipTM and min interface PAE. 6) Emit via provenance.predicted with software='boltz-2 2.2.1', uncertainty=across-seed sd, applicability naming msa mode and MPS. 7) BLOCKER to fix first: predictor.py _sanity lines 392-398 warns 'PAE is strongly asymmetric ... suggests the matrix was not produced by a predictor' above a 12.0 A threshold. Genuine Boltz-2 complexes trip it every time — 16.8 A on the true 1YCR complex, 19.2 A on AChE+B1. That threshold was tuned on single chains and must be re-derived from real two-chain output, or every real complex will be flagged as synthetic.

evidence.citation: Bennett NR, Coventry B, Goreshnik I, et al. Improving de novo protein binder design with deep learning. Nature Communications 14:2625 (2023). DOI 10.1038/s41467-023-38328-5
evidence.supports: Establishes that AlphaFold-derived INTERFACE metrics, not monomer confidence, are the decision variable in binder design, and that filtering on them raises experimentally verified success rates roughly ten-fold. Justifies replacing the platform's monomer-pLDDT column with ipTM / interface PAE.

evidence.citation: Bryant P, Pozzati G, Elofsson A. Improved prediction of protein-protein interactions using AlphaFold2. Nature Communications 13:1265 (2022). DOI 10.1038/s41467-022-28865-w; PMID 35273146
evidence.supports: The canonical demonstration that an AlphaFold confidence score becomes a decision rule only against an explicit non-interacting negative set: their pDockQ recovers 51% of true interacting pairs at 1% false-positive rate. This is the methodological template for the per-candidate empirical null.

evidence.citation: Evans R, O'Neill M, Pritzel A, et al. Protein complex prediction with AlphaFold-Multimer. bioRxiv 2021.10.04.463034. DOI 10.1101/2021.10.04.463034
evidence.supports: Defines ipTM as pTM restricted to inter-chain residue pairs, i.e. undefined without at least two chains — the formal reason all 22 lone-chain runs return 0.00 — and describes the widely used >0.8 confident / <0.6 failed bands.

evidence.citation: Measured this session on the project hardware. Native BasalAChE-GorgeBlock-B1 + AChE P22303 mature chain (583 aa), Boltz-2 2.2.1, MPS, msa=empty, recycling_steps=3, diffusion_samples=1, unseeded, 3 replicates: ipTM 0.2118 / 0.2967 / 0.4732. Three composition-matched shuffles of the same peptide: 0.3084 / 0.3346 / 0.7350. Interface PAE (Prediction.interface_pae) native min 16.84 A and 17.81 A, decoy min 16.45 A; genuine complex 1YCR min 0.56 A. Wall time 168.8 s uncontended for 619 tokens; 29.3 s for 121 tokens.
evidence.supports: Direct pilot evidence that (a) complex prediction runs today on this MacBook at practical speed, (b) the flagship AChE candidate carries no interface signal above its own amino-acid composition, and (c) an uncalibrated single-run ipTM of 0.735 from a random shuffle would be misread as a hit.

ideas.effort: 3-4 days of engineering plus roughly 24 h of unattended MPS compute for the full 35-candidate x 26-run design; a 6-candidate pilot is one overnight run.
success_criteria: A committed table of all 35 candidates with native ipTM (mean +/- sd over 5 seeds), decoy-null mean and sd, empirical p-value, and min interface PAE, using receptor domains resolved to UniProt accession and residue range.
At least one candidate reported as indistinguishable from its scrambled null (p > 0.05) and published as such rather than dropped — on the pilot evidence BasalAChE-GorgeBlock-B1 will be one.

The mechanistically inverted candidates (extracellular peptides aimed at cytoplasmic targets) score no better than their off-target panel, confirming the null has discriminative power in the direction we already know the answer.
predictor.py parses pair_chains_iptm, complex_iplddt and complex_ipde, and the PAE-asymmetry sanity threshold no longer fires on genuine two-chain Boltz-2 output (currently fires at 16.8 A on 1YCR).
Every emitted value carries provenance.status=PREDICTED with software 'boltz-2 2.2.1', a seed list, and uncertainty set to the across-seed sd.
risks: Single-sequence mode may depress ipTM uniformly, but this biases native and decoy identically, so the empirical p-value is robust to it even though the absolute ipTM is not. AIML-STRUCT-3 removes the confound.

Boltz-2 was not trained or benchmarked on de novo designed peptide binders; absolute confidences are out of its demonstrated applicability domain. The null is what makes the comparison meaningful regardless, and this must be stated in the applicability field rather than papered over.

Using the declared domain rather than the full receptor changes the surface available for binding. Where the declared domain is a fragment of a larger fold (KEAP1 Kelch, GRIN2A ATD), the domain choice must be recorded as a modelling decision, and at least one target should be run both ways to size the effect.
20 decoys give a minimum achievable p of 1/21 = 0.048; detecting a strong design needs more decoys, so N should scale with how strong a claim is being made.

Composition-matched shuffling preserves charge and hydrophobicity but destroys any real motif; a design whose signal comes from a genuine short linear motif could be penalised relative to a null that occasionally reconstitutes one by chance. Reporting the full decoy distribution rather than only the p-value mitigates this.
ideas.why_now: This is the single largest scientific gap the brief identifies, it is the cheapest to close, and the pilot already run this session shows the answer is likely to be negative for at least one flagship candidate — which is the most valuable thing this platform can currently produce. Everything downstream (affinity, ADMET, prioritisation) is wasted effort spent on candidates whose interfaces have never been tested against a null.

ideas.title: DockQ-anchored calibration of Boltz-2 confidence on a leakage-free local benchmark
ideas.one_line: Build a post-training-cutoff peptide-protein benchmark from the PDB, predict it with the exact local Boltz-2/MPS configuration, score with DockQ, and publish the reliability curve that converts ipTM into P(correct interface) with a confidence interval.
ideas.scientific_rationale: AIML-STRUCT-1 produces ipTM values; nothing in the repository says what an ipTM means. The commonly quoted >0.8 / <0.6 bands come from AlphaFold-Multimer on general heterodimers with full MSAs on CUDA — none of which describes this setup. Peptide-protein complexes are a distinct and harder regime than the heterodimers those bands were derived on, and this install runs a different model, in single-sequence mode, on an MPS backend where at least one operator (aten::linalg_svd) silently falls back to CPU. So the platform currently has no basis for any threshold at all, and a threshold is exactly what a screening decision requires. The fix is a local calibration against structural ground truth, which — unlike calibration against measured affinity — needs no wet lab. Boltz-2's PDB training cutoff is 2023-06-01, so any complex released after that date is a genuine temporal holdout. I verified the whole loop end-to-end this session: an RCSB search for post-cutoff, protein-only, two-chain entries with a 5-40 residue partner at better than 2.5 A returns 1107 entries; DockQ 2.1.3 builds a native macosx_26_0_arm64 wheel here; and Boltz-2 on MPS predicted MDM2/p53 (1YCR) in single-sequence mode in 29.3 s to ipTM 0.9085, which DockQ scores at 0.649 (Medium quality), iRMSD 1.615 A, LRMSD 3.462 A, fnat 0.625, zero clashes. That is one calibration point already on disk. A hundred of them is a reliability curve.
ideas.what_it_answers: What fraction of interfaces that this specific Boltz-2/MPS/single-sequence pipeline scores at ipTM 0.30 are actually correct — and does the local install reproduce published Boltz-2 accuracy, or is it degraded by the MPS backend and the empty-MSA setting? Today the platform reports predicted confidences with no calibration whatsoever and therefore cannot convert any confidence into a probability, a threshold, or an error bar. The memory ledger's stated calibration requirement asks for ipTM against MEASURED AFFINITY, which needs wet-lab data this project does not have; structural ground truth is free and available now.
ideas.method: 1) Build the set with the RCSB Search API (query verified this session, 1107 hits): rcsb_accession_info.initial_release_date > 2023-06-01, selected_polymer_entity_types = 'Protein (only)', polymer_entity_count_protein = 2, entity_poly.rcsb_sample_sequence_length in [5,40], resolution_combined < 2.5. Deduplicate at 30-40% sequence identity on the receptor — either via the polymer entity rcsb_cluster_membership field or a local mmseqs2 pass; note I did NOT get the server-side group_by clustering call to validate (HTTP 400), so treat the exact clustering API call as unfinished implementation detail rather than a verified step. Sample ~100 representatives. 2) Predict each with the identical configuration the platform uses for candidates, so the calibration transfers. 3) Score with DockQ v2 against the deposited structure using explicit chain mapping. 4) Fit and commit data/calibration/iptm_dockq.json: P(DockQ >= 0.23 | ipTM bin) with Wilson score intervals, plus AUROC of ipTM as a discriminator of acceptable-or-better, plus expected calibration error, plus the same for min interface PAE. 5) Add predictor.calibrated_interface_probability(iptm) returning a probability WITH its interval, and raising rather than extrapolating outside observed bins — so an ipTM from a sparsely populated region returns 'not calibrated here' instead of a fabricated probability. 6) Feed the resulting threshold back into AIML-STRUCT-1 so its p-values sit on a calibrated scale. 7) Report the benchmark's own DockQ distribution against the Boltz-2 paper's published numbers; a large gap is evidence the local configuration is degraded, which is itself a finding worth committing.

evidence.citation: Basu S, Wallner B. DockQ: A Quality Measure for Protein-Protein Docking Models. PLoS ONE 11(8):e0161879 (2016). DOI 10.1371/journal.pone.0161879
evidence.supports: Defines the DockQ score from Fnat, LRMS and iRMS and the Incorrect/Acceptable/Medium/High bands (0.23/0.49/0.80) that reproduce the CAPRI classification at ~94% PPV. Supplies the ground-truth axis of the calibration curve and the 0.23 success threshold.

evidence.citation: Mirabello C, Wallner B. DockQ v2: improved automatic quality measure for protein multimers, nucleic acids, and small molecules. Bioinformatics 40(10):btae586 (2024). DOI 10.1093/bioinformatics/btae586; PMID 39348158
evidence.supports: The implementation actually used here (DockQ 2.1.3), including Cython-accelerated scoring and multimer/chain-mapping support. Confirmed to build a native arm64 wheel and to score Boltz-2 mmCIF output directly on this machine.

evidence.citation: Passaro S, Corso G, Wohlwend J, et al. Boltz-2: Towards Accurate and Efficient Binding Affinity Prediction. bioRxiv 2025.06.14.659707. DOI 10.1101/2025.06.14.659707; PMID 40667369
evidence.supports: Gives the PDB training cutoff of 2023-06-01 and the temporal-split evaluation strategy, which is what makes a post-2023-06-01 PDB selection a genuine leakage-free holdout rather than a memorisation test.

evidence.citation: Tsaban T, Varga JK, Avraham O, et al. Harnessing protein folding neural networks for peptide-protein docking. Nature Communications 13:176 (2022). DOI 10.1038/s41467-021-27838-9; PMID 35013344
evidence.supports: Establishes peptide-protein docking as a distinct regime for folding networks with its own accuracy characteristics, so confidence bands derived from general heterodimers cannot be assumed to transfer to 26-47 residue peptides.

evidence.citation: Measured this session. RCSB Search API returned total_count 1107 for the post-cutoff peptide-protein query. DockQ 2.1.3 built dockq-2.1.3-cp312-cp312-macosx_26_0_arm64.whl. Boltz-2 2.2.1 on MPS, 1YCR (MDM2 106 aa + p53 15 aa, 121 tokens), msa=empty: 29.3 s, ipTM 0.9085, DockQ 0.649, iRMSD 1.615 A, LRMSD 3.462 A, fnat 0.625, clashes 0. Same system with a ColabFold receptor MSA and --seed 7: ipTM 0.9636, DockQ 0.678, iRMSD 1.513 A, fnat 0.667.
evidence.supports: Proves every component of the loop — benchmark retrieval, prediction, and DockQ scoring — executes today on this hardware, and yields the first two calibration points.

ideas.effort: 4-5 days of engineering plus roughly 2-5 h of MPS compute for 100 complexes (median size in this size class runs ~1-3 min each).
success_criteria: data/calibration/iptm_dockq.json committed, containing N, the per-bin P(DockQ >= 0.23) with Wilson intervals, AUROC, and expected calibration error, for both ipTM and min interface PAE.
Every entry in the benchmark has a PDB accession and a release date after 2023-06-01, and the deduplication threshold and method are stated.

predictor.calibrated_interface_probability refuses to return a number for ipTM values outside populated bins, and validate.py gains a violation category for any PREDICTED interface value surfaced without a calibration reference.

The local pipeline's DockQ success rate on this set is reported next to the Boltz-2 paper's published figures, with the gap quantified and attributed (MSA mode, MPS backend, peptide-length regime) rather than left unexplained.
A stated, defensible ipTM threshold for this platform, derived from the curve, replaces any borrowed 0.8 heuristic.
risks: Domain shift is the central caveat: natural peptide-protein complexes in the PDB are not hand-assembled cationic amphipathic designs, so the curve is transferable only insofar as the designs resemble natural peptide binders. This must be stated on the plot, not buried, and the designs' distance from the benchmark distribution should be quantified.

PDB two-chain 'peptide' entities include crystallisation tags, purification handles and fragments of the same protein; the set needs manual or rule-based curation or the calibration is against a partly meaningless target.
DockQ chain mapping can be ambiguous for near-symmetric cases; use explicit --mapping and record it.

Post-cutoff does not fully guarantee no leakage — homologues of the holdout may sit in training. Clustering against the training distribution at 40% identity, as Boltz-2 itself does, is the mitigation, and residual leakage should be acknowledged as an upward bias.
100 complexes gives wide Wilson intervals in sparsely populated ipTM bins; the honest output is a curve with visible uncertainty, not a smooth fitted sigmoid presented as precise.
ideas.why_now: AIML-STRUCT-1 generates numbers that no one can act on until this exists — a p-value against a null says a design is not special, but only calibration says whether a design that IS special is likely to be right. It also directly tests whether the local install is scientifically usable at all, which currently nobody knows; the ledger's headline Huperzine A affinity failure of 2.41 log units is uninterpretable for exactly this reason. It is fully proven feasible and needs no wet lab, no GPU, and no paid service.

ideas.title: Make predictions reproducible and quantify the inference-configuration variance (seed, MSA, sampling)
ideas.one_line: Pass a seed, run seed replicates and diffusion ensembles, add the ColabFold receptor MSA as a controlled factor, and attach the resulting spread as the uncertainty on every predicted structural value.
ideas.scientific_rationale: Every structural number this project has produced was generated in the fastest and explicitly not-recommended configuration, and none of them can be reproduced. Boltz's own documentation states: 'To force single-sequence mode (not recommended, as it reduces accuracy), set msa: empty' — which is what all 22 runs used. The same document gives AlphaFold3's defaults as --recycling_steps 10 --diffusion_samples 25; the platform ran 3 and 1. And boltz/main.py line 1102 calls seed_everything(seed) only if seed is not None, with the CLI default None, while run_boltz in structure.py never passes --seed at all. The consequence is not theoretical. I ran the identical AChE + B1 job three times this session and got ipTM 0.2118, 0.2967 and 0.4732 — sd 0.133 on a 0-1 metric, a range of 0.26 on the number that would decide whether a candidate advances. A single unseeded diffusion_samples=1 run is a draw from a wide distribution reported as a point estimate, which is the same class of error as the original hardcoded values, just with a real model behind it. The MSA arm matters independently: the ledger's headline validation result — Huperzine A + AChE mispredicted by 2.41 log10 units — was run at msa=empty, so the project currently cannot distinguish 'Boltz-2 is inaccurate on this target' from 'we ran Boltz-2 crippled'. I verified the ColabFold MSA path works here: --use_msa_server fetched the MDM2 MSA in ~2 s and on 1YCR raised ipTM from 0.9085 to 0.9636 and DockQ from 0.649 to 0.678 (confounded with a seed change, which is precisely the confound this experiment is designed to remove).
ideas.what_it_answers: How much of the platform's structural verdicts is an artifact of inference configuration rather than biology — specifically, what is the across-seed error bar that belongs on every reported pLDDT and ipTM, and how much does a receptor MSA change the answer? The platform cannot answer either: no seed is recorded anywhere, so no result is reproducible even in principle, and MSA depth has never been varied, so its contribution is entirely unmeasured.
ideas.method: 1) Add seed, use_msa_server, msa_server_url, sampling_steps and step_scale as parameters of run_boltz (platform/cbc/compute/structure.py, command list at lines 191-195), and record every one of them in the returned provenance dict alongside the existing msa_mode. Fix _collect_boltz_outputs (line 220) to return all diffusion samples rather than sorted(...)[0], so ensembles are retrievable. 2) Cache receptor MSAs once per target: 16 a3m files under data/msa/, fetched via the ColabFold MMseqs2 server and committed, so the experiment is reproducible offline and the public service is hit 16 times, not thousands. Keep msa=empty for the peptide chain and say why — a hand-assembled designed sequence has no homologues, so an MSA for it would be meaningless or actively misleading. 3) Factorial on ~8 candidate-receptor pairs plus the 1YCR positive control: MSA in {empty, receptor-a3m} x seed in {1,2,3,4,5}, at diffusion_samples=5. Report per-cell mean and sd for ipTM, pTM, complex_plddt and min interface PAE, and the MSA main effect with the seed variance partialled out. 4) Direct retest of the ledger's headline measurement: re-run Huperzine A + AChE through the Boltz-2 affinity head with the receptor MSA and seeded, and report whether the 2.41 log10 error shrinks. This is a falsifiable retest of a recorded claim, not a new claim. 5) Wire the across-seed sd into Provenance.uncertainty, which today defaults to empty and renders as 'unquantified'. 6) Add a validate.py gate category: any value with status PREDICTED that lacks seed, software version, sample count and across-seed sd is a violation. 7) Note for the record that aten::linalg_svd falls back from MPS to CPU in boltz/model/loss/diffusionv2.py — a performance characteristic of this backend worth documenting alongside timings.

evidence.citation: Boltz prediction documentation, jwohlwend/boltz docs/prediction.md (retrieved this session): 'To force single-sequence mode (not recommended, as it reduces accuracy), set msa: empty.' Same document gives AlphaFold3 defaults as '--recycling_steps 10 --diffusion_samples 25'.
evidence.supports: Primary vendor documentation that the exact configuration used for all 22 existing predictions is the one its authors advise against, and that the sampling budget used was 1/25th of the AF3 reference. Not a DOI-bearing source; cited as documentation.

evidence.citation: Mirdita M, Schutze K, Moriwaki Y, Heo L, Ovchinnikov S, Steinegger M. ColabFold: making protein folding accessible to all. Nature Methods 19:679-682 (2022). DOI 10.1038/s41592-022-01488-1
evidence.supports: The MMseqs2-based MSA service that Boltz's --use_msa_server calls, and the reference establishing that fast remote homology search is a practical substitute for a local sequence database — which is what makes the MSA arm feasible on a laptop with no UniRef/BFD mirror.

evidence.citation: Abramson J, Adler J, Dunger J, et al. Accurate structure prediction of biomolecular interactions with AlphaFold 3. Nature 630:493-500 (2024). DOI 10.1038/s41586-024-07487-w; PMID 38718835
evidence.supports: Establishes the AF3-class generative diffusion sampling that Boltz-2 inherits: predictions are stochastic draws, multiple seeds and samples are the intended usage, and ranking is performed across samples. Grounds the requirement to report a distribution rather than a point estimate.

evidence.citation: Measured this session. Three unseeded replicates of the identical AChE(583 aa)+B1(36 aa) job, Boltz-2 2.2.1, MPS, msa=empty, recycling_steps=3, diffusion_samples=1: ipTM 0.2118 / 0.2967 / 0.4732, sd 0.133. Source verified at /Users/seunghojung/Documents/DeepMind_Bio/.venv312/lib/python3.12/site-packages/boltz/main.py:1102, seed_everything(seed) guarded by 'if seed is not None' with CLI default None; run_boltz never passes --seed. ColabFold MSA path exercised successfully: 1YCR with receptor MSA and --seed 7 gave ipTM 0.9636 / DockQ 0.678 versus 0.9085 / 0.649 unseeded without MSA.
evidence.supports: Quantifies the reproducibility defect directly (the 22 numbers in data/real_vs_hardcoded.json cannot be regenerated) and shows the seed-induced spread is comparable in size to the entire native-versus-decoy effect in AIML-STRUCT-1, making seed replication a precondition for that experiment rather than a refinement of it.

ideas.effort: 2-3 days of engineering plus roughly 5 h of MPS compute for the 8-pair factorial; the MSA fetch is a one-time 16-call network step.
success_criteria: data/real_vs_hardcoded.json is regenerated with a recorded seed per run and is byte-reproducible on a second execution.
A committed table giving, for 8 candidate-receptor pairs, ipTM and complex_plddt as mean +/- sd over 5 seeds in both MSA conditions, with the MSA main effect and its uncertainty stated.
The Huperzine A + AChE affinity prediction is re-run with a receptor MSA and a seed, and the resulting log10 error is reported next to the recorded 2.41 — including if it does not improve.
Provenance.uncertainty is populated with the across-seed sd for every PREDICTED structural value, so none renders as 'unquantified'.
validate.py fails on any PREDICTED value missing seed, software version, sample count or spread, and the new check is covered by verify_all.py.
risks: The public ColabFold MSA server is a free third-party service with rate limits and no availability guarantee; caching 16 a3m files in-repo is the mitigation, and the seed half of the experiment runs entirely offline if the server is down.

MSAs increase memory and token footprint on MPS; --num_subsampled_msa may need lowering from the 1024 default for the larger receptors (GRIN2A ATD ~534 aa, TLR4 ectodomain ~608 aa), and any such change must be recorded as part of the configuration.

A receptor MSA may not improve a designed-peptide interface at all, since the peptide contributes no evolutionary signal. That is a legitimate finding either way, but it means the MSA arm should not be assumed to be an improvement before it is measured.

diffusion_samples=5 with 5 seeds multiplies compute 25-fold over current practice; the full 35-candidate catalogue at that budget is days, not hours, so the factorial must stay on a subset and the chosen production budget must be justified from the measured variance.

Reporting honest error bars will widen intervals enough that some candidates become indistinguishable from each other, removing the appearance of a clean ranking. That is the correct outcome and should be stated in advance so it is not mistaken for a regression.
ideas.why_now: This is a precondition, not a parallel track: the measured seed spread of 0.133 on ipTM is the same magnitude as the native-versus-decoy difference AIML-STRUCT-1 is trying to detect, so running that screen unseeded at diffusion_samples=1 would produce a table of noise. It is also the cheapest of the three, it fixes a live reproducibility defect in already-published numbers, and it converts the project's headline validation failure from an uninterpretable result into a controlled one.

proposals.expert: ML evaluation and benchmarking — data leakage, split design and reproducibility failures in scientific ML; 16 years post-PhD

ideas.title: Leakage-audited retrospective affinity benchmark with a measured noise ceiling and a stated null floor
ideas.one_line: Turn the single Huperzine A affinity data point into a scored benchmark that reports RMSE with a bootstrap interval, bracketed above by the experimental noise ceiling and below by a k-NN memorisation baseline, with every test compound labelled for Boltz-2 training-set overlap.
ideas.scientific_rationale: An error figure is uninterpretable without two anchors. The upper anchor is the irreducible noise of the ground truth: Kramer et al. showed a model whose error is below experimental uncertainty is necessarily overtrained (sd 0.54 pKi; max attainable R^2 ~0.81). I measured that same quantity on THIS repo's data/corpus_ACHE.json today: 18 replicate pairs from independent ChEMBL documents give mean |dlog10| = 0.448 and an implied single-measurement sd of 0.376 log10 units (NEOSTIGMINE spans 1.04 log across two documents, TACRINE 0.88 across five). The lower anchor is a trivial predictor: predicting the corpus mean gives RMSE 1.644 log10 units on the 17 compounds that carry a numeric potency. Boltz-2's one recorded error, 2.41 log10 units on Huperzine A, is LARGER than the null model. n=1 proves nothing — which is exactly the argument for building the benchmark. Second mechanism, and the decisive one: Boltz-2's affinity head was trained on ~3M standardised Ki/Kd/IC50 records drawn from ChEMBL, BindingDB, PDBbind and MF-PCBA. The platform's ground truth IS ChEMBL, fetched live by platform/cbc/corpus.py. Scoring Boltz-2 against corpus_ACHE.json is, with high prior probability, scoring a model on its own training set. Wallach & Heifets showed that measured benchmark performance tracks train/validation redundancy rather than skill, so a number produced without a leakage audit is not an accuracy estimate at all.
ideas.what_it_answers: When CognitionBioChem reports a predicted binding affinity, what is its error distribution, is that error smaller than predicting the corpus mean, and how much of any apparent skill is recall of Boltz-2's own training data? The platform today has exactly one affinity number, no baseline, no interval, and no leakage status for it.
ideas.method: New package platform/cbc/bench/ with affinity.py, split.py, baselines.py, stats.py. (1) Ground truth: extend platform/cbc/corpus.py with a Landrum-Riniker 'maximal curation' aggregator — group activities by (full InChIKey, target, matched ChEMBL assay metadata), aggregate to one pAct per compound-target by geometric mean, and retain the replicate spread. Emit sigma_exp from the independent-document replicate-pair distribution as a pv.literature() record with explicit uncertainty. (2) Three splits, always reported side by side: random 5-fold (shown only to expose the optimism gap), Murcko scaffold split via rdkit.Chem.Scaffolds.MurckoScaffold, and a Sheridan temporal split on earliest ChEMBL document.year with the boundary set at the ChEMBL v34 release that Boltz-2 trained on. (3) Per-compound leakage audit: exact (compound,target) presence in the pre-cutoff snapshot, plus max ECFP4/Tanimoto to any pre-cutoff compound measured on the same target; all metrics additionally stratified into similarity bins <0.4 / 0.4-0.7 / >0.7, because that is where memorisation lives. (4) Baselines that must be beaten, all seconds of CPU: predict-the-mean (measured today at 1.644 log10 RMSE), 1-NN and similarity-weighted k-NN on ECFP4 over the pre-cutoff set (the memorisation baseline), and a two-descriptor ridge on MW + cLogP from admet.rdkit_scores(). (5) System under test: run_boltz(..., affinity_binder='B', accelerator='mps') in platform/cbc/compute/structure.py. Measured cost today from /private/tmp/aff/run.log: 2 min 21 s structure + 43 s affinity = 3 min 4 s wall for 543-residue hAChE (P22303 mature, msa=empty) plus Huperzine A. 200 complexes is therefore a ~10 h overnight batch on this MacBook, no GPU. Run every compound in both msa=empty and with a receptor MSA computed once and reused across that target's ligands, so the documented single-sequence penalty is measured rather than assumed. (6) Reporting: RMSE, MAE, Spearman rho and Kendall tau, each with a BCa bootstrap 95% CI resampled over COMPOUNDS not measurements, plus the paired delta against each baseline with its own CI, and a predicted-vs-measured plot with the +/- sigma_exp band drawn. Hard rule enforced in code: when the CI on the paired delta spans zero, the emitted headline is 'not distinguishable from the null model at n=N', never a bare RMSE. (7) Add a suite to verify_all.py that regenerates data/benchmark_affinity.json and fails if any reported metric lacks an interval, a denominator, or a leakage label.

ideas.effort: 2-3 days of implementation plus one overnight (~10 h) MPS batch; the ceiling, the null floor and the baselines are computable in minutes with zero new inference.
success_criteria: data/benchmark_affinity.json exists and contains, for each of the three splits, n, RMSE, MAE, Spearman rho and Kendall tau, each with a BCa bootstrap 95% CI, plus the paired delta versus the null and k-NN baselines with their own CIs.

sigma_exp is reported from a stated number of independent-document replicate pairs (target >=50 after multi-target scale-out; 18 available today) and is drawn as a band on the predicted-vs-measured plot.

Every test compound carries two leakage fields: in_pre_cutoff_chembl (bool) and max_tanimoto_to_pre_cutoff (float), and all headline metrics are additionally reported stratified into <0.4 / 0.4-0.7 / >0.7 similarity bins.

The README accuracy claim takes exactly the form 'RMSE X.XX log10 units (95% CI a-b, n=N, scaffold split, sigma_exp=0.YY)' or the literal string 'not distinguishable from the null model at n=N'. No bare RMSE is renderable.
A verify_all.py suite fails the build if any emitted benchmark metric lacks an interval, a denominator, or a leakage label.
risks: ChEMBL's REST API returned HTTP 500 on every activity query during this session (including the exact query pattern in corpus.py that previously worked). The multi-target scale-out is blocked until it recovers, or until the ChEMBL SQLite/PostgreSQL dump is downloaded locally — which is also the more reproducible option.

A true ChEMBL v34 snapshot for the leakage audit requires downloading the archived release (multi-GB). The document-year proxy is weaker and must be labelled as a proxy in the output, not passed off as an exact overlap test.

After maximal curation, n stays small: AChE alone yields 17 compounds with a numeric potency under the current NP-tier filter. Confidence intervals will be wide. Wide honest intervals are the correct output, and the code must not be tuned to narrow them.

Boltz-2's affinity_pred_value unit convention (believed log10(IC50) in micromolar, consistent with 0.10516 -> 1.27 uM against a measured 5.0 nM) must be confirmed from the Boltz source, not assumed. A wrong convention offsets the entire benchmark by a constant and would make the whole exercise wrong in the same way the original platform was wrong.
Mixing IC50 and Ki in one label column adds noise; either separate them or apply the Kalliokoski factor-of-2 offset and say which was done.
ideas.why_now: The platform is one step away from publishing affinity numbers, and the single data point it already has is worse than predicting the mean. Every downstream use — ranking the 35 candidates, triaging natural products, claiming a hit — is undefined until the sign of the skill is established. This is also the cheapest of the three: the noise ceiling and the null floor were computed in seconds from files already in the repo.

ideas.title: Pose-accuracy and physical-validity benchmark on a post-cutoff temporal holdout, with confidence-score calibration
ideas.one_line: Score the platform's protein-ligand poses against crystal ground truth using symmetry-corrected RMSD plus PoseBusters validity checks, split into a pre-cutoff recall set and a genuine post-2023-06-01 holdout, and measure whether ipTM predicts anything at all.
ideas.scientific_rationale: Two independent gaps. First, the platform is structurally blind to ligands: Prediction.geometry_check() in platform/cbc/predictor.py only checks consecutive C-alpha distances against 3.80 A, and parse_mmcif keeps a row only if label_atom_id == 'CA'. I confirmed today that the 18 Huperzine A atoms in /private/tmp/aff/out/.../in_model_0.cif are therefore discarded entirely. The platform cannot detect a ligand docked into the wrong pocket, a non-planar aromatic ring, or a ligand interpenetrating the protein. Second, pLDDT and ipTM are self-reported confidences, not accuracy. PoseBusters showed that RMSD <= 2 A alone is insufficient — deep-learning docking methods routinely clear the RMSD bar with chemically or sterically impossible poses, and their headline result was that no DL method beat classical docking once physical validity was enforced. Boltz-2 is a DL cofolding model; exemption cannot be assumed. And because its PDB training window closes at 2023-06-01, scoring on older complexes measures recall, not prediction. The decisive fact is that the first data point costs nothing: I computed today that the existing Huperzine A pose contacts Phe338 (2.81 A), His447 (2.81), Tyr133 (2.86), Phe297 (2.96), Tyr124 (3.33), Trp86 (3.41), Tyr337 (3.58), Ser203 (3.58) and Gly120/121 — the catalytic anionic site and oxyanion hole, qualitatively correct. Yet PDB 4EY5 (human AChE + (-)-huperzine A, ligand HUP, 2.30 A) has existed since 2012 and no RMSD against it has ever been computed. The platform got the pose roughly right and the affinity wrong by 2.41 log units in the SAME run, and can currently measure neither.
ideas.what_it_answers: When the platform produces a protein-ligand complex, is the ligand in the right place, is the pose physically possible, and do the confidence scores it displays (ipTM 0.714, ligand_iptm 0.714, complex_plddt 0.930 on the one run it has) predict either of those things? None of these three questions is answerable today.
ideas.method: (1) Install posebusters and spyrmsd into .venv — verified today from the PyPI JSON API that posebusters 0.6.5 ships as a py3-none-any wheel requiring only rdkit>=2024.9 (repo has 2026.03.5), pandas, numpy and pyyaml, and that spyrmsd 0.9.0 is likewise pure Python. No compiler, no Boost, no GPU, so this does not repeat the AutoDock Vina arm64 failure. (2) Fix platform/cbc/predictor.py: parse_mmcif must retain HETATM and non-polymer entities as a separate Prediction.ligands list instead of dropping every non-CA row, and gain an interface_contacts() method. This is a genuine defect for this use case, not a feature request. (3) New platform/cbc/bench/pose.py: fetch the reference entry and ligand instance coordinates from data.rcsb.org; superpose the Boltz-2 model onto the reference receptor by Kabsch over matched C-alpha pairs; transform the predicted ligand into the reference frame; compute symmetry-corrected RMSD with spyrmsd; run posebusters in redock mode (predicted ligand + reference ligand + receptor) and record every check individually. Define success exactly as PoseBusters does — RMSD <= 2 A AND PB-valid — and also report the two components separately, because the gap between them is the interesting quantity. (4) Two sets, reported separately and never pooled. RECALL SET (pre-2023-06-01, explicitly labelled 'inside Boltz-2's PDB training window; this measures recall, not prediction'): 4EY5 huperzine A / HUP, 4EY7 donepezil / E20, 4EY6 galantamine / GNT, all released 2012-10-17 at 2.30-2.40 A, plus the wider hAChE holo series. TEMPORAL HOLDOUT: I executed an RCSB Search API v2 query this session and found 81 experimental entries released after 2023-06-01, at <=2.5 A, with at least one non-polymer entity, mapping to the cognition-target UniProt set P22303 (hAChE), P04058 (TcAChE), P06276 (BuChE), P27338 (MAO-B), P21397 (MAO-A), P56817 (BACE1), Q9Y5Z0 (BACE2), P02766 (TTR), P05067 (APP), P37136. That is a real, sufficient, entirely unused holdout. (5) Calibration: for every case record ipTM, ligand_iptm, protein_iptm, complex_plddt, complex_iplddt and complex_ipde against measured RMSD; emit a reliability curve and the AUROC of each confidence score for the event RMSD <= 2 A, with a bootstrap CI. (6) Report success rates as proportions with Wilson score 95% intervals, which are correct at n ~ 40-80 where the normal approximation is not. (7) Fix top-1 versus top-5 diffusion-sample selection in the protocol BEFORE running, and record the choice. (8) Cost: 3 min per complex measured today, so 81 holdout plus ~20 recall cases is a 5-6 h overnight MPS batch.

evidence.citation: Buttenschoen M, Morris GM, Deane CM. 'PoseBusters: AI-based docking methods fail to generate physically valid poses or generalise to novel sequences.' Chem Sci 2024;15(9):3130-3139. DOI 10.1039/D3SC04185A (arXiv:2308.05777).
evidence.supports: Establishes the PB-valid convention and the finding that RMSD <= 2 A alone is insufficient because DL docking methods produce physically implausible poses; concludes no DL method yet outperforms classical docking. Benchmark data at zenodo.org/record/8278563.

evidence.citation: Passaro S, Corso G, Wohlwend J, et al. 'Boltz-2: Towards Accurate and Efficient Binding Affinity Prediction.' bioRxiv 2025.06.14.659707. DOI 10.1101/2025.06.14.659707 (PMID 40667369).
evidence.supports: Identifies the model, its controllability features and its dual structure/affinity outputs — the system whose pose accuracy and confidence calibration are being measured.

evidence.citation: Wan S, Zhang X, Xue X, Coveney PV. 'On the Reliability of AI Methods in Drug Discovery: Evaluation of Boltz-2 for Structure and Binding Affinity Prediction.' arXiv:2603.05532v1.
evidence.supports: Independent evaluation finding Boltz-2 protein backbone RMSD ~0.4-1.8 A but wide ligand-pose RMSD distributions (a plateau at 22-50 A for 3CLPro) and weak global affinity correlation (Pearson 0.24 for 3CLPro, 0.45 for TNKS2). Confirms good receptor geometry does not imply a good ligand pose, and that this paper performed NO temporal-split or leakage analysis — the gap this proposal fills.

ideas.effort: ~3 days of implementation (predictor.py ligand parsing, RCSB reference fetch, Kabsch superposition, PoseBusters wiring) plus one overnight ~6 h MPS batch. The first data point, 4EY5 versus the existing model, is a few hours of work with no inference at all.
success_criteria: data/benchmark_pose.json exists with, per case, symmetry-corrected ligand RMSD, the complete per-check PoseBusters table, ipTM / ligand_iptm / complex_plddt / complex_ipde, the PDB id, and the entry's initial_release_date.

Two headline proportions with Wilson score 95% intervals — %(RMSD <= 2 A) and %(RMSD <= 2 A AND PB-valid) — reported separately for the pre-2023-06-01 recall set and the post-2023-06-01 holdout, and never pooled into one figure.
AUROC with a bootstrap CI for ipTM (and separately complex_plddt) predicting RMSD <= 2 A. If the CI includes 0.5, the platform stops displaying that score as a quality indicator and says so.

platform/cbc/predictor.py parses non-polymer entities, with a regression test asserting the Huperzine A model yields 18 ligand atoms whose ten nearest protein residues include Trp86, Ser203 and His447.
The top-1 versus top-5 diffusion-sample selection rule is recorded in the output file and was fixed before the batch ran.
risks: Construct mismatch: 4EY5 is glycosylated recombinant hAChE with NAG and DMS present and likely disordered loops, while the prediction used the bare P22303 mature sequence. Superposition must use matched residues only, and the alignment coverage must be recorded per case or the RMSD is not comparable across cases.

'Released after 2023-06-01' is not the same as 'unseen'. A near-identical complex may sit inside the training window. Following PoseBusters' own novel-sequence analysis, report per-case max ligand Tanimoto and receptor sequence identity against the pre-cutoff set, and stratify results by them.

The 81 holdout entries will include covalent adducts, cofactors, cryoprotectants and fragments that are not fair small-molecule docking targets. The inclusion protocol must be executable and versioned — reuse the InclusionProtocol pattern already in corpus.py — with a stated denominator, exactly as the AChE corpus does.
Boltz-2's shipped predict config uses diffusion_samples 5; reporting best-of-5 RMSD without saying so is cherry-picking and would reproduce the class of error the rebuild exists to remove.
Some holdout receptors are large (MAO-B dimer, BACE1 with long loops), so per-complex MPS time may exceed the 3 min measured for hAChE; budget headroom in the overnight batch.
ideas.why_now: The platform already owns a co-folded protein-ligand structure that has never been scored, and a crystal reference for it that has been public since 2012. It is also the prerequisite for interpreting anything ipTM-based, including the 35 candidates. Doing this before the affinity work would be defensible; doing it after would mean the affinity benchmark's structural inputs were never validated.

ideas.title: Composition-matched scramble control for the 35 designed candidates
ideas.one_line: Co-fold each designed candidate with its stated receptor alongside twenty length- and composition-matched shuffles, and report a permutation p-value for whether any score the platform computes is attributable to the sequence rather than to its amino-acid composition.
ideas.scientific_rationale: No measured ground truth exists for the 35 candidates in data/dataset.json and none will without a wet lab, so no accuracy figure is obtainable for them. A specificity control, however, is obtainable, and it is the standard remedy when labels are absent: a permutation null. The candidates are GGGGS-linked concatenations of published motifs, several mechanistically inverted, and every score the platform can compute for them is a deterministic function of the sequence. If a shuffle preserving length and amino-acid composition scores indistinguishably from the design, the score encodes composition, not design intent, and no amount of provenance discipline makes it informative. Several existing outputs are provably composition functions by construction — MW, net charge at pH 7.4, pI and GRAVY in platform/cbc/peptide.py are all order-invariant, so a shuffle reproduces them exactly, which means they carry literally zero design information and should be relabelled on the candidate cards. Whether ipTM to the receptor carries any order information is an open empirical question and the whole point of the experiment. This also closes the largest named gap directly: not one of the 35 has ever been predicted together with its receptor, which is why ipTM was 0.00 for all 22 folded so far — they were folded as lone chains, and ipTM is undefined for a single chain.
ideas.what_it_answers: Is anything the platform reports about its 35 designed candidates attributable to their actual sequence, or would a length- and composition-matched shuffle of the same residues score the same? The platform currently reports scores for these molecules with no null distribution of any kind, so the question has never been posed.
ideas.method: New platform/cbc/bench/scramble.py. (1) Start with the ten candidates in data/dataset.json that carry an explicit receptor in their target field — 'AChE PAS Gorge' (36 aa), 'Keap1 Kelch Domain' (28), 'TrkB Ig-like D5 Domain' (49), 'GSK-3beta ATP Pocket' (32), 'alpha7 nAChR ECD' (41), 'NMDA GluN2B NTD' (45), 'Frizzled-8 CRD' (40) and the rest. (2) For each, generate K=20 controls of three kinds with the RNG seed recorded in the output: a full composition-matched shuffle (Fisher-Yates over the residue multiset, which preserves length, composition, charge, pI and GRAVY exactly); a linker-preserving shuffle (shuffle within each motif segment, keep the GGGGS linkers in place) isolating motif-internal order; and a motif-block permutation isolating the arrangement hypothesis. (3) Co-fold every sequence with its receptor using run_boltz() with two protein chains and accelerator='mps'. Median candidate is 36 aa and hAChE is 543, so ~580 tokens — directly comparable to the 3 min 4 s run measured today. Ten candidates x 21 sequences is ~210 runs, roughly 11-14 h, so two overnight batches, or K=10 for a first pass. (4) Per run record ipTM, pair_chains_iptm, interface PAE via the existing Prediction.interface_pae(), and the count of interface contacts to the INTENDED epitope residues — for AChE the peripheral anionic site, Trp286, Tyr72, Tyr124, Asp74, which is checkable with the same contact code I used on the Huperzine A model today. (5) Statistic: per candidate, empirical permutation p = (1 + #{controls >= design}) / (1 + K), plus a standardised effect size (design - mean(controls)) / sd(controls). Apply Holm-Bonferroni across the ten candidates. Publish the full null distribution, not just the p-value. (6) Separately run peptide.py's sequence-only scores on design versus controls to demonstrate quantitatively which existing platform outputs are order-invariant and therefore carry no design information; those get relabelled or removed from the candidate cards. (7) Emit data/benchmark_scramble.json and add a verify_all.py suite that fails if a candidate card renders a score not tagged with its scramble-control verdict.

evidence.citation: Passaro S, Corso G, Wohlwend J, et al. 'Boltz-2: Towards Accurate and Efficient Binding Affinity Prediction.' bioRxiv 2025.06.14.659707. DOI 10.1101/2025.06.14.659707 (PMID 40667369).
evidence.supports: Boltz-2 supports multi-chain protein-protein cofolding and emits ipTM and pair_chains_iptm, which are the quantities the permutation test operates on. It is the only such model runnable here.

evidence.citation: Wallach I, Heifets A. 'Most Ligand-Based Classification Benchmarks Reward Memorization Rather than Generalization.' J Chem Inf Model 2018;58(5):916-932. DOI 10.1021/acs.jcim.7b00403 (arXiv:1706.06619).
evidence.supports: The general principle that an apparently strong score can be an artefact of dataset structure rather than of the property being modelled, motivating an explicit null-distribution control rather than a bare score.

evidence.citation: Buttenschoen M, Morris GM, Deane CM. 'PoseBusters: AI-based docking methods fail to generate physically valid poses or generalise to novel sequences.' Chem Sci 2024;15(9):3130-3139. DOI 10.1039/D3SC04185A.
evidence.supports: Demonstrates that DL structure predictors generalise poorly to novel sequences — the exact regime the 35 hand-assembled designs occupy, since none has a natural homolog. Justifies treating their scores as unvalidated until a control is run.

evidence.citation: Measured locally this session: /private/tmp/aff/run.log shows Boltz-2 v2.2.1 on MPS completing a 543-residue receptor plus ligand in 3:04 wall; the confidence file reports iptm 0.7136 with protein_iptm 0.0 because only one protein chain was present. data/dataset.json holds 35 candidates of length 26-100 aa, median 36.
evidence.supports: Establishes both the per-run cost for a ~580-token two-chain job and the mechanism behind the reported ipTM 0.00 — the peptides were folded alone, so no protein-protein interface existed to score. Confirms the compute budget for 210 runs is two overnight batches on this machine.

evidence.citation: Read locally this session: platform/cbc/peptide.py computes MW, net charge at pH 7.4, pI and GRAVY, all of which are functions of the amino-acid multiset and therefore invariant under permutation of the sequence.
evidence.supports: Proves a priori that a subset of the platform's current candidate scores cannot distinguish a design from a scramble, so those scores carry zero design information and must be relabelled regardless of what the folding experiment shows.

evidence.citation: Wan S, Zhang X, Xue X, Coveney PV. 'On the Reliability of AI Methods in Drug Discovery: Evaluation of Boltz-2 for Structure and Binding Affinity Prediction.' arXiv:2603.05532v1.
evidence.supports: Independent evidence that Boltz-2 confidence outputs can be high while the underlying prediction is poor, so a high ipTM on a designed peptide cannot be read as binding evidence without a matched control.

ideas.effort: ~2 days of implementation (two-chain cofold path, scramble generators with seeded RNG, permutation statistics) plus two overnight MPS batches totalling ~11-14 h at K=20 over ten candidates; a K=10 pilot on three candidates is a single 2 h run.
success_criteria: data/benchmark_scramble.json records, per candidate, the design score, every control score, the control type, the RNG seed, the permutation p-value and the standardised effect size.
Each candidate receives an explicit verdict string: 'sequence-specific (Holm-corrected p < 0.05)' or 'indistinguishable from a composition-matched shuffle'.

Every score rendered on a candidate card is tagged either sequence-specific, composition-determined, or untested; MW, net charge, pI and GRAVY are tagged composition-determined by construction, before any folding runs.
All 35 candidates (or the ten in the first tranche) have been co-folded with a named receptor at least once, so protein_iptm is no longer 0.00 by construction.
If no candidate passes the control, that null result is the headline in the README, not a footnote.
risks: K=20 gives a minimum attainable p of 1/21 = 0.048, which barely survives Holm correction over ten tests. Either adopt a pre-registered two-stage design (K=20 screen, K=100 confirmation for survivors, with the promotion rule fixed in advance) or report effect sizes and full null distributions instead of p-values.

Single-sequence mode (msa: empty) degrades receptor cofolding. The comparison stays internally valid because all arms share the mode, but absolute ipTM must not be read as binding evidence. Computing one receptor MSA and reusing it across every arm of that target reduces this at modest cost.

Passing the scramble control is necessary, not sufficient. It shows a score responds to sequence order; it says nothing about whether the predicted interaction is real. This must be stated in the output text or the result will be over-read as validation.

Several candidates are mechanistically inverted (extracellular peptides aimed at cytoplasmic targets, an aggregation-nucleating core inside a purported fibril disruptor). A candidate can pass the scramble control and still be biologically nonsensical; the control does not substitute for the mechanistic audit.

~14 h of sustained MPS load on a laptop invites thermal throttling; wall-clock estimates derived from the single 3 min run may be optimistic at scale, and per-run timings should be logged rather than assumed.
ideas.why_now: This is the only quantitative, falsifiable statement obtainable about the 35 candidates without a wet lab, and it costs two overnight batches. It simultaneously closes the single largest named scientific gap — no candidate has ever been predicted together with its receptor — and it can retire a set of candidate-card scores that are provably uninformative before anyone else reads them as evidence.

ideas.title: Turn the single Huperzine data point into a measured error bar: local calibration, null model and decoy AUROC for the Boltz-2 affinity head
ideas.one_line: Run a ≥60-pair ChEMBL-anchored retrospective benchmark of Boltz-2's affinity head on this exact hardware and MSA mode, so any emitted ΔG carries a locally measured RMSE, a null-model comparison and a hard applicability gate.
ideas.scientific_rationale: A predicted affinity is only a scientific statement if its error distribution is known. The repository currently has exactly one validation point — Huperzine A + human AChE, predicted IC50 1274 nM vs ChEMBL 5.0 nM, 2.41 log10 units (memory/ledger/affinity-compute.jsonl). One point yields no RMSE, no correlation, no confidence interval, and — critically — no answer to whether the model beats the trivial baseline of guessing each target's median measured potency. Docking-score validation practice is unambiguous here: a scoring function that does not outperform a per-target constant is not adding information, however plausible its individual numbers look. Boltz-2's affinity head is trained on a mixture of Ki/Kd/IC50 all mapped to log10(µM), so its output is an assay-blended potency-like quantity, not a thermodynamic ΔG; converting it with dG=(6−y)×1.364 (verified in the ledger to equal RT·ln10 at 298.15 K, consistent with thermo.RT=0.59248) is arithmetically sound but inherits that assay heterogeneity. The error bar therefore has to be measured on this box, in this mode, not borrowed from the authors' benchmark.
ideas.what_it_answers: If this platform emits a computed binding free energy for any small molecule, what is its error, and does the predictor beat guessing the target's median measured potency? Neither the magnitude nor the informativeness of a Boltz-2 affinity number is currently knowable from n=1.
ideas.method: New module platform/cbc/compute/affinity.py, built on the refusal pattern already proven in platform/cbc/compute/admet.py (which refuses peptides and >1000 Da) and calling structure.run_boltz(..., affinity_binder=...) from platform/cbc/compute/structure.py, whose _write_boltz_input already emits the `properties: - affinity: binder:` block. (1) PREFLIGHT GATE, using RDKit via platform/cbc/chem.py: refuse any peptide chain outright; refuse >128 heavy atoms (Boltz hard cap); mark 56 < N ≤ 128 as outside the recommended range and record it as a caveat rather than silently computing. I measured the eight dataset natural products with RDKit today — Huperzine A 18, Baicalein 20, Curcumin 27, Ginkgolide B 30, Asiatic acid 35, Salvianolic acid B 52, Ginsenoside Rg1 56, Onjisaponin V 123 heavy atoms — so Onjisaponin V sits inside the hard cap but at 2.2× the recommended limit and must not silently produce a number. (2) CALIBRATION SET from the existing live ingestion in platform/cbc/corpus.py: extend the np-cognition-v1 InclusionProtocol beyond CHEMBL220/ACHE to GSK3B, KEAP1, CHRM1 and NOS3 drawn from the 16 curated entries in dataset.json target_records; keep min_assay_confidence=8 and single-protein assignment; require a measured IC50/Ki/Kd. Aim for ≥60 pairs spanning ≥3 log units and ≥4 targets so within-target ranking and cross-target calibration can be scored separately. (3) RECEPTORS: mature chain from target_records, whose numbering is already resolved (the ACHE record carries the verified 'P22303 minus 31' mature convention and the Torpedo→human mapping W84→W86, Y121→Y124, W279→W286). (4) THREE ARMS, one variable each: (a) msa=empty, matching the one existing datapoint; (b) --use_msa_server on a paired subset of ≥20, to quantify the single-sequence penalty the Boltz docs warn about and that run_boltz already records in provenance; (c) DECOY CONTROL — each ligand against 3 unrelated receptors from the registry, giving an AUROC for affinity_probability_binary (the Huperzine run scored only 0.44, i.e. the model was not confident it binds at all; without a decoy distribution that number is uninterpretable). (5) METRICS: MAE/RMSE in log10 and in kcal/mol, Spearman ρ within-target and pooled, bootstrap 95% CIs, and a paired test against the per-target-median null. (6) WRITE-BACK: insert the measured value into thermo.METHOD_ACCURACY under a new key such as 'boltz-2 affinity head (2.2.1, single-sequence, Apple MPS, this repo)', so the platform's error table stops being purely literature-sourced; emit values only as Status.PREDICTED with uncertainty=measured RMSE+CI and applicability=the gate that was checked.

risks: Training-set leakage: Boltz-2 was trained on ChEMBL-derived affinity data, so a ChEMBL-drawn benchmark is leakage-suspect and the measured RMSE is optimistic. Assay heterogeneity: pooling IC50 with Ki/Kd inflates apparent error independently of the model. Report per-activity-type as well as pooled.

A good AUROC with a bad RMSE is the likely outcome (ranking without calibration). That must be reported as such and must not be laundered into an absolute ΔG.
ideas.why_now: It is the only affinity route on this hardware that has already produced a real number against measured ground truth, so it is the cheapest path from 'not_computed' to 'computed with a stated error'. Every other route requires new machinery first. And the cost of deferring it is that the one number already in the ledger cannot be interpreted at all.

ideas.title: Co-fold every candidate with its actual receptor, and measure — before emitting anything — how wrong a contacts-based ΔG would be on predicted peptide–protein structures
ideas.one_line: Build the receptor registry, replace the 22 lone-chain folds with real complexes, and run a pre-registered applicability-domain measurement of PRODIGY on crystal→predicted and protein→peptide, so the peptide ΔG decision is made on a measured error rather than an assertion.
ideas.scientific_rationale: Two domain shifts stand between PRODIGY and these molecules, and they compound. PRODIGY's published performance — Pearson r = −0.73, RMSE 1.89 kcal/mol — was obtained on 81 crystal protein–protein complexes whose affinities came from reliable direct methods (ITC/SPR/stopped-flow); on the complexes measured indirectly the correlation collapsed to r ≈ 0.04–0.05. Shift one: feeding it a Boltz-2 model instead of a crystal structure means the interfacial-contact count reflects the predictor's pose, not the physical interface — and every candidate folded so far has ipTM = 0.00 because it was folded alone, so there is currently no interface at all. Shift two: PRODIGY is a protein–protein model, and peptide interfaces are smaller and differently composed; the protein–peptide affinity literature exists precisely because protein–protein predictors are applied to peptides indiscriminately. Neither shift has ever been measured for this pipeline. The correct move is not to guess whether PRODIGY transfers, but to measure the transfer error first and let a pre-registered threshold decide. Note also a concrete argument against transcribing the equation: I retrieved the eLife 2015 regression twice this session from two independent sources and obtained two mutually sign-flipped forms of it. That is exactly the reconstruct-from-memory failure the project already prohibits, and it is why the reference implementation must be installed rather than reimplemented.
ideas.what_it_answers: For the 35 peptide candidates, is there any runnable method whose error is small enough to justify emitting a binding free energy — and if not, what is the measured size of the error we are declining to report? Today the not_computed note asserts absence of calculation; it cannot state how wrong the available method would be, and no candidate has ever been predicted in the presence of its receptor.
ideas.method: Executed in a fixed order, with the decision rule fixed in writing before any candidate is run. (1) RECEPTOR REGISTRY. The candidates' `targets` field is anatomical text ('CNS -> Brain -> Hippocampus (CA1 Cholinergic Terminals...)'), not a protein, so the mapping must be assembled from `bindingSites` + `mechanism` + the 16 curated target_records. Residue-level numbering is already resolved there: the ACHE record documents that the legacy string 'AChE CAS (Trp84, Phe330, Tyr121) & PAS (Trp286, Tyr72, Tyr341)' mixed two species' numbering, and supplies the verified mature convention (P22303 minus 31) plus the Torpedo→human map. (2) INSTALL, DON'T REIMPLEMENT. pip install prodigy-prot==2.4.0 — I verified this session that it installs cleanly on macOS arm64 (pure-Python wheel; freesasa 2.2.1 sdist compiles; Biopython pulls in). Pin the version in provenance.software. (3) REPRODUCE ON CRYSTALS FIRST. Run it on the crystal complexes of the Kastritis 2011 144-complex structure-based affinity benchmark subset used in the eLife study and confirm we recover r ≈ −0.73 / RMSE ≈ 1.89 kcal/mol. This is a wiring check: if we cannot reproduce the published number on the published inputs, nothing downstream is interpretable. (4) MEASURE THE TWO SHIFTS SEPARATELY. (a) crystal → predicted: Boltz-2 co-fold the same benchmark complexes and re-run PRODIGY on the models; report RMSE degradation as a function of ipTM. (b) protein–protein → protein–peptide: repeat on a protein–peptide structure+affinity set. (5) PRE-REGISTERED RULE: emit binding_free_energy for peptides only if RMSE on Boltz-predicted peptide complexes ≤ 2.0 kcal/mol AND Spearman ρ is significantly non-zero. The platform's own thermo.METHOD_ACCURACY already calls 1.1 kcal/mol the practical FEP ceiling and 2.5 for MM-GBSA, so 2.0 is deliberately generous. Otherwise binding_free_energy stays not_computed — but with a measured justification and a stated figure for how wrong it would have been. My expectation is that it fails the threshold; the measured refusal is the deliverable. (6) RUN THE CANDIDATE CO-FOLDS REGARDLESS, unconstrained as primary. structure.Chain/run_boltz already accepts multiple chains, so this needs a registry and a driver, not new inference code. Boltz's documented `pocket` and `contact` constraints could steer the peptide onto the bindingSites residues, but a pocket-forced score is circular evidence for the mechanism the pocket encoded; the constrained run is reported only as a secondary, explicitly labelled hypothesis-conditioned result, and the unconstrained ipTM/interface-PAE is what enters the record. This replaces the ipTM = 0.00 artefact with a real interface metric for all 35.

If the peptide arm cannot be built, say so: fall back to the crystal-PP result plus the retrieved statement that the domain is unsupported, and leave peptide ΔG not_computed — do not extrapolate the protein–protein RMSE onto peptides.

A high ipTM for such a pair is not therapeutic evidence; the mechanism liability must stay attached to the record and be surfaced next to any interface metric.

Receptor truncation to the curated domain would speed folding but changes the answer — AChE's catalytic gorge requires the whole fold. Run the full mature chain for gorge/pocket targets and accept the cost.
Single-sequence mode degrades the receptor fold too, not just the interface. Pair at least a subset with --use_msa_server (shared with CBC-CC-1) so the penalty is quantified once for both ideas.
ideas.why_now: This is the stated single largest scientific gap — 22 candidates folded as lone chains with ipTM = 0.00 — and the infrastructure to close it already exists (run_boltz takes multiple chains; target_records already carries UniProt accessions, domain boundaries and a resolved numbering frame). What is missing is the registry, the applicability measurement and the pre-registered rule. Doing the measurement before the reporting is also the only ordering that keeps a negative result publishable rather than embarrassing.

ideas.title: Quantify the uncertainty that comes from the molecules not being chemically defined: disulfide-isomer sensitivity, with OpenMM implicit solvent as a physics filter and an explicit refusal to call it an affinity
ideas.one_line: For the 21 candidates with ≥4 cysteines, enumerate or sample disulfide connectivities, re-fold and relax each in Amber14/GBn2, and report the resulting spread in ipTM and interface contacts as an irreducible uncertainty that must be added to any method error before a ΔG is reported.
ideas.scientific_rationale: Every structure and every affinity computed so far has silently accepted whatever disulfide bonding Boltz-2 happened to produce. Measured from the sequences today: of 35 candidates, 21 carry ≥4 cysteines — four with 8 Cys (105 distinct pairings each), four with 6 Cys (15 each), three with 4 Cys (3 each) — and 15 of 35 carry an odd cysteine count, so at least one free thiol is unavoidable. disulfide_connectivity is not_computed for 31. A cystine-rich peptide's fold and its interface are determined by connectivity; folding one arbitrary isomer and reporting its ipTM as 'the' value conflates model uncertainty with chemical indeterminacy. Reporting a ΔG with a ±1.9 kcal/mol method error while the input molecule is one of 105 possible chemical species is a category error of the same family the project already fixed once. On the free-energy side the verdict must be stated plainly and enforced in code: single-trajectory MM-GBSA must NOT be used to populate binding_free_energy here. These are 26–100 residue, highly charged peptides with no congeneric series; MM-GBSA neglects configurational entropy and is dominated by large cancelling electrostatic terms, and the 2.5 kcal/mol figure already in thermo.METHOD_ACCURACY applies to relative ranking within a congeneric small-molecule series and does not transfer. OpenMM's legitimate role here is as a mechanical consistency filter on the pose, not as an energy function.
ideas.what_it_answers: How much do ipTM, interfacial contacts and any downstream ΔG move when the only thing that changes is a disulfide connectivity that was never specified? Nothing in the platform answers this — and it is a prerequisite for the error bars produced by CBC-CC-1 and CBC-CC-2 to mean anything for the cysteine-rich majority.
ideas.method: (1) SCOPE to the 8–10 worst offenders (≥6 Cys). Enumerate connectivities exhaustively for 4 and 6 Cys (3 and 15 pairings); for 8 Cys sample a bounded set — the pattern inherited from the parent published motif (the motifs are natural peptides with solved parent structures, retrievable via motif_provenance in dataset.json) plus ~15 random draws from the 105. (2) ENFORCE each connectivity in the co-fold via Boltz's documented bond constraint, `constraints: - bond: {atom1: [A, i, SG], atom2: [A, j, SG]}`. The docs state bond constraints are 'currently only supported for CCD ligands and canonical residues' but do not confirm intra-chain SG–SG, so this must be verified empirically against a solved disulfide-rich control (a conotoxin or an EGF-like domain) BEFORE use; if it fails, connectivity is instead imposed in the relaxation stage. (3) RELAX AND FILTER with OpenMM. Verified this session on this machine: openmm 8.5.2 ships a macosx_11_0_arm64 wheel, installs, and exposes Reference / CPU / OpenCL platforms; pdbfixer 1.12.0 builds. All candidate residues are canonical, so Amber14 + GBn2 implicit solvent applies with no custom parameterisation. Per isomer: protonate at pH 7.4 consistent with the Henderson–Hasselbalch model already in platform/cbc/peptide.py, create the specified SS bonds, minimise, run a short restrained equilibration, then unrestrained implicit-solvent MD; record interface heavy-atom contact survival and interface RMSD drift. (4) REPORT A SPREAD, NOT A VALUE. For each candidate, min/median/max of ipTM and of PRODIGY interfacial-contact counts across isomers. That range is an irreducible uncertainty attributable to undefined chemistry and must be combined in quadrature with the method RMSE from CBC-CC-1/2 before any ΔG is reported. (5) ENFORCE THE REFUSAL IN CODE: the module computes no MM-GBSA ΔG and exposes no path to write one into binding_free_energy; verify_all.py gains a check that no candidate with ≥4 Cys and undefined connectivity may carry a PREDICTED ΔG without the isomer spread attached.
