A verify_all.py check that fails the build if any candidate with ≥4 Cys and undefined connectivity carries a PREDICTED binding_free_energy without an attached isomer spread — and a check that no code path can write an MM-GBSA value into binding_free_energy.
risks: Apple's OpenCL is deprecated and may be no faster than the multithreaded CPU platform. Benchmark both before committing; if only CPU is viable, cut MD length to minimisation plus a short restrained run, and state the reduced sampling rather than quietly shortening it.

Force-field relaxation can hold an incorrect pose together for nanoseconds. A 'pass' is a weak negative filter only — an exclusion criterion, never evidence of binding — and must be labelled that way in the record.

The 15 odd-cysteine candidates can never be fully oxidised; the free-thiol position is a further undetermined variable. Report it as an additional degree of freedom rather than capping it arbitrarily.
Sampling 15 of 105 pairings for the 8-Cys cases gives a lower bound on the spread, not the full range. State it as a lower bound.
Amber14 covers canonical residues only; if any candidate turns out to require non-canonical chemistry it is excluded from this analysis, not approximated with substitute parameters.
Scope creep: this could expand into a folding study. Hold the line at 8–10 candidates and treat the spread, not any individual structure, as the deliverable.
ideas.why_now: Both CBC-CC-1 and CBC-CC-2 will attach error bars to numbers whose input molecule is not chemically defined for 21 of 35 candidates. Measuring that conditionality once is far cheaper than generating more conditional numbers, and it is the only way the quoted uncertainties are honest rather than partial. It also converts a second standing not_computed field (disulfide_connectivity, 31 candidates) from an open gap into either a computed answer or a measured statement of why it cannot be one.

proposals.expert: Structural biology (X-ray crystallography and cryo-EM; deposited-structure validation), 21 years post-PhD

ideas.title: All-atom physical-validity gate, and disulfide connectivity read off the coordinates the model already produced
ideas.one_line: Replace the Cα-only geometry audit with a PoseBusters-class all-atom check (chirality, ω, clashes, S–S distance/χ3, sulfur valence) calibrated against deposited structures, which simultaneously converts `disulfide_connectivity` from not_computed to a computed, provenance-carrying value for the cysteine-containing candidates.
ideas.scientific_rationale: `Prediction.geometry_check()` measures exactly one quantity: the distance between consecutive Cα atoms. That is a necessary condition for a polypeptide and almost nothing more. It cannot see a D-amino acid, an eclipsed disulfide, a trivalent sulfur, a non-planar peptide bond, or a steric clash — all known failure modes of diffusion-based structure generators, and all of them the checks PoseBusters was written to enforce. Worse, platform/cbc/predictor.py:227 (`if f[idx["label_atom_id"]].strip('"') != "CA": continue`) discards every atom needed to detect them before any check runs, so the platform is structurally incapable of the audit. I ran the missing checks this session on the 22 Boltz-2 mmCIFs still sitting in /tmp/cbc_boltz. Backbone stereochemistry is clean (0 D-residues in 22 structures, 1 cis peptide bond, ~0 non-bonded heavy-atom contacts <2.2 Å) — so the check is not vacuous, it discriminates. Sulfur chemistry is not clean. Across 38 predicted S–S contacts the distances run 1.705–2.552 Å (mean 2.081, sd 0.203), 21 of 38 outside 1.95–2.15 Å, against a measured experimental reference of 2.031–2.064 Å in human AChE 4EY7. χ3 (Cβ-Sγ-Sγ-Cβ) in 4EY7 is +89.7/−75.5/−83.3°, the classical gauche geometry Thornton documented; the predictions include χ3 of −1.1°, +156.0°, +163.8° and +174.4°, eclipsed and anti conformations no real disulfide adopts. Four candidates (BasalM1-PAM-B2 Cys9, BasalSuper-AChE-TrkA-B5 Cys17, MicroDual-Trem2-Nrf2-M5 Cys10, MicroNrf2-AntiInflam-M2 Cys23) place one cysteine within 2.5 Å of two others — a trivalent sulfur, chemically impossible. None of this is visible in pLDDT: PfcACh-PAM-P1, with a 1.705 Å S–S, carries no flag at all. Separately, the current gate has a measured false-positive mode: the single Cα-Cα outlier in 4EY7 is the genuine cis-Tyr105-Pro106 bond at 2.853 Å (ω = −1.7°), which `abs(v - 3.80) > 0.5` counts as an error. At 4EY7's length one cis bond is 0.19% and harmless, but 27 of 35 candidates carry ≥2 prolines, and in a 26–33-residue peptide two cis bonds is 6.7–8.0%, over the 5% threshold at predictor.py:159 — the gate would declare a correct structure "not a folded polypeptide".
ideas.what_it_answers: Are the coordinates the platform's own predictor emitted chemically possible at all — and what disulfide connectivity does the model actually assign to the 30 cysteine-containing candidates whose `disulfide_connectivity` field currently reads not_computed for 31 of 35 entries? The platform today can answer neither; it can only say that consecutive Cα atoms are 3.8 Å apart.
ideas.method: 1) Widen the parser. `parse_mmcif` at platform/cbc/predictor.py:178-249 keeps one CA per residue; add an all-atom path (or swap to gemmi 0.6.5, already installed in .venv312 as a Boltz dependency, so no new install) retaining N, CA, C, O, CB, SG. Keep the CA-only path for the light-weight display route. 2) New module platform/cbc/structval.py with: chirality via the N-CA-C-CB improper; ω via gemmi.calculate_omega with cis/trans/twisted bands; non-bonded heavy-atom clashes via gemmi.NeighborSearch + gemmi.ContactSearch(Ignore.AdjacentResidues); bond lengths and angles against Engh & Huber; disulfide detection via Sγ-Sγ distance plus χ3 from gemmi.calculate_dihedral plus a valence check that no sulfur appears in two bonds. 3) Calibrate every threshold empirically, not from memory: build the reference distribution by running the same code over the ~60 deposited structures already named in data/dataset.json -> target_records.targets[*].pdb_examples (4EY7, 4EY6, 2FLU, 3FXI, 1WWW, …), fetched from files.rcsb.org. I measured the reference on 4EY7 this session: N-CA-C-CB improper −122.63 ± 3.19° over 481 residues with zero sign flips; S–S 2.031–2.064 Å; χ3 near ±90°. Store the reference distribution as a data file with its own provenance so no constant is hard-coded from recall. 4) Optionally cross-check with `pip install posebusters` (0.6.5 on PyPI, pure Python over rdkit/numpy/pandas, no GPU) for ligand-side checks when small molecules enter the pipeline. 5) Emit `disulfide_connectivity` as a real ProvenanceValue with status PREDICTED, method "Sγ-Sγ < 2.5 Å in Boltz-2 v2.2.1 coordinates, msa=empty", and the measured distance and χ3 in the uncertainty field — refusing to emit it (leaving not_computed) where the sulfur-valence or χ3 check fails, which is the honest outcome for those four candidates. 6) Fix the durability bug first: platform/compare_real_vs_hardcoded.py:39 sets WORK = Path('/tmp/cbc_boltz') and data/real_vs_hardcoded.json records zero coordinate paths, so the only copy of the 22 structures lives in a directory macOS purges. Move it under a repo path and record the mmCIF path in every row. 7) Wire the checks into platform/validate.py as new violation categories and into verify_all.py's 215 checks.

evidence.citation: Buttenschoen M, Morris GM, Deane CM. PoseBusters: AI-based docking methods fail to generate physically valid poses or generalise to novel sequences. Chemical Science (2024). DOI 10.1039/d3sc04185a
evidence.supports: Establishes that deep-learning structure generators routinely emit poses that pass learned confidence scores while violating basic physical and chemical constraints, and defines the check battery (stereochemistry, bond geometry, internal and intermolecular clashes) this module reimplements for the protein side.

evidence.citation: Williams CJ, Headd JJ, Moriarty NW, et al. MolProbity: More and better reference data for improved all-atom structure validation. Protein Science 27:293-315 (2018). DOI 10.1002/pro.3330
evidence.supports: The reference-data-driven validation philosophy adopted here: thresholds derived from a curated set of high-resolution deposited structures rather than from remembered constants; also the source of the clashscore and Ramachandran framing.

evidence.citation: Thornton JM. Disulphide bridges in globular proteins. Journal of Molecular Biology 151:261-287 (1981). DOI 10.1016/0022-2836(81)90515-5
evidence.supports: The canonical survey of observed disulfide geometry in globular proteins — S–S length and the strong χ3 preference near ±90° — the literature anchor for treating χ3 of −1° or +174° as a physical violation.

evidence.citation: Engh RA, Huber R. Accurate bond and angle parameters for X-ray protein structure refinement. Acta Crystallographica Section A 47:392-400 (1991). DOI 10.1107/s0108767391001071
evidence.supports: Standard restraint targets for protein bond lengths and angles, used as the reference for the covalent-geometry arm of the check.

evidence.citation: PDB 4EY7, Crystal Structure of Recombinant Human Acetylcholinesterase in Complex with Donepezil, 2.35 Å; primary citation Cheung J, Rudolph MJ, Burshteyn F, et al. Structures of human acetylcholinesterase in complex with pharmacologically important ligands. J Med Chem 55:10282-10286 (2012). DOI 10.1021/jm300871x. Coordinates retrieved this session from files.rcsb.org.
evidence.supports: The experimental reference I actually measured against: Cys69-Cys96 2.056 Å χ3 +89.7°, Cys257-Cys272 2.064 Å χ3 −75.5°, Cys409-Cys529 2.031 Å χ3 −83.3°; improper −122.63 ± 3.19° over 481 residues; one cis peptide bond (Tyr105-Pro106, Cα-Cα 2.853 Å, ω −1.7°). It is also the target-record PDB for ACHE, so the reference set is already curated inside the repo.

evidence.citation: Passaro S, et al. Boltz-2: Towards Accurate and Efficient Binding Affinity Prediction. bioRxiv 2025.06.14.659707 (2025). DOI 10.1101/2025.06.14.659707
evidence.supports: Identifies the model whose output is being validated (v2.2.1, installed in .venv312) and its confidence outputs, none of which include a physical-validity statement.

ideas.effort: 2 days. gemmi 0.6.5, biopython and DockQ are already installed in .venv312; the 22 mmCIFs already exist; I ran the complete disulfide/chirality/ω/clash analysis over all 22 in under a second of wall time this session. The only new cost is the reference-set download (~60 mmCIFs, minutes) and the write-up into validate.py.
success_criteria: platform/cbc/structval.py exists and, run over the 22 mmCIFs, reproduces the numbers measured this session: 38 S–S contacts <2.6 Å, mean 2.081 Å, sd 0.203, range 1.705-2.552; 21/38 outside 1.95-2.15 Å; exactly 4 candidates with a cysteine in two bonds (BasalM1-PAM-B2 Cys9, BasalSuper-AChE-TrkA-B5 Cys17, MicroDual-Trem2-Nrf2-M5 Cys10, MicroNrf2-AntiInflam-M2 Cys23); 0 D-residues; 1 cis peptide bond.
Running the same module over the deposited reference set produces zero sulfur-valence violations and zero D-residues — a false-positive rate of 0 on real crystal structures.
The ±0.5 Å Cα-Cα rule is replaced by an ω-aware rule, verified by 4EY7's Tyr105-Pro106 being classified as a legitimate cis peptide bond rather than a geometry outlier.

data/dataset.json carries a non-null disulfide_connectivity for candidates whose predicted S–S set passes distance, χ3 and valence, each with status PREDICTED and the measured S–S distance recorded; candidates failing valence keep not_computed with the violation stated as the reason.
data/real_vs_hardcoded.json records an mmCIF path for every row, those files live outside /tmp, and verify_all.py passes with the new checks added.
risks: Boltz-2 does not declare bonds, it places atoms. Reading connectivity from Sγ-Sγ proximity is an inference about the model's intent, not a chemical measurement, and must be labelled PREDICTED with the distance shown, never MEASURED. The four trivalent-sulfur cases prove the inference can be ill-posed and must be allowed to return 'undetermined'.

Single-sequence mode (msa=empty) is a known accuracy penalty; distorted S–S geometry may be an artefact of that rather than of the sequences. The honest reading is 'this pipeline configuration does not produce disulfide geometry of experimental quality' — itself a finding — not 'these peptides cannot fold'. An MSA-mode re-run on two cases would separate the two.

Threshold choice on χ3 is genuinely fuzzy; strained disulfides do occur in real proteins. Report the value alongside the verdict and set bands from the measured reference distribution rather than a single cut.
A 26-residue peptide gives a tiny sample; per-structure outlier fractions are noisy and should be reported as counts with the denominator, not as percentages.
ideas.why_now: It is the only proposal here needing no new prediction run, no network dependency and no GPU time — the coordinates exist and the tooling is installed, as demonstrated. It also has a deadline: the 22 mmCIFs sit in /tmp/cbc_boltz, which macOS will purge, and nothing in the repository records their location. And it removes a live overstatement: `plausible_protein: true` currently appears in data/real_vs_hardcoded.json for every one of the 22 structures, including the four with chemically impossible sulfur — precisely the kind of unearned green light this rebuild exists to eliminate.

ideas.title: Held-out benchmark against deposited structures: run the production pipeline on complexes whose answer is already known, and publish the measured accuracy
ideas.one_line: Fold the platform's own targets — and the peptide–receptor complexes among them that already have crystal structures — in the exact production configuration (Boltz-2 v2.2.1, msa=empty, MPS), score against the deposited coordinates with DockQ v2 and gemmi superposition, and attach that measured accuracy to every confidence number the platform reports.
ideas.scientific_rationale: The platform reports pLDDT, pTM, ipTM and PAE with no statement of what those numbers are worth in this configuration. That is the same category of error the rebuild was meant to fix, one level up: the values are now genuinely computed, but their meaning is still asserted rather than measured. Confidence metrics are model self-assessments and their relationship to accuracy is regime-dependent — the AlphaFold-Multimer and pDockQ literature exists precisely because ipTM had to be calibrated against DockQ before it could be used as a screening criterion. The platform is unusually well placed to do this and has not: data/dataset.json -> target_records already carries a curated, verified PDB list for all 16 targets (ACHE 4EY7/4EY6/1B41, KEAP1+NFE2L2 2FLU, NTRK1 1WWW/2IFG, TLR4 3FXI, FZD8 5UN5, TREM2 6XDS, …) with domain boundaries and numbering conventions already resolved by the curation workflow. Among them are genuine peptide-in-groove complexes of exactly the class being predicted: 2FLU is the KEAP1 Kelch domain (308 residues) bound to a 16-mer Neh2 peptide, AFFAQLQLDEETGEFL, at 1.5 Å — I retrieved and confirmed both entities from RCSB this session. Predicting that complex is a direct, held-out test of whether this pipeline can place a short peptide in the site where the platform's own KEAP1-decoy candidates (HippoNrf-KeapDecoy-X3, CogNrf-KeapDis-03, MicroNrf2-AntiInflam-M2) claim to bind. The compute objection is weaker than it looks: the 22 existing runs took 26 s each on MPS, essentially independent of length from 26 to 100 residues, so fixed overhead dominates at these sizes and a ~320-token Kelch+peptide job is minutes-scale, not hours. The receptor-monomer arm is nearly free — gemmi.calculate_superposition ran in under a millisecond and gave 0.177 Å over 525 Cα between 4EY7 and 4EY6 when I tested it, so the accuracy readout machinery is a solved problem.
ideas.what_it_answers: When this pipeline reports ipTM = 0.6 or pLDDT = 78, what is the measured probability that the structure is right? The platform cannot answer this for any value, because it has never once predicted a system whose answer is known. Concretely: (a) how accurate is Boltz-2 msa=empty on the platform's own 16 receptors, in Å against their crystal structures; (b) on the peptide–receptor complexes among them, what DockQ does it achieve, and what ipTM threshold — if any — separates acceptable from incorrect models here?
ideas.method: 1) Receptor-monomer arm. For each of the 16 targets, fold the domain of interest whose boundaries are already recorded in target_records (NTRK2 Ig2 295-365; KEAP1 Kelch propeller; TREM2 Ig-V ectodomain), Boltz-2 msa=empty on MPS, same settings as platform/cbc/compute/structure.py:run_boltz. Superpose on the deposited chain with gemmi.calculate_superposition(..., SupSelect.CaP) and report Cα RMSD and TM-score. Repeat MSA-on for two or three cases so the cost of single-sequence mode is measured rather than assumed. 2) Complex arm. Identify deposited entries in target_records containing a receptor plus a short peptide or protein ligand — 2FLU (KEAP1 Kelch + Neh2 16-mer, 1.5 Å) is cleanest; 1WWW/2IFG (TrkA d5 + NGF) and 3FXI (TLR4 + MD-2) extend the set. Re-predict each from sequence alone and score against the deposited complex with DockQ 2.1.3, already installed in .venv312 (`DockQ` CLI on PATH; `DockQ.DockQ.run_on_all_native_interfaces` importable — I verified both this session). Report DockQ, iRMSD, LRMSD, fnat and CAPRI class alongside the model's own ipTM and pTM. 3) Build the calibration table: ipTM vs DockQ for every benchmark case, stored in data/ as a provenance-carrying artefact. 4) Wire it into the reporting layer so no ipTM is displayed without the benchmark N, the measured DockQ distribution, and an explicit statement when N is too small to support a threshold. 5) Cross-check against retrieval where possible: platform/cbc/compute/structure.py already has fetch_alphafold_db, so for each natural receptor the AlphaFold-DB model gives a second independent comparison at zero compute cost.

evidence.citation: Basu S, Wallner B. DockQ: A Quality Measure for Protein-Protein Docking Models. PLoS ONE 11:e0161879 (2016). DOI 10.1371/journal.pone.0161879
evidence.supports: Defines the continuous quality measure and its mapping onto CAPRI acceptable/medium/high classes — the scoring standard for the complex arm.

evidence.citation: Mirabello C, Wallner B. DockQ v2: Improved automatic quality measure for protein multimers, nucleic acids, and small molecules. bioRxiv 2024.05.28.596225 (2024). DOI 10.1101/2024.05.28.596225
evidence.supports: The version actually installed here (DockQ 2.1.3 in .venv312), extending DockQ to multimers and small molecules, which matters because several targets are membrane or multi-chain systems.

evidence.citation: Evans R, O'Neill M, Pritzel A, et al. Protein complex prediction with AlphaFold-Multimer. bioRxiv 2021.10.04.463034 (2021). DOI 10.1101/2021.10.04.463034
evidence.supports: Introduces ipTM and demonstrates that it must be validated against DockQ on held-out complexes before use as a screening criterion — the precedent for making calibration a prerequisite rather than an optional extra.

evidence.citation: Zhang Y, Skolnick J. Scoring function for automated assessment of protein structure template quality. Proteins 57:702-710 (2004). DOI 10.1002/prot.20264
evidence.supports: TM-score, the length-independent monomer accuracy measure used in the receptor arm, where plain Cα RMSD is misleading across domains of very different size.

evidence.citation: Zhang C, Shine M, Pyle AM, Zhang Y. US-align: universal structure alignments of proteins, nucleic acids, and macromolecular complexes. Nature Methods 19:1109-1115 (2022). DOI 10.1038/s41592-022-01585-1
evidence.supports: Reference implementation for complex-level structural alignment, should gemmi's sequence-dependent superposition prove insufficient for cases with chain-order or numbering mismatches.

evidence.citation: PDB 2FLU, Crystal Structure of the Kelch-Neh2 Complex, X-ray 1.5 Å, two polymer entities (KEAP1 Kelch 308 aa; Neh2 peptide AFFAQLQLDEETGEFL, 16 aa); primary citation Lo S-C, Li X, Henzl MT, Beamer LJ, Hannink M. Structure of the Keap1:Nrf2 interface provides mechanistic insight into Nrf2 signalling. EMBO Journal 25:3605-3617 (2006). DOI 10.1038/sj.emboj.7601243. Entry and entity records retrieved this session from data.rcsb.org.
evidence.supports: The concrete anchor case: a high-resolution receptor + 16-mer peptide complex of exactly the size and class the platform needs to predict, already named in the repository's own KEAP1 and NFE2L2 target records.

ideas.effort: 4-6 days. The scoring stack is installed and verified working. The real work is chain mapping and residue-numbering reconciliation between deposited entries and predictions — the target records already resolve the numbering conventions, which removes the worst of it. Compute is modest for domain-sized systems (26 s per lone chain measured; a ~320-token complex is minutes) but full-length AChE at ~590 tokens has not been timed on MPS and pair-representation cost scales roughly with N², so run a timing pilot before committing to the large targets and fall back to domain constructs where the boundary is already recorded.
success_criteria: data/benchmark_structures.json exists with one row per benchmark case: PDB ID, resolution, chains, prediction settings, Cα RMSD, TM-score and — for complexes — DockQ, iRMSD, LRMSD, fnat, CAPRI class, plus the model's ipTM and pTM.

The 2FLU case runs end to end: Kelch + 16-mer Neh2 predicted from sequence alone and scored with DockQ 2.1.3 against the deposited complex, with the CAPRI class reported whatever it turns out to be — including 'incorrect', which is a valid and publishable result.
At least 8 of the 16 receptor domains have a measured Cα RMSD and TM-score against a deposited structure, with the msa=empty vs msa-on difference measured on at least two.

No ipTM value anywhere in the platform's output or UI appears without the benchmark N and the measured DockQ distribution attached; where N is too small to support a threshold, the output says so explicitly rather than implying one.
The whole benchmark re-runs from a single command and is covered by verify_all.py.
risks: Boltz-2's training set includes PDB entries deposited before its cutoff, so 2FLU (2006), 4EY7 (2012) and the rest are almost certainly memorised. The measured DockQ is therefore an optimistic ceiling, not an unbiased estimate, and must be reported as such. Mitigations: state it plainly in the artefact; prefer entries released after the Boltz-2 training cutoff where any exist among the target list; and treat the benchmark as 'the pipeline cannot do better than this' rather than 'the pipeline achieves this on novel designs'.

Fifteen-odd benchmark cases is a small N. It can support a statement like 'in this configuration the pipeline reached CAPRI-acceptable on k of n cases' but cannot support a calibrated ipTM cut-off. The deliverable must refuse to publish a threshold the N cannot carry.

Several targets are membrane proteins (CHRM1, PTAFR, SLC1A2, CHRNA7) whose deposited structures involve detergents, nanobodies, fusion partners or cryo-EM at modest resolution. RMSD against these is confounded by construct differences; restrict the monomer arm to soluble domains with clean crystal structures and record the exclusion reason for the rest.

Chain-mapping and numbering errors are the classic silent failure in this kind of benchmark: a low DockQ can mean a wrong model or a wrong alignment. Every case needs a stored superposition and a chain-correspondence record so a bad score can be distinguished from a bad comparison.
ideas.why_now: The record already states that no candidate has ever been predicted with its receptor. The moment receptor complexes start being predicted, the platform will begin emitting nonzero ipTM values — and without a calibration measured first, those numbers become exactly the kind of confident, uninterpretable figure the 97-finding review was convened over. Building the benchmark before the complexes, not after, is the difference between a validation workbench and a new generation of unearned numbers. The prerequisites are unusually cheap here because the curation workflow has already done the hard part: a verified PDB list and resolved numbering conventions for all 16 targets sit unused in data/dataset.json.

ideas.title: Interface forensics with a scrambled-sequence null: buried surface area, contact maps and epitope overlap, each reported against its own decoy distribution
ideas.one_line: For every candidate–receptor complex, compute buried SASA, the residue-residue contact map and hot-spot residues, test whether the predicted epitope overlaps the experimentally observed ligand site from the target's own PDB entry, and report every one of those quantities against a matched distribution from sequence-scrambled decoys folded against the same receptor.
ideas.scientific_rationale: Once complexes are predicted, the platform will face a harder question than 'what is the ipTM': is the interface real, and is it in the right place? Both are answerable from coordinates and neither is answerable now. `Prediction.interface_pae()` at predictor.py:126-140 is the only interface-aware code in the repository and it returns a single scalar; there is no buried-surface-area calculation, no contact map, no hot-spot identification, and no comparison to where the natural ligand actually binds. The last matters enormously for this catalogue, because the review already established that several candidates are mechanistically inverted — an Aβ-nucleating core inside a molecule labelled a fibril disruptor, extracellular peptides aimed at cytoplasmic targets. Epitope overlap is the structural test that catches that class of error empirically rather than by argument: if a KEAP1-decoy peptide's predicted contacts do not overlap the Kelch residues that contact the Neh2 ETGE motif in 2FLU, the mechanism claim is falsified from coordinates. The decoy arm is what makes any of it interpretable. Structure predictors will place two chains together and report a nonzero interface for almost any pair; without a null distribution from scrambled sequences of identical composition folded against the same receptor, a buried area of 700 Å² or an ipTM of 0.35 is a number without a scale. This is the standard PISA-style analysis of an interface — area, contacts, chemistry — combined with the null-model discipline the pDockQ work made routine. The tooling is in place and fast: Biopython's Shrake-Rupley implementation computed residue-level SASA over the full 543-residue AChE model in 0.9 s when I ran it this session, and gemmi's contact search over the same structure returned in milliseconds.
ideas.what_it_answers: Is a predicted candidate–receptor interface distinguishable from what this model produces for a scrambled sequence of identical amino-acid composition against the same receptor — and does the interface it predicts sit on the site where the natural ligand or inhibitor is experimentally observed to bind? The platform can answer neither. It has no measure of interface size or composition, no epitope comparison, and no null model of any kind, so it currently has no way to tell a designed binder from a peptide that merely lands somewhere on a large protein.
ideas.method: 1) platform/cbc/interface.py: given a multi-chain prediction, compute per-residue SASA with Bio.PDB.SASA.ShrakeRupley for each chain in isolation and in complex, derive buried SASA per residue and total (ΔSASA = SASA_free − SASA_complex, halved per convention and stated as such); build the inter-chain residue contact map with gemmi.NeighborSearch/ContactSearch at a stated heavy-atom cutoff; classify contacts polar, hydrophobic or charged; rank hot-spot residues by buried area and contact count; report interface polarity and the fraction of interface residues below pLDDT 70. Add pDockQ from interface contact count and interface pLDDT as a second, published interface score independent of Boltz's own. 2) Epitope reference. For each target, extract the experimentally observed binding-site residue set from the deposited entry already named in target_records — Kelch residues contacting the Neh2 peptide in 2FLU, gorge and peripheral-anionic-site residues contacting donepezil in 4EY7 — using the same contact code, so predicted and experimental epitopes are defined identically. Report Jaccard overlap between predicted candidate epitope and experimental ligand epitope. This also cross-checks the residue-level claims in data/residue_audit.json, which found eight fabricated binding-site residues; an epitope defined from coordinates is immune to that failure mode. 3) Decoy arm. For each candidate–receptor pair, fold N ≥ 20 shuffled variants of the candidate sequence (composition preserved, order randomised, seed recorded) against the same receptor under identical settings, and report every metric — ipTM, buried SASA, contacts, pDockQ, epitope overlap — as the candidate's value plus its percentile in the decoy distribution. A candidate that does not exceed its own scrambles is reported as indistinguishable from noise. 4) Gate the whole thing on Idea 2: no interface number is displayed until the benchmark establishes what this pipeline can do on complexes it should get right.
