evidence.citation: PDB 4EY7 (human AChE + donepezil, 2.35 Å) and PDB 2FLU (KEAP1 Kelch + Neh2 16-mer, 1.5 Å), both retrieved this session from RCSB and both already listed in data/dataset.json target_records for ACHE, KEAP1 and NFE2L2.
evidence.supports: Provides experimentally observed ligand epitopes for two of the platform's targets, against which predicted candidate epitopes can be scored — the ground truth for the epitope-overlap arm.

ideas.effort: 1 week of implementation once Idea 2 exists, plus compute for the decoy arm. The analysis code is cheap and the libraries are installed and timed. The decoy folding is the cost: 20 scrambles × a dozen candidate–receptor pairs is 240 complex predictions. At the measured 26 s per lone chain that would be trivial, but complexes are several times larger and the MPS scaling is unmeasured — time one complex first and size the decoy set to the measured rate. This is honestly the arm most likely to want a GPU; if it does, say so and run a reduced decoy set (N = 10, three candidates) rather than dropping the null model, since a small null is far better than none.
success_criteria: platform/cbc/interface.py reports, for any multi-chain prediction: total and per-residue buried SASA, the inter-chain contact map, ranked hot-spot residues, interface polarity, mean interface pLDDT and pDockQ — validated by reproducing the known KEAP1-Neh2 interface from the deposited 2FLU coordinates before it is ever applied to a prediction.

Epitope overlap is computed with identical contact criteria on both sides, and the experimental epitopes extracted for ACHE (4EY7, donepezil) and KEAP1 (2FLU, Neh2) match the binding-site descriptions already verified in target_records.

Every candidate interface metric in data/ carries its decoy percentile and the decoy N; any candidate not exceeding the 95th percentile of its own scrambles is labelled 'not distinguishable from a composition-matched scramble'.

The three KEAP1-directed candidates (HippoNrf-KeapDecoy-X3, CogNrf-KeapDis-03, MicroNrf2-AntiInflam-M2) each carry a stated Jaccard overlap with the experimental Neh2 epitope, whatever that value is — including zero.
No interface number reaches the UI without its decoy percentile and the Idea 2 benchmark context attached; verify_all.py enforces this as a data-integrity rule.
risks: Composition-preserving shuffles are an imperfect null: they destroy sequence motifs but also destroy foldability, so a scramble may under-bind for the wrong reason. Report a second null — the same candidate against an unrelated receptor from the target list — so the two can be compared, and state the limitation.

Buried SASA depends on probe radius, hydrogen treatment and side-chain rotamer placement, and predicted side chains in single-sequence mode are unreliable. Report the settings, report backbone-only and all-atom variants, and do not over-interpret differences below roughly 100 Å².

Epitope overlap presumes the deposited ligand site is the only functionally relevant one, which is false for allosteric targets — the AChE peripheral anionic site is a second real site and the target record already flags it. Score overlap against every annotated site separately rather than collapsing to one number.

This is the most compute-hungry proposal of the three and the only one whose cost I could not measure. If the timing pilot shows complexes take hours rather than minutes on MPS, the honest response is a reduced decoy set with the reduced N stated, not a silently dropped null model.
ideas.why_now: Ideas 1 and 2 make the platform's structural output trustworthy; this is what makes it useful. It is also the only proposal that tests the mechanistic claims directly from coordinates rather than from argument — the review found eight fabricated binding-site residues and several mechanistically inverted designs, and an epitope defined by contacts in a predicted complex, compared against contacts in a crystal structure, is immune to both failure modes. It comes third because it is meaningless without Idea 2's calibration: a buried surface area from a pipeline of unmeasured accuracy is a precise number about nothing.

proposals.expert: Medicinal chemistry (natural products, pharmacophore analysis, assay-interference debunking); 20 years post-PhD

ideas.title: Warhead conjugability: ligand burial and gorge-escape exit vectors from experimental holo structures
ideas.one_line: Compute, from real co-crystal structures, whether each natural-product warhead has any solvent-exposed atom that can carry a linker without destroying the observed binding mode — and how long that linker would have to be to reach bulk solvent.
ideas.scientific_rationale:
Every one of the 25 hand-assembled conjugates presumes that a natural-product motif can be covalently tethered to a peptide and still bind its target. That presumption is a geometric claim about the holo complex, and it is falsifiable from experimental coordinates alone. A ligand fully enclosed by protein has no exit vector: any substituent added at any atom must displace protein, so conjugation is not a linker-optimisation problem but a binding-mode-destruction problem. This is the classic fragment-growing vector analysis, run in reverse as a veto.

I ran the calculation this session on the exact case named in the dataset. Candidate HippoAChE-AlkaPept-X2 declares chemStruct = 'Huperzine A Pyridone Core (C15H18N2O) + Cys-Lys Amide Coupling'. Using PDB 4EY5 (recombinant human AChE + (-)-huperzine A) and Biopython's Shrake-Rupley implementation, huperzine A's SASA falls from 406.6 A^2 free to 6.2 A^2 in the complex — 98.5% buried. Per-atom, the most exposed atom is N2, the exocyclic primary amine, retaining 4.33 A^2 (12.3% of its free value); every other atom retains <1.2 A^2 and eleven atoms retain exactly zero. A methylene needs roughly 20-30 A^2 of solvent-facing area to project a substituent; 4.33 A^2 is not an exit vector, it is a crack.

Worse, N2 is not a spare handle. Its nearest protein neighbours in 4EY5 are Tyr337-OH at 3.01 A and Trp86 CG/CB at 3.49/3.51 A — a direct hydrogen bond plus face packing on the catalytic-anionic-site tryptophan. The pyridone carbonyl O1 hydrogen bonds Tyr133-OH at 2.55 A, and C7/C8/C9 sit 3.19-3.84 A from His447 of the catalytic triad. Amide-coupling at N2, the only nucleophile in the molecule, simultaneously deletes the Tyr337 hydrogen bond and pushes bulk into a pocket floored by Trp86. So the platform's own AChE conjugate is, on experimental evidence, mechanistically void — and the platform has no way to say so, because it has never placed a ligand in a receptor at all (Boltz-2 folded all 22 candidates as lone chains, ipTM = 0.00).

The same analysis generalises: for warheads that DO have an exposed vector, the computation returns a minimum linker length in Angstroms, which converts directly to a minimum GGGGS residue count. That turns 'add a GGGGS linker' from a decoration into a constrained design parameter.
ideas.what_it_answers: For each natural-product warhead named in a candidate's chemStruct field, is there any atom at which a linker can be attached without occluding protein, and if so, what is the minimum linker length (in Angstroms, and in GGGGS residues) needed to reach bulk solvent? The platform cannot currently answer this for any of the 25 conjugates: it has no ligand-in-receptor geometry of any kind, no SASA computation, and no exit-vector concept. It cannot even distinguish a surface-groove binder from a 20-A-deep gorge binder.
ideas.method:
New module platform/cbc/exitvector.py, reusing the mmCIF parsing already in /Users/seunghojung/Documents/DeepMind_Bio/platform/cbc/predictor.py and the RDKit layer in /Users/seunghojung/Documents/DeepMind_Bio/platform/cbc/chem.py.

1. Holo-structure registry: map each warhead to experimental complexes by PDB chemical-component ID (huperzine A = HUP in 4EY5; donepezil = E20 in 4EY7; galantamine in 4EY6). Fetch from files.rcsb.org (verified working this session, 4EY5.cif = 935 KB). Refuse warheads with no experimental complex rather than substituting a docked pose — the same refusal discipline admet.py already applies to peptides.

2. Burial: Bio.PDB.SASA.ShrakeRupley (biopython 1.88 is installed; freesasa is not) at n_points=960, computed twice per ligand — ligand alone, and ligand within the receptor chain — giving per-atom SASA_free, SASA_complex, and fraction_retained. Shrake-Rupley is implemented by the library, not reconstructed from memory, satisfying the repository's unretrieved-equation rule.

3. Contact census: per ligand heavy atom, the three nearest protein atoms with distances and residue identities (prototyped this session; it reproduces the known Tyr133 / Trp86 / Tyr337 / His447 contact set for 4EY5 without being told to).

4. Escape path: straight-line distance to the nearest protein atom with SASA > 25 A^2 is a LOWER BOUND only (4EY5 gives 3.7-8.8 A for HUP, but those lines pass through protein). The real metric is a breadth-first search over a 1.0-A cubic grid of points that are >= probe-radius clear of all protein atoms, seeded at the ligand atom and terminated at bulk solvent — a few seconds of CPU per complex. Path length is the minimum linker span; divided by ~3.5 A per residue for an extended Gly-Ser linker it gives a minimum residue count.

5. Verdict per attachment atom, emitted through the existing provenance.py envelope with status COMPUTED and the PDB ID + resolution as source: NO_VECTOR (retained SASA < 5 A^2 and no clear path), PHARMACOPHORE_CONFLICT (atom makes a hydrogen bond or salt bridge < 3.5 A), or VIABLE with a stated minimum linker length.

6. Wire into /Users/seunghojung/Documents/DeepMind_Bio/platform/validate.py as a new failure category so a candidate whose declared coupling chemistry lands on a NO_VECTOR atom fails the gate instead of being published.

Nothing here needs a GPU, a wet lab, or a paid API. It is deterministic and reproducible from a PDB accession.

evidence.citation: Cheung J, Rudolph MJ, Burshteyn F, Cassidy MS, Gary EN, Love J, Franklin MC, Height JJ. Structures of human acetylcholinesterase in complex with pharmacologically important ligands. J Med Chem. 2012;55(22):10282-10286. DOI 10.1021/jm300871x. PDB 4EY5 = recombinant human AChE + (-)-huperzine A.
evidence.supports: Provides the experimental human AChE / huperzine A complex on which the burial and contact analysis was run. Downloaded and parsed this session.

evidence.citation: Sussman JL, Harel M, Frolow F, Oefner C, Goldman A, Toker L, Silman I. Atomic structure of acetylcholinesterase from Torpedo californica: a prototypic acetylcholine-binding protein. Science. 1991;253(5022):872-879. DOI 10.1126/science.1678899. PMID 1678899.
evidence.supports: Establishes that the AChE catalytic site lies at the base of a deep, narrow gorge rather than on the surface — the structural reason a bound gorge ligand has no exit vector, and why linker length is the governing design variable.

evidence.citation: Shrake A, Rupley JA. Environment and exposure to solvent of protein atoms. Lysozyme and insulin. J Mol Biol. 1973;79(2):351-371. DOI 10.1016/0022-2836(73)90011-9. PMID 4760134.
evidence.supports: The solvent-accessible-surface algorithm used, as implemented in Bio.PDB.SASA.ShrakeRupley (biopython 1.88, verified installed in /Users/seunghojung/Documents/DeepMind_Bio/.venv).

evidence.citation: Raves ML, Harel M, Pang YP, Silman I, Kozikowski AP, Sussman JL. Structure of acetylcholinesterase complexed with the nootropic alkaloid, (-)-huperzine A. Nat Struct Biol. 1997;4(1):57-63. DOI 10.1038/nsb0197-57. PMID 8989325. PDB 1VOT.
evidence.supports: Independent (Torpedo) huperzine A complex, available as a cross-check that the burial result is not a 4EY5 crystallographic artefact.

evidence.citation: In-session computation on 4EY5 chain A using Bio.PDB.SASA.ShrakeRupley (n_points=960): huperzine A SASA 406.6 A^2 free, 6.2 A^2 bound = 98.5% buried; max per-atom retained SASA 4.33 A^2 at N2; N2-Tyr337:OH 3.01 A, O1-Tyr133:OH 2.55 A, C8-His447:CD2 3.60 A.
evidence.supports: Direct measured proof that the method runs today on this hardware and returns a decisive verdict on the platform's own HippoAChE-AlkaPept-X2 candidate.

ideas.effort: 2-3 days. Steps 1-3 are already prototyped and working; the grid BFS in step 4 is the only new algorithmic work (~80 lines of numpy). No new dependencies beyond biopython, already installed.
success_criteria: platform/cbc/exitvector.py reproduces, from 4EY5.cif alone, huperzine A total buried fraction 98.5% +/- 0.5% and identifies N2 as the maximally exposed atom at 4.33 +/- 0.3 A^2, with a unit test pinning both numbers.

The same pipeline run on PDB 4EY7 (donepezil, a known dual-site AChE ligand spanning CAS to PAS) returns a strictly larger exposed fraction and at least one atom with a clear escape path — a positive control that the method is not simply reporting 'everything is buried'.

Every candidate in /Users/seunghojung/Documents/DeepMind_Bio/data/dataset.json whose chemStruct names a warhead is annotated with either a per-atom viability table or an explicit NOT_COMPUTED with the reason 'no experimental holo structure'.
validate.py gains a failure category for declared coupling chemistry on a NO_VECTOR or PHARMACOPHORE_CONFLICT atom, and HippoAChE-AlkaPept-X2 fails it.
The retracted_claims field of any candidate failing the gate is updated through the append-only memory/ ledger, not by silent edit.
risks: A single crystal structure is one conformational snapshot; AChE's gorge is known to breathe and Trp86 is mobile. Mitigation: run all available complexes for a warhead and report the range, and state explicitly that a NO_VECTOR verdict is 'no vector in the observed pose', not a thermodynamic proof.

Crystallographic occupancy, alternate conformers, and bound cryoprotectant (4EY5 contains EDO, DMS, NO3) can perturb SASA. Mitigation: strip non-biological heteroatoms and waters, and log exactly what was stripped.

A ligand can in principle bind in a different pose when conjugated. This is a real limitation and must be stated: the analysis rules out retention of the CRYSTALLOGRAPHIC binding mode, which is the mode the potency data was measured on. It does not rule out some other unmeasured mode.
The grid BFS escape path assumes a rigid receptor; a linker threading a flexible gorge may need less clearance than the grid demands. Report path length as an upper bound and note the assumption.
ideas.why_now: This is the cheapest possible attack on the platform's largest admitted gap. Co-folding all 25 candidates with their receptors (the obvious fix for ipTM = 0.00) is expensive on MPS and would still yield predictions of unknown accuracy — the Boltz-2 affinity head has already shown >1 log error on a single case. Exit-vector analysis instead uses experimental coordinates, costs seconds, and can invalidate a conjugate before any prediction is attempted. It also reframes the ipTM problem correctly: a co-folded model of a conjugate whose warhead cannot physically fit would be a confident prediction of an impossible thing.

ideas.title: Evidence-grade activity layer: measured potency as a distribution with a stated noise floor, not a single retrieved number
ideas.one_line: Replace single literature potency values with endpoint-filtered activity distributions carrying a published experimental noise floor, so model error can be reported against the data's own reproducibility instead of against a cherry-picked point.
ideas.scientific_rationale:
The platform's headline benchmark reads: Boltz-2 predicted IC50 1274 nM for huperzine A on human AChE against a ChEMBL measured value of 5.0 nM, an error of 2.41 log units. I pulled the underlying data this session. ChEMBL holds 25 activity records for huperzine A (CHEMBL395280) against human AChE (CHEMBL220). The IC50 values span 0.54 nM to 5280 nM — 3.99 log units. The median is 47 nM; the geometric mean is ~80 nM. The 5.0 nM used as ground truth is the second most potent of 23 IC50s.

Scored against the median, Boltz-2's error is 1.43 log. Against the geometric mean, 1.20 log. The platform overstated its own model's error by roughly a full log unit — by treating one retrieved measurement as the truth. In a repository whose non-negotiable rule is that no number may be a choice presented as a result, this is the same defect class as the trigonometric pLDDT, only inverted: it is self-flagellating rather than self-flattering, which is exactly why nobody caught it.

There is a published floor for how well this can ever be done. Kalliokoski et al. measured the reproducibility of heterogeneous public IC50 data: sigma = 0.68 log units, mean unsigned error 0.55 log, and 68.2% of measurements agreeing only within a factor of 4.8. My own scan of /Users/seunghojung/Documents/DeepMind_Bio/data/corpus_ACHE.json reproduces this independently on the platform's own data — same compound, same target CHEMBL220, same activity type: neostigmine 22 and 2.0 nM (1.04 log spread), tacrine 218.78/254/33.5/143/95 nM (0.88 log), donepezil 2.33 and 16 nM (0.84 log), physostigmine 30/14.13/27.9/61 nM (0.64 log). A model cannot be scored below this floor, and any claimed accuracy tighter than ~0.7 log on public data is measuring noise.

Two concrete defects fall out of the same investigation. First, the corpus's inclusion protocol advertises 'assay confidence >= 8' in protocol_summary(), but iter_target_activities() reads a.get('confidence_score') from the /activity endpoint — and I confirmed against the live API that confidence_score is not a field on activity records (it lives on /assay; CHEMBL643374 returns confidence_score 8 there). Every one of the 27 activities in corpus_ACHE.json has assay_confidence = None, so the filter has never excluded anything. The protocol summary is currently a false claim about the data. Second, endpoint semantics are unchecked: among the 25 huperzine A records mapped to CHEMBL220, one (CHEMBL1771986, IC50 5.0 nM) is 'Inhibition of AChE-induced amyloid beta aggregation' — a peripheral-anionic-site phenotype, not catalytic inhibition — and four are 'AChE (unknown origin)' assigned to the human target. Pooling those with Ellman catalytic IC50s produces a number that means nothing.
ideas.what_it_answers: What is the measured potency of compound X against target Y, as a distribution with a defensible central estimate, a spread, an endpoint definition, and an experimental noise floor — and is a given model prediction outside that noise floor? The platform currently stores each activity as an isolated literature value with the boilerplate 'single reported value; assay conditions vary' (corpus.py, to_provenanced) and has no aggregation, no endpoint typing, no working confidence filter, and no noise floor. So it cannot state whether any prediction error is real signal or is inside the data's own scatter.
ideas.method:
Changes concentrated in /Users/seunghojung/Documents/DeepMind_Bio/platform/cbc/corpus.py plus a new platform/cbc/evidence.py.

1. Fix the inert filter. Batch-fetch /assay?assay_chembl_id__in=... for every assay seen, join confidence_score onto each Activity, and make InclusionProtocol.summary() assert only what was actually enforced. Add a regression test that fails if any admitted activity carries assay_confidence None while min_assay_confidence > 0.

2. Retain the metadata already being thrown away. The /activity response carries assay_description, bao_label, bao_format, data_validity_comment, potential_duplicate, pchembl_value, standard_relation, and document_year — I enumerated the full field list live. The Activity dataclass keeps four of them. Retain all; standard_relation in particular distinguishes '=' from '>' and censored values must never be pooled with exact ones.

3. Endpoint typing. Cluster activities under a target by (standard_type, bao_label, normalised assay_description) into ENDPOINT CLASSES, and require a class to be named before values are pooled. Catalytic inhibition by Ellman is one class; Abeta-aggregation inhibition is another; SPR Kd is another. Classes are declared in a versioned table alongside the InclusionProtocol so the decision is inspectable, not buried in a regex.

4. Aggregate within class only. Emit n, median, geometric mean, min, max, log10 range, and interquartile range in log space. Use pchembl_value where ChEMBL supplies it (it already applies the -log10 transform, so no equation is reconstructed here).

5. Attach the noise floor. Every aggregate carries a reference_sigma from Kalliokoski et al. (0.68 log for heterogeneous public IC50) alongside the corpus's own empirically observed within-compound sigma, tagged LITERATURE and COMPUTED respectively. Do not invent a pooled sigma when n is small; report n and let it show.

6. Re-score the existing benchmark. Recompute the Boltz-2 huperzine A comparison against the catalytic-inhibition class median and publish the corrected figure through the memory/ ledger as a retraction-with-replacement, since the 2.41 log claim is currently in the record.

evidence.citation: Kalliokoski T, Kramer C, Vulpetti A, Gedeck P. Comparability of mixed IC50 data - a statistical analysis. PLoS ONE. 2013;8(4):e61007. DOI 10.1371/journal.pone.0061007. PMID 23613770.
evidence.supports: Supplies the published noise floor for heterogeneous public IC50 data: sigma 0.68 log units, MUE 0.55, median UE 0.43, with 68.2% of measurements agreeing only within a factor of 4.8; and the intra-lab contrast (rolipram/PDE4D sigma 0.22, cilostamide/PDE3 sigma 0.17). Retrieved and quantitatively confirmed from the open-access article this session.

evidence.citation: Live ChEMBL API query, this session: GET /activity?molecule_chembl_id=CHEMBL395280&target_chembl_id=CHEMBL220&standard_units=nM returns 25 records spanning IC50 0.54-5280 nM (median 47 nM, geometric mean ~80 nM), including CHEMBL1771986 'Inhibition of AChE-induced amyloid beta aggregation' and four 'AChE (unknown origin)' assays.
evidence.supports: Demonstrates the 3.99-log spread hidden behind the platform's single 5.0 nM ground-truth value, and the endpoint-semantics contamination in the same target mapping.

evidence.citation: Live ChEMBL API query, this session: the /activity record field list contains no confidence_score key; GET /assay/CHEMBL643374 returns confidence_score 8, assay_type B, bao_label 'single protein format'.
evidence.supports: Proves that InclusionProtocol.min_assay_confidence is never enforced by iter_target_activities() in platform/cbc/corpus.py, and that protocol.summary()'s 'assay confidence >= 8' is therefore an unsupported claim about data/corpus_ACHE.json.

evidence.citation: In-session analysis of /Users/seunghojung/Documents/DeepMind_Bio/data/corpus_ACHE.json: within-compound, same-target, same-activity-type log10 spreads of 1.04 (neostigmine, n=2), 0.88 (tacrine, n=5), 0.84 (donepezil, n=2), 0.64 (physostigmine, n=4); all 27 activities carry assay_confidence None.
evidence.supports: Independent reproduction of the Kalliokoski noise floor on the repository's own data, and confirmation that the confidence filter is inert in the shipped corpus.

ideas.effort: 2 days. One extra ChEMBL endpoint call per batch, a dataclass widening, an endpoint-class table, and aggregation arithmetic. No new dependencies. The heaviest item is curating the endpoint-class table for AChE, which is a medicinal-chemistry judgement call and must be written down rather than inferred.
success_criteria: A rebuilt data/corpus_ACHE.json in which every admitted activity carries a non-null assay_confidence, and a test that fails the build otherwise.
Huperzine A / CHEMBL220 resolves to at least two distinct endpoint classes, with the amyloid-beta-aggregation record excluded from the catalytic-inhibition aggregate by rule, not by hand.

The catalytic-inhibition aggregate for huperzine A reports n, median, and log10 range, and the Boltz-2 comparison is republished against it — the recomputed error should be near 1.4 log, and the 2.41 log figure formally retracted in memory/ with its replacement linked.

Every aggregate carries both an empirical within-compound sigma (COMPUTED, with n) and the Kalliokoski reference sigma (LITERATURE, cited), and any model-vs-measurement comparison prints the ratio of error to noise floor.
protocol.summary() text is regenerated from the filters actually applied, verified by a test that mutates a filter and asserts the string changes.
risks: Endpoint classification is a judgement call and will be contested. Mitigation: make the class table a versioned, human-readable artefact that travels with the corpus, exactly as InclusionProtocol does, so a disagreement is a diff rather than an argument.

Fetching /assay for every assay roughly doubles ChEMBL round-trips and ChEMBL is already slow (the module's own comment says 20-40 s is normal). Mitigation: batch with assay_chembl_id__in and cache by assay ID; assay records are immutable within a ChEMBL release.

Small n. Many compound-target pairs will have n=1, where a median is a single number wearing a hat. The output must show n prominently and refuse to print a spread when n < 3 rather than printing zero.
Retracting the 2.41 log figure will look like backsliding to anyone reading only the headline. It is the opposite, but the ledger entry must say so explicitly.
ideas.why_now: Every downstream number the platform will ever compute — affinity benchmarks, co-folding validation, any future scoring function — is measured against this evidence layer. Building more prediction on top of a ground truth that is a single unqualified literature value propagates the error. It also costs almost nothing and fixes a live false claim: the shipped corpus asserts an assay-confidence filter it does not apply, precisely the defect class the rebuild exists to eliminate.

ideas.title: Interference-by-readout: cross-check reactivity substructures against the physical detection chemistry of the supporting assay
ideas.one_line: Flag not merely that a compound matches a PAINS or reactive-electrophile pattern, but that its specific interference mechanism collides with the specific readout that produced its potency value — the join no public tool performs.
ideas.scientific_rationale:
PAINS flagging alone is close to useless on natural products; corpus.py's own docstring says so correctly, and it defaults exclude_pains to False for good reason. But the module then never computes the flag at all, so the documented policy of 'flagged, not excluded' is unimplemented — there is no PAINS code anywhere in the repository (grep confirms only comments). More importantly, an uncontextualised flag is the wrong artefact. Baell's own seven-year retrospective stresses utility AND limitations: a PAINS match is a hypothesis about a mechanism, and it becomes actionable only when that mechanism can actually operate in the assay that produced the number.

That join is computable here and is specific to this platform's target. The dominant AChE potency assay in the corpus is Ellman's method — named verbatim in the ChEMBL assay descriptions I retrieved for huperzine A (CHEMBL1065425, CHEMBL1663835). Ellman's readout is the absorbance of the 5-thio-2-nitrobenzoate anion at 412 nm, generated when enzymatically released thiocholine reduces DTNB. That readout has two orthogonal failure modes mapping directly onto substructure classes: (i) thiol-reactive electrophiles scavenge thiocholine or react with DTNB directly, suppressing signal and mimicking inhibition; (ii) compounds absorbing near 412 nm distort the optical measurement — and interference by coloured herbal constituents in exactly this assay is documented in the natural-product literature.

I ran RDKit's FilterCatalog (PAINS_A/B/C + Brenk + NIH) over the eight curated natural products this session. Curcumin matches beta-keto/anhydride and Michael_acceptor_1. Baicalein matches catechol_A(92) and catechol. Salvianolic acid B matches catechol, Michael_acceptor_1, and >=5 phenolic OH. All three are thiol-reactive or redox-active classes; curcumin is additionally an intensely yellow chromophore absorbing in the Ellman window, and Nelson et al. classify it as both a PAINS and an IMPS with no successful double-blind placebo-controlled trial after 120+ attempts. Two of these three are already embedded in the dataset as candidate warheads: HippoNrf-KeapDecoy-X3 declares 'Curcumin Bis-ortho-methoxyphenol Core'. The platform reports curcumin's MW, cLogP, and TPSA as if it were a well-behaved reversible ligand and carries no field capable of recording that its supporting evidence may be an artefact of the detection chemistry.

The deliverable is not a blacklist. It is a per-value evidence downgrade: this potency number was produced by a readout whose physics this compound's chemistry can perturb, therefore treat it as a lower-confidence measurement, and say which mechanism and which reference.
ideas.what_it_answers: For a given measured potency value, is there a named, mechanistic reason to distrust it arising from the collision between the compound's reactive chemistry and the assay's detection physics? The platform currently treats every ChEMBL LITERATURE value as equally admissible evidence, computes no interference substructures at all despite documenting a flagging policy, and discards the assay_description and bao_label fields that would identify the readout.
ideas.method:
New module platform/cbc/interference.py, consumed by the evidence layer of MEDCHEM-IDEA-2 (independently useful, far stronger once assay_description is retained).

1. Substructure layer: rdkit.Chem.FilterCatalog with PAINS_A/B/C, BRENK, and NIH catalogues. The SMARTS ship with RDKit 2026.03.5 (verified installed and working this session), so Baell's patterns are used as distributed, never transcribed — which respects the repository's rule against reconstructing definitions from memory. Record catalogue name, entry description, and matching atom indices.

2. Mechanism table: map each catalogue entry to one or more MECHANISM CLASSES — thiol_reactive, redox_cycling, chromophore, chelator, colloidal_aggregator, covalent_electrophile. This table is hand-written medicinal chemistry and must be versioned with a citation per row, exactly like the InclusionProtocol.

3. Readout table: map assay detection formats (from bao_label and normalised assay_description) to the physical quantities they measure and the perturbations that corrupt them. Ellman/DTNB -> absorbance 412 nm, corrupted by thiol_reactive and by chromophore; AlphaScreen -> singlet oxygen, corrupted by quenchers; fluorescence -> corrupted by autofluorescence at the excitation/emission pair.

4. The join: emit a COLLISION record only where a compound's mechanism class intersects the corrupting set of the assay that produced that specific activity value. No collision, no flag — this is what keeps the false-positive rate tolerable on natural products.

5. Chromophore check: for the absorbance-readout case, compute the extent of the conjugated system from RDKit ring/conjugation perception and flag extended conjugation with donor substitution as a candidate 412 nm absorber. State honestly that this is a structural heuristic, not a computed spectrum; give it status PREDICTED, never COMPUTED.

6. Surface as a per-activity evidence_grade downgrade in the provenance envelope, with the mechanism named and the primary reference attached, and add a validate.py category for a candidate whose declared warhead's supporting evidence is entirely collision-flagged.

evidence.citation: Baell JB, Holloway GA. New substructure filters for removal of pan assay interference compounds (PAINS) from screening libraries and for their exclusion in bioassays. J Med Chem. 2010;53(7):2719-2740. DOI 10.1021/jm901137j. PMID 20131845.
evidence.supports: Source of the PAINS SMARTS distributed in RDKit's FilterCatalog, used as-shipped rather than transcribed.

evidence.citation: Baell JB, Nissink JWM. Seven year itch: pan-assay interference compounds (PAINS) in 2017 - utility and limitations. ACS Chem Biol. 2018;13(1):36-44. DOI 10.1021/acschembio.7b00903.
evidence.supports: Establishes that a PAINS match is a mechanistic hypothesis with stated limitations rather than a verdict — the direct justification for the readout-collision join instead of blanket flagging.

evidence.citation: Nelson KM, Dahlin JL, Bisson J, Graham J, Pauli GF, Walters MA. The essential medicinal chemistry of curcumin. J Med Chem. 2017;60(5):1620-1637. DOI 10.1021/acs.jmedchem.6b00975. PMID 28074653.
evidence.supports: Classifies curcumin as both PAINS and IMPS and records that no double-blind placebo-controlled trial has succeeded despite 120+ attempts. Curcumin is a curated compound in data/curated.json and the declared warhead of candidate HippoNrf-KeapDecoy-X3.

evidence.citation: Bioguided isolation and structure identification of acetylcholinesterase enzyme inhibitors from Drynariae Rhizome. PMC7059089. Reports that background colour of compounds or herbal extracts interferes with the Ellman secondary reaction, readily yielding false positives or false negatives, motivating a UPLC-MS/MS alternative.
evidence.supports: Documents the chromophore-versus-412-nm-absorbance collision specifically in AChE Ellman assays on natural products — the exact readout and compound class this platform relies on. Retrieved this session by PMCID; DOI not separately confirmed.

evidence.citation: In-session RDKit 2026.03.5 FilterCatalog run over data/curated.json: curcumin -> beta-keto/anhydride, Michael_acceptor_1; baicalein -> catechol_A(92), catechol; salvianolic acid B -> catechol_A(92), catechol, Michael_acceptor_1, gte_5_phenolic_OH; onjisaponin V -> Michael_acceptor_1, saponine_derivative; physostigmine, tacrine, donepezil and the aminoacridines -> no hits. grep across platform/ confirms zero PAINS-computing code exists.
evidence.supports: Shows the flags are real, non-trivial, hit three of eight curated natural products while leaving the clean synthetic actives unflagged, and are currently uncomputed despite corpus.py documenting a flagging policy.

ideas.effort: 1-2 days for the substructure layer and the join; the mechanism and readout tables are the real work and are curation, not code. Start with Ellman/DTNB only, since it dominates the AChE corpus, and refuse to grade values from readouts not yet in the table rather than defaulting to 'clean'.
success_criteria: platform/cbc/interference.py annotates all eight curated natural products and all 18 corpus compounds with catalogue name, entry, and matching atom indices, reproducing the flags listed in E5 under test.

A collision is emitted for curcumin only where the supporting assay's readout is absorbance-based or thiol-dependent, and NOT for assays with orthogonal readouts — demonstrated with a negative control that must stay unflagged.
Physostigmine, tacrine, donepezil and the aminoacridines return zero PAINS flags (confirmed this session), so the module demonstrably does not flag everything.
Every mechanism-table and readout-table row carries a citation, and a test fails the build if any row lacks one.
No activity value is ever deleted or numerically downweighted; the downgrade is a labelled evidence_grade with a named mechanism, preserving the raw value and its provenance.
risks: Over-flagging natural products is the exact failure PAINS filters are notorious for, and the mechanism table is where that failure would enter. Mitigation: emit nothing unless the readout join fires, and track the flag rate against the corpus denominator so over-flagging is visible as a number rather than an impression.
The 412 nm chromophore call is a structural heuristic, not a computed UV-Vis spectrum. It must be status PREDICTED with the heuristic stated, and it must never be reported as a measured absorbance.

Assay-description text is free-form and inconsistent across ChEMBL documents, so readout classification by string normalisation will miss cases. Mitigation: prefer bao_label where present, and classify unmatched descriptions as UNKNOWN_READOUT rather than guessing — an unknown readout yields no collision and no downgrade.

A collision flag can be read as 'this compound does not work', which is not the claim. The output wording must say the measurement is lower-confidence and name the mechanism, not that the compound is inactive.

Some of the reactivity classes (Michael acceptors especially) are genuine, intended pharmacology for Keap1/Nrf2 — curcumin's electrophilicity is arguably its mechanism at that target. The mechanism table must therefore be target-aware, or it will flag the intended mode of action as an artefact.
ideas.why_now: It is the cheapest of the three and it protects the other two. Idea 2 builds activity distributions; if those distributions pool artefact-contaminated values the aggregate is a confidently-stated wrong number, the failure mode this repository was rebuilt to eliminate. It also closes a live documentation-versus-code gap: corpus.py states that PAINS are flagged rather than excluded, and nothing flags them. Doing it as a contextualised join rather than a blacklist is what makes it defensible on natural products, where naive PAINS filtering would delete most of the real chemistry.

proposals.expert: Human genetics / statistical genetics — 16 years post-PhD; therapeutic target validation via GWAS, drug-target Mendelian randomization and QTL colocalization

ideas.title: Indication-anchored genetic evidence layer: an executable Target Product Profile as the join key, release-pinned Open Targets/gnomAD retrieval, and a calibrated denominator
ideas.one_line: Make the indication a typed, required field on every candidate, then compute genetic support against it as provenanced Values pinned to a named data release, with a rank denominator so a score is interpretable and a drift gate so it cannot silently rot.
ideas.scientific_rationale: Genetic support is quantified per target-INDICATION pair, not per target (Minikel 2024). The platform declares no indication anywhere — `candidates[].targets` is anatomical prose such as 'CNS -> Brain -> Hippocampus (CA1/CA3 Pyramidal Neurons)' — so the single best-quantified prior on clinical success is not merely unreported, it is uncomputable in principle. Separately, the genetic numbers that DO exist in /Users/seunghojung/Documents/DeepMind_Bio/data/dataset.json live inside free-text strings in `target_records.targets[].genetic_evidence_for_cognition` ('Open Targets direct ... = 0.124', 'pLI 1.000, LOEUF 0.219'). This is a live hole in the repo's own contract: `audit()` in platform/cbc/provenance.py walks dicts, lists and numeric leaves but has no `str` branch — the `elif isinstance(val, (int, float))` test at line 187 never fires for a number embedded in prose. Every genetics number in this repository is therefore exempt from the very check the repository was rebuilt to enforce. The cost is already measurable in the repo's own history: an adversarial verifier flagged eight of these prose scores as 'wrong' when they were merely stale (memory/views/claims.md, finding on 'Systematic upward drift in Open Targets aggregate scores'). I reproduced the drift live today against Open Targets dataVersion 26.06: ACHE-Alzheimer direct overall is now 0.634 (ledger records 0.641), and the gnomAD constraint quoted for NTRK2 (LOEUF 0.219, 13 obs / 94.5 exp) is the v2.1.1 value — the gnomAD API returns exactly those numbers today, while Open Targets 26.06 returns lof oe 0.0585 with oeUpper 0.123 from the larger v4 callset. Two live authorities differ 1.8-fold on the same gene's LOEUF, and the dataset names no version, so the number is unreproducible by construction. Finally, a bare score has no denominator: nothing in the repo says whether 0.124 is good or bad.
ideas.what_it_answers: For each of the 35 candidates: which disease, in which patients, measured on which endpoint — and given that named indication, how much human genetic support does its target carry, from which named data release, and where does that rank among all genes associated with the same disease? The platform currently cannot state an indication at all, so none of these are askable.
ideas.method: 1) New `platform/cbc/tpp.py`: a frozen `TargetProductProfile` dataclass with required fields — `indication_id` (EFO/MONDO CURIE, validated against the Open Targets `disease(efoId:)` resolver so a typo cannot pass), `disease_stage`, `population` (free text plus optional `genetic_stratum`), `primary_endpoint`, `comparator`, `comparator_effect_size` as a pv.Value, `route`, `max_acceptable_risk`. Construction raises if `indication_id` is absent, exactly as `Provenance.__post_init__` already raises for a COMPUTED value with no `software`. 2) New `platform/cbc/genetics.py` reusing corpus.py's `_ssl_context()` and `_get()` (I hit the documented CERTIFICATE_VERIFY_FAILED trap from /tmp with bare urllib this session, so reuse is not optional). It POSTs to https://api.platform.opentargets.org/api/v4/graphql and stores `meta{ apiVersion{x y z} dataVersion{year month} }` — returning 26.6.3 / 26.06 today — into every `Provenance.source_id` as e.g. `OpenTargets:26.06:ENSG00000095970:MONDO_0004975`. Per target it retrieves `associatedDiseases`/`associatedTargets` overall score plus the `datatypeScores` breakdown, and `geneticConstraint{constraintType score oe oeLower oeUpper}`; constraint is emitted as two separate Values, gnomAD-v4-via-OT and gnomAD-v2.1.1-via-https://gnomad.broadinstitute.org/api, never merged. 3) Calibration: one call to `disease(efoId:"MONDO_0004975"){ associatedTargets(page:{index:i,size:500}, enableIndirect:false){ count rows{...} } }` yields the ranked list and `count` = 13289, giving each target a rank and percentile. I ran this today; the table is the deliverable: ACHE #7 (0.634, genetic_association ABSENT — carried by literature 0.936 and clinical 0.996, i.e. the existence of donepezil, which is circular), GRIN2B #8, GRIN2A #11, GSK3B #28, TREM2 #29 (0.552, genetic_association 0.858 — the only target with a genetic datatype above 0.2), CHRNA7 #187, CHRM1 #227, NTRK1 #1205, NOS3 #1519, NTRK2 #1556, NFE2L2 #1585, TLR4 #1647, SLC1A2 #1696; FZD8, KEAP1 and PTAFR fall outside the top 2000. 4) `platform/cbc/provenance.py`: add a `str` branch to `audit()` that regex-scans string leaves for decimal numerals and reports `prose_embedded_number` — the same spirit as validate.py's existing `check_placeholder_text` for prose in sequence fields. 5) `platform/validate.py:main()`: add `check_tpp` (fail any candidate with no TargetProductProfile) and `check_genetic_drift` (re-fetch, compare to the stored release-pinned Value, fail on divergence beyond a stated tolerance). All numbers land as `pv.database(...)`, so `Value.to_display()` governs rendering and nothing can be printed unlabelled.

evidence.citation: Minikel EV, Painter JL, Dong CC, Nelson MR. Refining the impact of genetic evidence on clinical success. Nature 629:624-629 (2024). DOI 10.1038/s41586-024-07316-0; PMID 38632401
evidence.supports: Probability of success for genetically supported mechanisms is 2.6x that of unsupported ones, computed per target-indication pair and largely independent of effect size and MAF — so an undeclared indication makes the strongest available prior uncomputable, and small rare-variant evidence such as TREM2's cannot be dismissed as too small to act on.

evidence.citation: Open Targets Platform GraphQL API, https://api.platform.opentargets.org/api/v4/graphql, queried 2026-08-17; meta{apiVersion 26.6.3, dataVersion 2026-06}. Queries run: disease(MONDO_0004975).associatedTargets(enableIndirect:false) count=13289; target(ENSG*).geneticConstraint
evidence.supports: The release version is machine-retrievable and must be pinned; the 13,289-target ranked list supplies the missing denominator; the datatypeScores breakdown shows genetic_association is absent for 13 of the 16 platform targets and that ACHE/GRIN2A/GRIN2B/CHRM1/CHRNA7 scores are carried by clinical precedence, which is circular for target validation.

evidence.citation: gnomAD GraphQL API, https://gnomad.broadinstitute.org/api, queried 2026-08-17: NTRK2 gnomad_constraint = {pli 1.000, oe_lof 0.1376, oe_lof_upper 0.2188, mis_z 5.632, exp_lof 94.46, obs_lof 13}
evidence.supports: Reproduces the dataset's prose LOEUF 0.219 exactly and identifies it as the v2.1.1 value, while Open Targets 26.06 returns lof oe 0.0585 / oeUpper 0.123 for the same gene — a 1.8-fold disagreement between two live authorities that the unversioned prose cannot express.

evidence.citation: Chen S, Francioli LC, Goodrich JK, et al. A genomic mutational constraint map using variation in 76,156 human genomes. Nature 625:92-100 (2024). DOI 10.1038/s41586-023-06045-0
evidence.supports: gnomAD v4 rebuilds the constraint map on a much larger callset, which is why LOEUF is version-dependent and why a constraint Value without a release identifier is not a reproducible measurement.

evidence.citation: Karczewski KJ, Francioli LC, Tiao G, et al. The mutational constraint spectrum quantified from variation in 141,456 humans. Nature 581:434-443 (2020). DOI 10.1038/s41586-020-2308-7
evidence.supports: Defines LOEUF as the upper bound of the 90% CI on observed/expected LoF — the quantity Open Targets exposes as geneticConstraint.oeUpper, needed to map the two sources onto one another.

evidence.citation: US FDA, Early Alzheimer's Disease: Developing Drugs for Treatment — revised DRAFT guidance for industry, announced 11 March 2024; Federal Register document 2024-05178 (89 FR, 12 March 2024)
evidence.supports: Supplies the regulatory content of the TPP fields for an early-AD indication (diagnostic criteria, clinical staging, outcome-measure and surrogate-endpoint selection). Retrieved as a draft, not final — the TPP must record that status rather than imply settled requirements.

evidence.citation: van Dyck CH, Swanson CJ, Aisen P, et al. Lecanemab in Early Alzheimer's Disease. N Engl J Med 388:9-21 (2023). DOI 10.1056/NEJMoa2212948; PMID 36449413
evidence.supports: Gives the comparator field a real number: adjusted mean CDR-SB difference of -0.45 versus placebo at 18 months (27% slowing). Any early-AD candidate's TPP must state an effect size on this scale, not '+280% LTP'.

ideas.effort: 2-3 days. Roughly 400 lines of new Python plus two gate functions; all I/O is small JSON over HTTPS, no local model, no GPU. The 16 target queries and the four 500-row ranking pages each returned in seconds today on this machine.
success_criteria: `python3 platform/validate.py` reports a new `missing_tpp` category with 35 failures on the current dataset, and a new `prose_embedded_number` category with at least 16 failures (one per target record) — i.e. the gate detects the hole that exists today.

Every genetics number in data/dataset.json is a `{value, units, provenance}` object whose `source_id` contains a resolvable release token (`OpenTargets:26.06:...` or `gnomAD:v2.1.1:...` / `gnomAD:v4:...`), and `pv.audit()` on the rebuilt dataset returns zero problems.

Re-running the fetch against a later Open Targets release produces a diff report naming every changed score with old value, new value and both release ids, and the gate fails rather than silently overwriting.

Each of the 16 targets carries a rank and percentile against a stated denominator (13,289 for MONDO_0004975), and the README reports that 13 of 16 have no genetic_association datatype at all for the declared indication.
Constraint is stored twice with both gnomAD versions labelled; no code path merges or averages them.
risks: Open Targets scores drift every release by design; the drift gate must distinguish drift from error or it will cry wolf. Mitigation: the gate reports the release delta and requires an explicit re-pin, it does not assert the old value was wrong.

Choosing MONDO_0004975 (Alzheimer disease) as the indication is itself a scientific decision that will make most of the portfolio look bad. That is the correct outcome, but it must be a declared decision in the TPP, not a default buried in code. 'Cognitive enhancement in healthy adults' has no usable target-disease ontology term and essentially no tractable single-target genetics; if a candidate declares it, the gate should say so rather than fake a score.

The percentile denominator counts all targets with ANY evidence type, so a high rank driven by literature co-mention is not genetic support. The rank must always be reported alongside the datatype breakdown or it will be misread — ACHE at #7 with no genetic datatype is precisely that trap.

Open Targets is a Beta API; field names change between releases (I hit `variantEffect` and `datasourceSettings` both being renamed in this session). The client needs a schema-introspection self-test in the test suite.
ideas.why_now: Every other computation in the repository is downstream of this one. Boltz-2 co-folding, affinity prediction and ADMET all cost compute and all answer 'can this molecule bind?' — none answer 'should we be pushing this protein in a human at all?'. Wiring the genetics layer is cheap, needs no GPU, and reorders the queue: it would tell you today that 15 of 16 targets are not genetically supported for Alzheimer's, which is information you want before spending MPS hours on receptor co-folding.

ideas.title: Direction-of-effect layer: colocalization sign and the human allelic series, checked against each candidate's intended pharmacology
ideas.one_line: For every target-indication pair, retrieve the GWAS credible set, its colocalization with molecular QTLs including the beta-ratio sign, and the constraint/allelic-series context, then machine-check whether the candidate's agonism or inhibition pushes the target in the direction human genetics says is protective — or record UNDETERMINED, which is the honest answer for 15 of 16.
ideas.scientific_rationale: An association score is unsigned. It says a gene matters; it does not say which way to move it. This platform is full of directional commitments — TrkB and TrkA agonists, an AChE inhibitor, a Keap1 decoy that activates NRF2, a Frizzled-8 agonist, a PAFR antagonist — and none is anchored to a human allelic series. The repository's own ledger already contains the cautionary case in prose (the validated human TRK pharmacology is inhibition: larotrectinib), but prose is not a check. Open Targets added a direction-of-effect assessment across eight evidence sources in release 24.03, and I confirmed today that the live schema exposes `Evidence.directionOnTrait` and `Evidence.directionOnTarget`. Critically, I also confirmed that this layer is EMPTY where the platform needs it: for TREM2 and NTRK2 against Alzheimer disease, every gwas_credible_sets and europepmc row returns directionOnTrait=null and directionOnTarget=null; the only non-null directions in the whole 16-target sweep come from `clinical_precedence` (GRIN2A protect/LoF x67, ACHE protect/LoF x156) — which is derived from the existence of memantine and donepezil and is therefore circular as target validation. So a directional layer cannot be a thin wrapper around one Open Targets field; it must combine the colocalization sign, the constraint direction, and the ClinVar allelic series, and it must be able to return UNDETERMINED loudly. The colocalization route works and is cheap: `CredibleSet.colocalisation` exposes `h4`, `clpp` and `betaRatioSignAverage` with the partner `otherStudyLocus`, so the sign of the GWAS-vs-QTL effect ratio is retrievable in one call. Running it across all 16 targets today gave a stark result — 15 of 16 have zero Alzheimer GWAS credible sets; only TREM2 has any, with 14 credible sets colocalizing at h4=1.000, CLPP=0.995 against UKB-PPP plasma pQTLs and one Quach_2016 classical-monocyte eQTL. And the TREM2 sign ratios are not consistent across credible sets (+1, -1 and 0 all appear), which is exactly the ambiguity a platform must surface rather than resolve by assertion.
ideas.what_it_answers: For a given candidate: does human genetic variation that moves this target in the direction the molecule moves it raise or lower disease risk, and how strong is the evidence for that sign? Equivalently — is TrkB agonism, NRF2 activation or PAFR antagonism pointing the way the human allelic series points? The platform currently has no signed quantity anywhere; its mechanism strings assert direction with no human anchor.
ideas.method: Extend `platform/cbc/genetics.py` with a `DirectionOfEffect` record per (target, indication). Four independent signals, each stored as its own provenanced Value, never collapsed into a single number: (1) Colocalization sign — GraphQL `target(ensemblId:).evidences(efoIds:, datasourceIds:["gwas_credible_sets"]){ rows{ credibleSet{ beta study{id pubmedId} colocalisation(studyTypes:[eqtl,pqtl,sqtl,tuqtl]){ rows{ h4 clpp betaRatioSignAverage rightStudyType otherStudyLocus{ qtlGeneId study{ projectId biosample{biosampleName} } } } } } } }`, retaining only h4>=0.8, and recording `betaRatioSignAverage` per credible set rather than averaging across them. (2) Open Targets `directionOnTrait`/`directionOnTarget`, with `datasourceId` retained so `clinical_precedence` can be excluded from the genetic verdict and reported separately as pharmacological precedent. (3) Constraint direction from gnomAD (LoF-intolerant means partial inhibition is not phenotypically free — NTRK2 pLI 1.000, GRIN2A lof oe 0.185, versus LoF-tolerant TREM2 with lof pLI 6.6e-07 and oeUpper 1.211 retrieved today). (4) The Mendelian allelic series from ClinVar/eva evidence already present in the Open Targets datasource breakdown, classified as LoF-associated or GoF-associated where the source states it. Then a `direction_concordance` field on each candidate: a small explicit rubric comparing the candidate's declared modality (agonist / inhibitor / degrader / decoy — currently only inferable from prose in `candidates[].mechanism`, so a typed `modality` enum is a prerequisite) against the genetic direction, emitting CONCORDANT, DISCORDANT or UNDETERMINED, with UNDETERMINED the default and no silent third option. A new `check_direction` in platform/validate.py fails any candidate asserting a directional mechanism string while its direction_concordance is UNDETERMINED. Where the Open Targets colocalization is absent but summary statistics exist, the same arithmetic is reproducible locally as a two-sample cis-MR Wald ratio with coloc PP4 on a handful of cis-SNPs — kilobytes of data and milliseconds of CPU, no GPU — which is the extension path for brain-tissue QTLs that Open Targets does not currently colocalize (see GENO-C).

evidence.citation: Open Targets Platform GraphQL API queried 2026-08-17 (dataVersion 26.06): schema introspection confirms Evidence.directionOnTrait and Evidence.directionOnTarget; CredibleSet.colocalisation exposes h4, clpp, betaRatioSignAverage, colocalisationMethod, otherStudyLocus. Sweep of all 16 platform targets vs MONDO_0004975 returned gwas_credible_sets counts: TREM2 14, NTRK2 1, all other 14 targets 0. TREM2 colocalizations: h4=1.000, CLPP=0.995 with UKB_PPP_EUR blood-plasma pQTLs and one Quach_2016 CD14+CD16- classical-monocyte eQTL; betaRatioSignAverage values of +1, -1 and 0 across different credible sets.
evidence.supports: The directional machinery exists and is queryable today; it is empty for 15 of 16 targets; where non-null directions exist they come from clinical_precedence, not genetics; and TREM2's own sign is not uniform across credible sets. All four facts are needed to justify UNDETERMINED as the default verdict.

evidence.citation: Open Targets Platform 24.03 release announcement, https://blog.opentargets.org/open-targets-platform-24-03-release/ — 'a direction of effect assessment has been implemented for eight sources of target-disease association evidence'
evidence.supports: Documents the provenance and scope of the directionOnTrait/directionOnTarget fields, and that they cover only eight evidence sources — so absence of a direction is absence of assessment, not evidence of no direction.

evidence.citation: Sun BB, Chiou J, Traylor M, et al. Plasma proteomic associations with genetics and health in the UK Biobank. Nature 622:329-338 (2023). DOI 10.1038/s41586-023-06592-6
evidence.supports: Identifies the UKB_PPP_EUR project behind the TREM2 colocalizations: cis-pQTL mapping of 2,923 proteins in 54,219 participants, 14,287 primary genetic associations. This is the instrument source, and the paper is also the reference for the epitope caveat below.

evidence.citation: Giambartolomei C, Vukcevic D, Schadt EE, et al. Bayesian test for colocalisation between pairs of genetic association studies using summary statistics. PLoS Genet 10:e1004383 (2014). DOI 10.1371/journal.pgen.1004383; PMID 24830394
evidence.supports: Defines the H4 posterior that the h4 field reports and the assumption of a single causal variant per locus — the caveat that must be stored alongside any h4 value, and the method for the local-recomputation extension path.

Relative success improves with increasing confidence in the causal gene — colocalization at h4>=0.8 with a cis-molQTL is the operational form of that confidence, so the direction layer and the support tier are the same axis measured more finely.

evidence.citation: Karczewski KJ, et al. Nature 581:434-443 (2020). DOI 10.1038/s41586-020-2308-7 (retrieved this session only via the gnomAD API values it underpins, not the paper text)
evidence.supports: Constraint supplies the safety half of direction: LoF-intolerant targets bound how far inhibition can be pushed, LoF-tolerant targets have living human carriers whose phenotype is the readout.

ideas.effort: 3-4 days for the API-driven layer (the queries above already run). Add roughly a week if the local cis-MR/coloc recomputation path is built, which needs a small GWAS summary-statistics fetch — still CPU-only and well under a laptop's limits for cis windows.
success_criteria: Every (candidate, target, indication) triple carries a `direction_concordance` of CONCORDANT / DISCORDANT / UNDETERMINED with the four constituent signals stored separately and individually provenanced.

On the current dataset the layer reports UNDETERMINED for at least 34 of 35 candidates, and validate.py fails each one whose `mechanism` string asserts a direction — reproducing, as a machine check, what the ledger currently states only in prose.

TREM2-directed records carry the colocalization detail verbatim: h4=1.000, CLPP=0.995, source UKB_PPP_EUR blood plasma and Quach_2016 monocyte, with the non-uniform sign ratios listed rather than averaged.
clinical_precedence-derived directions are stored in a separate field from genetics-derived directions and are excluded from the concordance verdict; the code comments state why (circularity).
A candidate whose modality is flipped in a test fixture flips the verdict from CONCORDANT to DISCORDANT — i.e. the check is sensitive to the thing it claims to test.
risks: cis-pQTL colocalization can be an assay artifact: a protein-altering variant that changes an antibody or aptamer epitope shifts measured protein level without changing biology. TREM2's AD signal is driven by the R47H missense, so the plasma-pQTL colocalization is exactly the case where this applies. The record must carry the caveat and must not be presented as clean directional evidence.

betaRatioSignAverage is an average over colocalizing variants and is sign-ambiguous when the effect allele orientation differs between studies. It should be reported per credible set, never pooled, and never converted into a scalar 'direction score'.

Soluble ectodomain versus full-length receptor: a plasma pQTL measures the shed protein, which for TREM2 is not the same species as the membrane receptor the candidate would engage. Direction inferred in plasma may not transfer to the target compartment.

Absence dominates. With 15 of 16 targets returning zero credible sets, the layer's main output is UNDETERMINED. That is genuinely informative but will read as the tool being broken unless the empty-state text explains that the denominator was checked and found empty.
coloc's single-causal-variant assumption is violated at loci with allelic heterogeneity; h4 near 1 is not proof of a shared causal variant.
ideas.why_now: Because it is the check that fails cheapest. The repository already knows that 19 of 22 legacy pLDDT values were overstated; the analogous unexamined assumption on the biology side is that pushing these proteins is beneficial. Ranking a candidate by predicted affinity before knowing the sign of the desired effect optimizes a quantity whose sign is unknown. And it must precede receptor co-folding, the stated largest scientific gap: co-folding a TrkB agonist with TrkB is a lot of MPS time spent on a direction nobody has checked.

ideas.title: Cell-type-resolved expression and instrument provenance: test the five-brain-region claim, and record which cell type each genetic instrument came from
ideas.one_line: Replace the narrative region/cell-type assignment with retrieved expression evidence, and require that any QTL used as directional evidence be annotated with the tissue and cell type it was measured in — because today the only colocalizing QTLs for the platform's one supported target are plasma and monocyte, not brain.
ideas.scientific_rationale: The '5-brain-region targeted' map is the platform's primary organising frame, and it rests on assertion. That much the ledger already records. What the ledger does not address, and what the genetics layer makes newly urgent, is the mirror-image problem on the evidence side: a molecular QTL is only a valid instrument for a target if the regulatory effect it measures is present in the cell type where the drug must act. My sweep today makes this concrete. TREM2 is the platform's only genetically supported target, and its Alzheimer colocalizations come from UKB-PPP blood plasma and Quach_2016 CD14+CD16- classical monocytes. No brain-tissue and no microglial QTL colocalization was returned for any of the 16 targets. Yet the AD-implicated cell type is microglia (Bellenguez 2022, 75 loci, microglial pathway enrichment), and the platform's own candidate HippoNrf-KeapDecoy-X3 names 'Microglial Mitochondria'. So the instrument and the intended site of action are in different cell types, and nothing in the platform records that mismatch. The same logic exposes the region claims: KEAP1 and GSK3B are ubiquitously expressed with no CNS enrichment, so 'hippocampal CA1' is a label, not a property, and for systemically dosed agents on ubiquitous targets that is the classic route to on-target peripheral toxicity. CHRNA7 additionally cannot be read from bulk RNA-seq at all without handling CHRFAM7A, the human-specific partial duplication at 15q13.3 that confounds read mapping — a mapping artifact, not a biology result, and a reason the expression layer must carry paralog warnings rather than a bare TPM.
ideas.what_it_answers: Is the target actually expressed in the cell type the candidate claims to act on, and is the genetic instrument used to argue direction measured in that same cell type? Neither is answerable today: the platform has no expression field of any kind, and its genetics layer (once GENO-B exists) would otherwise silently use a plasma pQTL as evidence about a hippocampal neuron.
ideas.method: 1) Bulk regional baseline, yes-today: use the already-vendored /Users/seunghojung/Documents/DeepMind_Bio/.agents/skills/gtex-database/scripts/gtex_cli.py (GTEx API v2, dataset gtex_v10) to pull median TPM across the 13 GTEx brain regions plus the peripheral tissues, and compute a stated specificity index (brain-region median divided by whole-body median, plus the maximum non-brain tissue and its fold-difference). Emit as pv.database Values keyed `GTEx:v10:<gencodeId>:<tissueSiteDetailId>`. A `check_region_claim` gate in platform/validate.py fails any candidate whose `region` string names a brain region while its target's peak expression is extra-CNS by more than a stated fold. 2) Cell-type resolution, yes-with-work: for the AD-relevant cell types, add microglial eQTL/sQTL from MiGA (255 primary human microglial samples, 100 donors, multiple brain regions) and brain-tissue eQTL from MetaBrain (8,613 RNA-seq samples, 14 datasets, cell-type-inferred cis-eQTLs). Both publish summary statistics; the cis window around 16 genes is small, so this is a bounded download and CPU-only colocalization using the same coloc arithmetic as GENO-B — no GPU. 3) Instrument provenance, yes-today and the cheapest half: every DirectionOfEffect record from GENO-B already receives `otherStudyLocus.study.biosample.biosampleName` and `projectId` from the same query; store them as required fields and add a `cell_type_match` verdict comparing the instrument's biosample against the candidate's declared cell type. On today's data that verdict is MISMATCH for every TREM2 record (instrument: blood plasma / classical monocyte; claimed site: brain). 4) CHRNA7 gets an explicit paralog flag: any expression Value for CHRNA7 carries a note that CHRFAM7A confounds short-read quantification at 15q13.3, and the Value is marked with reduced confidence rather than silently reported.

ideas.effort: Step 1 and step 3 (GTEx regional specificity plus instrument-provenance annotation) are 2-3 days and yes-today. Step 2 (MiGA and MetaBrain colocalization) is roughly a week, dominated by fetching and harmonizing summary statistics to GRCh38 with consistent effect-allele orientation; the computation itself is trivial CPU. No GPU, no wet lab.
success_criteria: Every target carries GTEx v10 regional medians plus a specificity index with an explicit formula, all as provenanced Values; `check_region_claim` fails at least the candidates whose targets peak outside the CNS.

Every DirectionOfEffect record from GENO-B carries a non-empty instrument biosample and project id, and a `cell_type_match` verdict; the TREM2 records return MISMATCH against any brain cell-type claim.

At least one brain-tissue or microglial cis-QTL colocalization is attempted for each of the 16 targets, with the result — including 'no instrument available' — recorded as an explicit Value rather than an absent field.
CHRNA7 expression Values carry the CHRFAM7A paralog warning and are not reported as a bare TPM.
No expression number appears anywhere in the UI without its tissue, dataset version and the specificity denominator.
risks: Bulk GTEx brain tissue is a mixture; a low bulk TPM does not exclude high expression in a rare cell type, and a high bulk TPM does not establish the claimed cell type. The specificity index must be presented as a bulk-level screen, not a cell-type measurement.

MiGA and MetaBrain sample sizes (100 donors and 8,613 samples respectively) are far smaller than UKB-PPP, so brain instruments are weak; a null brain colocalization is frequently a power problem, not biological absence. The record must distinguish 'tested, not colocalized' from 'no instrument'.
Post-mortem brain expression reflects end-stage tissue with cell-composition shifts driven by the disease itself, which can induce reverse-causation artifacts in eQTL-to-disease inference.

Summary-statistics harmonization (build, strand, effect allele) is the usual source of silent sign errors — the exact class of failure this repository exists to prevent — so orientation must be asserted by test, not by convention.
This is the largest of the three in data-plumbing terms and the least self-contained; it should follow GENO-A and GENO-B rather than run in parallel.
ideas.why_now: GENO-B produces directional evidence, and without this layer that evidence would be attached to the wrong cell type without anyone noticing — a plasma pQTL quietly standing in for a hippocampal neuron is the same category of error as a trigonometric expression standing in for pLDDT. Doing it third is right; not doing it makes the second idea unsafe to trust.

ideas.title: Junction-resolved MHC-II immunogenicity screen with a human self-proteome filter
ideas.one_line: Predict CD4+ T-cell epitopes across an HLA-DR/DP/DQ panel for all 35 constructs, classify each binding core as self (present in the human proteome) or neo, and attribute every neo-epitope to the specific GGGGS join that created it.
ideas.scientific_rationale: The disclosure in data/dataset.json states plainly that these molecules are 'hand-assembled concatenations of published natural motifs joined by GGGGS linkers'. That construction method is the single most immunogenic decision available to a peptide designer, and the mechanism is specific rather than vague. Central tolerance is imposed against peptides derived from the expressed self proteome. Each parent motif is human-derived and therefore largely tolerized, but a 15-mer that straddles a motif-motif or motif-linker boundary is a sequence that exists nowhere in the human proteome. If such a 15-mer binds a common HLA-II allele, it is a bona fide neo-epitope with no thymic deletion behind it, and it is the classic driver of T-cell-dependent anti-drug antibody responses to fusion biologics (Jawa et al. 2013). Critically, this liability is invisible to every method in the repository: peptide.py flags 'length >= 30 raises anti-drug-antibody risk' as a static string for any long peptide, which is composition-blind and identical for a fully human sequence and a chimera. Immunogenicity is also the one major liability of a 3-11 kDa peptide that is fully determined by primary sequence — it needs no structure, no receptor, no MSA — so it is exactly the gap that can be closed honestly on this hardware. The self/non-self census is not a heuristic: it is an exact substring test against a downloadable reference proteome, and the repository already performs a SwissProt-wide exact-match scan (evidenced in memory/ledger/curation-verifier.jsonl, which audits a 575,503-entry SwissProt motif scan), so the machinery and the discipline for it already exist.
ideas.what_it_answers: For each construct: how many CD4+ T-cell epitopes does it present across a reference HLA class II allele panel; how many of those binding cores are absent from the human proteome (i.e. non-tolerized neo-epitopes); and how many of those neo-epitopes were manufactured by the GGGGS joins rather than inherited from the parent motifs? The platform currently reports no immunogenicity quantity of any kind — not an epitope count, not an allele, not a self/non-self call.
ideas.method: New module platform/cbc/compute/immuno.py, built on the same refusal-and-provenance pattern as compute/admet.py and the BackendInfo registry in compute/structure.py. (1) Backend registry with two independent MHC-II predictors: NetMHCIIpan-4.3 standalone, which DTU ships as a Darwin_arm64 package under a free academic licence and which covers HLA-DR/DQ/DP plus 600+ alleles (%Rank_EL thresholds: strong <1%, weak <5%); and MixMHC2pred-2.0, whose Mac executable is a direct GitHub release download with no request form, giving a path that works even before the DTU licence clears. Both are CPU-only feed-forward networks — no CUDA, no MPS needed. Where neither binary is installed the module returns a BackendUnavailable-style record with the install instruction, exactly as boltz_info() does, and emits no number. (2) Enumerate all 15-mers of each candidate sequence (data/dataset.json candidates[].sequence), run against a fixed, declared allele panel, and record %Rank plus the predicted 9-mer core. (3) Self filter: download the UniProt human reference proteome UP000005640 once, index all 9-mers, and mark each predicted core SELF if it occurs exactly, NEO otherwise. (4) Junction attribution: the dataset already carries data/dataset.json motif_provenance with 16 exactly-attributed motifs (verified: 'exact_match': true, with UniProt accessions and residue ranges). Locate each motif by substring search in the candidate, derive the boundary offsets, and tag a 15-mer as JUNCTIONAL if its span crosses a motif boundary or overlaps a GGGGS/GS linker. (5) Report per candidate as provenance.predicted() values: n_binders, n_strong_binders, n_neo_cores, n_junctional_neo, allele coverage fraction. (6) Validation gate before any candidate number is emitted: run the predictor on a positive control with published binding (e.g. an immunodominant HA307-319-class epitope) and on a scrambled negative, and refuse to report if the installed binary does not reproduce the expected strong/weak call — the same calibration discipline the repo already applied to Boltz-2 with Huperzine A. (7) Wire into platform/validate.py so the new fields are subject to the existing data-integrity gate.
