evidence.citation: Repository file /Users/seunghojung/Documents/DeepMind_Bio/data/dataset.json, key motif_provenance (16 motifs, each with uniprot_accession, residue_range and exact_match: true); and /Users/seunghojung/Documents/DeepMind_Bio/memory/ledger/curation-verifier.jsonl line 7 (audit of a 575,503-entry SwissProt exact-match scan)
evidence.supports: Junction coordinates are derivable today from data already in the repository, and exact proteome-wide substring scanning is already an established, audited capability here.

ideas.effort: About 2-3 days. Roughly 1 day for the backend registry, 15-mer enumeration, allele panel and refusal paths; half a day for the UP000005640 download and 9-mer self index (~20k proteins, trivially fast and small on a laptop); half a day for junction attribution off motif_provenance; half a day for the control-calibration gate and validate.py wiring. The only schedule risk is the NetMHCIIpan academic download form, which MixMHC2pred fully de-risks.
success_criteria: The installed predictor reproduces the expected strong-binder call on a published positive-control epitope and a non-binder call on its scrambled counterpart, and this control result is written to the provenance ledger before any candidate is scored.

All 31 sequence-valid candidates receive n_binders, n_neo_cores and n_junctional_neo as PREDICTED values carrying software name+version, allele panel, and %Rank threshold; the 4 candidates with ambiguous residues receive an explicit refusal, not a zero.
Every predicted 9-mer core is labelled SELF or NEO by exact match against UP000005640, and the index build is reproducible from a recorded proteome release version.
Junctional attribution is checkable by hand: for at least one candidate, the reported junctional 15-mers can be regenerated from motif_provenance offsets by an independent reader.

With neither MHC-II binary installed, the module emits zero numbers and one refusal record per candidate — verified by a test in platform/tests/test_platform.py, mirroring the existing ADMET refusal test.
platform/validate.py passes with the new fields present, and python3 verify_all.py still returns all checks green.
risks: MHC-II binding prediction has good sensitivity but modest positive predictive value for clinical ADA incidence. The output must be reported as a comparative risk ranking across the 35 constructs, never as an immunogenicity probability. Provenance uncertainty text must say this.

Exact 9-mer presence in the human proteome is a crude tolerance proxy: thymic presentation is not guaranteed by proteome membership, expression level and tissue matter, and register shifts mean a core can be self while its flanks are not. The SELF label must be documented as 'sequence present in the human proteome', not 'tolerized'.
NetMHCIIpan's academic licence is per-user and non-redistributable; the binary must not be committed to the repository, and the module must degrade to refusal rather than to a bundled copy.
Allele panel choice changes the counts. The panel must be fixed, declared in provenance, and justified — not silently tuned until the numbers look acceptable.
ideas.why_now: This is the highest-value gap because it is the only major liability of the primary modality that is (a) entirely determined by sequence, so it needs none of the missing pieces — no receptor complex, no MSA, no docking; (b) served by a validated, CPU-only, arm64-native tool; and (c) a direct interrogation of the specific design decision the project has already admitted to. Every other open question here (ipTM, binding free energy) requires modelling a complex that has never been built. This one can be answered completely, today, with the data already in dataset.json, and the answer speaks directly to whether the GGGGS-concatenation strategy is viable at all.

ideas.title: Structure-aware proteolysis map: what is the actual circulating species?
ideas.one_line: Compute a per-bond protease-susceptibility census for every construct using pyteomics' shipped Expasy cleavage rules, gate each site on solvent exposure and secondary structure taken from the Boltz-2 model, and report the predicted fragment population instead of a hand-written sentence about serum peptidases.
ideas.scientific_rationale: peptide.py currently emits, for any candidate of length >= 30, the fixed string 'unmodified linear peptides of this length are cleared by serum peptidases with plasma half-lives of minutes'. That sentence is scientifically correct in the aggregate and computationally empty in the particular: it is identical for a disulfide-constrained 47-mer knottin and for a fully flexible polycationic 100-mer, and it tells a reader nothing about which molecule is worse or where it breaks. The mechanistic point that makes this computable is well established: limited proteolysis of a folded protein requires roughly ten residues of locally extended, solvent-exposed, flexible backbone to thread the protease active-site cleft — sequence specificity alone does not predict cleavage, and buried or helically-constrained sites are protected (Hubbard 1998). The repository already has both halves of that calculation available. Sequence specificity comes from pyteomics.parser.expasy_rules, which ships 35 protease rule sets as package data — I verified this in-session on this machine (trypsin regex '([KR](?=[^P]))|((?<=W)K(?=P))|((?<=M)R(?=P))' loaded correctly, arm64) — so no coefficient or rule is transcribed from memory, which is precisely the failure class this repo exists to eliminate. Structural gating comes from the Boltz-2 models, whose per-residue pLDDT the repo already parses in predictor.py. This turns proteolysis from prose into geometry. It also produces a concrete, falsifiable prediction about the design method: GGGGS/GS linkers are the most exposed and least structured segment of any fusion, and flexible GS linkers are documented as proteolytically labile in vivo (Chen, Zaro & Shen 2013), so the constructs should be predicted to fragment at the joins and release the parent motifs. For CogAbeta-Clearer-08 and BasalAChE-Abeta-B4 that consequence is severe and specific: the released fragment is unmodified all-L Abeta16-35, which motif_provenance already documents as the complete fibril-forming core. The polarity error the repo has flagged qualitatively becomes a quantified seeding hazard with a named release mechanism. Separately, this exposes an infrastructure defect I found while looking: a filesystem-wide search for *.cif and boltz output directories in the repository returns nothing. The 22 Boltz-2 runs were performed and only their summary scalars survive in data/real_vs_hardcoded.json — the coordinates themselves were discarded. A structure prediction whose coordinates are not retained cannot be re-audited, which contradicts the project's own traceability rule.
ideas.what_it_answers: For each construct: which peptide bond is cut first, how many fragments the molecule becomes, what fraction of cuts fall in the linkers versus the functional motifs, and therefore what species actually circulates and reaches (or fails to reach) the target. Specifically: does administering CogAbeta-Clearer-08 or BasalAChE-Abeta-B4 liberate free amyloidogenic Abeta16-35? The platform can currently answer none of this; binding_free_energy, dissociation_constant, plddt and herg are all not_computed for all 35, and there is no metabolite or fragment concept anywhere in the schema.
ideas.method: New module platform/cbc/compute/proteolysis.py. (1) Sequence census: for each candidate, enumerate cleavage sites with pyteomics.parser.expasy_rules for a declared protease panel — trypsin, chymotrypsin high specificity, pepsin pH2.0, thermolysin, proteinase K, Glu-C — and compute fragment-length distributions with parser.cleave(). I already ran this on all 35 candidates this session: 215 trypsin-like sites across the catalogue; the three duplicated copies of KWWKFLRRFWRRLKKYFEELWKKLAEKYFELLKKYG (HippoAChE-AlkaPept-X2, BasalAChE-GorgeBlock-B1, CogAChE-PAS-02) carry 24 trypsin+chymotrypsin sites in 36 residues, mean tryptic fragment 1.5 residues, longest tryptic fragment 7 residues; the 100-mer CogDual-TrkB-PAS-10 carries 35. AstroPafr-Block-A4 has zero — a real discriminating result, not noise. (2) Persist Boltz outputs: amend the driver so run_boltz() copies the model mmCIF, confidence JSON, plddt npz and pae npz into a versioned data/structures/<code>/ directory, and record the file paths in provenance source_id. This must happen before anything structural can be computed. (3) Structural gating: load the mmCIF with biotite 1.7.1 (verified installed, arm64, this session), compute per-residue relative SASA with biotite.structure.sasa or freesasa 2.2.1 (both verified installed), and assign secondary structure with biotite.structure.annotate_sse. Classify each sequence-matched site as EXPOSED-EXTENDED (predicted accessible), BURIED, or HELIX/SHEET-CONSTRAINED. (4) Confidence gate: use the per-residue pLDDT that predictor.py already parses. Sites in regions with pLDDT < 70 are reported as 'structurally undetermined — treated as accessible', with the fraction of such sites reported per candidate; frac_below_70 is already present in data/real_vs_hardcoded.json, so the gate is auditable. (5) Emit per candidate: n_sites by protease, predicted-accessible site list ranked by relative SASA, fragment-length distribution, linker-cut fraction, and for the two Abeta constructs an explicit 'released fragment identity' record cross-referenced to motif_provenance. All as provenance.computed() with software versions, or not_computed where the structure is missing.

evidence.supports: Establishes the mechanistic basis for gating sequence-specificity on structure: proteolysis requires local backbone flexibility and solvent exposure over an extended stretch, so accessible/disordered segments are cut and buried or constrained segments with identical P1 residues are not.

evidence.supports: Documents flexible GS-rich linkers as a recognised in vivo proteolytic liability in fusion constructs, grounding the falsifiable prediction that these GGGGS-joined molecules fragment at the joins and release their parent motifs.

evidence.citation: Repository state, verified this session: filesystem search for *.cif and for boltz output directories under /Users/seunghojung/Documents/DeepMind_Bio (excluding .venv*) returns zero results, while data/real_vs_hardcoded.json records 22 completed Boltz-2 v2.2.1 predictions with plddt_mean, frac_below_70 and Ca-Ca geometry audits.
evidence.supports: The structural half of this idea requires re-running or re-persisting Boltz-2 output; the coordinates from the completed runs were not retained, which is itself a traceability defect worth fixing.

ideas.effort: About 3-4 days. The sequence census is essentially done — I ran it across all 35 candidates in this session, so that part is under a day to productionise with provenance. The structural half needs the Boltz-2 runs repeated with output persistence: 22 candidates already completed once on this machine's MPS accelerator, so wall-clock is known-tolerable, but budget a day of compute plus a day for the SASA/SSE/pLDDT gating logic and a day for tests and validate.py wiring.
success_criteria: Every sequence-valid candidate carries a cleavage census with per-protease site counts and fragment-length distribution, each as a COMPUTED value naming pyteomics and its version; the numbers are exactly reproducible by re-running parser.cleave().
data/structures/<code>/ contains the retained mmCIF, confidence JSON and pLDDT array for every Boltz-2 run, and every structural value's provenance source_id points at a real file on disk.

Each cleavage site is annotated with relative SASA and secondary-structure state, or explicitly marked 'structurally undetermined' where local pLDDT < 70, with the undetermined fraction reported per candidate.

The linker-cut fraction is reported for the 12 candidates with non-zero GGGGS/GS linker content (measured this session: linker fraction ranges 0.06 to 0.29), and the predicted released fragments for CogAbeta-Clearer-08 and BasalAChE-Abeta-B4 are cross-referenced by exact substring to the KLVFFAEDVGSNKGAIIGLM entry in motif_provenance.
No half-life in time units is emitted anywhere. The module must be incapable of printing a t1/2, and a test asserts this.
python3 verify_all.py stays green and platform/validate.py accepts the new fields.
risks: The Expasy rule set covers digestive and laboratory proteases, not the plasma and CNS peptidase panel that actually governs peptide clearance (neprilysin, insulin-degrading enzyme, DPP-4, ACE, plasmin, kallikrein). Trypsin-like and chymotrypsin-like specificity is a legitimate proxy for the plasmin/kallikrein class, but the output must be labelled a susceptibility census, not a metabolic-stability prediction. Overclaiming here would reproduce the original sin.

Single-sequence Boltz-2 models are the weakest input available. Nineteen of 22 legacy pLDDT values were overstated by 10-46 units and several computed models sit near 49; a SASA computed on a wrong fold is a wrong SASA. The pLDDT gate must be conservative and the undetermined fraction must be reported prominently rather than buried.

Disulfide connectivity is not_computed for 31 candidates, and connectivity strongly determines exposure in the cysteine-rich ones (HippoTrk-Saponin-X1 has 8 cysteines and 105 possible pairings). Structural gating for those candidates is conditional on an arbitrary Boltz-chosen pairing and must say so.

No experimental stability data exists here to calibrate against, so the ranking cannot be converted into absolute risk. Wet-lab plasma-stability LC-MS would be needed for that, and this project has no wet lab.
ideas.why_now: Proteolysis is the rate-limiting liability for this modality — before immunogenicity, before receptor engagement, before the BBB, the question is whether the intact molecule exists in plasma for long enough to matter. It is the only remaining big DMPK question that can be answered from assets already on hand: the sequences, the motif attributions, and compute that has already been shown to run on this laptop. It also forces a fix to a real infrastructure defect (discarded Boltz coordinates) that blocks every future structural analysis, and it converts the repo's most serious existing finding — the inverted amyloid constructs — from a labelling criticism into a mechanistic prediction about what those molecules would release in vivo.

ideas.title: Membrane-lysis and hemolysis risk, calibrated against measured control peptides — and an honest verdict on the BBB
ideas.one_line: Replace peptide.py's binary composition heuristic with a hydrophobic-moment calculation benchmarked against melittin, magainin-2, LL-37 and a non-lytic control, add a domain-gated hemolysis predictor, and answer the BBB question by measuring how few candidates any BBB-peptide model can legitimately accept.
ideas.scientific_rationale: admet.py correctly refuses to give these molecules a hERG number and states, in its own refusal text, that 'for polycationic amphipaths, membrane lysis' is a governing liability. Nothing in the repository then measures it. What exists instead is a single composition rule in peptide.py — frac_cationic >= 0.30 AND frac_aromatic >= 0.15 — which is amphipathicity assessed without reference to whether the cationic and hydrophobic residues actually segregate onto opposite faces of a helix. That distinction is the entire mechanism of membrane lysis: it is the hydrophobic moment, not the amino-acid census, that determines whether a helix has a lytic face, and ideally amphipathic Leu/Lys designs can exceed melittin's hemolytic potency purely by improving facial segregation at constant composition (Cornut et al. 1994). I measured the consequence in this session using modlAMP's Eisenberg-scale moment (max over an 18-residue window, 100 degrees per residue): melittin 0.558, magainin-2 0.509, LL-37 0.897, insulin B-chain 0.160 as a non-lytic negative. Against that calibration, six candidates score 0.886-0.894 — at or above LL-37, a genuinely membrane-lytic human cathelicidin — and 17 of the 31 sequence-valid candidates exceed 0.40. The current composition rule fires on only 4 of 35. It misses CogDual-TrkB-PAS-10 entirely: the largest construct in the catalogue at 100 residues and 11.4 kDa, net charge +8.4, hydrophobic moment 0.894. That is a false negative on the molecule with the largest exposure of any in the set. Separately, the BBB question deserves a blunt answer rather than a prediction. The honest finding is that no peptide BBB model has an applicability domain that reaches these molecules: B3Pred, the standard tool, was trained on 269 experimentally validated BBB-penetrating peptides and accepts sequences of 5-30 residues only, whereas these constructs run 26-100 residues. By length alone, at most 4 of 35 are admissible, and none of those is a 5 kDa polycation of the kind the model saw. The scientifically correct deliverable is therefore a refusal plus a deterministic census: does the construct contain any documented receptor-mediated-transcytosis shuttle motif at all? That is an exact substring test with a yes/no answer, and it is the actual determinant of brain exposure for a molecule of this size.
ideas.what_it_answers: Which candidates are membrane-lytic, ranked against measured reference peptides on the same scale, and with what predicted hemolytic concentration? And: for how many candidates is any published BBB-peptide predictor even in its applicability domain, and does any construct carry a documented BBB shuttle motif? The platform currently has no hemolysis field, no hydrophobic-moment calculation, and no BBB assessment beyond a molecular-weight sentence that fires identically for all 35 molecules.
ideas.method: Extend platform/cbc/peptide.py and add platform/cbc/compute/membrane.py. (1) Hydrophobic moment via modlAMP 4.3.0 (verified installed and working on this machine's arm64 Python 3.14 in this session): PeptideDescriptor(seq,'eisenberg').calculate_moment(window=18, angle=100, modality='max'), plus mean hydrophobicity. The Eisenberg scale ships inside modlAMP, so no scale is transcribed by hand. (2) Mandatory control panel: every report renders the candidate's moment alongside the four measured-behaviour references I computed this session (melittin 0.558, magainin-2 0.509, LL-37 0.897, insulin B-chain 0.160) so a reader can interpret the number rather than trust a threshold. Controls are recomputed at runtime, not stored as constants. (3) Structural gate: the moment assumes an alpha-helix. Use the Boltz-2 secondary-structure assignment from DMPK-IDEA-2 to mark whether the high-moment window is actually helical in the model; for the disulfide-rich, low-pLDDT candidates report the moment as conditional. (4) Hemolysis: HemoPI2 (pip install hemopi2), classification plus HC50 regression, run first on the same four controls and used only if it ranks melittin hemolytic and insulin B-chain non-hemolytic — the same calibrate-before-you-report discipline already applied to Boltz-2 with Huperzine A. Enforce an applicability domain on length against the Hemolytik training distribution and refuse the 100-mer and 62-mer if they fall outside it. (5) BBB: implement B3Pred's own stated domain as a gate (5-30 residues) and emit an explicit refusal record for every candidate outside it, listing the count. Then run a deterministic RMT shuttle-motif census by exact substring against a small, cited, versioned table of documented BBB shuttles (Angiopep-2, T7/HAIYPRH, RVG29, and similar), each entry carrying its own DOI, and report a simple present/absent per candidate. (6) Retire the frac_cationic/frac_aromatic boolean as a liability trigger, or demote it to a secondary descriptor, and replace the triggering logic with the moment plus the calibrated controls. All values via provenance.computed() or provenance.predicted() with software versions.

evidence.citation: Cornut I, Büttner K, Dasseux JL, Dufourcq J. 'The amphipathic alpha-helix concept. Application to the de novo design of ideally amphipathic Leu, Lys peptides with hemolytic activity higher than that of melittin', FEBS Letters 349(1):29-33 (1994). PMID 8045297
evidence.supports: Establishes that facial segregation (hydrophobic moment), not amino-acid composition, drives hemolytic potency in cationic amphipathic helices — de novo Leu/Lys designs 5-10x more hemolytic than melittin. This is why the existing composition rule in peptide.py is the wrong descriptor.

evidence.citation: Müller AT, Gabernet G, Hiss JA, Schneider G. 'modlAMP: Python for antimicrobial peptides', Bioinformatics 33(17):2753-2755 (2017). DOI 10.1093/bioinformatics/btx285; PMID 28472272
evidence.supports: Supplies the Eisenberg-scale hydrophobic-moment implementation with the scale as package data. Verified installed and executed on this machine (modlamp 4.3.0, arm64, Python 3.14) in this session; the melittin/magainin-2/LL-37/insulin-B control values quoted above are outputs from that run.

evidence.citation: Rathore AS, Choudhury S, Arora A, Tijare P, Raghava GPS. 'Prediction of hemolytic peptides and their hemolytic concentration', Communications Biology 8:176 (2025). DOI 10.1038/s42003-025-07615-w
evidence.supports: HemoPI2 provides both hemolytic classification and HC50 regression for peptides against mammalian RBCs, is distributed as a pip-installable Python 3 standalone (pypi 'hemopi2', github.com/raghavagps/HemoPI2), and runs on CPU — the only hemolysis capability the platform could honestly acquire without a wet lab.

evidence.citation: Kumar V, Patiyal S, Dhall A, Sharma N, Raghava GPS. 'B3Pred: A Random-Forest-Based Method for Predicting and Designing Blood-Brain Barrier Penetrating Peptides', Pharmaceutics 13(8):1237 (2021). DOI 10.3390/pharmaceutics13081237
evidence.supports: States the applicability domain explicitly: trained on 269 experimentally validated BBB-penetrating peptides from B3Pdb, supporting sequences of 5-30 amino acids only. This is the citation that makes 'we refuse to predict BBB penetration for 31 of 35 constructs' a documented, defensible position rather than an evasion.

evidence.citation: Measured in this session from /Users/seunghojung/Documents/DeepMind_Bio/data/dataset.json: Eisenberg hydrophobic moment (18-residue window, modlAMP 4.3.0) exceeds 0.40 for 17 of 31 sequence-valid candidates and reaches 0.886-0.894 for six, while peptide.py's frac_cationic>=0.30 AND frac_aromatic>=0.15 rule fires for only 4 of 35; CogDual-TrkB-PAS-10 (100 aa, 11.4 kDa, net charge +8.4) scores 0.894 and is not currently flagged.
evidence.supports: Quantifies the false-negative rate of the descriptor the platform uses today, and identifies the specific molecule the current rule misses.

ideas.effort: About 2 days. The hydrophobic-moment work and the control panel are close to done — I executed them across the whole catalogue in this session, so productionising is under a day including tests. HemoPI2 adds roughly half a day plus a large one-time ESM/PyTorch model download; the B3Pred domain gate and the RMT motif census are half a day, since the census is an exact substring test over a small cited table.
success_criteria: Every sequence-valid candidate reports an Eisenberg hydrophobic moment computed by modlAMP, rendered alongside the four control peptides recomputed at runtime; melittin must land at 0.558 +/- 0.001 on each run or the module refuses to report.
HemoPI2 is used only after it classifies melittin as hemolytic and insulin B-chain as non-hemolytic on the same invocation; the control result is written to the provenance ledger.

Candidates outside HemoPI2's or B3Pred's stated applicability domain receive a refusal record with the stated domain and the candidate's violating property — matching the existing admet.py refusal pattern and testable the same way.

The BBB section reports an explicit count of how many of 35 candidates any BBB-peptide predictor can legitimately accept, with B3Pred's 5-30-residue domain cited, and a present/absent RMT shuttle-motif call for every candidate with each shuttle entry carrying its own DOI.
The frac_cationic/frac_aromatic boolean no longer triggers a liability on its own, and a regression test demonstrates that CogDual-TrkB-PAS-10 is now flagged where it previously was not.
python3 verify_all.py stays green; platform/validate.py accepts the new fields.
risks: The hydrophobic moment assumes an alpha-helical conformation. For the cysteine-rich candidates (HippoTrk-Saponin-X1 has 8 cysteines, PfcTrk-ErkEnhancer-P2 has 7, CogTrk-DeNovo-01 has 9) the helix assumption is likely wrong, and the value must be reported as conditional on the Boltz secondary structure rather than as a property of the molecule.

HemoPI2's Hemolytik-derived training data is dominated by short antimicrobial peptides; the 100-mer and 62-mer are almost certainly outside it. Refusing them is correct but leaves the two largest constructs without a hemolysis number, which must be stated plainly rather than filled.

Predicted HC50 is a model output with no calibrated interval and no wet-lab anchor available in this project. It can rank candidates; it cannot support a safety-margin argument. Only an actual RBC lysis assay could, and there is no wet lab here.

The RMT shuttle-motif census only detects motifs on its curated list. A negative result means 'no listed shuttle', not 'no possible transport mechanism', and the list's provenance and version must travel with the result.

There is a real risk of the panel being read as a green light where a candidate scores low on everything. Low predicted hemolysis does not make a 5 kDa polycation deliverable; the BBB refusal must be rendered at least as prominently as the hemolysis number.
ideas.why_now: admet.py's refusal is currently a dead end: the platform correctly declines to score its own primary modality and then offers nothing in its place, so the 35 lead molecules have no deliverability assessment at all. This closes that hole with the two liabilities that actually govern a polycationic amphipath — membrane lysis and brain access — and it does so cheaply, because the calculation is already demonstrated working on this hardware. It also corrects a live false negative rather than merely adding a field: the current heuristic passes the largest, most highly charged construct in the catalogue as non-amphipathic when its hydrophobic moment matches a known lytic cathelicidin. Fixing a wrong answer ranks above adding a new one.

proposals.expert: Metascience and research software engineering — reproducibility, provenance standards, and software peer review (JOSS reviewer); 18 years post-PhD

ideas.title: Recompute-or-retract: a replay harness, introspected runtime capture, and seeded structure prediction
ideas.one_line: Make every published number re-derivable from a clean checkout, replace the two hand-typed software-version literals with introspected runtime facts, and put a recorded seed on every Boltz-2 run so the platform's headline pLDDT result can be reproduced and its noise floor measured.
ideas.scientific_rationale:
The rebuild's founding principle is that a number and its origin must be inseparable. That principle is currently enforced everywhere except at the one place it is easiest to violate silently. `Provenance.__post_init__` (platform/cbc/provenance.py:64) requires a `software` string for COMPUTED/PREDICTED — but `platform/build_dataset.py:34` supplies it as the string literal `RDKIT_VER = "RDKit 2026.03.5"`, and `platform/cbc/corpus.py:318` writes `getattr(chem, 'RDKIT_VERSION', '2026.03.5')` against a module that defines no `RDKIT_VERSION` (verified: `hasattr(chem,'RDKIT_VERSION')` is False), so the fallback literal is always taken. Every `software` field in dataset.json is therefore an assertion nobody computed — true today by coincidence, false the moment anyone installs a different RDKit. That is the exact failure class the rebuild exists to eliminate, surviving inside the module built to prevent it.

The second half is worse because a scientific conclusion rests on it. Boltz-2 is a diffusion sampler; `boltz 2.2.1 --help` documents `--seed INTEGER  Seed to use for random number generator. Default is None (no seeding).` `run_boltz()` (platform/cbc/compute/structure.py:191-195) never passes it, and runs with `diffusion_samples=1`. The 22 pLDDT values in `data/real_vs_hardcoded.json` — from which the platform concludes that 19 of 22 legacy values were overstated by 10-46 units — came from an unseeded single-sample stochastic process, and no mmCIF, confidence JSON, PAE array, or weights checksum was retained anywhere in the repository (searched: no Boltz output directory exists). Without a seed-to-seed spread the 10-unit deltas and the 46-unit deltas are scientifically indistinguishable claims. If run-to-run spread is 8 pLDDT units, a '10-unit overstatement' is noise and must be withdrawn; a 46-unit one survives. The platform has no way to tell these apart, and neither does a reader.

Third: the ledger asserts integrity it never checks. Re-hashing every ARTIFACT record in memory/ledger/*.jsonl against the working tree gives ok=10, mismatch=4, missing=0 — `data/dataset.json`, `data/real_vs_hardcoded.json`, `platform/validate.py`, and `reviews/REVIEW_REPORT.md` no longer match their recorded sha256, and none of the 215 checks notices.
ideas.what_it_answers: "If a third party checks this repository out on their own machine today and runs it, which of its published numbers come back identical, which come back different, and by how much?" The platform cannot answer this and does not ask it: the 215 checks verify internal consistency and parsing, never reproduction. A corollary it also cannot answer: "is the 10-unit pLDDT discrepancy larger than the sampler's own run-to-run noise?"
ideas.method:
1. New `platform/cbc/env.py::runtime()` returning introspected facts only: `rdkit.__version__`, `sys.version`, `platform.machine()`/`platform.mac_ver()`, `torch.__version__` and `torch.backends.mps.is_available()`, boltz version obtained by executing the .venv312 interpreter, and sha256 of the Boltz-2 weight files under `~/.boltz`. Delete the literal at build_dataset.py:34 and the `getattr` fallback at corpus.py:318; both call `runtime()`. Add a check to `verify_all.py`: every distinct `provenance.software` string in data/dataset.json must appear in the runtime manifest, otherwise exit non-zero. This closes the one provenance field the constructor cannot police.
2. Pass `--seed` (fixed, recorded) plus `--recycling_steps`/`--diffusion_samples` on every Boltz invocation in structure.py, and persist the returned mmCIF, `confidence_*.json`, and `pae_*.npz` under `runs/<content-hash>/`, registering each with the ledger's existing ARTIFACT record type (which already carries path + sha256). Re-fold one candidate twice at the same seed and three times at different seeds; publish the seed-to-seed pLDDT envelope in `data/real_vs_hardcoded.json` alongside each legacy delta, and downgrade any delta smaller than 2x that envelope from "overstated" to "indistinguishable from sampling noise".
3. New `platform/reproduce.py`: rebuild dataset.json from `data/extracted_raw.json` + `data/curated.json` into a temp dir, walk both trees leaf-by-leaf, and classify each value `identical | within_declared_tolerance | differs | absent`. Emit `data/reproduction_report.json`; exit non-zero if any leaf lands in `differs` without a declared tolerance and reason. Add the ledger ARTIFACT re-hash loop I ran above as a permanent check.
4. Environment pinning and containerization, stated honestly. Ship `requirements.lock` with hashes for the 3.14 env and `requirements-boltz.lock` for the 3.12 env (recording *why* they are separate: boltz pins a scipy with no cp314 wheel, already documented at structure.py:36-38). Containerize only the deterministic CPU layer — a `linux/arm64` image running chem/peptide/thermo/validate/build_dataset. Do NOT containerize Boltz: Docker Desktop on macOS runs a Linux VM with no Metal/MPS passthrough, so the neural layer inside a container would silently fall back to CPU and produce different wall times and, unseeded, different coordinates. Record that limitation in the manifest instead of shipping an image that quietly does not do what it claims.
5. Prerequisite, and currently the largest single reproducibility defect: `git ls-files` returns nothing under `platform/`, `data/`, `memory/`, `research/`, or `reviews/`. The only tracked content is the discredited mockup (`app.js`, `index.html`, `styles.css`, `README.md`) plus `.agents/`. Anyone cloning today receives the fabricated version and none of the remediation. Commit the rebuild, add an OSI LICENSE, and add a GitHub Actions workflow running `verify_all.py` + `reproduce.py` (the CPU layer only; MPS is not available on hosted runners, so the Boltz suite must be marked as a locally-run tier, not silently skipped).

evidence.citation: Sandve GK, Nekrutenko A, Taylor J, Hovig E. Ten Simple Rules for Reproducible Computational Research. PLoS Comput Biol 9(10):e1003285 (2013). doi:10.1371/journal.pcbi.1003285
evidence.supports: Rule 6 is to record the exact software versions actually used, and Rule 6/8 explicitly cover setting and recording the seed of any stochastic component so a run can be repeated. Both are the specific rules this repository currently breaks (literal version strings; unseeded diffusion sampling). DOI verified live via Crossref this session.

evidence.citation: Passaro S, Corso G, Wohlwend J, et al. Boltz-2: Towards Accurate and Efficient Binding Affinity Prediction. bioRxiv 2025.06.14.659707 (2025). doi:10.1101/2025.06.14.659707
evidence.supports: The model the platform actually runs, confirming it is a diffusion-based sampler whose output depends on sampling. Title/authors/DOI retrieved live from the bioRxiv API this session.

evidence.citation: Boltz 2.2.1 CLI, installed at /Users/seunghojung/Documents/DeepMind_Bio/.venv312/bin/boltz — `boltz predict --help` output
evidence.supports: Executed this session. Emits verbatim: `--seed INTEGER  Seed to use for random number generator. Default is None (no seeding).` The flag exists, is free, and is not used by platform/cbc/compute/structure.py:191-195.

evidence.citation: Live repository measurement: SHA-256 re-verification of every `rec:"ARTIFACT"` record across memory/ledger/*.jsonl against the working tree
evidence.supports: Run this session: ok=10, mismatch=4, missing=0. Mismatching artifacts are data/dataset.json, data/real_vs_hardcoded.json, platform/validate.py, reviews/REVIEW_REPORT.md. The ledger records integrity hashes that nothing verifies.

evidence.citation: Abramson J, Adler J, Dunger J, et al. Accurate structure prediction of biomolecular interactions with AlphaFold 3. Nature 634:493 (2024). doi:10.1038/s41586-024-07487-w
evidence.supports: Establishes the AF3-class diffusion architecture (of which Boltz-2 is the MIT-licensed reimplementation) and the seed/sample-count dependence of its confidence outputs, which is why an unseeded single-sample pLDDT is not a reproducible quantity. DOI verified live via Crossref this session.

ideas.effort: 2-3 days of engineering for env.py, reproduce.py, lockfiles, the CPU-layer container and CI; plus several hours to overnight of MPS wall time to re-fold the 22 candidates with recorded seeds and run the 5 repeat folds for the noise envelope. No new hardware, no paid API, no wet lab.
success_criteria: `grep -rn 'RDKit 20' platform/` returns no hits inside provenance construction; every distinct `provenance.software` value in data/dataset.json is present in `env.runtime()` output, enforced by a check in verify_all.py that fails when RDKit is downgraded in a scratch venv.

`platform/reproduce.py` exits 0 on a clean checkout, and `data/reproduction_report.json` classifies 100% of numeric leaves, with every `differs` leaf carrying a declared tolerance and a stated reason.
Ledger ARTIFACT re-hash reports 0 mismatches; deliberately appending a byte to data/dataset.json makes the check exit non-zero.

Every Boltz result record carries `seed`, `diffusion_samples`, `recycling_steps`, `boltz_version`, `weights_sha256`, and a path to the retained mmCIF and confidence JSON; two same-seed runs are compared and either byte-identical or their divergence is quantified and documented.

A published seed-spread table for at least one candidate (n>=3 seeds), and every legacy-pLDDT delta in data/real_vs_hardcoded.json re-labelled against it as `exceeds sampling noise` or `indistinguishable`.
`git ls-files platform/ | wc -l` is non-zero, a LICENSE exists, and CI runs the CPU tier on every push with the MPS tier explicitly reported as locally-run rather than silently skipped.
risks: PyTorch does not guarantee run-to-run determinism on the MPS backend even with a fixed seed. If same-seed repeats diverge, the honest deliverable is a measured run-to-run envelope, not a determinism claim — and that must be stated as such rather than papered over with a tolerance chosen to make the test pass.

Measuring the seed envelope may show that several of the 19 'overstated' pLDDT values sit inside sampling noise, weakening the platform's headline result. That is the correct outcome of the check and must be published, but it is a real cost to a claim the project currently leans on.
Retaining mmCIF + PAE for 22+ runs adds tens of MB to a git repository; needs git-lfs or a policy of storing PAE npz hashes plus a regeneration recipe rather than the arrays.

Tolerances are the soft joint of any recompute-and-diff harness. If they are set after seeing the diff, the harness becomes theatre. They must be declared per-quantity with a stated physical justification (e.g. RDKit cLogP to 3 decimals is exact-by-algorithm; Boltz pLDDT is not) before the first comparison is run.
ideas.why_now: This is the precondition for everything else. A provenance graph (META-2) that points at a version string nobody measured, or a pre-registered benchmark (META-3) whose model runs are unseeded and whose outputs are discarded, inherits the defect rather than fixing it. It is also the cheapest of the three — the seed flag is one argument, and `env.runtime()` is fifty lines — and it removes the only remaining place in the codebase where a hand-typed string is accepted as a computed fact, which is the specific sin the entire rebuild was undertaken to expiate.

ideas.title: FAIR release: PROV-O/RO-Crate export of the existing ledger, resolvable source identifiers, and a citable artifact
ideas.one_line: Map the 1350-record append-only ledger onto W3C PROV-O, package repository and runs as an RO-Crate with Workflow Run Crate profiles, replace free-text `source_id` strings with resolvable IRIs, and release the whole thing under an explicit licence with a DOI so an outsider — or a machine — can trace and cite any single number.
ideas.scientific_rationale:
The provenance data already exists and is unusually good: `memory/ledger/*.jsonl` records `RUN` (host, pid, python version, timestamp), `ARTIFACT` (path, kind, sha256), and `CLAIM` (text, `source{type,ref,locator}`, confidence, tags), append-only, 1350 lines, 803 claims, 356 edges. That is a provenance graph in everything but vocabulary. What is missing is the three things that make provenance usable by anyone other than its author: a standard serialization, dereferenceable identifiers, and a licence.

Today a `Value`'s origin is prose. `pv.database(smiles, "SMILES", f"PubChem CID {ref['pubchem_cid']}")` in build_dataset.py:60 produces `source_id = "PubChem CID 5281378"` — a human can follow it, `rdflib` cannot, and nothing checks that the CID exists. Likewise `software: "RDKit 2026.03.5"` and `method: "Kd = exp(dG / RT), RT = 0.59248 kcal/mol at 298.15 K"` are unparseable strings. Against the FAIR principles this repository fails F1 (no global persistent identifier — it is an untracked private directory), I1 (no formal, shared knowledge-representation language for its metadata), and R1.1 (no licence at all, on code or data; there is no LICENSE file, and the ChEMBL-derived corpus in data/corpus_ACHE.json silently inherits ChEMBL's CC-BY-SA licensing constraint, which the repository nowhere states).

The scientific necessity, not merely the tidiness: this project's genuinely novel content is its *absences*. Thirty-five candidates carry `binding_free_energy`, `dissociation_constant`, `plddt`, and `herg` as NOT_COMPUTED with a specific machine-readable reason, and a set of retracted claims preserved verbatim rather than deleted. No conventional dataset export represents any of that. Exported as an ordinary table, the distinguishing feature of the work becomes invisible — an empty cell indistinguishable from a missing measurement. PROV-O gives the retractions a proper predicate (`prov:wasInvalidatedBy`) and lets the NOT_COMPUTED reasons ride as first-class typed statements, so a consumer machine can tell 'we chose not to compute this, here is why' apart from 'no data'.
ideas.what_it_answers: Two questions, neither answerable today. (a) "Given one number — `HippoTrk-Saponin-X1` pLDDT 78.03 — what exact inputs, software, parameters and agent produced it, and can I follow that chain programmatically without reading Python?" The chain currently exists only as free text plus a private JSONL with an undocumented schema. (b) "How do I cite this work, what version am I citing, and under what terms may I reuse the ChEMBL-derived corpus?" There is no DOI, no CITATION.cff, no LICENSE, and no statement of the inherited data licence.
ideas.method:
1. `platform/cbc/prov_export.py`: mechanical mapping of the existing ledger onto PROV-O. `RUN` -> `prov:Activity` with `prov:startedAtTime`; `ARTIFACT` -> `prov:Entity` identified by its recorded sha256 (content-addressed, so the identifier survives a move); `CLAIM` -> `prov:Entity` with `prov:wasDerivedFrom` its artifacts and `prov:wasAttributedTo` a `prov:SoftwareAgent` carrying the `env.runtime()` manifest from META-1. Each retracted claim in dataset.json gets `prov:wasInvalidatedBy` pointing at the audit activity that discredited it. Serialize as JSON-LD and Turtle.
2. Typed, resolvable sources. Extend `Provenance` with an optional `source_iri`, and change the DATABASE/LITERATURE constructors to mint one: `https://identifiers.org/chembl.compound:CHEMBL54126`, `https://identifiers.org/pubchem.compound:5281378`, `https://identifiers.org/uniprot:P22303`, `https://doi.org/...`. Keep the human string; add the machine one. Then enforce it — extend `verify_all.py` so a DATABASE or LITERATURE `Value` whose `source_id` yields no resolvable IRI fails the gate, with a cached weekly (not per-commit) HTTP HEAD sample confirming resolution.
3. Package as RO-Crate 1.1: a root `ro-crate-metadata.json` describing the repository, its datasets, its scripts and its licences, using the Process Run Crate / Workflow Run Crate profiles for each recorded compute step so the crate states which script, which parameters, which inputs and which outputs constituted each run. This is exactly the granularity the ledger already records; the profile supplies the vocabulary.
4. Make the artifact citable: `CITATION.cff`, `codemeta.json`, separate LICENSE files for code (e.g. MIT/Apache-2.0) and data (with the ChEMBL CC-BY-SA inheritance stated explicitly for data/corpus_ACHE.json), and a Zenodo-minted DOI on first tagged release.
5. Publication venue, answering the brief's 'what and where'. Three distinct outputs, not one: (i) the versioned artifact + RO-Crate on Zenodo with a DOI, cited by the other two; (ii) a short methods/negative-result preprint on bioRxiv or ChemRxiv reporting the findings that are genuinely novel and currently unpublished — 19 of 22 asserted pLDDT values overstated by up to 46 units, ipTM identically 0.00 across all 22 because every candidate was folded as a lone chain, and a 2.41 log-unit Boltz-2 affinity error on huperzine A/AChE in single-sequence mode; (iii) JOSS only *after* META-1 lands, since JOSS requires an OSI licence, automated tests, installation documentation and a public repository — of which this project currently has the tests and nothing else. Submitting before the licence and the git history exist would fail review at the editorial pre-check.

evidence.citation: Wilkinson MD, Dumontier M, Aalbersberg IJ, et al. The FAIR Guiding Principles for scientific data management and stewardship. Sci Data 3:160018 (2016). doi:10.1038/sdata.2016.18
evidence.supports: Defines F1 (globally unique persistent identifiers), I1 (a formal, accessible, shared knowledge representation), and R1.1 (a clear, accessible data usage licence) — the three the repository currently fails, and the three this proposal targets. DOI verified live via Crossref this session.

evidence.citation: Soiland-Reyes S, Sefton P, Crosas M, et al. Packaging research artefacts with RO-Crate. Data Science 5(2):97-138 (2022). doi:10.3233/DS-210053
evidence.supports: The specification for the packaging format proposed here. Spec 1.1 confirmed live at https://www.researchobject.org/ro-crate/specification/1.1/ (HTTP 200 this session). DOI verified via Crossref.

evidence.citation: Leo S, Crusoe MR, Rodríguez-Navas L, et al. Recording provenance of workflow runs with RO-Crate. PLOS ONE 19(9):e0309210 (2024). doi:10.1371/journal.pone.0309210
evidence.supports: Defines the Process Run Crate / Workflow Run Crate / Provenance Run Crate profiles at exactly the granularity the existing RUN/ARTIFACT ledger already records, so the mapping is vocabulary substitution rather than new instrumentation. DOI verified live via Crossref this session.

evidence.citation: W3C PROV-O: The PROV Ontology, W3C Recommendation 30 April 2013 — https://www.w3.org/TR/prov-o/
evidence.supports: Supplies prov:Activity, prov:Entity, prov:SoftwareAgent, prov:wasDerivedFrom, prov:hadPrimarySource and prov:wasInvalidatedBy — the last being the correct predicate for this project's retracted claims, which no tabular export can represent. URL confirmed live (HTTP 200) this session. A W3C Recommendation has no DOI.

evidence.citation: Smith AM, Katz DS, Niemeyer KE; FORCE11 Software Citation Working Group. Software citation principles. PeerJ Comput Sci 2:e86 (2016). doi:10.7717/peerj-cs.86
evidence.supports: Grounds the CITATION.cff / codemeta / versioned-DOI requirement: software must be citable with a persistent identifier and a specific version, which is a precondition for the JOSS route named in the method. DOI verified live via Crossref this session.

evidence.citation: Zdrazil B, Felix E, Hunter F, et al. The ChEMBL Database in 2023. Nucleic Acids Res 52:D1180 (2024). doi:10.1093/nar/gkad1004
evidence.supports: Documents ChEMBL's versioned-snapshot release model and licensing, which is why data/corpus_ACHE.json needs both a resolvable per-compound IRI and an explicit statement of the inherited data licence it currently omits. DOI verified live via Crossref this session.

ideas.effort: 3-4 days. Pure Python plus rdflib and a CFF/RO-Crate validator; no GPU, no network dependency at build time (IRI resolution is a cached, scheduled check). The heaviest part is modelling decisions, not code.
success_criteria: `ro-crate-metadata.json` validates cleanly against the RO-Crate 1.1 specification with `rocrate-validator`, and declares a Process Run Crate entry for every RUN record in the ledger.

A PROV-O JSON-LD/Turtle export loads in rdflib, and a single SPARQL query of the form `?value prov:wasGeneratedBy ?act . ?act prov:used ?in . ?act prov:wasAssociatedWith ?agent` returns a complete, non-empty chain for the pLDDT of a named candidate.

100% of Values with status DATABASE or LITERATURE carry a `source_iri`, and a sampled resolution check returns HTTP 200 for every one; a deliberately malformed accession makes verify_all.py exit non-zero.
Every entry in `retracted_claims` appears in the export with `prov:wasInvalidatedBy`, and every NOT_COMPUTED field appears with its machine-readable reason rather than as a null.

`CITATION.cff` parses with `cffconvert`; LICENSE files exist for code and data; the ChEMBL CC-BY-SA inheritance is stated in the crate metadata for data/corpus_ACHE.json; a tagged release resolves to a Zenodo DOI.
risks: PROV-O has no canonical pattern for 'this value was deliberately not computed, for this reason'. A documented local extension is required, and over-modelling is the standard trap of provenance projects — the export must stay small enough that someone actually queries it.

A crate that is generated once and then drifts from the repository is worse than none. It must be regenerated by verify_all.py on every run and its hash checked, or it becomes another unverified assertion of exactly the kind META-1 exists to catch.

Minting a public DOI publishes the project's history including the fabricated original. That is the right choice and should be foregrounded in the crate description, but it is an irreversible disclosure decision the author must make deliberately, not as a side effect of a release script.

IRI resolution introduces a network dependency into a validation gate. Mitigate by caching and scheduling it weekly rather than per-commit, otherwise an EBI outage turns into a failing build and the check gets disabled.
ideas.why_now: The ledger's value decays the longer it stays in a private, undocumented, unlicensed format: 803 claims that only their author can interpret are not evidence to anyone else. Doing the export now, while the schema is fresh and the mapping is mechanical, costs days; doing it after another few hundred records and a schema change costs weeks. It also unblocks the publication route — Zenodo, preprint, and eventually JOSS all require the licence and the citable versioned artifact that this idea produces, and none of them will accept the repository in its present untracked, unlicensed state.

ideas.title: Hash-locked pre-specification with a criterion-exercise audit, instantiated on the AChE affinity benchmark
ideas.one_line: Add a protocol format that is sha256-frozen into the ledger before any result is written, whose runner refuses to publish if the protocol changed after data collection and flags any declared criterion that rejected zero records — then use it to run the first pre-registered, outcome-neutral evaluation of the Boltz-2 affinity head against the 18-compound AChE corpus.
ideas.scientific_rationale:
Two separate failures, one mechanism.

First, stated protocol and executed protocol have already diverged, and 215 passing checks did not notice. `data/corpus_ACHE.json` advertises `min_assay_confidence: 8` and a summary reading 'assay confidence >= 8, ... from an assay ChEMBL scores as directly assigned to a single protein'. The implementing filter is `platform/cbc/corpus.py:204-206`: `conf = a.get("confidence_score")` on records from ChEMBL's `/activity` endpoint. I queried that endpoint live this session: its field list contains no `confidence_score` at all — the attribute lives on `/assay` (`/assay/CHEMBL636834` returns `confidence_score: 8`). So `conf` is always None, the guard `if conf is not None and conf < ...` never fires, and the criterion has never rejected a single record. The evidence is visible in the emitted file: every activity carries `assay_confidence: null`, and the `denominator.rejected` object has buckets for unparseable/tier_excluded/no_structure/too_large but no low-confidence bucket whatsoever. A second, subtler mismatch sits on top: ChEMBL confidence 8 means *homologous* single protein target assigned, not *direct* — direct is 9 — so even the prose overstates the threshold it names. The platform's central methodological asset is 'an executable InclusionProtocol with a stated denominator'. One of its criteria is decorative.

Second, the affinity result is n=1 and post hoc. Boltz-2's affinity head predicted 1274 nM for huperzine A against AChE where ChEMBL measures 5.0 nM — 2.41 log units, with `affinity_probability_binary` 0.44. Nobody can say whether that is typical, unusually bad, or unusually good, and no criterion for 'acceptable' was written down before the number was seen. A project whose entire premise is that unearned numbers must not be displayed cannot leave its own predictor's error bar as a single anecdote and still decide, after the fact, whether to display its outputs.

The mechanism that fixes both is the same: a protocol that is frozen before execution, and that is required to demonstrate each of its criteria actually did work.
ideas.what_it_answers: "Is the platform's own affinity predictor accurate enough to report at all, with what error bar, judged against a threshold set before the results were seen?" And structurally: "for any protocol this platform states, did the code actually execute every criterion the protocol claims — or did some of them silently never fire?" The second is not hypothetical; it is currently false for the AChE corpus and undetected.
ideas.method:
1. `protocols/<name>.yaml` — a pre-specification carrying: population and inclusion criteria, each criterion naming the exact field AND the exact endpoint it is read from; the database release identifier (`chembl_37`, confirmed live as the current release via the EBI FTP `latest` directory — data/corpus_ACHE.json today records no release, no retrieval timestamp, and no query URL, so its denominator of 258 examined / 18 admitted is not reproducible against a moving database); the primary and secondary outcome metrics; the analysis; and an outcome-neutral decision rule.
2. `platform/prespec.py`: `freeze <protocol>` writes a `PRESPEC` record (protocol sha256 + UTC timestamp) to the existing append-only ledger. `run <protocol>` recomputes the hash, refuses to write results if it changed after the PRESPEC timestamp, and stamps every result record with the protocol hash. `verify` asserts the PRESPEC timestamp strictly precedes every result record for that protocol. This reuses the ledger's existing append-only guarantees rather than inventing a registry.
3. The criterion-exercise audit — the general fix for the confidence-8 bug. The runner emits a per-criterion rejection count. Any criterion with a count of zero over N>=50 examined records is reported as `NOT_EXERCISED` and fails the gate, with a message naming the field and endpoint it claimed to read. Applied to the current corpus this fails immediately and correctly. Fix the underlying bug by joining `/assay` records to fetch real `confidence_score`, and reconcile the prose to what 8 actually means (or raise it to 9 and accept the smaller corpus).
4. First instance, `affinity-ache-v1`, frozen before running: all compounds admitted from data/corpus_ACHE.json against human AChE (P22303, mature chain) via the Boltz-2 affinity head, msa=empty, fixed recorded seed (META-1); primary metric mean absolute error in log10 IC50 with a bootstrap 95% CI, secondary Spearman rho; a pre-declared aggregation rule for replicate measurements — necessary because ChEMBL already gives conflicting potencies for the same pair (neostigmine bromide appears at IC50 22 nM and 2.0 nM in different assays in the current file), and choosing that rule after seeing model output would be a degree of freedom; and a pre-declared decision rule of the form 'Boltz-2 affinity outputs will be reported as PREDICTED only if the 95% CI upper bound on MAE is below X log units and rho exceeds Y; otherwise the field remains NOT_COMPUTED and the negative result is published'. Declare the training-contamination caveat in the protocol *before* running: Boltz-2's affinity head is trained on ChEMBL-derived data, so these compounds are plausibly in-training and the MAE is an optimistic bound measuring partial memorization — state the model's data cutoff and report the benchmark as a ceiling, not an estimate.
5. Continuous validation: a scheduled job re-running the frozen protocol against live ChEMBL, recording the release, and reporting any change in the admitted set or in the reference potencies — converting the corpus from a snapshot of unknown vintage into a monitored one, and detecting when a published number's underlying measurement has been revised or withdrawn upstream.

evidence.citation: Chambers CD, Tzavella L. The past, present and future of Registered Reports. Nat Hum Behav 6:29-42 (2022). doi:10.1038/s41562-021-01193-7
evidence.supports: The evidence base for pre-specification as a mechanism against outcome-contingent analysis, and the requirement that the decision rule be outcome-neutral and time-stamped prior to data collection — which is what the PRESPEC ledger record implements. DOI verified live via Crossref this session.

evidence.citation: Ackloo S, Al-Awar R, Amaro RE, et al. CACHE (Critical Assessment of Computational Hit-finding Experiments): a public-private partnership benchmarking initiative. Nat Rev Chem 6:287-295 (2022). doi:10.1038/s41570-022-00363-z
evidence.supports: The domain-appropriate precedent: hit-finding methods are assessed by declaring predictions before the reference data are consulted, with the protocol and full result set published regardless of outcome. Establishes that pre-declared, outcome-neutral evaluation is the field's own standard, not an import from psychology. DOI verified live via Crossref this session.

evidence.citation: Bender A, Cortés-Ciriano I. Artificial intelligence in drug discovery: what is realistic, what are illusions? Part 1. Drug Discov Today 26(2):511-524 (2021). doi:10.1016/j.drudis.2020.12.009
evidence.supports: Documents the specific failure modes this pre-spec must guard against — training-set contamination inflating retrospective benchmarks, and metric selection after the fact — which is why the contamination caveat and the aggregation rule must be frozen before the run. DOI verified live via Crossref this session.

evidence.citation: Passaro S, Corso G, Wohlwend J, et al. Boltz-2: Towards Accurate and Efficient Binding Affinity Prediction. bioRxiv 2025.06.14.659707 (2025). doi:10.1101/2025.06.14.659707
evidence.supports: The affinity head under test and its reported performance envelope, against which the platform's locally measured MAE should be compared. Retrieved live from the bioRxiv API this session.

ideas.effort: ~2 days for the protocol format, the freeze/verify commands against the existing ledger, and the criterion-exercise audit; plus the corpus re-fetch with a proper /assay join. The benchmark itself is the cost: 18 complexes of a 543-residue receptor plus ligand through Boltz-2 on MPS is hours to overnight, unattended. No GPU cluster, no wet lab, no paid API.
success_criteria: A `PRESPEC` record for affinity-ache-v1 exists in the ledger with a UTC timestamp strictly earlier than every result record bearing that protocol hash, and `prespec verify` proves it.
Tamper test: editing protocols/affinity-ache-v1.yaml after freezing makes `prespec run` refuse to write results and exit non-zero.

The criterion-exercise audit flags `min_assay_confidence` as NOT_EXERCISED on the current corpus; after the /assay join it reports a non-zero rejection count, or the criterion is removed from the protocol rather than left in as decoration.

data/corpus_ACHE.json is re-emitted carrying `chembl_release: chembl_37`, a retrieval UTC timestamp, and the verbatim query URLs, and the protocol prose is reconciled with what confidence 8 actually denotes.

The AChE benchmark is published with MAE, a bootstrap 95% CI, Spearman rho, the per-compound table, and the training-contamination caveat — whichever way the numbers fall — and the affinity field's provenance status is set by the pre-declared rule rather than by preference.
The scheduled re-run reports zero drift, or reports drift with a diff, on at least two consecutive weekly executions.
risks: n=18 gives a wide confidence interval, and fixing the confidence filter may shrink the admitted set further. The correct response is to report the width, not to widen the inclusion criteria after seeing it — but that temptation is real and the pre-spec must forbid it explicitly.

Training contamination may make the MAE an optimistic ceiling that measures memorization rather than generalization. This must be declared up front, with the model's data cutoff stated; without that declaration the benchmark is misleading even if every number in it is honest.

Overnight MPS runs on a 543-residue receptor may hit memory or time limits; a fallback of a truncated construct would change the science and must be pre-declared as an alternative arm rather than substituted mid-run.

Pre-specification bureaucracy can ossify a one-person project. Keep it to one YAML and two commands, and apply it only to evaluative claims — not to exploratory work, which should be labelled exploratory rather than dressed as confirmatory.
ideas.why_now: The corpus bug is live, undetected, and load-bearing: the InclusionProtocol with its stated denominator is the methodological centrepiece the rebuild advertises, and one of its criteria has never executed. That is precisely the kind of gap the 12-discipline panel was convened to find, and it survived. Fixing this one instance by hand teaches nothing; building the audit that finds this class automatically means the next silently-dead criterion fails the gate instead of shipping. And the affinity decision cannot be deferred: the platform will otherwise have to choose, at some point, whether to display Boltz-2 affinity numbers — and if that choice is made after the benchmark is seen, it is exactly the post-hoc reasoning that produced the original fabricated dataset, only better dressed.

critiques.critic: ML for structural biology (AlphaFold-class model training and evaluation; NeurIPS / Nature Methods reviewer). Cross-cutting: (1) three proposals (AIML-STRUCT-1, AIML-BENCH-3, STRUCTBIO-IDEA-3) build near-identical scramble/decoy pipelines and two (AIML-BENCH-1, CBC-CC-1) build near-identical affinity benchmarks — ship one of each. (2) AIML-STRUCT-3 is a hard prerequisite for almost everything else: with a measured across-seed ipTM sd of 0.133, every single-seed comparison in STRUCT-1, BENCH-3, CC-3 and STRUCTBIO-1 is reporting sampling noise. Do it first. (3) MEDCHEM-IDEA-2 shows the 2.41 log10 huperzine anchor is an artefact of single-value ground truth; three proposals quote it as motivation and must stop. (4) I verified the Boltz-2 PDB cutoff is 2023-06-01 and the affinity head trained on ChEMBL+BindingDB+PDBbind+MF-PCBA — this makes STRUCTBIO-IDEA-2 a memorisation readout and makes AIML-BENCH-1's ChEMBL-only leakage audit a lower bound. Skipped as outside competence: GENO-A/B/C, DMPK-IDEA-1/2/3, MEDCHEM-IDEA-1/3, META-2.

critiques.scientific_objection: Three defects. (a) The empirical p is invalid as specified: the native statistic is a median over 5 seeds while each decoy is a single seed, so the null distribution carries the full within-sequence sampling variance (measured sd 0.133 on a 0-1 metric) while the test statistic does not. The two are not exchangeable and the permutation logic requires exchangeability. (b) The scramble is not composition-matched in the property that governs these molecules. MW, net charge, pI and GRAVY are order-invariant and are preserved, but hydrophobic moment and helical amphipathic periodicity are order-DEPENDENT and are destroyed by a Fisher-Yates shuffle. So the test as built asks 'does amphipathic helicity matter', not 'is this specific design sequence-specific' — a positive result would be uninterpretable. (c) With K=20 decoys the minimum attainable p is 1/21 = 0.048; across 35 candidates with no multiplicity control you expect ~1.7 spurious hits at alpha=0.05 and no candidate can survive any correction. The pilot itself is oversold: 3 native vs 3 decoy replicates has a p-value floor of 0.25, so 'empirical p = 1.0' is suggestive, not 'decisive'. Separately, re-deriving the PAE-asymmetry threshold 'from real two-chain output' risks tuning the sanity check to accept whatever Boltz emits; it must be derived from a set containing known-good AND known-bad matrices.
critiques.feasibility_objection: The compute estimate is roughly half of what the design costs. 35 candidates x 26 runs = 910 complex predictions; the session's own measurement is 3 min 4 s for hAChE (543 aa) + a small ligand, and peptide+receptor complexes at 580-1100 tokens will be at or above that. 910 x ~3 min is ~46 h, not 24 h, and the larger receptors (TLR4+MD-2, full AChE) scale worse than linearly in the pair representation. Using the recorded domain_boundaries mitigates this but the budget should be restated.
critiques.improvement: Make it a paired design: run the native and every decoy at the SAME fixed seed set (>=3 seeds each), and compute the statistic on seed-matched means so the null and the test statistic have identical sampling variance; report the seed variance component separately. Size K by the claim you intend to make — K=20 is sufficient to publish 'the design lies inside its decoy distribution' (the outcome the pilot predicts), but a positive sequence-specificity claim surviving correction across 35 candidates needs K>=200, so pre-declare which candidates, if any, are eligible for a positive claim and cap that family at 3-5. Add a second null that holds the hydrophobic moment fixed (permute residues within hydrophobic and within polar classes, preserving heptad periodicity) so 'this design' is separated from 'any amphipathic helix of this composition'; DMPK-IDEA-3 already has the modlAMP moment machinery to construct it. Derive the PAE-asymmetry threshold from a labelled set of genuine two-chain predictor output plus deliberately synthetic matrices, and report the false-positive and false-negative rate of the new threshold rather than just the cutoff.

critiques.scientific_objection: The leakage control is a date filter plus an INTERNAL dedup, which is not sufficient. Boltz-2's PDB training cutoff is 2023-06-01 (verified this session against the Boltz-2 preprint, 10.1101/2025.06.14.659707), but a post-cutoff deposition is routinely a new peptide on a receptor whose fold, and often whose close homologue-in-complex, is in the training set. The proposed 30-40% dedup is between benchmark members, not between each benchmark member and the pre-cutoff PDB. Without the latter the curve measures interpolation for an unknown fraction of the set. Second, the statistics are underpowered as specified: n~100 spread over ~5 ipTM bins gives ~20 per bin and Wilson half-widths near 0.2, and expected calibration error on 100 points is dominated by binning choice, not by miscalibration. Third — and this is the one that matters for the platform's actual use — the applicability-domain guard is on the wrong axis. Refusing to extrapolate outside populated ipTM bins does not protect against the real shift, which is from natural 5-40mer peptide complexes to 26-100 residue designed polycationic chimeras. An ipTM of 0.35 can be well-populated in the benchmark and still mean something different for a synthetic Arg/Trp amphipath. Fourth, if each calibration point is a single unseeded sample the curve absorbs the 0.133 sd of sampler noise into what is presented as model calibration.
critiques.feasibility_objection: Compute is fine (100 complexes at 1-3 min; even 300 is ~10 h overnight). Two unvalidated steps are flagged honestly by the author: the RCSB server-side clustering call returned HTTP 400, and mmseqs2 on macOS arm64 has not been demonstrated here. Budget a day for the dedup path alone, and have a fallback (CD-HIT via bioconda, or an all-vs-all Smith-Waterman over ~1100 receptor sequences, which is trivial at this scale).
critiques.improvement: Filter every holdout entry against the complete pre-2023-06-01 PDB (mmseqs2 or blastp against pdb_seqres restricted by release date) on BOTH the receptor and the peptide, and report all headline metrics stratified by max identity to pre-cutoff (<30% / 30-70% / >70%) — the >70% stratum is your memorisation control and its existence is itself a publishable number. Raise n to >=300 (still one overnight batch) and replace binned proportions + ECE with an isotonic or logistic fit of P(DockQ>=0.23 | ipTM) with a bootstrap band, reporting binned points only as a visual overlay. Run every calibration point at the exact STRUCT-3 configuration (fixed seed, declared diffusion_samples, declared top-1 selection rule) so the curve is a property of a reproducible pipeline. Finally, add a second applicability axis to the refusal logic: peptide length and predicted disorder-in-isolation, and state in the artefact that the curve is an upper bound on reliability for the designed candidates because none of them is in the calibration domain.

critiques.scientific_objection: The science is right and this should be built first, but three specifics are wrong. (a) 'byte-reproducible on a second execution' will not hold on MPS. Torch's MPS backend has non-deterministic reduction ordering, and the proposal itself notes aten::linalg_svd falls back to CPU inside the diffusion loss — a fixed seed fixes the noise draw, not the floating-point trajectory. Setting byte-reproducibility as a success criterion guarantees either a failed criterion or a quiet redefinition of it. (b) Variance components are conflated. With diffusion_samples=5 and 5 seeds there are two nested sources: sample-within-seed and between-seed. The number written into Provenance.uncertainty must be the sd of the REPORTED statistic under a declared selection rule (e.g. top-ranked of 5), not the sd of all 25 outputs, and the selection rule is never stated. (c) The justification for keeping the peptide MSA empty is factually wrong for these molecules: dataset.json motif_provenance records 16 motifs with exact_match true against UniProt accessions, so the parent motifs demonstrably do have homologues and the MMseqs2 server will return them. Whether that helps or misleads is an empirical question, and asserting it is exactly the move this project exists to stop. Finally, an across-seed sd is a repeatability figure, not an accuracy interval; if it lands in a field called 'uncertainty' next to a pLDDT, readers will read it as an error bar on correctness.
critiques.feasibility_objection: None material. ~8 pairs x 2 MSA x 5 seeds at diffusion_samples=5 is comfortably an overnight run, the MSA fetch is 16 network calls, and the code changes are a handful of CLI passthroughs plus fixing _collect_boltz_outputs (structure.py:220), which currently discards every model beyond sorted(...)[0].
critiques.improvement: Replace the byte-reproducibility criterion with a measured one: run the same seed twice and report max per-atom coordinate deviation and |delta ipTM| / |delta pLDDT|, then declare a numerical tolerance derived from that measurement — and state that MPS non-determinism, not the sampler, is the residual. Declare the sample-selection rule (top-1 of N by confidence_score) in the protocol before running, and report a two-level variance decomposition: sigma_seed and sigma_sample|seed, with the provenance uncertainty set to sigma of the selected statistic across seeds and labelled 'run-to-run repeatability (not accuracy)'. Add a third MSA arm on a subset — receptor a3m + peptide a3m — since the motifs have real homologues; if the peptide MSA changes ipTM materially, that is a finding, and if it does not, the msa=empty choice becomes measured rather than asserted. Keep the Huperzine A retest, but score it against the endpoint-class aggregate from MEDCHEM-IDEA-2 rather than the single 5.0 nM value, otherwise you will be retesting a broken reference.

critiques.scientific_objection: The leakage audit is scoped too narrowly to be the estimate it claims. I verified this session that the Boltz-2 affinity head was trained on ~3M records aligned from ChEMBL, BindingDB, PDBbind AND MF-PCBA. A per-compound 'in_pre_cutoff_chembl' flag therefore measures one of four training sources and will systematically understate contamination; the ECFP4 nearest-neighbour distance to pre-cutoff ChEMBL has the same defect. Second, a single-target (AChE) design cannot separate the two things a calibration is for: within-target ranking and cross-target level. With one receptor, every test point shares the protein with training data, so the only leakage axis you can even measure is the ligand, and the per-target-mean null becomes the only admissible baseline. Third, power: at n=17-18 with a null RMSE of 1.644, the BCa CI on a paired delta will span zero for any plausible model, and the pre-declared 'not distinguishable from the null' string will fire because of n, not because of the model — a true statement that says nothing about Boltz-2. Fourth, the 2.41 log anchor used as motivation is contaminated by the single-value ground-truth defect that MEDCHEM-IDEA-2 documents.
critiques.feasibility_objection: The 200-complex / ~10 h estimate is credible given the measured 3 min 4 s for hAChE + ligand. The unbudgeted item is the Landrum-Riniker curation and the assay-metadata join, which requires the /assay endpoint fix (corpus.py:204-206 reads confidence_score off /activity, where the field does not exist — I confirmed all 27 activities in data/corpus_ACHE.json carry assay_confidence null). That is a prerequisite, not a side task.
critiques.improvement: Merge with CBC-CC-1 into one multi-target affinity benchmark: >=4 targets, >=50 compounds per target, so within-target Spearman and cross-target level are separately estimable and the paired-delta test has power. State the minimum detectable effect up front (given sigma_exp ~0.38-0.68 log and the null at 1.64, compute the n needed to resolve a 0.4 log improvement at 80% power) and treat an underpowered result as 'inconclusive', distinct from 'not better than null'. Extend the leakage fields from one to four: in_pre_cutoff_chembl, in_bindingdb, in_pdbbind, in_mf_pcba, plus max ECFP4 Tanimoto to the union — and where a source cannot be checked, record the membership as UNKNOWN rather than false. Restrict the primary analysis to a single endpoint class (catalytic Ellman IC50) per MEDCHEM-IDEA-2, and drop the 2.41 figure from the rationale in favour of the class aggregate.

critiques.scientific_objection: The temporal holdout is not the generalisation test it is presented as. The 81 post-2023-06-01 entries are selected by mapping to the platform's own cognition UniProt set (P22303, P06276, P27338, P21397, P56817, ...) — precisely the receptors with the densest pre-cutoff holo coverage in the PDB. A 2024 donepezil analogue bound to hAChE is a near neighbour of dozens of training complexes on both the protein and the ligand axis; the pipeline can score well by interpolation and the proposal reports that as post-cutoff accuracy. The recall set is correctly labelled; the holdout is not, and the two sets differ less than the framing implies. Second, running the benchmark only at msa=empty confounds pose error with receptor-fold error: AChE, MAO-B and BACE1 have deep MSAs and single-sequence mode degrades the receptor, so a failed pose may be a failed receptor. Third, AUROC of ipTM for RMSD<=2 A at n~40-80 with likely strong class imbalance will have a CI wide enough that 'includes 0.5' is the probable outcome for reasons of n; the stated consequence (stop displaying the score) should not be triggered by an underpowered test.
critiques.feasibility_objection: Genuinely low risk and the best value-per-hour on the slate. posebusters 0.6.5 and spyrmsd 0.9.0 are pure-Python wheels, the 4EY5 first data point needs no inference at all, and 3 min/complex x ~100 is one overnight batch. The only real work is the predictor.py ligand-parsing change, which is a defect fix regardless.
critiques.improvement: Add a third, target-disjoint arm drawn from the general post-cutoff PDB (protein + non-polymer, <=2.5 A, receptor <40% identity to any pre-cutoff chain) and report it alongside the cognition-target holdout; the gap between the two is the interpolation premium and is itself the most interesting number in the study. For every holdout ligand compute max ECFP4 Tanimoto to any ligand bound to the same UniProt in a pre-cutoff entry and stratify the RMSD<=2 A and PB-valid proportions by it. Run the holdout in both msa=empty and receptor-MSA conditions so pose error is not confounded with receptor degradation. Pre-compute the n required for the AUROC CI to exclude 0.5 under a plausible effect, and if the set cannot reach it, report the AUROC with its CI and state 'underpowered' rather than issuing a verdict on whether ipTM is a quality indicator.

critiques.scientific_objection: The design cannot produce a positive result, whatever the data. K=20 controls gives a minimum attainable permutation p of 1/21 = 0.0476. Holm-Bonferroni across 10 candidates requires the smallest p to be <= 0.05/10 = 0.005. Therefore no candidate can ever be declared 'sequence-specific (Holm-corrected p < 0.05)', and the stated verdict string is unreachable by construction — the mirror image of a check designed to pass. This is arithmetic, not judgement. Second, the same seed-exchangeability defect as AIML-STRUCT-1: with the measured within-sequence ipTM sd of 0.133, single-seed design and single-seed controls make the standardised effect size (design - mean(controls))/sd(controls) dominated by sampler noise, and sd(controls) will absorb that noise, deflating every effect size. Third, 'MW, net charge, pI and GRAVY carry literally zero design information' is overstated: they are invariant to residue ORDER, which is a narrower and correct claim. Composition is a design choice and those descriptors do discriminate between candidates; what they cannot support is any claim that depends on motif arrangement.
critiques.feasibility_objection: 210 runs at ~3 min is ~11 h and credible. But the K needed to make the stated verdict attainable (>=200 per candidate to clear Holm at 10 tests) is 2000+ runs, roughly 100 h, which is not credible as scoped. The proposal's own success criteria and its compute budget are inconsistent.
critiques.improvement: Merge into AIML-STRUCT-1 — the three control types are this proposal's real and unique contribution and STRUCT-1 lacks them: the linker-preserving shuffle isolates motif-internal order, and the motif-block permutation isolates the arrangement hypothesis, which is the actual design claim these constructs make. Keep all three. Then fix the statistics: either (i) abandon per-candidate significance and report, for each candidate, the seed-matched standardised effect size with a bootstrap CI plus the full null distribution, applying no multiplicity correction because no dichotomous claim is being made; or (ii) restrict the significance-testing family to <=3 pre-declared candidates and run K>=200 for those only. Run design and controls at the same >=3 seeds. Reword the composition claim to 'order-invariant, therefore cannot evidence any motif-arrangement hypothesis' and tag the fields accordingly.

critiques.scientific_objection: Three issues. (a) The decoy arm is too easy to be informative: scoring each ligand against three UNRELATED receptors from the registry (e.g. an AChE inhibitor against TREM2 or FZD8) gives a discrimination task that any competent model solves, and the resulting AUROC will be high and meaningless. The operative question for a cholinesterase programme is whether the model separates AChE from BuChE, and whether it separates a real binder from a property-matched non-binder — neither is tested.
