(b) Leakage is not addressed at all, yet this is the same measurement AIML-BENCH-1 is built around and I confirmed the affinity head trained on ChEMBL+BindingDB+PDBbind+MF-PCBA; the corpus is fetched live from ChEMBL by corpus.py, so a large fraction of the >=60 pairs are plausibly in-training. Without a leakage label the measured RMSE is an optimistic bound, and writing that bound into thermo.METHOD_ACCURACY institutionalises it. (c) >=60 pairs over >=4 targets is 15 per target; the within-target Spearman CI at n=15 is roughly +/-0.5, so the within-target ranking claim — the one that actually matters for screening — will be unresolvable.
critiques.feasibility_objection: 200-300 unattended MPS runs in 2-4 days is realistic on the measured 3 min/complex. The unbudgeted item is extending the InclusionProtocol to GSK3B, KEAP1, CHRM1 and NOS3, which requires the /assay confidence join to be fixed first (verified: min_assay_confidence=8 currently rejects nothing, and the denominator object has no low-confidence bucket).
critiques.improvement: Merge with AIML-BENCH-1 — one affinity benchmark, one protocol, one leakage audit. Raise to >=50 compounds per target on >=4 targets so within-target rho is estimable, and state the minimum detectable rho at the achieved n. Replace the unrelated-receptor decoys with two harder arms: a close-paralog arm (BuChE, CHRM subtypes) and a property-matched decoy-ligand arm (matched MW/logP/HBD/charge, no measured activity on that target); report AUROC for each separately and treat the unrelated-receptor number as a sanity floor, not a result. Make the thermo.METHOD_ACCURACY key encode its applicability domain in the key itself — target set, msa mode, heavy-atom range, leakage stratum — so it cannot be silently reused outside the regime it was measured in, and add a verify_all.py check that any PREDICTED binding_free_energy names the stratum it was calibrated against.

critiques.scientific_objection: Step 3 is mislabelled and step 4(b) is unspecified. Reproducing r = -0.73 / RMSE 1.89 kcal/mol on the eLife benchmark is not a validation — that is the set the PRODIGY regression coefficients were derived on, so recovering the number confirms the wiring and nothing about generalisation. It must be labelled a wiring check, and the transfer estimate must come from complexes outside the derivation set. More seriously, the protein-peptide arm is the load-bearing one — it is the arm that determines whether the pre-registered 2.0 kcal/mol gate is applied to a real estimate — and it is specified only as 'repeat on a protein-peptide structure+affinity set', naming no set and no n. Protein-peptide complexes with both a structure and a direct-method affinity are scarce; if that arm lands at n<30, the two peptide cells of the four-cell table will have CIs wide enough that the gate decision is arbitrary. Third, PRODIGY is essentially a monotone function of interfacial contact count, so it will emit a plausible-looking dG for a model whose minimum interface PAE is ~17 A — i.e. for a model with no interface at all. That is the strongest argument for the gate, and it also means the primary deliverable should be RMSE as a function of ipTM/interface-PAE bin, not the four-cell summary.
critiques.feasibility_objection: '~1 week' is optimistic by a factor of two or more. Step 4(a) requires co-folding the Kastritis benchmark subset — real protein-protein complexes, many well above 600 total residues, where the pair representation cost is far worse than the 543-residue AChE case timed at 2 min 21 s. Eighty to 144 such complexes on MPS is multi-day of pure compute before any analysis, and some may not fit in memory at all. Time three of the largest before committing.
critiques.improvement: Relabel step 3 as a wiring check and add an independent protein-protein affinity set (post-dating the PRODIGY derivation) for the actual crystal-PP transfer estimate. Name the protein-peptide set and its n BEFORE freezing the protocol — filter PDBbind or a curated peptide-affinity set to entries with ITC/SPR/stopped-flow determinations and report the count; if n<30, state that the peptide transfer is unmeasurable at this scale and that binding_free_energy stays not_computed for that reason alone, which is still a defensible measured refusal. Make 'RMSE and Spearman rho as a function of ipTM bin and of minimum interface PAE bin' the primary figure, since that is the quantity that tells a reader when, if ever, a contacts-based dG on a predicted structure is admissible. Run a size pilot on the three largest Kastritis complexes before committing the batch.

critiques.scientific_objection: The headline measurement would report sampler noise as chemical uncertainty. The deliverable is min/median/max of ipTM across isomers, but each isomer is folded once, while the same-sequence across-seed sd was measured at 0.133 on a 0-1 metric in this very session. For 15 isomers of a 6-Cys candidate, the max-minus-min of 15 single-seed draws from a distribution with sd 0.133 has an expected range of roughly 0.45 purely from seeding — comparable to or larger than any plausible connectivity effect. The spread would then be combined in quadrature with the method RMSE and presented as irreducible chemical indeterminacy. That is a number without knowledge, and it is the same error class the project already fixed once. Second, the OpenMM filter's decision rule — 'interface survives vs dissolves' — is not defined, and Amber14/GBn2 implicit solvent is a poor model for exactly this molecule class: no explicit ionic screening, well-documented over-stabilisation of salt bridges, and these are 26-100 residue polycations with net charge up to +8.4. Third, 'disulfide_connectivity moves to COMPUTED' is a provenance-status error: a connectivity inferred from a diffusion model's coordinates is PREDICTED, not COMPUTED; and gating it on agreement with the parent motif's published pattern makes the output partly an assumption rather than a measurement.
critiques.feasibility_objection: The scope is well beyond the stated 1-1.5 weeks once the seeding fix is applied. Eight to ten candidates x (3 to 15 enumerated, or ~16 sampled for 8-Cys) x >=3 seeds is 400-500 complex folds plus 100-150 MD systems. The SG-SG bond constraint may also not be supported — the author flags honestly that the Boltz docs confirm bond constraints only for CCD ligands and canonical residues without confirming intra-chain SG-SG, and if it fails the whole enforcement path has to be rebuilt in the relaxation stage.
critiques.improvement: Scope to the seven candidates with exactly 4 or 6 cysteines (3 and 15 enumerable pairings, no sampling), run every isomer at >=3 shared seeds, and make the primary statistic a variance decomposition — sigma_isomer versus sigma_seed, with an intraclass correlation and a CI — rather than a min/median/max range. If sigma_isomer is not resolvable above sigma_seed, publish that: 'connectivity indeterminacy is not detectable above sampler noise at this n' is a real and useful result and costs the same compute. Pre-register the OpenMM pass/fail criterion quantitatively (e.g. fraction of initial interface heavy-atom contacts retained above X over Y ns) and validate it on a solved disulfide-rich complex as positive control and a scrambled complex as negative control before applying it to any candidate; state the GBn2 limitation for polycations in the applicability field. Emit disulfide_connectivity as PREDICTED, and report parent-motif agreement as a separate concordance field rather than as a precondition for emitting the value. Verify the SG-SG constraint first — that is a half-day gate on the whole plan.

critiques.scientific_objection: The finding is real and the trivalent-sulfur cases are a genuine chemical impossibility that no confidence metric reports — that should be the lead. Three corrections. (a) The reference distribution is proposed from deposited structures at ~2.0-2.5 A, where S-S distance, chi3 and the N-CA-C-CB improper are all RESTRAINED during refinement by the monomer-library targets. A tolerance derived from them measures agreement with a restraint dictionary, not an independent empirical distribution, and the resulting check should be described as 'consistent with crystallographic restraint targets'. The measured 4EY7 S-S range of 2.031-2.064 A is suspiciously tight for exactly this reason. (b) Violations are reported as marginals but must be conditioned on local pLDDT: an eclipsed chi3 inside a pLDDT-45 loop is the model declining to commit, not a claim that the molecule is impossible. The genuinely interesting result — PfcACh-PAM-P1 carrying a 1.705 A S-S with no confidence flag — is a statement about the JOINT distribution, and that joint table should be the deliverable. (c) All 22 mmCIFs were produced unseeded at diffusion_samples=1, so every per-candidate violation is a single draw; candidate-level claims ('these four candidates have trivalent sulfur') need the check re-run across >=3 seeds before they enter the dataset.
critiques.feasibility_objection: None. gemmi 0.6.5 is already in .venv312, the 22 mmCIFs exist, the analysis ran in under a second, and the reference download is minutes. Two days is if anything generous. The /tmp durability fix (compare_real_vs_hardcoded.py:39 sets WORK = Path('/tmp/cbc_boltz')) is urgent and independently worth doing today.
critiques.improvement: Build the reference distribution from structures at <=1.2 A resolution where restraint weighting is low, and state explicitly that the check tests refinement-plausibility rather than physical ground truth. Add an independent label the module can be scored against: the deposited struct_conn category in the reference mmCIFs annotates SS bonds, so report precision and recall of your SG-SG detector against those annotations — that is a real external validation, unlike reproducing the numbers from this session's one-off script, which is circular if the script has a bug. Make the headline output a joint table of (violation type) x (local pLDDT decile) so the 'invisible to pLDDT' claim is quantified rather than anecdotal. Before writing any disulfide_connectivity into dataset.json, re-fold the affected candidates at >=3 recorded seeds and report violation persistence across seeds; a violation present in 1 of 3 seeds is a sampler artefact, a violation present in 3 of 3 is a property of the prediction. Replace the +/-0.5 A CA-CA rule with the omega-aware rule as proposed — that is a correct bug fix and the cis-Tyr105-Pro106 case in 4EY7 is a clean regression test.

critiques.scientific_objection: Every benchmark entry named is inside Boltz-2's training set, and the proposal never mentions the training cutoff. I verified this session that Boltz-2 trains on all PDB structures released up to 2023-06-01. 4EY7, 4EY6 and 4EY5 were released 2012-10-17; 2FLU, 1WWW, 2IFG, 3FXI, 5UN5, 6XDS and 1B41 all predate the cutoff by years to decades. Predicting them therefore measures recall of memorised structures, not predictive accuracy. That would be tolerable as a positive-control suite, but the proposal goes further and wires the result into the reporting layer as the mandatory calibration context for every ipTM the platform displays ('No ipTM value anywhere in the platform's output or UI appears without the benchmark N and the measured DockQ distribution attached'). That installs an optimistically biased accuracy statement as the platform's official uncertainty claim — a number that looks earned and is not, which is strictly worse than the current state of having no calibration. It also directly contradicts AIML-STRUCT-2 and AIML-BENCH-2, which handle the cutoff correctly; the slate cannot adopt all three as written. A secondary error: 'the 22 existing runs took 26 s each on MPS, essentially independent of length from 26 to 100 residues' generalises fixed-overhead-dominated timings to a regime where they do not hold — the session's own hAChE measurement was 2 min 21 s at 543 residues, and pair-representation cost scales worse than linearly.
critiques.feasibility_objection: The mechanics are sound and cheap: DockQ 2.1.3 and gemmi are installed and verified, the target records already resolve residue numbering, and domain-sized complexes run in minutes. The timing pilot the author already proposes for the large targets is the right instinct. Feasibility is not the problem here; the inferential frame is.
critiques.improvement: Relabel the entire suite as a positive-control / integration test rather than a calibration, with an explicit banner that all entries predate the 2023-06-01 training cutoff and that the measured DockQ therefore bounds recall, not prediction. Keep 2FLU (KEAP1 Kelch + Neh2 16-mer at 1.5 A) as the end-to-end wiring test — it is an excellent one, and a pipeline that fails it is broken — but state that passing it proves nothing about the designed candidates. Take every number that enters the reporting layer from AIML-STRUCT-2's post-cutoff, homology-filtered set instead. If you want an in-house calibration on the platform's own targets, restrict it to complexes for those UniProts deposited after 2023-06-01 and report the n honestly, including if it is zero for most of the 16. Finally, replace the 26 s length-independence claim with a measured timing curve across the 26-543 residue range before sizing any batch.

critiques.scientific_objection: The interface-forensics module is good and the epitope-overlap test against 2FLU/4EY7 is the right falsification instrument for the mechanistically inverted candidates. Three defects. (a) pDockQ's logistic parameters were fitted on AlphaFold2-Multimer interface pLDDT and contact counts; applying that published sigmoid to Boltz-2 outputs emits an uncalibrated probability under a recognised name, which is the smuggled-estimate failure mode this repository exists to prevent. (b) Jaccard overlap between a predicted epitope and an experimental one is confounded by interface size — a large promiscuous peptide burying more surface gains overlap by area alone, and these candidates are exactly that class. There is also no null: some overlap is expected by chance for any patch placed on a pocket-rich surface. (c) With N=20 decoys, 'exceeds the 95th percentile of its own scrambles' is the maximum order statistic of 20 draws, the noisiest summary available, and it inherits the same single-seed exchangeability problem as AIML-STRUCT-1 and AIML-BENCH-3. (d) The proposal correctly gates itself on Idea 2, but Idea 2 as written is leakage-broken, so the gate points at the wrong benchmark.
critiques.feasibility_objection: The analysis code is cheap and the libraries are installed and timed (ShrakeRupley over 543 residues in 0.9 s). The decoy folding is the cost and the author is honest that MPS scaling for complexes is unmeasured and that this arm is the one most likely to want a GPU. The instinct to run a reduced null rather than no null is right. 240 complex predictions at ~3 min is ~12 h, so it is feasible, but only if the decoy set is shared with AIML-STRUCT-1 rather than folded twice.
critiques.improvement: Do not emit pDockQ as a probability. Report the raw pair (interface contact count, mean interface pLDDT), and if you want a calibrated interface probability, refit the logistic locally on AIML-STRUCT-2's post-cutoff DockQ set — then it is a measured local quantity with a stated n, not a borrowed constant. For epitope comparison report three numbers, not one: Jaccard, recall of the experimental epitope (fraction of experimentally contacting residues recovered), and predicted interface size — plus a random-patch null giving the expected overlap for a same-size surface patch placed at random on the same receptor, so a Jaccard of 0.2 can be read against what chance gives. Replace the 95th-percentile rule with a seed-matched standardised effect size and a bootstrap CI, and share one decoy folding run across STRUCT-1, BENCH-3 and this proposal — three separate 20-scramble campaigns on the same candidates is a waste of the compute budget. Re-point the gate from STRUCTBIO-IDEA-2 to AIML-STRUCT-2. Validating the module by reproducing the KEAP1-Neh2 interface from deposited 2FLU coordinates before applying it to any prediction is exactly right and should be kept.

critiques.scientific_objection: Minor, and none that changes the conclusion. I independently confirmed the mechanism in the repository: all 27 activities in data/corpus_ACHE.json carry assay_confidence: null, the denominator object has rejection buckets for unparseable / tier_excluded / no_structure / too_large and no low-confidence bucket at all, and neostigmine bromide appears at 22 nM (CHEMBL636834) and 2.0 nM (CHEMBL645004) from two documents. The min_assay_confidence=8 criterion has therefore never rejected a record, exactly as claimed. Two cautions on the write-up. (a) 'The platform overstated its own model's error by roughly a full log unit' is itself aggregator-dependent — 1.43 against the median, 1.20 against the geometric mean, and an unknown value against the catalytic-inhibition class aggregate that has not been built yet. The corrected figure should not be quoted until the endpoint-class curation exists, or the retraction repeats the original error in the opposite direction. (b) The sigma = 0.68 log figure: I retrieved Kalliokoski et al. 2013 this session (PubMed, DOI 10.1371/journal.pone.0061007). The abstract establishes that mixed public IC50 data are noisier than Ki data by about 25% and that mixing adds moderate noise, but it does not state 0.68. Under this repository's own rule against reconstructing constants from memory, that number must be lifted from the full text with a table or page reference, or recorded as unretrieved.
critiques.feasibility_objection: None. One extra ChEMBL /assay batch call, a dataclass widening, an endpoint-class table and aggregation arithmetic. Two days is realistic. The endpoint-class table is medicinal-chemistry curation and is correctly identified as the heaviest item.
critiques.improvement: State the general principle the finding implies and enforce it in code: no single-compound model-versus-measurement comparison may ever be a headline, because with a 4-log within-compound spread on huperzine A the per-compound error is dominated by which measurement you picked. Make the aggregate the only comparable object, and make the platform incapable of rendering a per-compound error without the within-compound n and log-range beside it. Retrieve the Kalliokoski sigma from the full text and cite it with a locator, or mark it unretrieved and use only the corpus's own empirically observed within-compound sigma (18 replicate pairs, mean |dlog10| 0.448) until it is. Publish the retraction of the 2.41 figure as retraction-with-replacement in the ledger and propagate it: AIML-BENCH-1, CBC-CC-1 and META-3 all currently use 2.41 as their motivating anchor and all three need updating in the same commit, otherwise the retracted number survives in three proposals.

critiques.scientific_objection: The diagnosis is right — I confirmed run_boltz (structure.py:169-216) passes no --seed and that _collect_boltz_outputs keeps only sorted(cifs)[0] — but two of the remedies are not sound. (a) 'two same-seed runs are compared and either byte-identical or their divergence is quantified' offers byte-identity as the good outcome; on MPS it will not occur, for the same non-determinism reasons noted in AIML-STRUCT-3, so the criterion will always resolve to the fallback and should simply be stated as the fallback. (b) The noise-envelope design is too thin to support the conclusion it is meant to license. Re-folding ONE candidate at three seeds and applying that envelope to all 22 assumes the seed variance is sequence-independent, which it is not — a confidently-folded amphipathic helix and a 47-residue cysteine-rich low-pLDDT construct will have very different run-to-run spreads, and the 22 candidates span exactly that range. The '2x the envelope' downgrade rule then propagates a single-candidate estimate into 22 retract-or-keep decisions. The rule is also arbitrary: the right object is an interval on each delta, not a multiple of a global sd.
critiques.feasibility_objection: None material, and the fix is cheaper than the flawed version. At the measured ~26 s per lone chain, three seeds on all 22 candidates is ~30 minutes of MPS time. There is no compute argument for extrapolating from one candidate. The env.py introspection, the lockfiles, the CPU-layer container and CI are straightforward, and the decision NOT to containerise the Boltz layer (no Metal passthrough in Docker Desktop on macOS) is correct and well-reasoned.
critiques.improvement: Re-fold all 22 candidates at >=3 recorded seeds — half an hour of compute — and give each candidate its own seed envelope; then classify each legacy delta by whether the legacy value falls inside or outside that candidate's own across-seed interval, rather than against a global 2x rule. Report the envelope as a function of mean pLDDT so the sequence-dependence is visible. Replace the byte-identity criterion with a measured same-seed divergence (max per-atom RMSD and |delta pLDDT|) and a declared tolerance derived from it. The three independent findings — RDKit version string asserted rather than introspected (build_dataset.py:34 and the dead getattr at corpus.py:318), 4 of 14 ledger ARTIFACT hashes mismatching, and nothing under platform/ or data/ being tracked by git — are correct, verified-adjacent, and the git one is the single largest defect on the whole slate. Commit the rebuild before anything else on this list ships.

critiques.scientific_objection: The criterion-exercise audit is the most original idea in the slate and I confirmed the bug it was derived from. But three problems. (a) The pre-registration is partly retrospective: the huperzine A result and its 2.41 log error are already in the ledger, so affinity-ache-v1 cannot be pre-specified in the epistemically meaningful sense for that compound, and any threshold X and Y chosen now is chosen with knowledge of a data point. (b) The decision rule conflates two failures. With n=18 compounds on one target, 'the 95% CI upper bound on MAE is below X' will fail for reasons of sample size regardless of model quality, and the protocol would then record a refusal that reads as a verdict on Boltz-2 when it is a verdict on the benchmark. (c) The zero-rejection rule in the criterion-exercise audit has a false-positive mode: a criterion can legitimately reject nothing on a particular corpus — max_mol_weight=2000 rejecting zero small molecules is correct behaviour, and the current denominator shows exactly that (too_large: 0). Flagging it NOT_EXERCISED and failing the gate would train people to delete valid criteria. (d) The training-contamination caveat is correctly pre-declared but understated: I verified the affinity head trained on ChEMBL, BindingDB, PDBbind and MF-PCBA, so ChEMBL membership is a lower bound on contamination and the protocol should say so.
critiques.feasibility_objection: Two days for the protocol format, freeze/verify against the existing append-only ledger, and the audit is realistic; the /assay join is small. The benchmark itself — 18 complexes of a 543-residue receptor plus ligand at the measured 3 min 4 s — is well under an hour of compute, not 'hours to overnight'; the estimate is conservative, which is the safe direction.
critiques.improvement: Declare huperzine A as the pilot observation that motivated the protocol and exclude it from the primary analysis, or state in the protocol that the thresholds were set with one datapoint visible — either is honest, silence is not. Add a minimum-n / minimum-detectable-effect clause so that a run failing on power returns INCONCLUSIVE, a third outcome distinct from 'reported' and 'refused'; compute the required n from sigma_exp and the null RMSE before freezing. Replace the zero-count rule with a demonstration requirement: every criterion must ship a unit-test fixture — a synthetic record engineered to trip it — and the gate fails if the criterion does not reject that fixture. That catches decorative criteria without punishing criteria that legitimately reject nothing on real data, and it would have caught the confidence_score bug immediately. Reconcile the prose (confidence 8 is homologous single protein, 9 is direct) and record chembl_release, retrieval timestamp and verbatim query URLs as proposed — the current denominator of 258 examined / 18 admitted is not reproducible against a moving database.

critiques.critic: ML evaluation and benchmarking (data leakage, split design, reproducibility failures in scientific ML)

critiques.scientific_objection: Three defects, one of them fatal to the stated conclusion. (1) NO POSITIVE CONTROL. The pilot's own numbers — min interface PAE 16.84 A native vs 16.45 A scramble, against 0.56 A on 1YCR — are much better explained by 'this pipeline places no interface at all for a 36-mer against a 543-residue receptor in single-sequence mode' than by 'these designs are not sequence-specific'. As designed, the experiment cannot distinguish design failure from method impotence, and every result it produces is therefore uninterpretable. (2) P-VALUE GRANULARITY. With N=20 decoys the smallest attainable empirical p is 1/21 = 0.048. Across 35 candidates, no multiplicity-corrected result can ever be significant, and the success criterion 'at least one candidate with p > 0.05' is satisfied by the resolution of the estimator rather than by any property of the candidates — a criterion that cannot fail is not a criterion. (3) VARIANCE MISMATCH. Comparing a 5-seed native median against 20 single-seed decoy draws contrasts a mean with single realisations. With the measured seed sd of 0.133 on a 0-1 scale, most of the decoy spread is sampler noise, not composition, so the null is a mixture distribution and the p-value is not calibrated for the hypothesis being tested. Two further confounds: ipTM depends on chain-length ratio, so an off-target panel drawn from 16 receptors spanning ~67-608 residues confounds specificity with size; and a composition shuffle destroys helical propensity as well as order, so the null differs from the design in more than the one variable named.
critiques.feasibility_objection: Compute is defensible (24 h unattended MPS), but the budget is misallocated: 26 runs/candidate x 35 buys precision on an uninterpretable contrast while zero runs are spent establishing that the assay has power. Also, three proposals on this list (AIML-STRUCT-1, AIML-BENCH-3, STRUCTBIO-IDEA-3) are the same experiment; running all three triples the only scarce resource here.
critiques.improvement: Spend the first overnight batch on a SENSITIVITY PANEL, not on candidates: >=10 solved peptide-receptor complexes (2FLU KEAP1+Neh2 is the ideal seed case; prefer PDB entries released after 2024-01-01, see my AIML-STRUCT-2 note) run through the byte-identical pipeline, each with its own 20 composition-matched scrambles. Report the fraction of genuine binders whose native beats its own scramble distribution. That fraction is the assay's power, and it must be published as the denominator of every candidate verdict; if it is near chance, the candidate arm is cancelled rather than run. Then: raise N to >=200 decoys on a reduced candidate set (10, not 35) so Holm/BH correction is arithmetically reachable; match variance by comparing seed-matched draws (10 decoys x 2 seeds beats 20 x 1) or by fitting iptm ~ group + (1|seed) and reporting the contrast with a CI instead of a bare p; size-match the off-target panel to the cognate receptor within +/-20% residues; add sequence reversal and the motif-block permutation as second and third nulls. Finally, do not re-tune the PAE-asymmetry check to make real complexes pass — that calibrates the fraud detector on the data it polices. Re-derive it as a classifier: score it on genuine two-chain Boltz-2 output AND on the legacy trigonometric matrices (regenerate them), and publish its TPR/FPR.

critiques.scientific_objection: The benchmark is not leakage-free, and I can show it from the model's own paper, which I retrieved and read this session (Boltz-2, bioRxiv DOI 10.1101/2025.06.14.659707). Two hard facts. (a) The PDB training cutoff is indeed 2023-06-01 — but the AUTHORS' OWN VALIDATION SET is exactly PDB entries released after 2023-06-01 and on or before 2024-01-01 (n=398). The released checkpoint was selected using that window. A benchmark built from 'initial_release_date > 2023-06-01' therefore overlaps the model-selection set, and any calibration fit on it is optimistic by an unquantified amount. (b) The authors additionally required that 'all the protein sequences of the chains are not present in any training set clusters' at mmseqs --min-seq-id 0.4, plus small-molecule Tanimoto <= 0.85 to any training ligand. The proposal's 1107-hit query applies neither filter, so most of those receptors sit inside training clusters; deduplicating the test set internally at 30-40% identity (as proposed) removes redundancy WITHIN the benchmark and does nothing about train-test proximity. That is the single most common split-design error in scientific ML and it is present here. Separately, the calibration's intended use is out of domain: a curve fitted on natural peptide-protein complexes is then applied to GGGGS-linked designed chimeras for which no DockQ ground truth can ever exist. Restricting extrapolation to populated ipTM BINS does not address covariate shift — an in-range ipTM from an out-of-distribution input still returns a fabricated probability.
critiques.feasibility_objection: n=100 is under-powered for the stated deliverables: with ~5 bins that is ~20/bin, Wilson intervals roughly +/-0.22, an AUROC CI of about +/-0.10-0.12, and an expected-calibration-error estimate dominated by binning noise. The proposal commits to committing ECE and per-bin probabilities that the sample size cannot support. At 1-3 min/complex the fix is affordable, so this is a sizing error, not a hardware limit. The proposal also concedes the RCSB clustering call returned HTTP 400 and was never validated — the deduplication step, which is the scientific core, is unimplemented.
critiques.improvement: Rebuild the set as: initial_release_date > 2024-01-01 (escapes the authors' validation window), AND receptor chain not in any mmseqs easy-cluster --min-seq-id 0.4 cluster of the pre-2023-06-01 PDB sequence set (run mmseqs2 locally; do not rely on the RCSB group_by call), AND ligand/peptide max Tanimoto <= 0.85 to training-window partners. Report three strata side by side — clean holdout, post-cutoff-but-cluster-overlapping, pre-cutoff recall — and never pool them. Do a power calculation before running: state the target CI width on P(DockQ>=0.23) per bin, and size N from it (expect 300-500, which is 10-25 h on MPS, still one weekend). Replace binned ECE with a bootstrapped isotonic or logistic reliability curve plus a smooth-calibration-error estimate; report per-bin n on the figure. Make calibrated_interface_probability refuse on covariate-space distance, not just bin occupancy: fit a simple domain classifier (natural vs designed, length ratio, composition) on the calibration inputs and return 'out of calibration domain' for the 35 candidates unless they fall inside it — which, being GGGGS chimeras, they will not, and saying so is the honest deliverable.

critiques.scientific_objection: Correct diagnosis, three flaws in the instrument. (1) Wiring the across-seed sd into Provenance.uncertainty will be read as an error bar on the truth when it is only the sampler's dispersion. A tightly reproducible but systematically wrong prediction would render as high-confidence. This is precisely the 'number without knowledge' failure the project exists to prevent, one level up. (2) The factorial is specified at diffusion_samples=5, but every legacy value was produced at ds=1. The sd of a 5-sample-selected score is a different statistic from the sd of a single draw, so the error bars produced by this experiment cannot be used to re-interpret the 22 legacy deltas — which is the stated motivation. (3) The MSA arm and the retest of the Huperzine result are confounded in the same direction as the pilot the proposal criticises: adding a receptor MSA changes the input distribution to the affinity head as well as to the structure module, so a change in the 2.41 log error is not attributable to MSA depth alone unless seed and diffusion_samples are held fixed across arms and the structure is held fixed in one condition.
critiques.feasibility_objection: 'data/real_vs_hardcoded.json is byte-reproducible on a second execution' is very likely unattainable and should not be a success criterion: torch on the MPS backend does not guarantee bitwise-deterministic reductions, and the proposal itself notes an operator falling back to CPU. Seeding fixes the noise draw, not kernel non-determinism. Also, if AIML-STRUCT-2 proceeds at 300-500 complexes with --use_msa_server, the public ColabFold MMseqs2 service is hit hundreds of times, not 16.
critiques.improvement: Rename the field: emit sampling_sd (or seed_spread) as a distinct provenance key and leave uncertainty empty until an accuracy-anchored quantity exists (from AIML-STRUCT-2 / AIML-BENCH-2). Add a validate.py rule that sampling_sd may never be rendered as an error bar on the value. Keep one arm at diffusion_samples=1 so the legacy deltas remain re-interpretable, and report the seed envelope separately per quantity and per regime (monomer pLDDT, complex pLDDT, ipTM, min interface PAE) — a lone confident helix and a 580-token complex do not share a variance. Measure determinism before promising it: run the same seed twice, report bitwise identity or coordinate RMSD and score deltas, and write whichever it is into the manifest. For the MSA arm, add a fixed-structure condition (predict once, score affinity twice) to separate the structural from the affinity effect.

critiques.scientific_objection: The design is right; two of its three anchors are miscomputed, and I checked both against the repo's own file. (1) THE NOISE CEILING IS OVERSTATED IN PRECISION. The claimed sigma_exp = 0.376 from '18 replicate pairs' comes from only FOUR compounds — tacrine contributes 10 of the 18 pairs and physostigmine 6 — so the pairs are not independent and n=18 is not the sample size. Pooling within-compound variance properly on data/corpus_ACHE.json gives sigma = 0.421 log10 on df = 9, 95% CI [0.289, 0.768]. Kalliokoski's 0.68 (PLoS ONE 2013, DOI 10.1371/journal.pone.0061007, sigma_pIC50 = 0.68, MUE 0.55, raw R^2 = 0.40 — retrieved and verified this session) lies INSIDE that interval. The proposal's implicit claim that this corpus is quieter than the public literature is not supported, and a sigma_exp band drawn on a plot without its CI is exactly the kind of unearned number the project bans. (2) THE LEAKAGE METRIC IS COMPUTED AGAINST THE WRONG REFERENCE SET. max_tanimoto_to_pre_cutoff measured against 'the pre-cutoff snapshot' as instantiated by this repo's 300-activity slice will be a severe underestimate of true nearest-neighbour proximity in Boltz-2's actual training set. An underestimated leakage metric is worse than no metric, because it licenses a 'clean' label that is false. The good news is that the true membership predicate is now knowable exactly: the Boltz-2 paper (bioRxiv 10.1101/2025.06.14.659707, read this session) states the affinity set was extracted from ChEMBL v34 with confidence_score EXACTLY 9, target_type SINGLE PROTEIN, standard_type in {Ki,Kd,IC50,XC50,EC50,AC50}, PAINS REMOVED, and molecules with more than 50 heavy atoms filtered out. (3) The temporal split is conceptually wrong: splitting on ChEMBL document.year does not separate in-training from out-of-training, because curation date and publication date are decoupled — a 2019 paper can enter ChEMBL after v34. The split that matters is by database release.
critiques.feasibility_objection: n=17 compounds with a numeric potency (I counted; predict-the-mean RMSE on those 17 is 1.664, matching the proposal's 1.644 up to aggregation rule). Three splits, scaffold clustering, similarity strata and BCa CIs on paired deltas are not defined at that n — a scaffold split of 17 compounds yields folds of 3-5. The whole design is contingent on the multi-target scale-out, which is itself contingent on fixing the corpus's inert confidence filter (verified broken: every assay_confidence in the file is null). Sequence that first or the benchmark cannot start.
critiques.improvement: Replace the guessed leakage audit with the exact one: reconstruct Boltz-2's own extraction on a ChEMBL v34 archive (confidence 9, SINGLE PROTEIN, listed standard types, PAINS removed, <=50 heavy atoms) and label every test compound in_boltz_affinity_train true/false/unknown. This buys two free, genuinely out-of-training strata at zero inference cost: PAINS-flagged natural products (curcumin, baicalein, salvianolic acid B were excluded from Boltz-2's affinity training by construction) and compounds above 50 heavy atoms (salvianolic acid B 52, ginsenoside Rg1 56, onjisaponin V 123). Those strata are the only place a real accuracy estimate lives. Replace the year-based temporal split with a release-based one (v34 vs current). Report sigma_exp as 0.42 log10 [0.29, 0.77], df=9, n=4 compounds, and state that it is statistically indistinguishable from the literature value; do not draw a band without the interval. Set a minimum-n gate in code: no headline metric renders below a pre-declared n (>=50 compounds/target) — below it, emit only the per-compound table. Use per-target median, not the corpus mean, as the null.

critiques.scientific_objection: The recall/holdout separation is exactly right and is the best split thinking on this list — but the holdout as specified is not a holdout. Two verified problems. (1) The 81 entries are drawn from release_date > 2023-06-01, which includes the window (2023-06-01, 2024-01-01] that the Boltz-2 authors used as their VALIDATION set for model selection (bioRxiv 10.1101/2025.06.14.659707, read this session; n=398 validation structures from exactly that window). Post-training-cutoff is not post-model-selection. (2) The receptor set — P22303, P04058, P06276, MAO-A/B, BACE1/2, TTR, APP — is the most structurally over-represented family in the PDB for this indication. Every one of those receptors has dozens of pre-cutoff holo entries, so every chain sits inside a training cluster at 40% identity, and most post-2023 depositions are congeneric follow-ups from the same groups. A date filter alone gives you interpolation onto a memorised pocket with a near-neighbour ligand and calls it prediction. The proposal applies the ligand-novelty stratification it correctly demands of AIML-BENCH-1 to nothing here. Third, smaller: for a cofolding model the receptor is predicted too, so ligand RMSD after global superposition can be inflated or masked by receptor error; the AF3/PoseBusters convention is pocket-aligned RMSD and the choice must be stated.
critiques.feasibility_objection: Sound (~6 h MPS, pure-Python deps verified). But the binary decision rule 'if the AUROC CI includes 0.5, stop displaying the score' is under-powered at n≈81: a truly useful AUROC of 0.65 will routinely produce a CI containing 0.5 at that n, so the rule discards good information with high probability. That is an asymmetric-cost decision made without a power calculation.
critiques.improvement: Add two stratification axes to every holdout case and report the headline proportions within strata, never pooled: (a) receptor chain in / not in a pre-2023-06-01 mmseqs-0.4 training cluster; (b) max ECFP4 Tanimoto of the ligand to any ligand co-crystallised pre-cutoff with the same UniProt, binned <0.4 / 0.4-0.7 / >0.7. Add a third temporal tier, release_date > 2024-01-01, and label the 2023-06-01..2024-01-01 tier explicitly as 'inside the Boltz-2 authors' validation window — model-selection leakage'. State the superposition convention (pocket-aligned, defined as reference residues within 6 A of the reference ligand) in the output file. Replace the AUROC on/off switch with a pre-registered interval rule: report AUROC with CI and permit the score to be displayed only alongside that CI, with a stated minimum n before any threshold is quoted; if the CI is wide, the honest output is 'not yet resolvable at n=81', not silent removal of a possibly-informative signal.

critiques.scientific_objection: The stated success criterion is mathematically unreachable, which I can show by arithmetic on the proposal's own parameters. With K=20 controls the smallest attainable empirical p is (1+0)/(1+20) = 0.0476; Holm-Bonferroni across 10 candidates multiplies the smallest by 10, giving a floor of 0.476. No candidate can ever be labelled 'sequence-specific (Holm-corrected p < 0.05)' under this design, and at the K=10 pilot the floor is worse. The experiment can therefore only ever return the null verdict — it is a test that cannot reject, which is the mirror image of the corpus's confidence filter that could never exclude. Second, as with AIML-STRUCT-1, there is no positive control, so a universal null result cannot be attributed to the designs rather than to Boltz-2 msa=empty having no peptide-docking ability at 580 tokens. Third, the promise to 'demonstrate quantitatively which existing outputs are order-invariant' is wasted compute: MW, net charge, pI and GRAVY are order-invariant by construction, which is a proof, not a measurement.
critiques.feasibility_objection: Compute estimates are credible (~3 min/complex, 210 runs, 11-14 h), but at K=20 the runs cannot answer the question asked, so the batch is spent to produce an inevitability. Raising K to the ~200 needed for Holm over 10 candidates is 2000 runs, roughly 100 h — no longer an overnight job on this MacBook.
critiques.improvement: Merge into AIML-STRUCT-1 as one experiment with one design; the distinctive contributions here (linker-preserving shuffle, motif-block permutation, epitope-contact counting against the intended residues, relabelling composition-determined fields) are the parts worth keeping. Then fix the statistics: either control FDR (Benjamini-Hochberg) instead of FWER, or drop to 3-5 candidates so K=200 is affordable, or abandon per-candidate p-values in favour of a standardised effect size (design minus decoy mean, over decoy sd) with a bootstrap CI, which is estimable at K=20 and is the quantity a reader actually wants. Replace the order-invariance experiment with a unit test asserting invariance under permutation, and relabel those fields on the candidate cards before any folding. Add the sensitivity panel of solved peptide-receptor complexes described in my AIML-STRUCT-1 note; without it the headline null result is not attributable.

critiques.scientific_objection: The core insight — beat the per-target median or emit nothing — is the correct decision rule and is better specified here than in AIML-BENCH-1. Two defects. (1) The decoy AUROC uses ASSUMED negatives: ligand versus three unrelated registry receptors, scored as non-binders. Natural products are promiscuous, so an unknown fraction of those pairs are real binders, and the resulting label noise deflates AUROC by an unquantifiable amount — the number cannot be interpreted in either direction. (2) Writing a single measured RMSE into thermo.METHOD_ACCURACY next to literature FEP and MM-GBSA figures invites exactly the misuse the table was built to prevent: an RMSE from ~60 pairs across 4 targets carries a CI of roughly +/-0.3 log units and is target-composition-dependent, and a bare scalar in a lookup table loses both facts. (3) The applicability gate is calibrated on the wrong boundary: the proposal uses 56 and 128 heavy atoms, but the Boltz-2 paper (bioRxiv 10.1101/2025.06.14.659707, read this session) states the affinity training data was filtered to molecules with at most 50 heavy atoms. Fifty is the empirical domain edge; 56 and 128 are engineering limits.
critiques.feasibility_objection: Extending the corpus to GSK3B, KEAP1, CHRM1 and NOS3 at 'min_assay_confidence=8' cannot work until the confidence filter is repaired — verified inert in this repo (every assay_confidence in data/corpus_ACHE.json is null, because confidence_score is an /assay field and the code reads it off /activity). 200-300 Boltz runs at the measured ~3 min is 10-15 h, fine; the gating dependency is the schedule risk, not the compute.
critiques.improvement: Replace assumed-negative decoys with MEASURED inactives: ChEMBL records for the same compound-target pair reported as inactive or with standard_relation '>' at >=10 uM. Where none exist, state that the AUROC rests on presumed negatives and report it as a bound. Set the heavy-atom applicability gate at 50 (Boltz-2's own training filter), refuse above it by default, and report every dataset natural product's position relative to that line. Make METHOD_ACCURACY's new key a structured record — rmse, ci_low, ci_high, n_pairs, n_targets, msa_mode, accelerator, date — and add a verify_all.py check that no consumer may read rmse without the interval. Note also that ChEMBL confidence 9, not 8, is what Boltz-2 trained on; use 9 both for the corpus and as the in-training leakage label, and report accuracy separately for confidence-9 pairs (probably memorised) and everything else.

critiques.scientific_objection: The pre-registered decision rule is the right instrument but the threshold is set in the wrong units. 'RMSE <= 2.0 kcal/mol' is an absolute criterion with no reference to the spread of the data it is measured on: for a protein-peptide affinity set whose ground-truth range is typically 3-4 kcal/mol, a method at 2.0 kcal/mol can be indistinguishable from predicting the set mean. A pre-registration that can be passed by a constant predictor is not a gate. Second, the crystal-benchmark reproduction step is correctly labelled a wiring check, but the proposal then treats the four-cell table (crystal PP / predicted PP / crystal peptide / predicted peptide) as a clean two-factor decomposition — it is not, because the peptide set and the protein-protein set differ in interface size, affinity range and measurement method simultaneously, so the 'peptide shift' cell confounds all three. Third, the load-bearing input — a protein-peptide structure-plus-affinity set — is never named, and its size, affinity range and measurement modality determine whether any of the four cells is estimable.
critiques.feasibility_objection: '~1 week' is optimistic given that step 4(a) requires Boltz-2 co-folding of the Kastritis benchmark subset (dozens to 144 complexes, many far larger than 580 tokens) on MPS, whose scaling with sequence length has not been measured beyond ~590 tokens; pair-representation cost grows roughly quadratically. Time three complexes across the size range before committing. The prodigy-prot install claim is credible and the refusal-to-reimplement discipline is right.
critiques.improvement: Re-express the pre-registered rule in reference units: emit binding_free_energy only if PRODIGY-on-Boltz-models beats the per-set mean predictor by a stated margin with a paired bootstrap CI excluding zero, AND the RMSE upper CI bound is below the measured spread of the ground truth. Name the protein-peptide affinity set explicitly in the pre-registration, with its n and its ground-truth measurement modality, and freeze it before running — PRODIGY's own published collapse to r ~ 0.04-0.05 on indirectly-measured affinities means the set's measurement modality is a first-order determinant of the answer, not a detail. Decompose the two shifts with a matched design: run the SAME complexes as crystal and as predicted structure (isolates the structure shift cleanly), and match peptide and protein-protein subsets on interface buried area before comparing them. Stratify the predicted-structure cell by ipTM bin as proposed, and report n per bin.

critiques.scientific_objection: Chemical indeterminacy is a real and under-recognised uncertainty source, and the refusal to let MM-GBSA touch binding_free_energy is correct. But the quantitative machinery is unsound in two places. (1) 'Combine the isomer spread in quadrature with the method RMSE' adds a min/median/max RANGE over a discrete, unequally-probable set of chemical species to a Gaussian sd. Those are different objects; quadrature requires two independent standard deviations of the same quantity. Combining them produces a number with no distributional interpretation, which is the exact failure mode the project is remediating. The isomer set is a scenario ensemble, not a noise term. (2) The OpenMM 'interface survives vs dissolves' pass/fail is a classifier with no measured operating characteristic. Short restrained implicit-solvent MD on a predicted, possibly-nonexistent interface will dissolve true and false interfaces alike; without running the identical filter on solved disulfide-rich complexes (true positives) and on scrambled or off-target pairs (true negatives), its TPR and FPR are unknown and its verdicts carry no information. The success criterion 'disulfide_connectivity moves to COMPUTED where exactly one connectivity survives the filter' promotes a value to COMPUTED on the strength of an uncharacterised filter.
critiques.feasibility_objection: 1-1.5 weeks understates it. The Boltz SG-SG bond constraint is explicitly unverified (the docs are quoted as covering CCD ligands and canonical residues without confirming intra-chain SG-SG), and the fallback path — imposing connectivity during relaxation — is a different experiment with different failure modes, not a drop-in substitute. 100-150 isomer systems each needing fold + minimise + restrained equilibration + unrestrained MD on MPS is a substantially larger compute item than stated, and OpenMM on this box exposes Reference/CPU/OpenCL, not a fast Metal path.
critiques.improvement: Drop the quadrature. Report the isomer ensemble as what it is: a set of scenarios with min/median/max per candidate, and state the headline as an interval attributable to undefined chemistry, kept dimensionally separate from method error; if a single number is needed, report the range width and label it a bound, not a sigma. Before the filter gates anything, characterise it: run the identical Amber14/GBn2 protocol on >=10 solved disulfide-rich complexes and >=10 negative pairs and publish its confusion matrix; if it cannot separate them, the filter reports nothing and disulfide_connectivity stays not_computed with the spread attached. Verify the SG-SG constraint on the solved control FIRST and treat a negative result as terminating the constrained arm rather than as a trigger for an unvalidated substitute. Finally, scope to the 4- and 6-Cys candidates where enumeration is exhaustive (3 and 15) and defer the 8-Cys sampling entirely — a 15-of-105 random sample gives a badly-estimated range with no stated coverage.

critiques.scientific_objection: Commenting on the evaluation design rather than the stereochemistry, which is outside my lane. The success criteria are pinned to numbers from an unrepeatable run: 'reproduces the numbers measured this session — 38 S-S contacts, mean 2.081, sd 0.203, exactly 4 candidates with trivalent sulfur' over 22 mmCIFs that were produced UNSEEDED at diffusion_samples=1 and that live in /tmp, which macOS purges (the proposal itself flags the durability bug). A regression test whose expected values come from a stochastic process that cannot be re-run is not a regression test; it is a fingerprint of one draw. Worse, the interesting quantities are sampler-dependent — re-fold the same candidates with a different seed and the S-S census will change — so the headline finding 'four candidates place a cysteine in two bonds' needs a seed envelope before it is a property of the candidate rather than of the draw. Second, the reference distribution is partly circular for the bonded-geometry checks: deposited structures at 2.3-2.4 A are refined under Engh-Huber restraints and disulfides are commonly restrained, so 'zero violations on real crystal structures' partly measures the refinement library, not independent chemistry.
critiques.feasibility_objection: Genuinely 2 days; gemmi is installed and the analysis ran in under a second. No objection.
critiques.improvement: Commit the 22 mmCIFs (plus confidence/PAE arrays) into the repo under a content-addressed path FIRST, and write the regression test against those committed files — then the pinned numbers are reproducible by construction. Separately, re-fold >=5 of the affected candidates at >=5 recorded seeds and report the S-S distance and chi3 distributions across seeds; promote 'four candidates have trivalent sulfur' to a finding only if it survives across seeds, and report the per-seed count otherwise. For threshold calibration, prefer a high-resolution subset (<1.5 A) and state the restraint circularity explicitly for bond lengths/angles; chi3 and the sulfur-valence check are much less restraint-contaminated and should carry the weight. Report the checks' false-positive rate on the reference set together with the reference set's own n and resolution distribution.

critiques.scientific_objection: Right question, wrong benchmark. Every case named — 4EY7, 4EY6, 1B41, 2FLU, 1WWW, 2IFG, 3FXI, 5UN5, 6XDS — was released long before Boltz-2's 2023-06-01 PDB training cutoff (verified from the Boltz-2 paper, bioRxiv 10.1101/2025.06.14.659707, this session), and the receptors are the canonical, heavily-deposited members of their families. Folding a 4EY7 monomer and reporting 0.5 A Ca RMSD measures memorisation, and the proposal does not label it as such (AIML-BENCH-2, by contrast, explicitly partitions recall from holdout — this one should copy that discipline). The 2FLU complex case is genuinely valuable, but as a POSITIVE CONTROL for pipeline power, not as an accuracy estimate: the KEAP1-Neh2 complex is in training. Second, the deliverable 'calibration table of ipTM vs DockQ' cannot be built from the three complexes available here (2FLU, 1WWW/2IFG, 3FXI); the proposal concedes N is too small to support a threshold, which means the central artefact is not produced.
critiques.feasibility_objection: 4-6 days is realistic and the scoring stack is verified. The problem is not effort but that the effort duplicates AIML-STRUCT-2, which proposes the same DockQ calibration on a set two orders of magnitude larger and temporally partitioned. Running both spends the same MPS budget twice for one table.
critiques.improvement: Merge into AIML-STRUCT-2 and keep only the two things this proposal has that STRUCT-2 lacks: (a) the curated receptor/domain-boundary/numbering registry, which is real work already done and is the prerequisite for every co-folding proposal on this list; (b) 2FLU and the other in-registry complexes as a labelled POSITIVE-CONTROL panel — 'inside Boltz-2's training window; establishes that the pipeline can place a known peptide in a known groove' — which is exactly the missing power measurement that AIML-STRUCT-1 and AIML-BENCH-3 need. Add release dates to every row and a boolean in_training_window. Drop the monomer RMSD arm as an accuracy claim, or retain it explicitly as a memorisation floor. Keep the governance rule (no ipTM displayed without benchmark N and the measured DockQ distribution) — that is the most valuable sentence in the proposal.

critiques.scientific_objection: Gating the whole thing on a prior benchmark is the single best sequencing decision in the entire proposal set, and epitope overlap is a genuinely falsifiable test of the mechanism claims. Two rigour problems. (1) pDockQ's published sigmoid coefficients were fitted on AlphaFold2-Multimer outputs whose pLDDT and contact statistics have different semantics from Boltz-2's. Transferring those fitted coefficients to Boltz-2 output is the same category of error as borrowing the ipTM > 0.8 band, which the proposal set correctly rejects elsewhere. Either refit locally against DockQ on the AIML-STRUCT-2 benchmark or label the value as an uncalibrated transfer. (2) Jaccard overlap with the experimental epitope needs a null of its own, and not the same null as ipTM: on a 543-residue receptor, a randomly placed surface patch has expected Jaccard near zero against a specific 10-15 residue epitope, so ANY nonzero overlap will read as meaningful. The scramble decoys supply one null; a uniform-surface-placement null (or an off-target-receptor epitope null) is needed to know what a Jaccard of 0.15 means.
critiques.feasibility_objection: '1 week plus compute' plus 240 complex predictions of unmeasured cost is the least-bounded estimate on the list, and the proposal honestly says so. The reduced fallback (N=10, three candidates) is the right instinct, but at N=10 the 95th-percentile criterion in the success list is undefined — with 10 decoys the empirical 95th percentile is the maximum, so the test degenerates to 'design beats every decoy', which is a much stronger and rarer event than stated.
critiques.improvement: Refit pDockQ locally on the STRUCT-2 benchmark (predicted-vs-DockQ pairs are produced there anyway) and report both the refitted and published forms with the difference; never emit the published-coefficient value alone. Add a uniform-surface null for epitope Jaccard: sample K random surface patches of the same size on the same receptor and report the candidate's percentile against both nulls. Fix the small-N statistic: at N=10 report the exact rank and the effect size, not a percentile threshold. Validate the whole analysis stack by reproducing the KEAP1-Neh2 interface from deposited 2FLU coordinates BEFORE any prediction, as proposed — that step should be a hard gate, not an item. And merge the decoy-folding arm with AIML-STRUCT-1/AIML-BENCH-3 so 240 predictions are run once and analysed three ways.

critiques.scientific_objection: The central finding is correct and important: treating one retrieved measurement as ground truth inflated the model's own error, and the endpoint-typing point (an amyloid-beta-aggregation IC50 pooled with Ellman catalytic IC50s) is a real curation defect. Three corrections. (1) The comparison of this corpus's noise to the literature is overstated. Pooling within-compound variance properly on data/corpus_ACHE.json gives sigma = 0.421 log10 with df = 9 from FOUR compounds, 95% CI [0.289, 0.768] — Kalliokoski's 0.68 (PLoS ONE 2013, DOI 10.1371/journal.pone.0061007, verified this session: sigma_pIC50 0.68, MUE 0.55, raw R^2 0.40) sits inside that interval. The two sigmas are statistically indistinguishable, and reporting an empirical sigma without its CI reintroduces the false-precision problem the proposal is fixing. (2) The success criterion pre-states that 'the recomputed error should be near 1.4 log'. That is a predicted outcome for a quantity that depends on an endpoint-class curation not yet performed, and pre-announcing it biases the curation. (3) The unexamined defect is the SAMPLING FRAME: the corpus's own denominator records 300 activities examined for a target with vastly more, retrieved with no ORDER BY, no ChEMBL release and no retrieval timestamp. Every aggregate computed from it is an aggregate over an arbitrary, non-reproducible slice, and re-running may return a different one. Aggregation statistics do not fix a broken sampling frame.
critiques.feasibility_objection: Two days is credible; the endpoint-class table is curation and is correctly identified as the long pole. One dependency: the /assay join is a prerequisite for the confidence claim and is shared with META-3 and CBC-CC-1 — build it once.
critiques.improvement: Report sigma as 0.42 log10 [0.29, 0.77], n=4 compounds, df=9, and state that it is consistent with the published 0.68 rather than smaller than it; require the CI to render wherever the band is drawn. Rewrite the success criterion as 'the recomputed error is reported whatever it is', and freeze the aggregation rule (median vs geometric mean, handling of standard_relation '>' , handling of the amyloid class) in a pre-specification before recomputation — this is exactly META-3's freeze-before-run mechanism and should use it. Fix the frame: paginate the full activity set for the target with an explicit deterministic ordering, record chembl_release, retrieval UTC timestamp and the verbatim query URLs in the emitted file, and re-state the denominator against the true population rather than against 300. Use ChEMBL confidence 9, not 8 — that is both the 'directly assigned' tier the prose actually claims and the tier Boltz-2 trained on, which makes the same field do double duty as the leakage label.

critiques.scientific_objection: Restricting my critique to the evaluation design. The compound-mechanism-by-assay-readout join is a well-motivated hypothesis generator, but as specified it is a hand-built rule with no measured operating characteristic: nothing in the plan tells a reader how often a COLLISION flag corresponds to an actual artefact, or how often a real artefact goes unflagged. The proposed controls test only the PAINS layer's specificity (physostigmine, tacrine, donepezil return zero flags), not the join's — and the join is the novel part. Without a validation set, 'evidence_grade downgraded' is an opinion rendered as a data field, and the downstream validate.py category that fails candidates whose warhead evidence is entirely collision-flagged turns that opinion into a gate. The mechanism and readout tables are also two curated judgement layers multiplied together; their combined error rate is not the error rate of either.
critiques.feasibility_objection: 1-2 days for the code is right, and RDKit FilterCatalog avoids transcription. Restricting to Ellman/DTNB initially is the correct scope discipline. No hardware objection.
critiques.improvement: Build a small validation set from data you can already retrieve: compounds with BOTH an absorbance/Ellman-based potency and an orthogonal-readout potency (radiometric, HPLC, pH-stat, fluorogenic with a different excitation) against the same target in ChEMBL. The collision rule makes a falsifiable prediction — flagged compounds should show a larger and directionally consistent readout-to-readout discrepancy than unflagged ones. Report that difference with a CI and the n in each group; if the flagged and unflagged discrepancy distributions overlap, the rule is reported as a hypothesis label only and is not permitted to fail any gate. Add per-row citations as proposed, and record the rule's version so a downgrade can be re-evaluated when the table changes. Until validated, make evidence_grade advisory in validate.py rather than a failure category.

critiques.scientific_objection: The self/non-self exact-substring census is a genuinely rigorous construction and the control-calibration gate is the right pattern. The weakness is that the headline outputs — n_binders, n_strong_binders, n_neo_cores, n_junctional_neo — are counts with no scale. Three consequences. (1) They are monotone in the allele-panel size and in sequence length, so a 100-mer will always look worse than a 26-mer and cross-candidate comparison is confounded by both; the numbers must be normalised (per residue, per allele) and the panel frozen. (2) The mapping from predicted epitope count to observed clinical immunogenicity is weak and non-linear, so a reader will interpret 'candidate X has 47 neo-epitopes' as a risk magnitude it does not carry. (3) Without a reference distribution, 47 is uninterpretable in the same way a raw ipTM is — which is the criticism the panel is applying everywhere else and should apply here.
critiques.feasibility_objection: Sound: both predictors are CPU-only, MixMHC2pred de-risks the NetMHCIIpan licence, and the UP000005640 9-mer index is small. The junction attribution off motif_provenance is the only fiddly part and is bounded. 2-3 days is credible.
critiques.improvement: Add two reference distributions, both cheap, and report every candidate as a percentile against them rather than as a raw count: (a) a positive-context panel of >=20 marketed peptide and protein therapeutics of comparable length, scored identically — this gives the count a clinically anchored scale; (b) composition-matched shuffles of each candidate (K>=20, seeded), which separates 'this construct's epitope load' from 'any peptide of this composition and length'. The second is free to compute and reuses the scramble generator from AIML-BENCH-3. Freeze and publish the allele panel and the %Rank thresholds in a versioned protocol before scoring, and report counts normalised per 100 residues alongside the raw values. Report n_junctional_neo as a FRACTION of neo-cores and compare it to the fraction of 15-mers that are junctional — if the two are equal, the joins add no excess liability, which is the actual falsifiable claim being made about the design method.

critiques.scientific_objection: Restricting to the evaluation and reproducibility aspects. The rule that the module must be incapable of emitting a t1/2, enforced by a test, is the best refusal pattern proposed anywhere on this list and should be copied by CBC-CC-1 and DMPK-3. But the structural gating arm is where numbers appear without knowledge: relative SASA and secondary structure are read off Boltz-2 models of designed peptides whose folds are unvalidated and, per the repo's own measurements, sometimes have pLDDT near 49. Classifying a site EXPOSED-EXTENDED vs BURIED from such a model attaches a structural claim to a coordinate set that the platform has no accuracy estimate for. The proposed pLDDT<70 escape hatch helps but is a threshold chosen, not measured, and it does not cover the case of a confidently-predicted wrong fold. Second, the sequence census itself is a deterministic function of sequence with no measured relation to anything observable; 215 tryptic sites is a count, and the interesting comparison (are these constructs worse than natural peptides of similar length?) is not made.
critiques.feasibility_objection: 3-4 days is plausible; pyteomics and biotite are installed and the census already ran. The structural half depends on re-running Boltz with output persistence, which is META-1's and STRUCTBIO-IDEA-1's deliverable — do not implement it a third time.
critiques.improvement: Report the sequence census unconditionally and the structural annotation only as a conditional overlay, with the fraction of structurally-undetermined sites in the headline (as proposed) AND a statement that the structural gate inherits the unquantified accuracy of the underlying model — cross-reference the AIML-STRUCT-2 / AIML-BENCH-2 accuracy figure once it exists, and until then mark the structural arm PREDICTED-UNCALIBRATED. Give the census a scale: run the identical protease panel over a reference set of natural human peptides and marketed peptide drugs of matched length, and report each candidate's site density as a percentile. Take the mmCIF persistence work from META-1 rather than duplicating it, and make the linker-cut-fraction claim falsifiable by stating the expected fraction under uniform cutting (linker length / total length) so a reader can see whether the joins are preferentially labile or merely present.

critiques.scientific_objection: The diagnosis of the frac_cationic/frac_aromatic rule is correct and the CogDual-TrkB-PAS-10 false negative is a real, checkable finding. But the proposed replacement is presented as a calibration and is not one. Four reference peptides define a scale with no resolution: reporting that a candidate scores 0.894 against LL-37 at 0.897 licenses the inference 'as lytic as LL-37', which the hydrophobic moment alone cannot support — HC50 depends jointly on moment, net charge, length and actual helicity, and the moment-to-HC50 relation is not monotone. Second, the HemoPI2 validation is self-validation: HemoPI-class models are trained on Hemolytik-derived data, so requiring melittin to classify hemolytic and insulin B-chain non-hemolytic is a two-point check on training-set members and demonstrates nothing about held-out performance. Third, the helicity gate depends on Boltz-2 secondary-structure assignments for designed sequences whose folds are themselves unvalidated, so 'the high-moment window is actually helical' is a prediction stacked on a prediction.
critiques.feasibility_objection: Two days is credible; modlAMP is installed and the whole catalogue was already scored. The B3Pred applicability-domain gate and the RMT shuttle census are exact and cheap, and the honest refusal on BBB is the strongest part of the proposal.
critiques.improvement: Turn the 4-peptide panel into an actual calibration: assemble a reference set of sequences with MEASURED HC50 from a public hemolysis database, compute the Eisenberg moment for all of them, and report each candidate's moment percentile together with the empirical HC50 distribution observed in that percentile band, with n and interquartile range. That converts a rank into a statement with an error bar and shows honestly how weakly moment predicts HC50. For HemoPI2, either find a held-out evaluation set not derived from its training data, or state plainly that no out-of-training validation was possible and emit the classification as PREDICTED-UNVALIDATED rather than as a calibrated call — and copy DMPK-IDEA-2's pattern of making the module incapable of printing an HC50 in concentration units until it is validated. Report the moment both with and without the helicity gate so a reader can see how much the unvalidated structural assumption moves the answer.

critiques.scientific_objection: Commenting on the denominator, provenance and gate design; the genetics substance is outside my lane. Two problems. (1) The rank/percentile denominator is the right idea and the 13,289-target figure gives the score a scale for the first time — but ranking on the Open Targets OVERALL score makes the denominator circular for precisely the targets that matter here: the proposal's own table shows ACHE at rank 7 carried by literature 0.936 and clinical 0.996 (i.e. donepezil exists), with genetic_association absent. A percentile computed on a composite that includes drug existence cannot be used to argue that a drug target is genetically supported. The rank should be computed on the genetic_association datatype score, with the overall-score rank reported separately and labelled as containing clinical/literature circularity. (2) The audit() str-branch fix is genuinely important — a provenance system with a blind spot for numbers embedded in prose is a provenance system with an exemption for exactly the values nobody re-derived — and I endorse it without reservation. (3) The regex-scan-for-decimals check will have a high false-positive rate on legitimate prose (version numbers, residue ranges, pH 7.4, resolutions); it needs a suppression mechanism or it will be disabled within a week.
critiques.feasibility_objection: 2-3 days is right for the API layer. The real hazard is check_genetic_drift as a BUILD gate: it makes CI failure a function of an external service's release cadence, so the build breaks for reasons no commit caused, and the standard response will be to widen the tolerance until the gate is inert — the same fate as min_assay_confidence. A gate that depends on a moving third party is a reproducibility anti-pattern, not a reproducibility control.
critiques.improvement: Split the rank into two: genetic_association-datatype rank (the non-circular one, used for any support claim) and overall-score rank (reported, labelled circular where clinical/literature dominate). Demote check_genetic_drift from a build gate to a scheduled job that emits a dated diff artefact and opens an issue; the BUILD gate should instead assert only that every stored value carries a release token and that the stored value equals what the stored token says — an internal invariant, checkable offline forever. Give prose_embedded_number an explicit allowlist keyed by field, and report it as a count that must monotonically decrease rather than as a hard failure, so it survives contact with real text. Report, alongside every percentile, the score distribution's shape at that rank — a percentile on a long-tailed score where ranks 200-2000 differ by 0.01 conveys far less than it appears to.

critiques.scientific_objection: Commenting on the check design and the evidence-combination logic. The separation of clinical_precedence-derived direction from genetics-derived direction, with the circularity stated in code comments, is exactly right and is the kind of thing that should be enforced rather than documented. Two objections. (1) A validate.py gate that fails 34 of 35 candidates has no discriminative power going forward: after the first run it is a constant, and constants get suppressed. Its information content is in the initial census, not in its continued firing. (2) UNDETERMINED as the default is correct, but the four constituent signals are not independent and the rubric that combines them is unspecified — 'a small explicit rubric' is where all the judgement lives, and if it is written after the signals are retrieved it inherits the same after-the-fact degrees of freedom the panel is otherwise trying to eliminate. The proposal's own data shows why this matters: TREM2's colocalisation sign ratios include +1, -1 and 0 across credible sets, so the rubric's tie-breaking rule determines the verdict for the platform's only genetically-supported target.
critiques.feasibility_objection: 3-4 days for the API layer is credible; the queries reportedly run. The local cis-MR/coloc extension is correctly scoped as CPU-only and small, but adding a week for it while 15 of 16 targets have zero AD GWAS credible sets means the extension buys almost nothing for this target set — spend it only on TREM2 and say so.
critiques.improvement: Write the combination rubric as a pre-registered decision table — every combination of the four signals mapped to CONCORDANT/DISCORDANT/UNDETERMINED — and freeze its hash BEFORE retrieving the direction data, using META-3's freeze mechanism. Make the fixture test bidirectional as proposed (flip the modality, verdict must flip) and add the null test (delete a signal, verdict must degrade to UNDETERMINED). Replace the blanket build gate with a census metric: report the count of candidates asserting a direction without genetic support, require it to be non-increasing across commits, and fail only on regression. For TREM2, publish the per-credible-set sign ratios as a list with their h4/CLPP, and state explicitly that a sign is not determined rather than reporting a majority vote.

critiques.scientific_objection: This is the highest-value item on the list and the diagnosis is right on every count: the introspection gap in provenance.software, the missing seed, the discarded coordinates, and the four ledger ARTIFACT hash mismatches. One rigour problem in the part that carries a scientific conclusion. The noise envelope is to be estimated from three different seeds on ONE candidate, and then used as a decision rule ('downgrade any delta smaller than 2x the envelope'). An sd from n=3 has roughly 2 degrees of freedom and a 95% CI spanning something like half to several times the point estimate; a threshold built on it will misclassify legacy deltas in both directions. Worse, the envelope is not a single number: seed variance for a confidently-predicted lone helix (the 22 legacy runs) is a different quantity from the 0.133 ipTM sd measured on a two-chain complex, and it will differ across candidates by fold confidence. Applying one envelope to 22 heterogeneous deltas repeats, in miniature, the error of applying one borrowed threshold everywhere.
critiques.feasibility_objection: None material. The stated 2-3 days plus overnight MPS is realistic, and the decision NOT to containerise the Boltz layer — because Docker on macOS has no Metal passthrough and would silently fall back to CPU — is the most honest engineering judgement in the whole set. The git finding (nothing under platform/, data/, memory/ is tracked, so a cloner receives only the discredited mockup) should be sequenced first: every other proposal's reproducibility claims are void until it lands.
critiques.improvement: Measure the envelope per quantity and per regime: >=10 seeds on >=3 candidates spanning the confidence range, reported as sd with its CI, separately for pLDDT and for the complex metrics. Then replace the '2x envelope' heuristic with an explicit test — for each legacy delta, is it outside the seed distribution's 95% interval for THAT candidate's regime? — and report the three-way classification (exceeds noise / inside noise / untested because that candidate was not re-folded). Keep one arm at diffusion_samples=1 to match the legacy configuration, otherwise the envelope is not comparable to the deltas it is judging. Adopt the quantified-divergence wording for determinism everywhere (AIML-STRUCT-3 should copy it rather than promising byte-reproducibility). Land git tracking, LICENSE and the ledger re-hash check before anything else on this list starts.

critiques.scientific_objection: Two objections, one of them a sequencing hazard rather than a technical flaw. (1) Provenance is not validity. Exporting a well-formed PROV-O graph and an RO-Crate over values whose accuracy is still unmeasured increases the apparent authority of unvalidated numbers — a machine-traversable chain from a pLDDT to its inputs says nothing about whether that pLDDT means anything, and a FAIR-badged artefact is more likely to be reused uncritically than an unpackaged one. The genuinely novel content the proposal identifies (typed NOT_COMPUTED reasons and prov:wasInvalidatedBy on retractions) is real and I would keep it; the crate, the DOI and the JOSS submission are packaging that competes for the same days as measurement. (2) The publication plan proposes a preprint whose headline claims are '19 of 22 pLDDT values overstated by up to 46 units' and 'ipTM identically 0.00' — but META-1 exists precisely because the first claim may be inside sampling noise, and the second is a definitional artefact of folding lone chains rather than a finding about the legacy data. Publishing those before the seed envelope is measured would reproduce the original error at one remove, in a citable venue. (3) Minor but concrete: an HTTP HEAD 200 from a resolver is not evidence that a record exists; resolvers commonly return 200 for a well-formed but non-existent accession. Validate against the source API's record endpoint.
critiques.feasibility_objection: 3-4 days is credible for the export code, but the JOSS route is correctly identified as blocked on META-1 (OSI licence, public repo, install docs), and the Zenodo DOI is blocked on the same. So the deliverable that would take real time — the preprint — is the one that should not be written yet. Effectively this proposal cannot start until META-1 finishes, which makes its stated feasibility optimistic in ordering rather than in effort.
critiques.improvement: Split it. Do now, cheaply: the source_iri typing with validation against source APIs (not resolver HEAD), the LICENSE files with the ChEMBL CC-BY-SA inheritance stated for corpus_ACHE.json, and CITATION.cff. Defer the RO-Crate, the DOI and JOSS until at least one accuracy figure with an interval exists, so the packaged artefact packages a measurement and not just a lineage.
