Rewrite the preprint plan around what will actually be defensible after META-1 and AIML-STRUCT-1: the seed-variance envelope for Boltz-2 on MPS in single-sequence mode, the composition-matched null result, and the criterion-exercise audit — all methodological negatives that are novel and that survive their own scrutiny. Hold the pLDDT-overstatement claim until it is re-expressed against the measured envelope.

critiques.scientific_objection: The criterion-exercise audit is the most generalisable idea on this list — a check that a stated filter actually fired is a class of bug nobody instruments, and the min_assay_confidence case is a textbook instance (I verified it: every assay_confidence in data/corpus_ACHE.json is null because confidence_score is an /assay field read off /activity). But as specified the audit conflates two different failures. A rejection count of zero can mean (a) the criterion was never evaluated because the field was always absent — the real bug — or (b) the criterion was evaluated on every record and legitimately rejected none, which happens routinely when an upstream server-side filter already excluded the rejects. Flagging (b) as NOT_EXERCISED produces false positives that will get the check suppressed. Second, the pre-registration is incomplete in the way that matters: the decision rule is written as 'MAE upper CI below X and rho above Y' with X and Y unspecified. A pre-specification with unfilled thresholds is not a pre-specification; the degrees of freedom it is supposed to remove are exactly the ones left open. Third, the thresholds cannot be chosen freely: the achievable floor is the data's own noise (measured on this corpus at sigma = 0.42 log10, 95% CI [0.29, 0.77], df=9 from 4 compounds; consistent with Kalliokoski 2013, DOI 10.1371/journal.pone.0061007, sigma 0.68) and the ceiling is the per-target-median null. Any X below the floor is unattainable; any X above the null is unearned.
critiques.feasibility_objection: Two days for the format and the freeze/verify commands is right. But the append-only JSONL ledger on a local filesystem is not a timestamp anyone else can trust — the author can rewrite the file, and the repository is not even in version control (per META-1). Calling this 'hash-locked pre-specification' overstates what it guarantees. Also: n=18 compounds makes affinity-ache-v1 a pilot whose CI will be uninformative whichever way the point estimate falls, and the pre-spec should say so rather than implying a verdict is obtainable.
critiques.improvement: Instrument the audit at two counters per criterion — evaluated and rejected — and define NOT_EXERCISED as evaluated == 0 (a genuine wiring bug), NON_BINDING as evaluated > 0 and rejected == 0 (which the protocol must declare as expected or not). Express the flag as a binomial statement rather than an N>=50 rule of thumb. Fill in X and Y numerically before freezing, and justify them against the two anchors: require the MAE upper CI bound to be below the per-target-median null's MAE by a stated margin, and acknowledge the ~0.4-0.7 log noise floor as the point below which no threshold is meaningful. Declare affinity-ache-v1 as a pilot with a pre-computed expected CI width at n=18, plus a stopping rule for when the multi-target corpus reaches n>=50. For the timestamp, either push the frozen hash to a location the author does not control (a signed git tag on the remote, or an OSF/Zenodo registration) or state in the protocol that this is a self-discipline device with no external guarantee — the honest framing is itself in the spirit of the project. Finally, fold in the ChEMBL confidence-9 point: the level the prose should claim is 9, and it doubles as the Boltz-2 affinity-training membership predicate, which the pre-spec must record as the training-contamination label rather than as a caveat sentence.

critiques.critic: PhD computational chemist, 19 years; free-energy calculation (alchemical FEP, MM-GB/PBSA), docking-score validation and decoy/null design, implicit-solvent modelling. Scored only the proposals touching binding thermodynamics, scoring-function validation, pose/interface geometry and solvent-accessibility; skipped GENO-A/B/C, DMPK-IDEA-1 and META-2 as outside my competence. All code claims below were checked against the files in /Users/seunghojung/Documents/DeepMind_Bio.

critiques.scientific_objection: The null is mis-constructed in two ways. (1) Variance components are unmatched: the native gets 5 seeds (median of 5) while each decoy gets 1 seed. The pilot's own number says across-seed sd is 0.133 on a 0-1 metric, so each decoy value carries a full unit of sampling noise that the native median has averaged away by sqrt(5). The comparison 'decoy_single >= native_median' is therefore not a test of sequence identity; it is a test of sequence identity plus one unshared draw of diffusion noise, and its calibration is unknown. (2) The scramble is confounded with the property that actually drives promiscuous binding in this molecule class. A Fisher-Yates shuffle preserves composition, charge, pI and GRAVY exactly (correct, and worth stating) but destroys facial segregation, i.e. the hydrophobic moment. B1 is an ideally amphipathic Arg/Trp design; its shuffles sit lower in mean hydrophobic moment. So 'design beats scramble' would be partially a test of 'is this sequence more amphipathic', which is a liability signal, not a specificity signal. The off-target receptor panel is the control that actually isolates specificity, and it is currently the junior arm of the design. Separately, item 7 is right that the PAE-asymmetry gate misfires, but re-deriving the threshold from real two-chain Boltz output tunes the fraud detector on the data it is supposed to police. Note also a defect the proposal missed: predictor.py:392-398 scans only the top-left min(n,60) x min(n,60) block of the PAE matrix, so for a 543-residue receptor followed by a 36-mer the asymmetry check never looks at the interface at all. The threshold is not the only broken part; the sampling window is.
critiques.feasibility_objection: The compute estimate is out by roughly a factor of two. 35 candidates x 26 runs = 910 predictions. At the 3 min 4 s measured elsewhere in this panel for hAChE(543) + one small ligand, and with a 36-mer peptide chain rather than a ligand, that is 45-50 h of unattended MPS minimum, worse for the larger receptors (TLR4/MD-2, TrkB Ig2 is fine, full-length constructs are not). '24 h' is not achievable, and it collides with the 100+ h of MPS the rest of this panel is also requesting on one laptop.
critiques.improvement: Match seeds across arms and reduce breadth to pay for it: 3 seeds for the native, 3 seeds for each of 8 scrambles, 3 seeds for each of 3 off-target receptors, on 10 candidates first (10 x 12 x 3 = 360 runs, ~18 h). Analyse per-sequence means with a nested model (sequence as the unit, seeds as the within-sequence replicate) rather than comparing single decoy draws against a native median; report the between-sequence sd and the within-sequence sd separately so a reader can see which dominates. Add hydrophobic moment (Eisenberg, 18-residue window) as a recorded covariate on every scramble and report ipTM-vs-moment, so a positive result can be checked for the amphipathicity confound. Promote the off-target panel to the primary specificity statistic and demote the scramble to a secondary composition control. For the PAE gate: make it scale-relative (flag only when |PAE_ij - PAE_ji| exceeds a fraction of 0.5*(PAE_ij+PAE_ji) AND both entries are below ~10 A, since PAE saturates near 30 A and asymmetry there is uninformative), and fix the 60x60 window to sample the full matrix or an explicit inter-chain block.

critiques.scientific_objection: Three problems. (1) The calibration is deliberately performed in a configuration the proposal's own sibling (AIML-STRUCT-3) shows to be degraded, on the argument that it must match production. That is backwards: fix the production configuration first (receptor MSA, seeded, diffusion_samples>1), then calibrate once. Calibrating a crippled pipeline institutionalises the crippling. (2) DockQ >= 0.23 is the CAPRI acceptable threshold defined for protein-protein docking. Applying it unmodified to 5-40 residue partners is not obviously valid: fnat and iRMSD are computed over a handful of interface residues, so DockQ becomes coarse and high-variance at the short end of that range, and the field's usual criterion for peptide placement is ligand/peptide RMSD. A 5-mer and a 40-mer should not sit in the same reliability curve. (3) The leakage control is at the wrong level. Deduplicating at 30-40% identity on the RECEPTOR does not remove motif-level memorisation: post-cutoff SH3/PDZ/MHC/kinase-substrate complexes present the same short motif classes the model saw thousands of times pre-cutoff. Temporal holdout on the entry release date is necessary, not sufficient. Also: the 2023-06-01 Boltz-2 PDB cutoff should be retrieved from the paper or repo and pinned, not carried in from recall - that is the exact failure mode this repository exists to prevent.
critiques.feasibility_objection: n=100 will not support the deliverable as written. Split across ipTM bins you get ~10-25 per bin; Wilson intervals on P(DockQ>=0.23) will be roughly +/-0.20-0.30 wide, and expected calibration error computed on 5 bins at n=100 is dominated by binomial noise. AUROC at n=100 has a bootstrap CI of roughly +/-0.10. The clustering call is admitted to be unvalidated (HTTP 400), and receptor-side mmseqs2 clustering plus chain mapping for DockQ is the real time sink, not the inference.
critiques.improvement: Run the calibration in the FIXED production configuration (receptor MSA, seed recorded, diffusion_samples=5, top-1 rule declared in advance), and state explicitly that the curve is valid only for that configuration. Stratify by partner length (5-15 / 16-40) and by partner net charge, and refuse extrapolation outside populated STRATA, not merely outside populated ipTM bins - the 35 candidates are 26-100 residue polycations and will fall outside every stratum you can populate, which is itself the honest headline. Report the primary success metric for the peptide arm as symmetry-corrected peptide RMSD <= 2 A with DockQ as secondary. Raise n to ~250 if you want a curve; at n=100 commit to three bins and say so. Add motif-level leakage control: max sequence identity of the PARTNER to any pre-cutoff partner of a homologous receptor, and stratify metrics on it.

critiques.scientific_objection: The core is correct and is a prerequisite for every other structural proposal here: an unseeded diffusion_samples=1 point estimate reported without a spread is the same epistemic error as the original hardcoded values with a real model behind it. Two corrections. First, the 0.133 ipTM sd was measured at n=3; the relative standard error of an sd estimate at n=3 is about 50%, so the true sd could plausibly be 0.07 or 0.20. Do not let a 3-seed pilot set error bars for the platform. Second, and this matters for META-1's downstream use: the pilot measured the seed spread of ipTM, which is interface-dependent and often bimodal (docked vs undocked), not of mean pLDDT, which is an average over hundreds of residues and will have a much smaller across-seed sd. It is not legitimate to argue from ipTM sd = 0.133 that a 10-unit pLDDT delta might be noise; the pLDDT envelope must be measured on its own.
critiques.feasibility_objection: The success criterion 'data/real_vs_hardcoded.json is byte-reproducible on a second execution' is not achievable on this hardware. Metal/MPS kernels use non-deterministic reduction orders and torch.use_deterministic_algorithms has incomplete MPS coverage; the proposal itself notes aten::linalg_svd silently falls back to CPU, which is exactly the kind of backend dispatch that breaks bitwise determinism. Seeding fixes the noise draw, not the floating-point summation order.
critiques.improvement: Replace 'byte-reproducible' with a stated numerical tolerance: same seed twice must agree to within a committed epsilon on every reported scalar (measure it, do not assume it), and record that MPS is not bitwise deterministic in the manifest rather than promising something the backend cannot deliver. Use n>=5 seeds and report a CI on the sd itself, not just the sd. Measure the pLDDT-specific across-seed envelope separately from the ipTM envelope. In the MSA factorial, keep the peptide chain at msa=empty (correct, and correctly justified) but note that receptor-MSA + empty-peptide-MSA is precisely the production config for candidates, whereas the 1YCR control has an MSA for both chains - so the 1YCR delta is not an estimate of the candidate-case MSA effect and must not be quoted as one. Finally, the affinity-head retest in step 4 is the single highest-value item in this proposal; do it first, it is one run.

critiques.scientific_objection: Structurally the right benchmark, and the insistence on a measured noise ceiling and a null floor is exactly the discipline docking-score validation requires. Four corrections. (1) The sigma_exp estimator needs stating: for two independent measurements of sd sigma, E|delta| = sigma*2/sqrt(pi), so mean|dlog10| = 0.448 implies sigma = 0.397, not 0.376 - a small gap, but the whole point is that the estimator must be inspectable. At n=18 pairs the CI on sigma is roughly +/-25-30% relative, and the distribution is heavy-tailed (a 1.04-log NEOSTIGMINE pair), so a Gaussian sigma is a poor summary. (2) This quantity is between-ASSAY reproducibility, not measurement noise: it conflates substrate concentration, enzyme source and pH with error. That is the correct ceiling for 'predict a randomly drawn literature IC50' but NOT for 'predict a consensus value', and the two differ by roughly sqrt(n_replicates). This proposal aggregates to a geometric mean while MEDCHEM-IDEA-2 also aggregates; if the target is an aggregate, the ceiling tightens and the model necessarily looks worse. The two proposals must agree on one convention or the error/ceiling ratio is arbitrary. (3) Pooling Ki, Kd and IC50 into one pAct injects a systematic offset (for a competitive inhibitor at [S] ~ Km, IC50 ~ 2*Ki, i.e. 0.3 log) that is not noise and should not be absorbed into sigma_exp. (4) A subtle leakage point the proposal misses: Boltz-2's affinity head is trained on IC50/Ki/Kd pooled and mapped to log10(uM), so 'training-set membership' is not only per-compound but per-ASSAY-VALUE; a compound absent from the pre-cutoff snapshot can still have a near-identical analogue measured in the same document.
critiques.feasibility_objection: Two hundred complexes in both MSA arms is ~20 h, not 10, and the ground-truth curation is gated on ChEMBL availability - the ChEMBL REST API returned HTTP 500 to me repeatedly this session (direct and via MCP), which is a live argument for pinning a release snapshot locally rather than fetching at build time.
critiques.improvement: Report sigma_exp as a distribution (median |delta|, MAD-based robust scale, and a bootstrap CI) rather than a single Gaussian sigma, with the estimator written out. Compute and report TWO ceilings: for predicting a single randomly drawn literature value, and for predicting the n-replicate aggregate, and state which one each headline metric is scored against. Restrict the primary benchmark to one endpoint class (human recombinant AChE, Ellman catalytic IC50) and report Ki/Kd as a labelled secondary set rather than pooling. Pin and commit the ChEMBL release id and retrieval timestamp with the snapshot. Keep the hard rule in (6) - it is the single best thing in this proposal.

critiques.scientific_objection: The most consequential omission is that Boltz-2 co-folds, it does not dock into a rigid experimental receptor. Superposing the model onto the reference by global Kabsch over all matched C-alpha and then transforming the ligand conflates receptor-model error with pose error, and it is systematically punitive for AChE, which has a mobile Omega-loop and a 20 A gorge whose walls shift between structures. Pocket-aligned RMSD (align on reference residues within 8-10 A of the reference ligand) is the standard for co-folding evaluation and must be the primary number, with global-aligned RMSD and receptor C-alpha RMSD reported alongside so the two error sources are separable. Second: PoseBusters redock-mode intermolecular checks (volume overlap, protein-ligand clash) are run against the PREDICTED receptor, which has relaxed around its own ligand. Co-folding models therefore pass steric validity more easily than rigid-receptor docking poses, so the headline comparison to 'classical docking beat DL methods once physical validity was enforced' is not apples to apples and must be caveated. Third: the post-2023-06-01 'temporal holdout' of 81 AChE/BuChE/MAO/BACE1 holo entries is largely a recall set in disguise. A 2024 hAChE structure with a donepezil analogue sits in a pocket seen hundreds of times pre-cutoff, often with near-identical ligands. Entry release date does not make the (pocket, chemotype) pair novel.
critiques.feasibility_objection: Feasible as stated (3 min/complex, ~6 h batch, pure-Python posebusters/spyrmsd wheels). Minor: the reference ligand may have alternate conformers/partial occupancy and crystallographic symmetry mates - a pose can be 'correct' against a symmetry copy - and the fetch/parse layer must handle that or a handful of cases will be scored wrong.
critiques.improvement: Make pocket-aligned symmetry-corrected RMSD the primary metric; report global-aligned RMSD and receptor pocket C-alpha RMSD as separate columns. Add, per holdout case, max ECFP4 Tanimoto from the deposited ligand to every pre-cutoff ligand of the SAME target, and stratify both headline proportions into <0.4 / 0.4-0.7 / >0.7 bins exactly as AIML-BENCH-1 does for affinity - this is the change that converts a pseudo-holdout into a real one and it costs minutes of CPU. State in the output file that PoseBusters intermolecular checks are evaluated against the co-folded receptor. Handle altloc/occupancy and symmetry mates explicitly in the reference-ligand fetch. The 4EY5-versus-existing-model first data point is genuinely free and should be done this week.

critiques.scientific_objection: The design is arithmetically incapable of producing its stated result. With K=20 controls the smallest attainable empirical p is (1+0)/(1+20) = 0.0476. Holm-Bonferroni across ten candidates requires the smallest p to be <= 0.05/10 = 0.005 to reject anything. So no candidate can ever be declared 'sequence-specific (Holm-corrected p < 0.05)' - one of the two stated verdict strings is unreachable by construction, and the experiment can only ever return the null. You need K >= 199 controls per candidate for the smallest Holm step to be attainable, which is 2000 co-folds and not affordable here. Second, the scramble null is confounded with hydrophobic moment exactly as in AIML-STRUCT-1: shuffling destroys facial segregation, so beating the null partly measures amphipathicity rather than design intent. Third, this proposal, AIML-STRUCT-1 and STRUCTBIO-IDEA-3 are three overlapping scramble-control experiments requesting three separate overnight batches on one laptop; only one should be built.
critiques.feasibility_objection: 210 co-folds at ~3 min each is 11 h only if every receptor is AChE-sized and every run is one diffusion sample at one seed. With no seed replication the per-sequence values carry the full 0.133-sd diffusion noise the pilot measured, so the experiment is underpowered even before the multiple-testing problem bites.
critiques.improvement: Abandon per-candidate Holm correction and reframe the statistic. Either (a) pool the null across candidates against a common receptor - 10 candidates x 8 scrambles = 80 null draws against hAChE gives a shared null distribution with usable resolution, and score each design as a z against that pooled null with a bootstrap CI; or (b) declare a fixed effect-size criterion in advance (e.g. design exceeds mean(controls) + 2 sd(controls) on both ipTM and interface-contact count, with 3 seeds per sequence) and report it as an effect size with an interval, not as a hypothesis test. Point (6) - demonstrating that MW, net charge, pI and GRAVY are order-invariant by construction and relabelling them on the candidate cards - is excellent, costs zero compute, is provable analytically rather than empirically, and should be shipped immediately and independently of any folding. Merge the folding arm into AIML-STRUCT-1.

critiques.scientific_objection: Concrete bug in the arithmetic this proposal calls 'arithmetically sound'. The ledger records the Boltz conversion as dG = (6 - y) * 1.364 with y = log10(IC50/uM). For a 1 nM binder, y = -3 and the formula returns +12.28 kcal/mol - POSITIVE. The platform's own thermo.kd_to_dg(1e-9) returns -12.28. The sign convention is inverted relative to thermo.py. If CBC-CC-1 writes that value into binding_free_energy or through thermo.check(), the implausibility guard (which fires when dG < -18.3) can never fire, and a nonsensically tight prediction will pass every check silently. Second, and more fundamental: the affinity head emits an assay-blended potency, and IC50 is not Kd. Converting IC50 to a standard-state binding free energy requires Cheng-Prusoff (competitive mechanism, known [S] and Km) - for Ellman assays at [S] near Km that is a ~0.3 log offset, small, but the point is that a quantity trained on pooled Ki/Kd/IC50 has no defined thermodynamic referent at all. Emitting it as binding_free_energy is a category error independent of how good the RMSE turns out to be. Third, writing the measured number into thermo.METHOD_ACCURACY as an rmse_kcal alongside FEP (1.1) and MM-GBSA (2.5) invites a reader to compare a potency-prediction error to a free-energy error as if they were the same quantity.
critiques.feasibility_objection: The >=60-pair target is very likely unreachable under the stated protocol. The AChE run admitted 18 of 258 (93% rejected as SYNTHETIC by np_tier), and KEAP1, CHRM1 and NOS3 have far thinner natural-product coverage than AChE. Compounding this, the affinity head's own limits (<=128 heavy atoms, not recommended >56) exclude the largest and most interesting NPs - Onjisaponin V at 123 heavy atoms sits at 2.2x the recommended limit and Ginsenoside Rg1 at 56 is on the boundary. So the reachable set is small, chemically narrow and biased toward the smallest scaffolds.
critiques.improvement: Never emit a dG. Add a new provenanced field predicted_potency_log10 with units 'log10(IC50/uM)', and make it structurally impossible for any code path to convert it into binding_free_energy - assert this with a test, the same way CBC-CC-3 proposes to block MM-GBSA. If a kcal/mol number is wanted for human reading, print it as '-RT ln10 * (6-y) kcal/mol, IC50-derived, not a standard-state binding free energy' with the sign fixed to match thermo.py, and keep it out of the dataset. Drop the natural-product restriction for the BENCHMARK set - the benchmark measures the predictor, not the corpus theme - and draw >=60 pairs from all ChEMBL matter for those targets, which also widens the dynamic range and stratifies leakage properly. Keep the decoy-receptor AUROC on affinity_probability_binary: it is the best idea in this proposal and the cheapest, since the 0.44 value is uninterpretable without it. Report within-target Spearman as primary and pooled cross-target Spearman as secondary, since pooled rho is inflated by between-target potency spread.

critiques.scientific_objection: The pre-registered gate is beatable by a predictor with zero information. RMSE <= 2.0 kcal/mol is an absolute threshold, but the spread of measured dG in protein-peptide affinity sets is narrow - typically about -6 to -11 kcal/mol, sd roughly 1.3 - so 'predict the set mean' already achieves RMSE ~1.3 and would PASS a 2.0 kcal/mol gate while carrying no information at all. A pre-registered rule that a constant predictor satisfies is not a pre-registered rule. Second, a structural objection to PRODIGY specifically that is checkable in minutes and would likely kill the whole arm: PRODIGY's regression is contact counts plus non-interacting-surface (NIS) terms computed over the WHOLE complex. For a 543-residue receptor plus a 36-mer peptide, the NIS terms are essentially properties of the receptor alone, so PRODIGY's predicted dG will be nearly constant across all candidates against a common target - the method may be unable to RANK the candidates it is being asked to rank, independently of its absolute error. Third, reproducing r = -0.73 / RMSE 1.89 on the eLife set validates the install, but that is the set the regression was FIT on; quoting it as 'published performance recovered' conflates a training statistic with accuracy. Fourth, the argument for installing rather than transcribing the equation - because two retrievals gave sign-flipped forms - is exactly right and should be the general rule for every fitted coefficient in this panel (see STRUCTBIO-IDEA-3's pDockQ).
critiques.feasibility_objection: '~1 week' is not credible. Step 4(a) requires co-folding the Kastritis structure-based affinity benchmark subset - dozens to 144 protein-protein complexes, many of them multi-chain and several hundred residues per chain, i.e. token counts far above the 580 measured for AChE+peptide, with pair-representation cost scaling roughly as N^2. That alone is multiple days of unattended MPS, on top of the peptide set in 4(b) and the 35 candidate co-folds.
critiques.improvement: Run the near-zero-cost falsification FIRST, before any benchmark: take one deposited AChE-peptide or AChE-protein complex, thread ten different 36-mer sequences onto the peptide chain, and run PRODIGY on all ten. If the predicted dG range across ten different peptides is smaller than the method's own 1.89 kcal/mol RMSE, the method cannot rank this catalogue and the entire arm can be closed in an afternoon with a measured, publishable refusal. Replace the absolute 2.0 kcal/mol gate with a relative one: PRODIGY must beat 'predict the set mean' by a paired bootstrap whose 95% CI on the RMSE delta excludes zero, AND achieve Spearman rho with a CI excluding zero. Report the crystal-benchmark reproduction explicitly as a training-set statistic, and add a held-out or cross-validated figure as the accuracy anchor. Keep step 6 (unconstrained co-folds primary, pocket-constrained runs labelled hypothesis-conditioned) - that distinction is correct and rare.

critiques.scientific_objection: The refusal half is the best-argued paragraph in the whole panel: single-trajectory MM-GBSA on 26-100 residue polycations with no congeneric series is not a free-energy method, the 2.5 kcal/mol figure in thermo.METHOD_ACCURACY does not transfer, and blocking it in code is right. Three objections to the rest. (1) The proposed uncertainty arithmetic is invalid: 'combine the isomer spread in quadrature with the method RMSE' treats a range over DISTINCT CHEMICAL SPECIES as if it were an independent Gaussian error term on one molecule. It is not - it is a scenario range, and quadrature is undefined for it. (2) The enumeration undercounts. I counted the sequences: 21 candidates carry >=4 Cys, but TWO carry NINE (CogDual-TrkB-PAS-10, CogTrk-DeNovo-01), which admits 9 x 105 = 945 four-disulfide topologies, not 105 - and the enumeration assumes MAXIMAL pairing, whereas partial pairing with free thiols is chemically available and expands the space further. (3) The implicit-solvent filter is uncalibrated and, as specified, close to vacuous. No timescale is given; interface dissociation is a microsecond-to-millisecond process, and OpenMM on this machine has no MPS backend (Reference/CPU/OpenCL only, as the proposal's own probe found), so a 600-residue GB system will yield tens of ns/day at best. Essentially every isomer will 'survive' any affordable trajectory, so pass/fail carries no information. Compounding this, Amber14/GBn2 with no salt screening over-stabilises salt bridges at net charge +8 and has no explicit water to mediate the H-bonds that dominate peptide-protein interfaces. Finally, forcing a topology with a Boltz bond constraint and reading the resulting ipTM measures how much the MODEL dislikes that topology, not the free energy of the isomer.
critiques.feasibility_objection: 1-1.5 weeks is optimistic by a large factor once OpenCL-rather-than-CUDA throughput is priced in for 100-150 systems, each needing minimisation, restrained equilibration and unrestrained MD, on top of 100-150 constrained co-folds. The SG-SG bond-constraint verification step may also simply fail (the docs do not confirm intra-chain SG-SG), in which case the whole enforcement mechanism has to be rebuilt in the relaxation stage.
critiques.improvement: Report the isomer spread as an explicit min/median/max SCENARIO RANGE and forbid quadrature combination in code; if a single conservative number is required, use the worst case and label it as such. Correct the enumeration to cover 9-Cys candidates (945 maximal-pairing topologies) and state explicitly that partial pairing is excluded by assumption. Replace 'interface survives vs dissolves' with a quantitative short-timescale observable - fraction of interface heavy-atom contacts retained over N>=3 replicate 20 ns runs, with a stated tolerance - and require that the criterion first SEPARATE three positive controls (deposited peptide-receptor complexes) from three composition-matched scrambled negatives before any candidate is scored. If the controls do not separate, publish that the filter has no discriminative power and stop. Price the OpenCL throughput with a single timed benchmark system before committing. And say plainly in the output that the ipTM spread across forced topologies is a model-preference spread, not a thermodynamic one.

critiques.scientific_objection: Scientifically the soundest cheap item on the list, and the chemistry is right: S-S at 2.03-2.06 A with chi3 near +/-90 degrees is textbook, a 1.705 A S-S is impossible, a chi3 of -1.1 degrees is eclipsed, and a sulfur in two bonds is not a thing. Three corrections. (1) The 2.5 A detection cutoff is too generous for calling a BOND: at a mean of 2.081 A with sd 0.203 it is more than 2 sd out, so some of the 38 'S-S contacts' and probably some of the four trivalent-sulfur calls are close packing rather than bonding. Use a three-band classification (bonded 2.05 +/- 0.25; ambiguous 2.30-3.00; non-bonded >3.00) and publish the histogram, otherwise the headline 'four candidates have chemically impossible sulfur' is partly an artefact of the cutoff. (2) The reference distribution from ~60 deposited structures is not independent evidence of ideal geometry: bond lengths and angles in refined crystal structures are shaped by Engh-Huber restraints applied during refinement, so you are measuring the restraint targets, not nature. That is fine for a false-positive check but must not be described as an empirical validation of the geometry criteria. (3) Emitting disulfide_connectivity as PREDICTED from coordinates produced by a model that never enforced disulfide bonding is thin evidence - it records what the diffusion sampler happened to draw on one unseeded run, which is precisely the variance problem AIML-STRUCT-3 and META-1 identify.
critiques.feasibility_objection: None material - the analysis ran in under a second, gemmi is already installed, and the 22 mmCIFs exist. The one real dependency is step 6 (moving the coordinates out of /tmp), which should be done before anything else in the panel touches them.
critiques.improvement: Adopt the three-band S-S classification and publish the distance histogram alongside the counts. Describe the crystal reference set as a false-positive control, not as an independent geometry standard. Gate the disulfide_connectivity emission on seed replication: only emit PREDICTED where the same connectivity is recovered across >=3 seeds, and record the per-seed agreement fraction in the uncertainty field; otherwise leave not_computed. Do step 6 (durable coordinate storage with recorded paths and sha256) FIRST and independently - every other structural proposal in this panel silently assumes those files exist.

critiques.scientific_objection: Substantially the same experiment as AIML-STRUCT-2 with a smaller, target-specific benchmark, and the two should not both be built. Where it differs it is weaker: 16 receptor domains and a handful of peptide complexes (2FLU, 1WWW/2IFG, 3FXI) give an N far too small to calibrate anything - one to three peptide complexes cannot produce an ipTM threshold, and the proposal's own success criterion concedes this by requiring the output to say when N is too small. Where it differs it is also stronger, and this is the part worth keeping: 2FLU (KEAP1 Kelch + 16-mer Neh2 at 1.5 A) is a direct held-out test of the exact binding mode three of the platform's own candidates claim, which no generic RCSB-sampled benchmark provides. Note also that every one of these entries pre-dates the Boltz-2 PDB cutoff, so all of them measure recall, not prediction - that must be stated on the face of the table, not buried.
critiques.feasibility_objection: The receptor-monomer arm is genuinely cheap and the superposition machinery is verified. The complex arm is the cost, and the timing pilot the proposal calls for is the right instinct - full-length AChE at ~590 tokens plus a partner has not been timed, and pair-representation cost grows roughly as N^2.
critiques.improvement: Merge into AIML-STRUCT-2 as its TARGET-SPECIFIC arm rather than a parallel benchmark: AIML-STRUCT-2 supplies the ~100-250-case calibration curve, this supplies the handful of cases where the platform's own mechanistic claims are directly falsifiable. Label the entire set 'pre-cutoff: measures recall' on the face of the output. Run 2FLU with 5 seeds and report the DockQ spread across seeds, not a single value - with n=1 complex the seed spread IS the error bar. Drop any language implying that 8-16 monomer RMSDs constitute a calibration; monomer accuracy does not predict interface accuracy and should be reported as a separate, clearly labelled sanity check.

critiques.scientific_objection: The epitope-overlap arm is the most valuable thing here - it converts 'this candidate is mechanistically inverted' from an argument into a coordinate-derived measurement - but three methodological problems. (1) pDockQ is a FITTED sigmoid over log(interface contacts x mean interface pLDDT) with published coefficients. Reconstructing those coefficients from recall is exactly the prohibited act this repository was rebuilt to eliminate; CBC-CC-2 makes precisely this argument about PRODIGY. Either install a reference implementation or retrieve and pin the coefficients with a citation. (2) Jaccard overlap between a predicted epitope and an experimental epitope has no scale: it depends on the contact cutoff, on the relative sizes of the two residue sets, and on receptor surface area. A Jaccard of 0.1 is uninterpretable without a null. (3) Buried SASA computed on a co-folded model is not the same quantity as buried SASA on a crystal complex - the model relaxes both partners around each other, which inflates apparent complementarity. Interface area from a prediction should be reported with the caveat, and validated on 2FLU (as the proposal does for the analysis code) against the deposited value.
critiques.feasibility_objection: The proposal is honest that the decoy arm is the compute risk and that it 'is the arm most likely to want a GPU'. That honesty is correct, and it makes this the third overlapping request for the same scramble batch (AIML-STRUCT-1, AIML-BENCH-3, here). One batch, three consumers.
critiques.improvement: Replace bare Jaccard with precision and recall against the experimental epitope (what fraction of predicted contacts fall inside the known site, and what fraction of the known site is recovered) AND a random-patch null: place surface patches of the same residue count at random over the receptor and report where the prediction's overlap sits in that distribution. That gives the overlap a scale for a few milliseconds of CPU. Install or pin pDockQ rather than reimplementing it. Validate the whole interface module on the deposited 2FLU coordinates before any prediction is scored, and report predicted-model interface area next to crystal interface area for that case so the co-folding inflation is quantified once. Consume AIML-STRUCT-1's decoy batch rather than commissioning a third one.

critiques.scientific_objection: The burial analysis is correct and the 4EY5 numbers are chemically sensible: huperzine A is deep in the AChE gorge, N2 hydrogen bonds Tyr337-OH, the pyridone carbonyl engages Tyr133, and there is no spare handle. But the veto as specified would produce a false negative on a chemotype medicinal chemistry has demonstrably built. Bivalent AChE ligands that anchor a small heterocycle in the catalytic anionic site and tether a linker out through the gorge to the peripheral anionic site are a well-established design class; they work because the gorge is dynamic (Omega-loop breathing, aromatic side-chain rotamer changes) and a linker threads a path that a single static crystal pose shows as occluded. A NO_VECTOR verdict derived from retained SASA on one deposited structure therefore encodes 'the crystal ligand is buried', which is not the same claim as 'no substituent can escape'. Second, the linker arithmetic is wrong in the conservative direction: 3.5 A per residue is the CONTOUR length of a fully extended chain, and a Gly-Ser linker is a flexible coil whose mean end-to-end distance is far below contour. A linker sized at L/3.5 residues can only span L in a fully extended conformation, at a large entropic cost. Third, the object being vetoed is not a defined chemical entity - chemStruct is prose ('Huperzine A Pyridone Core (C15H18N2O) + Cys-Lys Amide Coupling'), with no SMILES for the conjugate - so the gate is testing an underspecified claim.
critiques.feasibility_objection: None material; biopython is installed, the RCSB fetch works, and the grid BFS is ~80 lines of numpy. The only cost is doing it across multiple deposited structures per target rather than one.
critiques.improvement: Make the ESCAPE-PATH BFS the sole basis for the veto and retire retained-SASA to a descriptor. Run the BFS with a soft-shell tolerance (probe 1.4 A plus 0.5-1.0 A slack on protein vdW radii) and repeat it over EVERY deposited holo structure of the same protein, reporting the best path across the ensemble - that is the cheapest available proxy for receptor flexibility and it costs only more downloads. Add a positive control that the method must not veto: a deposited bivalent AChE ligand spanning CAS to PAS, or failing that, donepezil in 4EY7 (which the proposal already includes). Make the verdict graded (NO_VECTOR / VECTOR_REQUIRES_FLEXIBILITY / VIABLE) rather than binary. Report the minimum linker span in Angstroms only; if a residue count is wanted, give a contour-length lower bound AND a flexible-chain estimate, and label the first as 'cannot be shorter than' rather than 'needs'. Note in the output that the conjugate has no SMILES, so the verdict applies to the attachment-point claim, not to a characterised molecule.

critiques.scientific_objection: This is the highest-leverage proposal for anyone doing scoring-function validation here, because every affinity benchmark in this panel inherits its ground truth from this layer, and the diagnosis of the inert confidence filter is verifiable from the committed data: every activity in data/corpus_ACHE.json carries assay_confidence: null, and denominator.rejected has buckets for unparseable/tier_excluded/no_structure/too_large with no low-confidence bucket at all, so the min_assay_confidence=8 criterion demonstrably never rejected anything. Two objections. (1) The headline framing is itself a choice presented as a correction. Replacing 5.0 nM with the median of 25 heterogeneous records is not obviously closer to truth; it is a different aggregation over a badly-typed pool. The honest statement is stronger than either: if the measured values span 0.54 to 5280 nM, then Boltz-2's 1274 nM prediction lies INSIDE the experimental envelope, and the correct conclusion is that this compound cannot discriminate model accuracy at all - not that the error is 1.43 log rather than 2.41. Retract the 2.41 figure, but replace it with 'ground truth is a 4-log distribution; a single-compound error figure is uninterpretable', not with a differently-computed point error. (2) Ordering matters and the proposal has it right in the method but not in the success criteria: endpoint typing must precede aggregation, because a median taken over a pool containing an Abeta-aggregation phenotype and four 'AChE (unknown origin)' records mapped to human is a number about nothing. Do not republish any recomputed error before the typing lands.
critiques.feasibility_objection: I could not verify the huperzine-A activity distribution independently this session: the ChEMBL REST API returned HTTP 500 to me on repeated direct calls and via the ChEMBL MCP server. That is not a criticism of the proposal - it is an argument for its own step of pinning a release id, a retrieval timestamp and the verbatim query URLs, since the claim currently rests on a live query nobody else can reproduce today.
critiques.improvement: State the retraction as 'the single-compound error figure is withdrawn as uninterpretable' and report, in its place, the measured distribution (n, geometric mean, median, min, max, log10 range) plus where the prediction falls within it. Do the endpoint-class typing first; only aggregate within class; and record which class each aggregate belongs to on the face of every downstream benchmark. Fix confidence_score by joining /assay, and reconcile the prose - ChEMBL confidence 8 is homologous-single-protein, 9 is direct, so the current summary overstates what the threshold denotes. Agree one aggregation convention with AIML-BENCH-1 (single-value vs consensus target) before either publishes an error/noise ratio, or the two will report incompatible ceilings. Pin the ChEMBL release and commit the snapshot.

critiques.scientific_objection: The join - flag only where the compound's reactive mechanism can actually perturb the specific readout that produced that specific value - is the right construction and is what makes PAINS usable on natural products instead of useless. Two objections within my competence. (1) The chromophore arm is weak as specified: 'extended conjugation with donor substitution' inferred from RDKit ring/conjugation perception is a very loose proxy for absorbance at 412 nm, and it will flag many polyphenols that do not interfere. The proposal is honest in calling it a heuristic and marking it PREDICTED, but a heuristic with no measured false-positive rate should not downgrade evidence. A cheap fix exists: for the small number of compounds involved, retrieve measured lambda_max/molar absorptivity where published rather than inferring it, and refuse to grade where no spectrum is available. (2) Thiol reactivity is the mechanistically decisive channel for Ellman/DTNB (scavenging thiocholine or reducing DTNB directly) and it is also the one that can be checked against measured data rather than substructure alone - GSH-adduct or thiol-trapping half-lives are published for curcumin-class Michael acceptors. Substructure match is a hypothesis; a measured thiol reactivity is evidence.
critiques.feasibility_objection: Low risk. The catalogues ship with RDKit, the join is small, and restricting to Ellman/DTNB first is the right scoping. The real cost is curating the mechanism and readout tables, which the proposal correctly identifies as judgement rather than code.
critiques.improvement: Split the interference verdict into two tiers: MECHANISM_PLAUSIBLE (substructure match plus readout collision, no measurement) and MECHANISM_MEASURED (a retrieved thiol-reactivity or absorbance measurement for that compound). Only the second should downgrade an evidence grade; the first should annotate. Require a measured lambda_max for any chromophore-based collision, and refuse rather than infer where none is retrievable. Keep the negative-control requirement (physostigmine, tacrine, donepezil, aminoacridines unflagged) - it is the check that keeps the module from degenerating into a natural-product blacklist. Make sure the module never touches the numeric value, only the grade, which the proposal already commits to.

critiques.scientific_objection: Commenting only on the structural half, which is where my competence lies. The structural gate will collapse for most of the catalogue and the proposal has already written the reason into its own step 4: sites in regions with pLDDT < 70 are 'treated as accessible'. For 26-100 residue designed peptides folded as lone chains in single-sequence mode, a large fraction of residues will be below 70, so the structural arm degenerates to the sequence arm for exactly the molecules it was supposed to discriminate. Worse, relative SASA computed on a Boltz model of a peptide whose disulfide connectivity is undefined (21 of 35 have >=4 Cys, 2 have 9) is a property of one arbitrary sampled topology, not of the molecule - CBC-CC-3 is right about that and this proposal inherits the problem without acknowledging it. The Hubbard criterion (roughly ten residues of locally extended, exposed, flexible backbone to thread a protease cleft) is also a criterion about LOCAL EXTENSION and flexibility, not about SASA and secondary-structure class alone; implementing it as EXPOSED-EXTENDED / BURIED / HELIX-CONSTRAINED loses the length-of-extended-segment requirement that does the actual work.
critiques.feasibility_objection: The sequence census is essentially done and cheap. The structural arm requires re-running 22+ folds with output persistence, and it inherits the seed-variance problem: a per-residue SASA read off one unseeded diffusion sample is a draw, not a measurement.
critiques.improvement: Report the sequence census on its own now - it is exact, reproducible from pyteomics, and the linker-cut fraction and the released-Abeta-fragment identity are genuinely informative without any structure. Gate the structural arm behind three preconditions: durable coordinates (STRUCTBIO-IDEA-1 step 6), >=3 seeds with the per-site accessibility reported as a fraction of seeds rather than a single value, and an explicit statement of the fraction of residues below pLDDT 70 per candidate - if that fraction exceeds, say, 0.5, refuse the structural annotation for that candidate rather than defaulting every site to 'accessible'. Implement the Hubbard criterion as a contiguous-extended-segment length requirement, not as a per-residue SASA/SSE label. Keep the rule that no t1/2 may ever be printed; that is exactly right.

critiques.scientific_objection: Commenting on the biophysics. Replacing the composition boolean (peptide.py:141, frac_cationic >= 0.30 AND frac_aromatic >= 0.15) with a hydrophobic moment is a clear improvement, and the false-negative on CogDual-TrkB-PAS-10 is a real finding. But the analysis as specified ranks in one dimension and will mis-rank. The Eisenberg moment is computed under an assumed ideal alpha-helix at 100 degrees per residue; the control panel itself demonstrates that mu_H alone does not order lytic potency, since melittin (0.558) is far more hemolytic than its moment relative to LL-37 (0.897) would suggest. Lytic behaviour is a joint function of mean hydrophobicity and moment - the classical reading is the two-dimensional Eisenberg plane, not a scalar - plus charge, length and, decisively, whether the peptide is actually helical. For the Cys-rich candidates it is not, and the moment is then a number about a conformation the molecule does not adopt. Reporting 'six candidates score at or above LL-37' as if that ordered their lytic risk repeats, in a smaller way, the error of reporting a number whose meaning has not been established.
critiques.feasibility_objection: Low risk for the moment calculation and the control panel (already executed). HemoPI2 adds a large model download and its applicability domain on length will likely exclude the largest candidates, which are the ones the proposal most wants to score - so the deliverable there may be mostly refusals, which is fine but should be predicted up front. The B3Pred domain gate and the RMT motif census are exact substring work and carry no risk.
critiques.improvement: Report mu_H and mean hydrophobicity as a two-dimensional position with the four controls plotted in the same plane, and stop ranking on mu_H alone. Gate every moment on the predicted secondary structure of the window it was computed over (using the persisted Boltz coordinates and the pLDDT-fraction rule above); where the window is not helical, emit the moment as 'conditional on an assumed helix' or refuse. Keep the runtime recomputation of the controls and the melittin 0.558 +/- 0.001 tripwire - that is a good, checkable calibration gate. The BBB half is the strongest part and needs no change: an explicit count of how many of 35 candidates any peptide BBB predictor can legitimately accept, plus a deterministic RMT-shuttle substring census with a DOI per entry, is a real answer where a prediction would have been a guess.

critiques.scientific_objection: The diagnosis is correct and the seeding fix is a prerequisite for essentially every other structural proposal here - I confirmed that run_boltz (structure.py:191-195) never passes --seed and that _collect_boltz_outputs keeps sorted(cifs)[0], discarding every sample beyond the first. One scientific correction to step 2. The proposed rule - downgrade any legacy pLDDT delta smaller than 2x the seed-to-seed envelope to 'indistinguishable from sampling noise' - is right in spirit but the envelope must be measured for pLDDT specifically, not imported from the ipTM pilot. Mean pLDDT is an average over tens to hundreds of residues and its across-seed sd will be much smaller than the 0.133 measured for ipTM, which is an interface metric with a bimodal docked/undocked character. Using an ipTM-derived envelope would over-retract. Also, an envelope from n=3 seeds carries roughly 50% relative uncertainty on the sd itself, so '2x the envelope' from three runs is a soft threshold masquerading as a hard one.
critiques.feasibility_objection: The success criterion 'two same-seed runs are byte-identical' cannot be met on this hardware. Metal kernels use non-deterministic reduction ordering and torch determinism support on MPS is partial - the proposal's own observation that aten::linalg_svd falls back to CPU is evidence of exactly the dispatch variability that breaks bitwise reproducibility. Seeding controls the noise draw, not the summation order.
critiques.improvement: Measure a pLDDT-specific across-seed envelope with n>=5 seeds on at least three candidates spanning the length range, publish the sd with a CI on the sd, and re-label the legacy deltas against THAT, not against the ipTM pilot. Replace the byte-identical criterion with a measured numerical-agreement tolerance ('two same-seed runs agree to within epsilon on every reported scalar; epsilon measured, not assumed') and record MPS non-determinism as a documented property in the runtime manifest. Everything else - env.runtime() introspection replacing the RDKit string literal at build_dataset.py:34 and the dead getattr at corpus.py:318, the ARTIFACT re-hash loop, refusing to containerise the Boltz layer because Docker on macOS has no Metal passthrough, and committing the rebuild to git - is correct as written and should ship first, since the four hash mismatches mean the ledger currently asserts an integrity it does not have.

critiques.scientific_objection: The criterion-exercise audit is a genuinely good general mechanism and the specific bug is real - I confirmed from the committed data that every activity in corpus_ACHE.json has assay_confidence: null and that denominator.rejected contains no low-confidence bucket, so min_assay_confidence=8 has never rejected a record. The pre-specification framing is also right. But the decision rule, which is the entire point of pre-registration, is left as 'MAE below X log units and rho above Y' with X and Y unfilled. A pre-specification with unbound thresholds is not a pre-specification. Worse, at the stated n (18 compounds admitted for one target) the benchmark is underpowered to a degree that makes any threshold arbitrary: the 95% CI on Spearman rho at n=18 is roughly +/-0.45, so rho = 0.3 and rho = 0.7 are not distinguishable, and the bootstrap CI on MAE will be wide enough that almost any X either passes trivially or fails trivially. Also, the training-contamination caveat is correctly declared, but the consequence should be built into the decision rule rather than stated alongside it - a memorisation-inflated MAE that still fails the threshold is decisive, whereas one that passes is uninformative, and the rule should say so.
critiques.feasibility_objection: The freeze/verify machinery on the existing append-only ledger is genuinely two days. The affinity benchmark is the cost and is shared with CBC-CC-1 and AIML-BENCH-1 - three proposals commissioning overlapping AChE affinity batches. The weekly continuous-validation job also depends on ChEMBL being reachable, which it was not for me today (HTTP 500 on every attempt).
critiques.improvement: Bind the thresholds numerically before freezing, and derive them from the measured noise floor rather than picking round numbers: e.g. 'PREDICTED status is granted only if the 95% CI upper bound on MAE is below 2x sigma_exp for the endpoint class AND the paired bootstrap CI on the MAE difference versus the per-target-median null excludes zero'. Add a pre-declared power statement: at n=18 the protocol should state in advance that 'underpowered - no verdict' is a permitted and likely outcome, so a null result is not retro-fitted into a pass. Make the memorisation caveat operative: pre-declare that the measured MAE is an optimistic ceiling and that failure at the ceiling is dispositive while success at the ceiling is not. Merge the benchmark execution with AIML-BENCH-1 and CBC-CC-1 into a single frozen protocol and a single overnight batch. Keep the criterion-exercise audit as a general gate - it would have caught the confidence-8 defect and will catch the next one.

critiques.critic: Structural biology (X-ray crystallography and cryo-EM; validation of deposited structures), 21 years

critiques.scientific_objection: The design has no positive control, and without one its headline result is uninterpretable. If BasalAChE-GorgeBlock-B1 comes back at p=1.0 against its scramble, there are two explanations that this experiment cannot separate: (a) the design carries no sequence-specific information, or (b) this pipeline — Boltz-2, msa=empty, on MPS — cannot place ANY peptide on the AChE surface, in which case native and scramble both sample the same failure mode and p=1.0 is a property of the tool, not the molecule. The min interface PAE of ~17 A that the proposal itself reports is the signature of (b), not (a). A second, smaller problem: the pilot statistic is not matched. Natives were run at 3 seeds, decoys at 1 seed each, so the decoy spread contains seed variance plus sequence variance while the native mean is an average over 3 draws — the comparison is between distributions of different construction. Third, I confirmed the platform's own confidence data undercuts the premise that adding a receptor rescues these runs: median mean-pLDDT over the 22 existing lone-chain models is 61.0, and 14 of 22 have frac_below_70 between 0.76 and 1.00 (9 of them exactly 1.00). Co-folding a peptide whose own monomer confidence is uniformly under 70 against a receptor will produce an interface score dominated by peptide-side uncertainty. Fourth, a parsing trap the proposal will hit: I read /private/tmp/aff/out/.../confidence_in_model_0.json and pair_chains_iptm is NOT symmetric — [0][1]=0.4396 while [1][0]=0.7136, and the scalar 'iptm' equals the 0.7136 entry. For a two-protein complex the code must state which orientation it reports, or the headline ipTM becomes an undocumented max-statistic.
critiques.feasibility_objection: The 35 x 26 design is inflated. data/dataset.json contains 35 candidate records but only 26 unique sequences — KWWKFLRRFWRRLKKYFEELWKKLAEKYFELLKKYG appears three times (HippoAChE-AlkaPept-X2, BasalAChE-GorgeBlock-B1, CogAChE-PAS-02), SEAEFRLFRDVWANYCACYPGWLGC... three times, and five further sequences twice. Running and reporting them as 35 independent candidates triple-counts the exact molecule the pilot was run on. The compute estimate should be built on 26, and the p-value table must not present duplicates as independent tests. Separately, the ~24 h unattended MPS figure is derived from the AChE+peptide timing (~580 tokens); TLR4, TrkA/NGF and GluN2B NTD constructs are considerably larger and pair-representation cost scales ~N^2, so time a large case before committing.
critiques.improvement: Add a per-receptor positive control drawn from an experimentally solved peptide-in-groove complex on that same receptor, run in the identical configuration — 2FLU (KEAP1 Kelch + 16-mer Neh2, AFFAQLQLDEETGEFL, 1.5 A) is the cleanest, and for AChE use the bis-hupyridone gorge-spanning complexes rather than a peptide. Report every candidate's p-value next to the positive control's ipTM and min interface PAE from the same batch. Then a candidate at p=1.0 with a positive control at ipTM>0.8 is a statement about the molecule; a candidate at p=1.0 with a positive control also near 0.3 is a statement about the pipeline, and must be reported as 'pipeline not demonstrated competent on this receptor' rather than as a negative result about the design. Match the seed design: run every decoy at the same number of seeds as the native, or evaluate the native per-seed against the decoy distribution rather than native-median vs decoys. Deduplicate to 26 unique sequences and map codes onto sequences in the output. Record pair_chains_iptm as the full matrix with an explicit statement of which entry the reported ipTM is. Finally, the PAE-asymmetry BLOCKER is real and I confirmed it independently: on the genuine two-entity Boltz-2 run in /private/tmp/aff, max|PAE_ij - PAE_ji| is 20.30 A over the full 601x601 matrix and 17.54 A over the top-left 60x60 window that predictor.py:392-398 actually samples, against a 12.0 A threshold — the check fires on real output. Re-derive that threshold from a set of genuine two-chain runs and deposited-structure PAE, and record the derivation.

critiques.scientific_objection: Two problems with the ground truth and one with transfer. (1) DockQ >= 0.23 is the wrong success criterion at the short end of the proposed 5-40 residue range. DockQ's fnat/iRMSD/LRMSD combination and the CAPRI 'acceptable' boundary were calibrated on protein-protein interfaces; for a 5-10 residue partner the interface has too few native contacts for fnat to be stable, and DockQ becomes dominated by LRMSD. The community criterion for peptide docking is peptide-backbone RMSD after superposition on the receptor binding site, with 2 A as acceptable. Reporting a single DockQ-derived reliability curve across a 5-to-40-residue span mixes two different measurement regimes. (2) The leakage control is aimed at the wrong target. Deduplicating benchmark receptors at 30-40% identity against EACH OTHER prevents within-benchmark redundancy but does nothing about the receptor already being in Boltz-2's pre-2023-06-01 training set — which for a post-cutoff peptide complex on a long-known receptor is the normal case. A post-cutoff release date is a temporal holdout for the COMPLEX, not for the receptor fold, and the model's ability to place a peptide on a receptor it has memorised is not the quantity you want to advertise. (3) Transfer: a curve fitted on natural peptide-protein complexes with real evolutionary interfaces does not license a probability statement about 26-100mer GGGGS-linked polycationic chimeras. That is exactly the applicability-domain violation admet.py already refuses to commit for peptides.
critiques.feasibility_objection: The RCSB filter as written will pull a large fraction of junk. entity_poly.rcsb_sample_sequence_length in [5,40] on 'Protein (only)' two-entity structures captures crystallisation additives, uncleaved affinity tags, propeptide remnants, symmetry-mate fragments and nanobody CDR-only constructs — none of which is a biological interface, and several of which have no defined 'correct' answer at all. Expect to hand-inspect and discard a substantial fraction of the 1107, which the 4-5 day estimate does not budget for. The proposal is honest that the server-side clustering call returned HTTP 400 and is unvalidated; that is the right disclosure, but it means the deduplication step is unimplemented, not merely unfinished.
critiques.improvement: Split the benchmark by partner length and report separately: 5-15 residues scored by binding-site-superposed peptide backbone RMSD (<=2 A acceptable), 16-40 residues scored by both RMSD and DockQ. Add a required per-case leakage field: maximum sequence identity of the receptor chain to any pre-2023-06-01 PDB chain (mmseqs2 against a pre-cutoff PDB seqres dump), and stratify every reliability curve by that identity — <30%, 30-70%, >70%. Report the >70% stratum as recall, not prediction, exactly as AIML-BENCH-2 does for its 4EY5/4EY6/4EY7 set. Filter the RCSB hits by requiring the short entity to have a UniProt cross-reference and a buried surface area above a stated threshold against the partner, and publish the count discarded at each filter. Make calibrated_interface_probability refuse not only outside populated ipTM bins but outside the benchmark's structural domain, with the domain stated in terms of partner length, net charge and the presence of designed linkers — and require it to refuse for all 26 unique candidates unless a matched-domain calibration set is built.

critiques.scientific_objection: The uncertainty this proposal wants to propagate is itself far more uncertain than stated. An sd of 0.133 estimated from n=3 has roughly a 0.5x-to-2x sampling interval on the sd itself; writing that number into Provenance.uncertainty renders an unquantified quantity as a quantified one, which is the failure mode this repository exists to prevent — just at one remove. Second, the factorial as specified is under-determined at the reporting step: diffusion_samples=5 x 5 seeds gives 25 structures per cell, and Boltz emits a confidence per sample. Whether the cell value is the top-ranked sample, the mean over samples, or the mean over seeds of the top-ranked sample changes both the point estimate and the spread, and a top-1 selection over 5 samples is a max-statistic that inflates ipTM relative to the diffusion_samples=1 runs it is being compared against. Third, the peptide-side msa=empty justification is right for the designed chimeras but should be stated as a decision, not a fact: several candidates embed exactly-attributed natural motifs (motif_provenance records 16 with exact_match true), so parts of these sequences do have homologues; the claim is that an MSA over the chimera is meaningless, which is true, not that the sequence has no relatives.
critiques.feasibility_objection: None material. I confirmed run_boltz (platform/cbc/compute/structure.py:191-195) hardcodes out_dir/accelerator/recycling_steps/diffusion_samples/output_format/override with no --seed, and that _collect_boltz_outputs keeps sorted(...)[0] only. Both are small edits. One caution: --use_msa_server transmits every query sequence to a third-party ColabFold MMseqs2 server. For the 16 natural receptors that is harmless and the proposal correctly caches them; make explicit in code that no candidate sequence is ever sent.
critiques.improvement: Report the seed envelope as (n, min, max, and a bootstrap or Bayesian interval on the sd) rather than a bare sd, and require n>=10 seeds on at least the two or three cases whose spread will be reused as the platform-wide uncertainty; keep n=5 for the rest and say the sd is provisional. Pre-register the sample-selection rule (top-1 vs mean-over-samples) in writing before the batch runs and record it in every output row, since AIML-BENCH-2 raises the same point independently — fix it once, for all structural batches. Add one control condition the design is missing: two runs at the SAME seed and same settings, to establish whether the pipeline is bitwise deterministic under a fixed seed on MPS at all. If aten::linalg_svd falls back to CPU non-deterministically, same-seed runs may not reproduce, and then no amount of seed recording makes the platform reproducible; that is a one-hour experiment and it should be the first thing run. This is the highest value-per-day proposal in the panel and should be sequenced before AIML-STRUCT-1, AIML-BENCH-3, CBC-CC-3 and STRUCTBIO-IDEA-3, all of which consume its outputs.

critiques.scientific_objection: Partly outside my primary competence, but two points fall inside it. First, the system under test is not just an affinity head — it is a co-folding run whose STRUCTURE may be wrong, and the proposal never records structural confidence per benchmark case. An affinity error of 2.4 log units means something different when the ligand is in the catalytic gorge than when it is on the outside of the protein. Every affinity data point must carry the pose diagnostics from AIML-BENCH-2 (ligand_iptm, complex_plddt, and where a holo reference exists, ligand RMSD), so the error can be decomposed into 'wrong pose' versus 'right pose, wrong energy'. Second, the receptor construct is a hidden variable: the run in /private/tmp/aff used the P22303 mature chain as a single monomer, but human AChE is a disulfide-linked dimer/tetramer in vivo and, more importantly for this measurement, the gorge conformation and the Tyr337 rotamer that define the CAS are sensitive to the construct and to whether the PAS is occupied. Benchmarking against ChEMBL IC50s measured on native enzyme while predicting a monomeric mature chain is a construct mismatch that should be declared, not discovered later.
critiques.feasibility_objection: The ~10 h estimate for 200 complexes assumes 3 min each, but the proposal also requires every compound run in BOTH msa=empty and receptor-MSA conditions, which doubles it, and the MSA arm makes each run slower. Call it two overnight batches, not one. Also, this proposal, CBC-CC-1 and META-3 are three independent plans for the same AChE affinity benchmark, with three different compound sets, three metric sets and three decision rules. Running them separately wastes most of a week of MPS time and will produce three non-comparable numbers.
critiques.improvement: Merge with CBC-CC-1 and META-3 into a single frozen protocol before any compute is spent: META-3 supplies the hash-locked pre-specification and the criterion-exercise audit, AIML-BENCH-1 supplies the leakage stratification and the noise ceiling, CBC-CC-1 supplies the RDKit preflight gate (<=128 heavy atoms hard, 56-128 flagged) and the multi-target extension. Add a mandatory per-case structural record so affinity error can be conditioned on pose quality. State the receptor construct explicitly (accession, residue range, oligomeric state modelled, glycosylation absent) in the protocol, and note that all predictions are on a monomeric aglycosyl mature chain while the reference measurements are on native enzyme.

critiques.scientific_objection: The superposition protocol will systematically inflate RMSD. Kabsch over all matched C-alpha pairs fits the global fold, and for a 543-residue alpha/beta-hydrolase with a 20 A gorge, 0.5-1.5 A of global fit residual translates directly into apparent ligand displacement that has nothing to do with pose accuracy. The established practice — and what PoseBusters itself does in redock mode — is to superpose on the binding-site residues (heavy atoms within ~10 A of the reference ligand), then measure ligand RMSD in that local frame. Second, RMSD > 2 A conflates two qualitatively different failures: right pocket / wrong orientation, and wrong pocket entirely. These need separate reporting, because the platform's decision-relevant question for a warhead is 'is it in the gorge' before it is 'is it within 2 A'. Third, the 'temporal holdout' of 81 post-cutoff entries on ten cholinesterase/MAO/BACE/TTR accessions is temporally held out but not chemically held out: post-2023 AChE and BACE1 depositions are overwhelmingly close analogues of pre-cutoff series, so ligand-level memorisation survives the date filter. Fourth, a validation detail that matters for a PoseBusters run on deposited references: some of those reference ligands will themselves have poor real-space fit or ambiguous density; the reference pose is not automatically ground truth. Filter on ligand-level validation metrics from the wwPDB validation report (RSRZ / RSCC and the ligand geometry outliers), not only on entry resolution <= 2.5 A.
critiques.feasibility_objection: None material. I confirmed the parser defect the proposal is built on: platform/cbc/predictor.py line ~227 does `if f[idx["label_atom_id"]].strip('"') != "CA": continue`, so every ligand atom is discarded before any check. The fix is real work but bounded, and posebusters/spyrmsd are pure-Python. The 3 min/complex figure is consistent with the run log on disk.
critiques.improvement: Superpose on binding-site residues (heavy atoms within 10 A of the reference ligand, receptor-side only) and report both local-frame and global-frame RMSD so the difference is visible. Add a pocket-identification metric independent of RMSD: distance between predicted and reference ligand centroids, plus Jaccard overlap of the contacted-residue sets at a stated heavy-atom cutoff — for the existing huperzine model that set should include Trp86, Tyr124, Tyr133, Phe297, Tyr337, Phe338, His447, which is a strong regression assertion. Add a per-case max ECFP4 Tanimoto to any pre-cutoff ligand crystallised on the same target and stratify the holdout results at <0.4 / 0.4-0.7 / >0.7, borrowing AIML-BENCH-1's machinery. Filter reference entries on wwPDB ligand-level real-space fit, and exclude references whose ligand is flagged. Keep the recall/holdout separation exactly as proposed — that discipline is the strongest part of this idea.

critiques.scientific_objection: This is substantially the same experiment as AIML-STRUCT-1 and as the decoy arm of STRUCTBIO-IDEA-3, with a different RNG and a different output filename. Three teams each burning two overnight MPS batches on the same null model is the largest single waste in this panel. Beyond that: the scramble null does different work on different candidates and the proposal treats it as uniform. For the amphipathic helices (B1 and its two duplicates) a composition-matched shuffle preserves helical propensity and destroys facial segregation, so the null cleanly tests arrangement — that is the right control. For the cysteine-rich candidates (I counted 21 of 35 with >=4 Cys, 9 with 7-9 Cys) a shuffle relocates every cysteine and therefore changes the disulfide register and the fold class, so design-versus-shuffle is comparing two different folds, not two arrangements of one. A p-value pooled across both regimes is not interpretable. Third, no positive control, same objection as AIML-STRUCT-1.
critiques.feasibility_objection: The compute arithmetic is built on 35 (or 10) candidates, but the file contains 26 unique sequences among 35 records, and the shortlist of ten receptor-bearing candidates will contain duplicates. Also, the proposal cites '36 aa peptide plus 543-residue hAChE = ~580 tokens, comparable to the 3 min 4 s measured' — that measured run was hAChE plus an 18-heavy-atom LIGAND, not a 36-residue second protein chain with its own pair representation. Re-time before sizing the batch.
critiques.improvement: Merge into AIML-STRUCT-1 as its statistics module and delete the duplicate folding plan; one batch, one output file, one p-value table. Keep the part of this proposal that the others do not have and that costs zero compute: the demonstration that MW, net charge at pH 7.4, pI and GRAVY in platform/cbc/peptide.py are order-invariant and therefore carry no design information. That relabelling should ship immediately, before any folding, because it is provable by construction and it removes four numbers per candidate card that currently read as design results. Stratify the folding null by candidate class (amphipathic-helix vs cystine-rich) and state for the cystine-rich group that the shuffle changes fold class, so the test is 'is this fold-and-arrangement better than a random fold of the same composition', which is a weaker but still honest claim. Add the per-receptor positive control.

critiques.scientific_objection: The decoy arm as designed will overstate discrimination. Running each ligand against three UNRELATED receptors asks the model to distinguish AChE from, say, KEAP1 — a task solvable from gross physicochemical complementarity and one that any scoring function passes. The control that matters for a screening platform is discrimination WITHIN a target: actives versus property-matched inactives measured on the same target in the same assay class, which ChEMBL supplies directly. An AUROC of 0.9 against unrelated receptors and 0.55 against same-target inactives are the normal pattern, and only the second number tells you whether affinity_probability_binary is usable. Second, the AUROC confidence interval must be bootstrapped over LIGANDS, not over ligand-receptor pairs: three decoys per ligand are near-perfectly correlated within ligand, and resampling pairs will produce an interval several-fold too narrow. Third, the write-back into thermo.METHOD_ACCURACY needs a guard: an RMSE measured on AChE-family ligands must not be silently applied to a GSK3B or KEAP1 prediction, so the key should be per-target-class or the entry should carry an explicit applicability statement.
critiques.feasibility_objection: 200-300 unattended Boltz-2 runs at ~3 min is 10-15 h of pure inference, but the MSA arm on >=20 paired runs and the decoy arm at 3 receptors per ligand multiply the count; the honest figure is two to three overnight batches, not 2-4 days including coding. The RDKit preflight numbers are the strongest part and cost nothing.
critiques.improvement: Replace (or supplement) the unrelated-receptor decoys with same-target inactives drawn from the existing corpus pipeline — compounds with measured IC50 above a stated threshold on the same target and assay class — and report both AUROCs side by side, labelling the unrelated-receptor number as the easy control. Bootstrap over ligands. Make thermo.METHOD_ACCURACY's new key carry the applicability domain (target class, heavy-atom range, MSA mode, accelerator) and have verify_all.py refuse to apply it outside that domain. Fold the protocol into the merged AChE benchmark with AIML-BENCH-1 and META-3 rather than running a third independent version. Keep the heavy-atom preflight and the Onjisaponin V case (123 heavy atoms, inside the hard cap but 2.2x the recommended limit) exactly as written — that is a correctly-shaped refusal.

critiques.scientific_objection: Step 3 is not the validation it is presented as. PRODIGY's published r = -0.73 / RMSE 1.89 kcal/mol was obtained by fitting the contact-count regression on that benchmark; recovering those numbers by running the released implementation on the same complexes reproduces a training fit, and the proposal frames it as a wiring check that licenses downstream interpretation. It is a wiring check and nothing more, and the text should say so. More seriously, the outcome of the pre-registered test is knowable in advance from data already in this repository, which makes most of the proposed compute unnecessary. PRODIGY counts interfacial residue contacts. Its input here would be Boltz-2 models whose peptide chains have median mean-pLDDT 61 (I measured: 14 of 22 have frac_below_70 >= 0.76, 9 of them exactly 1.00) and whose interface PAE the AIML-STRUCT-1 pilot puts at ~17 A minimum. A contact count computed on coordinates with 17 A of positional uncertainty is not a degraded measurement, it is not a measurement. The four-cell table is a good design, but three of its four cells are predictable and the one that matters — predicted peptide complexes — can be settled with a handful of cases. Third objection: the constrained-pocket arm is correctly labelled circular, and that labelling should be load-bearing, i.e. the constrained runs must not enter any table that a reader could mistake for evidence.
critiques.feasibility_objection: Step 4(a) — co-folding the Kastritis structure-based affinity benchmark subset — is badly under-costed. Those are 81 to 144 genuine protein-protein complexes, commonly 300-900 residues total. Boltz-2 pair-representation memory and time scale roughly with N^2; the largest will not be an overnight job on a MacBook and some will exhaust unified memory. 'The benchmark co-folding dominates the remainder and runs unattended on MPS' is optimistic by a wide margin, and the proposal has not timed a single case at that size. The prodigy-prot install and the receptor registry are genuinely 2 days; the rest is not a one-week item.
critiques.improvement: Cut the scope to the decisive experiment. Run PRODIGY on (i) the deposited crystal structures of the handful of peptide-in-groove complexes this project can name — 2FLU is the obvious one — and (ii) Boltz-2 co-folds of those SAME complexes at several seeds. That is 5-10 systems, a few hours of compute, and it measures the crystal-to-predicted degradation on exactly the class of interface at issue. If the predicted-structure PRODIGY values scatter by more than the method RMSE across seeds on a complex whose answer is known, the pre-registered threshold is already failed and no further compute is justified. Publish that as the measured refusal. Keep step 6 (unconstrained co-folds of all candidates) but move it under AIML-STRUCT-1, where the null model lives. State plainly that step 3 reproduces a training fit. Retain the observation about retrieving two sign-flipped forms of the regression — that is a good argument for installing rather than reimplementing and should be recorded in the ledger.

critiques.scientific_objection: The chemical-indeterminacy argument is the best scientific point in the panel and I independently reproduced the underlying census: 21 of 35 candidate records carry >=4 cysteines, 15 carry an odd count, and the top of the list is CogDual-TrkB-PAS-10 and CogTrk-DeNovo-01 at 9 Cys each, then four at 8. But two things in the proposal are unsound. First, the success criterion is circular: 'disulfide_connectivity moves to COMPUTED for any candidate where exactly one connectivity survives the filter AND agrees with the parent motif's published pattern.' If agreement with the published parent pattern is a precondition, the published pattern is the answer and the calculation is decoration — worse, it is decoration that upgrades a LITERATURE fact to COMPUTED status, which is a provenance regression. Second, the OpenMM filter has no calibration.
