'Interface survives vs dissolves' after a short GBn2 implicit-solvent run is not a criterion until you have shown that a known-correct complex survives and a known-incorrect one dissolves under the identical protocol, with a stated simulation length and replicate count. Implicit-solvent MD of a highly charged 30-mer against a receptor will lose weak interfaces on nanosecond timescales more or less regardless of connectivity, and GBn2 systematically over-stabilises salt bridges — both failure directions are live. Third, and this governs the whole plan: the isomer spread you would measure is confounded with prediction noise. AIML-STRUCT-3's pilot puts the across-seed ipTM sd at ~0.13; unless the isomer-to-isomer spread is measured against that seed envelope, a spread of 0.15 across 15 connectivities is indistinguishable from re-running one connectivity 15 times.
critiques.feasibility_objection: 100-150 isomer systems, each a co-fold plus minimisation plus restrained equilibration plus unrestrained MD, is well beyond 1-1.5 weeks on this hardware, and openmm on Apple Silicon has no CUDA path — the available platforms are Reference/CPU/OpenCL, and OpenCL on Metal for a solvated-implicit peptide-protein system is not fast. Also, the Boltz bond-constraint question is genuinely open (the docs say bond constraints are supported for CCD ligands and canonical residues without confirming intra-chain SG-SG), and the entire plan is downstream of it; if it fails, the fallback 'impose connectivity in the relaxation stage' changes the experiment from 'what does the predictor do given this connectivity' to 'what does a force field do to a predictor's guess', which is a different and much weaker question.
critiques.improvement: Restructure around what the coordinates can actually support. (1) Take the parent motif's published disulfide pattern from its solved parent structure as the primary value, emitted with status DATABASE and the parent PDB accession — the motifs are natural peptides and motif_provenance already gives exact UniProt attribution for 16 of them. That is the honest, cheap, correct answer for most candidates and it does not require a single MD step. (2) Scope the isomer scan to the small number of candidates whose models are confident enough for side-chain placement to mean anything. On the existing 22, only PfcTrk-ErkEnhancer-P2 (mean pLDDT 85.0), AstroEaat2-Up-A2 (83.0) and HippoTrk-Saponin-X1 (78.0) qualify; nine candidates sit at frac_below_70 = 1.00 and should be excluded with that stated as the reason. (3) Report the isomer spread only alongside the across-seed envelope from AIML-STRUCT-3, measured on the same systems, and declare the isomer effect only where it exceeds the seed envelope. (4) Calibrate the OpenMM filter on at least one solved complex and one deliberately mis-docked control before any candidate is scored, and record the control result in the ledger, matching the discipline the proposal itself demands elsewhere. (5) Keep the code-enforced MM-GBSA refusal exactly as written — that is correct and should ship regardless of whether the rest does.

critiques.scientific_objection: I re-ran this analysis independently over the 22 mmCIFs in /tmp/cbc_boltz with gemmi 0.6.5 and every headline number reproduces exactly: 38 S-S contacts under 2.6 A, mean 2.081 A, sd 0.203, range 1.705-2.552, 21 of 38 outside 1.95-2.15, zero D-residues, and precisely the four named cysteines in two contacts (BasalM1-PAM-B2 Cys9, BasalSuper-AChE-TrkA-B5 Cys17, MicroDual-Trem2-Nrf2-M5 Cys10, MicroNrf2-AntiInflam-M2 Cys23). The proposal is evidentially sound. Three claims around it are wrong and need correcting before it ships. (1) 'Trivalent sulfur, chemically impossible' overstates what was measured. Every one of the four cases involves at least one contact well outside bonding distance — Cys17-Cys28 at 2.265 A, Cys10-Cys28 at 2.438 A, Cys11-Cys23 at 2.419 A, Cys10-Cys31 at 2.328 A. A 2.4 A S...S separation is not a disulfide; it is two thiols packed too close. The correct finding is that the model has not resolved which pair bonds — connectivity ambiguity — not that it drew a trivalent bond. That distinction changes the remedy: the right output is 'connectivity undetermined', not 'valence violation'. (2) 'None of this is visible in pLDDT' is false, and I measured it. Mean pLDDT at the SG atoms of geometrically bad contacts is 58.7 versus 66.9 at good ones, and the cited counterexample PfcACh-PAM-P1 with the 1.705 A contact has local SG pLDDT 55.5 and whole-model mean pLDDT 59.7 — it is below every confidence band the platform already computes. The model is not silently confident; it is loudly unconfident and nobody read the signal. (3) The 4EY7 false-positive analysis is incomplete. Running the platform's own rule over 4EY7 chain A gives THREE C-alpha outliers, not one: Tyr105-Pro106 at 2.853 A (the genuine cis peptide, omega -1.7 degrees) but also Pro258->Asn265 at 8.627 A and Asp494->Pro498 at 6.147 A. Those two are chain breaks across unmodelled loops, and an omega-aware rule does not catch them, because omega across a gap is meaningless. The stated success criterion of a zero false-positive rate on deposited structures will fail on the reference set as designed.
critiques.feasibility_objection: None. gemmi is installed, the coordinates exist, and I completed the full disulfide/chirality/contact pass over all 22 in about a second. One correction to the record that this proposal gets right and two others get wrong: DMPK-IDEA-2 asserts 'a filesystem-wide search for *.cif and boltz output directories in the repository returns nothing' and META-1 asserts 'no Boltz output directory exists'. Both are false. /tmp/cbc_boltz contains 22 complete boltz_results trees with input_model_0.cif, confidence JSON, and pae/plddt npz. STRUCTBIO-IDEA-1's framing — the files exist but live in a directory macOS purges — is the accurate one, and its step 6 is the correct and urgent fix.
critiques.improvement: Relabel the sulfur check: report S-S contacts in three bands (bonded 1.95-2.15 A, ambiguous 2.15-2.6 A, and anomalously short <1.95 A, which is as diagnostic as long and is a known diffusion-model artifact), and emit 'connectivity ambiguous' rather than 'trivalent' where a cysteine has more than one contact under 2.6 A with at least one outside bonding range. Add a residue-numbering-continuity precondition to the C-alpha rule so unmodelled-loop gaps in deposited structures are classified as chain breaks, not geometry errors — without this the reference-set false-positive criterion cannot be met. Gate the emission of disulfide_connectivity on local confidence, not only on geometry and valence: require mean SG pLDDT >= 70 for both partners in addition to distance and chi3. On the current 22 that admits roughly three structures (PfcTrk-ErkEnhancer-P2, AstroEaat2-Up-A2, HippoTrk-Saponin-X1), and reporting three PREDICTED connectivities plus nineteen not_computed-with-stated-reason is a far more defensible deliverable than filling in the field for all of them. Drop Engh & Huber bond lengths/angles from the first release — they are the least informative check on diffusion output — and keep chirality, omega, clashes and sulfur chemistry, which discriminate. Ship step 6 (move the coordinates out of /tmp, record the path in every row of data/real_vs_hardcoded.json) as a standalone fix this week, ahead of everything else in the panel; several other proposals silently depend on those files still existing.

critiques.scientific_objection: The receptor-monomer arm is close to worthless as calibration and consumes most of the described effort. hAChE, KEAP1 Kelch, TrkA d5 and TLR4 are all long-deposited, all inside Boltz-2's training window, and all already in AlphaFold-DB; a sub-angstrom C-alpha RMSD on 4EY7 measures memorisation and tells you nothing about the pipeline's behaviour on the systems the platform cares about. Reporting it next to the complex results invites exactly the wrong inference — 'the pipeline achieves 0.9 A RMSD' — about a platform whose actual task is peptide placement. Second, msa=empty is a serious confound on the complex arm specifically. A 300-residue six-bladed Kelch propeller predicted in single-sequence mode may fold correctly or may not, and if the receptor is wrong the DockQ is uninterpretable as a statement about interface prediction. Running the MSA-on comparison on 'two or three' monomers does not address this; it must be run on the complex cases. Third, n is far too small to do what the success criteria promise. Three or four complexes cannot support a calibration table, and criterion 4 — no ipTM displayed anywhere without the measured DockQ distribution attached — would attach an n=3 distribution to every number in the platform, which is a worse epistemic state than an honest 'uncalibrated'.
critiques.feasibility_objection: The compute reasoning contains an error that will bite. '26 s per lone chain, essentially independent of length from 26 to 100 residues, so fixed overhead dominates and a ~320-token Kelch+peptide job is minutes-scale' — length-independence from 26 to 100 residues does not extrapolate to 320 or 600 tokens, because the pair representation is O(N^2) in both memory and time and only becomes dominant above the fixed-overhead regime. The proposal half-acknowledges this for full-length AChE; apply the same caution to every complex. Also, TM-score requires a named implementation (TM-align/US-align, with the normalisation length stated) and the proposal does not name one; gemmi.calculate_superposition gives RMSD, not TM-score.
critiques.improvement: Delete the 16-receptor monomer arm or demote it to a one-line sanity note, and redirect that compute to complexes. Make the complex arm 2FLU plus every additional peptide-in-groove complex that can be found for these targets, run in BOTH msa=empty and receptor-MSA conditions, at >=3 seeds each, so ipTM/DockQ come with a spread. Then merge the resulting cases into AIML-STRUCT-2's ~100-complex leakage-audited benchmark rather than maintaining a second, tiny, target-specific calibration table — this proposal supplies the receptor-relevant cases, AIML-STRUCT-2 supplies the statistical power, and neither works alone. Name the TM-score implementation and normalisation. Replace success criterion 4 with: no ipTM is displayed without the benchmark N, and where N < a stated minimum the platform prints 'uncalibrated' and no distribution at all. Keep the 2FLU case as the flagship — it is genuinely the right experiment, it is cheap, and reporting 'incorrect' if that is the answer is exactly the right posture.

critiques.scientific_objection: One import in this proposal breaks the repository's own rule. pDockQ is a logistic fit whose coefficients were estimated on AlphaFold2-Multimer output, using AF2-Multimer's interface-pLDDT distribution and its contact statistics. Boltz-2 is a different model with a different confidence calibration; applying the published pDockQ sigmoid to Boltz-2 pLDDT is transferring a regression across models, which is the same class of error as reconstructing PRODIGY's equation from memory — and the proposal presents it as 'a second, published interface score independent of Boltz's own', which is precisely what it is not. It must be refit locally on the AIML-STRUCT-2 benchmark or reported as out-of-domain with no numeric output. Second, the interface analysis presumes coordinates worth analysing, and for most of this catalogue they are not: median mean-pLDDT over the existing 22 models is 61.0 and 14 of 22 have frac_below_70 >= 0.76, nine of them exactly 1.00. Per-residue buried SASA, hot-spot ranking and contact chemistry are side-chain-resolution quantities; computing them on a model where no residue exceeds pLDDT 70 produces numbers that will change completely on the next seed. The decoy percentile does not rescue this, because the decoys are equally unconfident — the percentile is then a comparison of two noise distributions and will look reassuringly well-behaved while measuring nothing. Third, a numbering trap specific to this repository: the experimental epitope from 4EY7 is in mature-chain numbering with the documented 'P22303 minus 31' convention, while a Boltz-2 model built from the mature sequence starts at 1. A Jaccard overlap computed without reconciling that offset will be silently near-zero, and the platform has already been burned once by species/numbering mixing in the legacy 'Trp84 / Trp286' string.
critiques.feasibility_objection: The proposal is honest that the decoy arm is the expensive part and that MPS scaling for complexes is unmeasured — that is the right disclosure. But the decoy arm is the third independent plan for the same scrambled-sequence null (see AIML-STRUCT-1 and AIML-BENCH-3), and none of the three should be funded separately.
critiques.improvement: Drop the folding/decoy arm entirely and consume AIML-STRUCT-1's outputs; this proposal's genuine contribution is the analysis layer, and it is the best-specified of the three. Refit pDockQ locally on the calibration benchmark or emit nothing for it. Add a per-interface confidence precondition: report buried SASA, hot spots and contact chemistry only where mean interface pLDDT exceeds a stated floor, and where it does not, emit not_computed with the measured interface pLDDT as the reason — that keeps the module honest for the two-thirds of the catalogue whose coordinates cannot support it. Add an explicit residue-numbering reconciliation step between deposited entry and model, with a unit test that the reconstructed 4EY7 donepezil epitope contains Trp86, Tyr337 and Phe338 in mature numbering. Keep the validate-on-2FLU-first discipline; reproducing the known KEAP1-Neh2 interface from deposited coordinates before touching any prediction is exactly right and should be the acceptance test.

critiques.scientific_objection: The burial measurement is probably correct and the veto built on it is falsified by an experimental crystal structure. Wong et al., J Am Chem Soc 125:363-373 (2003), DOI 10.1021/ja021111w, PMID 12517147, solved TcAChE complexes at 2.15 A with alkylene-linked dimers of hupyridone — 5-amino-5,6,7,8-tetrahydroquinolinone, the huperzine A fragment — tethered through the amino group, i.e. exactly the N2 position this proposal designates NO_VECTOR and PHARMACOPHORE_CONFLICT. The structures show one huperzine-like unit still bound at the anionic subsite adjacent to Trp84 in the identical pose to the TcAChE/(-)-HupA complex, with the tether running up the gorge and the second unit at Trp279 in the peripheral anionic site. Inhibition data in the same paper put (-)-bis(10)-hupyridone more than 170-fold TIGHTER on TcAChE than (-)-HupA. So amide-type conjugation at the exocyclic amine does not delete the binding mode; on this target it is the basis of a validated bivalent series with two orders of magnitude of gain, and bis(12)-hupyridone went on to in vivo AChE inhibition studies (Yu et al., J Pharm Biomed Anal 46:75-81, 2007, DOI 10.1016/j.jpba.2007.08.027, PMID 17931815). The methodological error is treating a single holo crystal structure as if it described the accessible conformational space. The AChE gorge is the textbook case against that: it is ~20 A deep, it breathes, Tyr337/Phe330 rotamers gate it, and the entire dual-site inhibitor literature exists because ligands span it. A static-SASA veto would have killed donepezil-class and bis-tacrine-class chemistry too. Note also that the proposal's own escape-path BFS, done correctly, should FIND the gorge — a ~20 A path matching the 10-12 methylene optimum — which means the method is sound and only the conclusion drawn from the straight-line prototype is wrong. Finally, the specific claim about deleting the Tyr337 hydrogen bond assumes the conjugate binds in the parent pose; the crystal structures show the bivalent ligand does retain the CAS pose, so the assumption happens to hold and the prediction still fails.
critiques.feasibility_objection: Modest. Biopython's Shrake-Rupley is fine and the contact census is prototyped. The grid BFS needs a stated probe radius and a stated definition of 'bulk solvent' (a fixed distance from the convex hull, or a SASA-positive termination criterion) or the path length is not reproducible; ~80 lines of numpy is optimistic once periodic re-seeding and path smoothing are handled, but it is a bounded task.
critiques.improvement: Reframe the output from veto to design parameter, and validate against the case that falsifies the veto. Make the primary deliverable the minimum escape-path length in angstroms and its GGGGS-residue equivalent, not a NO_VECTOR/VIABLE verdict. Add the bis-hupyridone TcAChE complexes as the mandatory positive control: the pipeline must return a viable path from the hupyridone amine through the gorge of length consistent with a 10-12 methylene tether, and if it returns NO_VECTOR on a structure where the tether is experimentally resolved, the method is refuted and must not be wired into validate.py. Report burial and escape path on the APO or unliganded-gorge structure as well as the holo one, so the number reflects accessible space rather than one induced-fit snapshot. Remove the validate.py failure category as specified, or restrict it to atoms with zero retained SASA AND no path in either apo or holo AND no published conjugate at that position; a gate that fails HippoAChE-AlkaPept-X2 for the same chemistry that produced a 170-fold-improved published series is a gate that will reject good work. Keep the per-atom contact census and the 4EY7 positive control — those are useful as they stand.

critiques.scientific_objection: Largely outside my primary competence, but the central endpoint-typing point is a structural distinction and I can speak to it. The 5.0 nM record used as ground truth (CHEMBL1771986) is inhibition of AChE-INDUCED amyloid-beta aggregation. That is a peripheral-anionic-site phenomenon — the Trp286/Tyr72/Tyr124 rim at the gorge mouth — and it is mechanistically a different measurement from catalytic-site inhibition measured by Ellman, which reports on the CAS at the gorge bottom near Trp86/His447. Huperzine A is a CAS binder; scoring a CAS-binder prediction against a PAS-phenotype assay is a category error independent of any statistics, and pooling the two into one aggregate would be worse. So the endpoint-class table is not a curation nicety, it is required for the number to mean anything. One caution on the proposed replacement: the geometric mean or median across a 4-log spread of heterogeneous assays is a summary of a heterogeneous population, not an estimate of a physical constant; report it with n and the full range every time, and never let a single central value stand alone in the way the 5.0 nM currently does.
critiques.feasibility_objection: None visible. One extra ChEMBL endpoint join and aggregation arithmetic. The confidence_score-lives-on-/assay-not-/activity finding is checkable and, if correct, means a stated filter has never rejected anything — that should be fixed before any benchmark is frozen, since three separate proposals in this panel plan to build an AChE benchmark on this corpus.
critiques.improvement: Sequence this before AIML-BENCH-1, CBC-CC-1 and META-3 — all three intend to score a model against this corpus, and all three would inherit both the inert confidence filter and the untyped endpoints. Add one field the proposal does not have: for each endpoint class, the structural site the assay reports on (CAS catalytic, PAS/aggregation, allosteric, unspecified), taken from the assay description, so a prediction made against a specific site can be matched to measurements of that site. Publish the retraction of the 2.41 log figure with its replacement as proposed — that is the right handling — and state in the same record that the replacement is a comparison against a class median with n and range, not against a truth value.

critiques.scientific_objection: The structural half cannot do the work claimed, and by the proposal's own gate it will mostly return nothing. Cleavage-site accessibility is gated on relative SASA and secondary structure computed from the Boltz-2 models, with sites below local pLDDT 70 reported as 'structurally undetermined, treated as accessible'. I measured the confidence distribution over the 22 existing models: nine candidates have frac_below_70 = 1.000, five more are between 0.76 and 0.97, and the median mean-pLDDT is 61.0. For those fourteen, every site is undetermined and the structural layer degrades exactly to the sequence census that already exists — while adding a SASA number and an SSE label that a reader will take as structural evidence. That is a number without knowledge for two-thirds of the catalogue. Second, relative SASA and biotite's SSE assignment are side-chain and hydrogen-bond-geometry quantities; on a pLDDT-50 model neither is stable across seeds, and the proposal has no seed replication. Third, a scientific point about the mechanism: the Hubbard requirement of ~10 residues of locally extended, flexible, exposed backbone is a statement about proteolysis of FOLDED globular proteins. These candidates are 26-100mers that are mostly not folded — the model says so — and for an unfolded or molten peptide the structural gate is vacuous and the sequence census is the correct and complete answer. The proposal would be stronger if it said that outright.
critiques.feasibility_objection: The stated premise is false and should be corrected before the plan is costed: 'a filesystem-wide search for *.cif and boltz output directories in the repository returns nothing... the coordinates themselves were discarded.' They were not. /tmp/cbc_boltz holds 22 complete boltz_results trees, each with input_model_0.cif, confidence_input_model_0.json, and pae/plddt npz files; I read all 22. They are in a purgeable directory, which is a real durability bug and is the same one STRUCTBIO-IDEA-1 step 6 fixes, but 'budget a day of compute to repeat the runs' is unnecessary — copy them, verify the hashes, and spend the day elsewhere.
critiques.improvement: Ship the sequence census as the deliverable and state that it is complete on its own for unfolded peptides; it is genuinely useful, it is already computed, and the AstroPafr-Block-A4 zero-site result shows it discriminates. Make the structural layer conditional and honest: apply it only where mean local pLDDT >= 70 over the ten-residue window around the site, and where it does not qualify, emit no SASA and no SSE label at all rather than a value plus a caveat — a printed number with a footnote is read as a number. Add seed replication before any SASA value is emitted, using AIML-STRUCT-3's machinery, and report SASA as a mean and spread over seeds. Adopt STRUCTBIO-IDEA-1's coordinate-persistence fix rather than duplicating it. The released-fragment identity check for the two Abeta constructs is the highest-value item here and needs no structure at all — it is an exact substring match against motif_provenance — so it should ship first and independently. Keep the hard constraint that no t1/2 in time units can ever be printed.

critiques.scientific_objection: Only the structural half is within my competence and it has a hole. The Eisenberg hydrophobic moment is defined for an ideal alpha-helix at 100 degrees per residue; the number is meaningful as a lytic-propensity descriptor only if the high-moment window actually adopts a helix. The proposal recognises this and proposes to gate on Boltz-2 secondary structure — but on the existing models that gate is unusable for most of the set: nine candidates have every residue below pLDDT 70 and five more are above 0.76 frac_below_70, so the SSE assignment for those windows is not evidence. The consequence is specific and matters for the headline finding: CogDual-TrkB-PAS-10, the 100-mer flagged as the largest false negative at moment 0.894, is not among the 22 folded models at all, and its 9 cysteines and GGGGS linkers make an uninterrupted 18-residue amphipathic helix a hypothesis rather than an observation. A moment of 0.894 computed over a sliding window of a sequence that may be a disulfide-constrained multi-domain chimera is a sequence statistic being presented as a membrane-interaction property. Second, the control panel is well chosen but it is a sequence-versus-sequence comparison: melittin's measured hemolysis is a property of a 26-mer that is unstructured in water and helical at the interface, and the mapping from moment to hemolytic concentration is not monotonic across scaffolds — a rank next to LL-37 is a hypothesis, not a risk estimate.
critiques.feasibility_objection: Low risk; modlAMP is installed and the calculation is seconds. The HemoPI2 and B3Pred arms are outside my competence to judge. One caution: the runtime-recomputed control panel with a hard assertion that melittin returns 0.558 +/- 0.001 is a good idea and should be extended to pin the modlAMP version, since a scale or window-default change upstream would silently shift every candidate's value while leaving the control assertion satisfiable only by coincidence.
critiques.improvement: Report the moment as a sequence descriptor and label it as such — 'maximum Eisenberg moment over an 18-residue window, assuming ideal helix' — with the helicity status as a separate, explicitly conditional field that reads 'helical in model (mean pLDDT X)', 'not helical in model', or 'no model / model confidence insufficient'. On the current data that third state applies to most of the catalogue and to CogDual-TrkB-PAS-10 specifically, which must be folded before its flag is presented as structural. Keep the runtime control panel and pin the library version in the assertion. The strongest and least contestable deliverable here is the BBB refusal census: stating that B3Pred's 5-30 residue domain admits at most 4 of 35 candidates, and running a deterministic, DOI-cited RMT shuttle-motif substring census with a present/absent call, is exact, cheap, and needs no structure — ship that half first.

critiques.scientific_objection: The seed and reproducibility argument is correct and important, and the inference it draws about the pLDDT deltas needs tightening. The proposed rule — 'downgrade any delta smaller than 2x the seed envelope from overstated to indistinguishable from sampling noise' — uses an arbitrary factor where an interval belongs. The right statement is whether the legacy value falls inside the across-seed distribution of the computed value, reported as an interval with its n, not a 2x heuristic. That matters here because the deltas are not marginal: I read data/real_vs_hardcoded.json and 15 of 22 deltas exceed 30 pLDDT units, with the largest at -46.19. Those will survive any plausible envelope, and framing the whole set as at risk understates what is already established. The three near-zero deltas (HippoAChE-AlkaPept-X2 at +0.37, BasalAChE-GorgeBlock-B1 at +0.96, MicroAutophagy-Tag-M4 at +3.43) are the ones that need the envelope, and the file's own interpretation text already makes the more important point about them — agreement on a trivially-confident amphipathic helix is not vindication. Second, a structural correction: the runs are recorded with accelerator 'gpu' in the provenance, not 'mps'. On this machine those are not the same thing, and a reader reconstructing the environment from the record would be misled. env.runtime() should capture the actual torch backend in use, not the CLI string passed.
critiques.feasibility_objection: One stated premise is false and inflates the plan. 'No mmCIF, confidence JSON, PAE array, or weights checksum was retained anywhere in the repository (searched: no Boltz output directory exists).' The search was scoped to the repository; the outputs exist at /tmp/cbc_boltz, 22 complete boltz_results trees with coordinates, confidence JSON and pae/plddt npz, which I read this session. So the historical runs are recoverable now — but only until macOS purges that directory, which makes rescuing them urgent rather than impossible. The seed-recording and re-fold work is still needed for reproducibility; the archaeology is not.
critiques.improvement: Copy /tmp/cbc_boltz into the repository and hash it TODAY, before anything else in this plan — it is a few minutes of work and it is the difference between having the historical evidence and losing it. Then adopt AIML-STRUCT-3's seed and configuration passthrough rather than implementing a second version; the two proposals specify the same change to the same lines of structure.py and should not both be built. Replace the 2x-envelope rule with an interval test and state n. Have env.runtime() record the resolved torch device and backend, and reconcile the existing 'gpu' strings. Keep the ledger ARTIFACT re-hash loop and the git-tracking finding — the fact that git ls-files returns nothing under platform/, data/ and memory/ while the discredited mockup is the only tracked content is, as stated, the single largest reproducibility defect here, and no other proposal in the panel addresses it.

critiques.scientific_objection: The criterion-exercise audit is a genuinely good general mechanism and I have no objection to it. One scoping point within my competence: the pre-specification for affinity-ache-v1 fixes the ligand set, the metrics and the decision rule, but says nothing about the RECEPTOR construct, which is a free parameter with real effect on the answer. Mature chain versus full-length, monomer versus dimer, which gorge conformation the model happens to produce, and whether the run is seeded are all degrees of freedom that can move a predicted affinity by more than the effect being measured. A protocol that freezes the compounds but leaves the receptor unpinned is not frozen. Second, the decision rule needs a structural precondition: an affinity prediction from a run whose predicted pose puts the ligand outside the gorge should not enter the MAE at all, or should enter a separately reported stratum, because averaging energy errors over poses that are simply wrong measures neither the affinity head nor the pose module.
critiques.feasibility_objection: None material, and the reuse of the existing append-only ledger for PRESPEC records rather than building a registry is the right call. The one real risk is duplication: this, AIML-BENCH-1 and CBC-CC-1 are three plans for the same AChE affinity benchmark with three different compound sets and three different decision rules, and freezing one protocol only helps if it is the protocol the others also run.
critiques.improvement: Make this the container for the merged affinity benchmark rather than a fourth parallel effort: freeze one protocol that carries AIML-BENCH-1's leakage stratification and noise ceiling, CBC-CC-1's RDKit preflight and applicability gate, and MEDCHEM-IDEA-2's endpoint-class aggregation as the reference-value rule. Add receptor construct to the required pre-specified fields — accession, residue range, oligomeric state, glycosylation, MSA mode, seed, recycling steps, diffusion samples, and the top-1-versus-mean selection rule — so the structural degrees of freedom are frozen alongside the chemical ones. Add a pre-declared pose-validity stratum so predictions whose ligand lands outside the target site are reported separately rather than averaged in. Fix the confidence_score join before the freeze, since the corpus is the protocol's population and a population defined by an inert filter cannot be pre-specified in any meaningful sense.

critiques.critic: Medicinal chemistry (natural products, pharmacophore analysis, assay-interference debunking) — 20 years. Verification performed this session against the live repo: reproduced huperzine A burial in 4EY5 (Shrake-Rupley, biopython 1.88: 406.64 A^2 free, 6.22 A^2 bound, 98.47% buried, N2 the only atom retaining >2 A^2 at 4.33 A^2; N2 contacts Tyr337-OH 3.01 A, Trp86 CG 3.49 A) and donepezil in 4EY7 (618.4 -> 82.73 A^2, 86.62% buried, max atom 19.75 A^2); reproduced the RDKit FilterCatalog flags (curcumin: beta-keto/anhydride + Michael_acceptor_1; baicalein: catechol_A(92) + catechol; donepezil/tacrine/physostigmine: zero) and found two the proposal missed (huperzine A and galantamine both flagged isolated_alkene by BRENK); confirmed corpus.py reads confidence_score off /activity and that all 18 corpus compounds carry assay_confidence=null; enumerated corpus_ACHE.json (18 compounds, 17 numeric, range 0.026 nM to 340,000 nM); found 35 candidates comprise only 26 distinct sequences; resolved warhead formulas against PubChem; reproduced the Eisenberg max-window hydrophobic moment and measured its length bias. ChEMBL REST returned HTTP 500 for every request throughout the session, so no live ChEMBL claim in any proposal could be independently audited.

critiques.scientific_objection: Every number reproduces exactly on my machine (4EY5, biopython 1.88 ShrakeRupley n_points=960: HUP 406.64 A^2 free / 6.22 A^2 bound / 98.47% buried; N2 4.33 A^2 retained = 12.3%; N2 to Tyr337-OH 3.01 A, to Trp86 CG 3.49 A). The positive control also holds: 4EY7 donepezil is 86.62% buried with a maximally exposed atom at 19.75 A^2, three-fold better than huperzine's best. So the measurement is sound. The INFERENCE is not. The proposal converts a burial map of the parent's crystal pose into a veto on conjugation, and that veto has a demonstrable false positive sitting inside this repository's own corpus. HUPRINE X is in data/corpus_ACHE.json at IC50 0.026 nM against CHEMBL220 — 200x more potent than huperzine A. Huprine X is a huperzine A / tacrine scaffold merge: RDKit FindMCS between the two corpus SMILES returns a shared 14-heavy-atom, 16-bond carbobicyclic core, and the growth is achieved by replacing huperzine's alpha-pyridone with 4-aminoquinoline. In my 4EY5 calculation the pyridone atoms O1, N1, C1 and C2 all retain exactly 0.00 A^2 and C3 retains 1.13 A^2. A rule of the form 'retained SASA below threshold implies no vector' evaluated on this holo pose therefore condemns precisely the region whose modification produced the best AChE inhibitor the platform holds. The structural basis of that tolerance is published (TcAChE + huprine X at 2.1 A, PMID 11863435, DOI 10.1021/bi011652i; huprine series review PMID 12369981, DOI 10.2174/1389557013406972). Underlying error: a monomer holo structure records where the parent sits, not the envelope the pocket can accommodate. AChE is the textbook counterexample because its 20 A gorge IS the linker channel — the dual-binding-site design paradigm exists precisely because deeply buried CAS warheads are routinely tethered out to the PAS.
critiques.feasibility_objection: None on the computation itself — I ran steps 1-3 in minutes with biopython already installed, and the grid BFS is the stated ~80 lines. The feasibility problem is coverage: the method only runs where an experimental holo complex exists for the exact warhead. Of the 25 declared warheads I extracted from chemStruct, holo complexes are plausibly available for huperzine A, donepezil-like and galantamine-like ligands and essentially nothing else — ginsenosides Rg1/Rb1/Rg3, onjisaponin/presenegenin, asiatic acid, salvianolic acid B, bilobalide and ginkgolide B in their declared receptors will nearly all return NOT_COMPUTED. The proposal will therefore deliver a verdict for roughly 1 of 25 conjugates while the validate.py gate it installs is written as if it covered the catalogue.
critiques.improvement: Three changes. (1) Put a warhead-identity and functional-group gate in FRONT of the geometry, because it runs on all 25 today with no PDB and no SASA, and it catches errors the exit-vector analysis structurally cannot. Resolve each chemStruct warhead to a PubChem CID / InChIKey, check the declared formula against the resolved structure, then check that the declared coupling chemistry has a reactive handle. Three failures fall out immediately, all verified this session: BasalNgf-TrkA-B3 declares 'Ginsenoside Rg3 Dammarane Core (C36H62O8)' but Rg3 is C42H72O13 (PubChem CID 9918693) — C36H62O8 is ginsenoside Rh2 (CID 119307), a different compound; HippoAChE-AlkaPept-X2 declares 'Cys-Lys Amide Coupling' on huperzine A, which RDKit shows has exactly one primary amine and zero carboxylic acids, zero thiols (so there is no amide bond to a Cys side chain — that is thioether chemistry — and the only nucleophile is the pharmacophoric N2); HippoDual-TrkB-AMPK-X5 declares a '1,2,3-Triazole Linker' on presenegenin, which carries neither azide nor alkyne, so an unstated handle-installation step is being smuggled in. Separately, AstroPafr-Block-A4 assigns bilobalide to a PAFR antagonist candidate while AstroZo1-Protect-A3 assigns ginkgolide B to a tight-junction candidate; the ginkgolide-series PAF receptor antagonist in the literature is BN52021, i.e. ginkgolide B (used as such in e.g. PMID 18665079, DOI 10.1097/MPA.0b013e3181661b07), so the two look swapped — confirm before acting, but a warhead-identity table is what surfaces it. (2) Rename the verdicts. Emit 'PARENT_BINDING_MODE_NOT_PRESERVABLE_AT_THIS_ATOM', which is what the data support and is falsifiable, instead of NO_VECTOR, which is a claim about chemistry the structure cannot make. (3) Before wiring any validate.py failure, measure the false-positive rate on known-potent conjugates and scaffold merges of buried warheads — huprine X against the huperzine A pose is the mandatory first case, and it must come back as a false positive of the naive rule, in writing. A gate that fails HippoAChE-AlkaPept-X2 is only credible once it is shown not to fail huprine X for the same reason.

critiques.scientific_objection: The diagnosis is right and I confirmed the mechanism in source: corpus.py's iter_target_activities reads a.get('confidence_score') from the /activity payload, and every one of the 18 compounds in data/corpus_ACHE.json carries assay_confidence: null while protocol_summary advertises min_assay_confidence 8. The replicate spreads reproduce from the file: neostigmine 2.0 and 22.0 nM (1.04 log), tacrine 33.5/95/143/218.78/254 (0.88 log), donepezil 2.33 and 16 (0.84), physostigmine 14.13/27.9/30/61 (0.64). But the central claim — 25 huperzine A records spanning 0.54 to 5280 nM, median 47 nM — I could not audit: the ChEMBL REST API returned HTTP 500 to every request I made this session, including via the MCP client, and corpus_ACHE.json itself holds only n=1 for huperzine A. So the re-scoring rests on an unverifiable retrieval. More seriously, the aggregation rule is being chosen after the outcome is visible. The proposal reports that median gives 1.43 log and geometric mean 1.20 log, and adopts the median. That is a researcher degree of freedom exercised in the model's favour, and it is not a cosmetic one: AIML-BENCH-1 measures the predict-the-mean null at 1.644 log RMSE on this same corpus, so the choice moves Boltz-2 from 'worse than guessing' (2.41) to 'better than guessing' (1.43). The proposal correctly diagnoses that the 2.41 figure was produced by an unstated choice, then replaces it with a differently-signed unstated choice. Second gap: stereochemistry is not an endpoint class and will not be caught by clustering on (standard_type, bao_label, assay_description). This corpus already demonstrates the problem — it holds PHYSOSTIGMINE (CHEMBL94) at 14.13-61 nM and (+)-PHYSOSTIGMINE (CHEMBL76640) at 9890 nM, a 2.55 log eudysmic gap between two entries a reader could easily pool. Huperzine A is sold and assayed both as the natural (-)-enantiomer and as racemate, and racemic records will drag any aggregate toward the mean of a 10-50x eudysmic ratio.
critiques.feasibility_objection: Two days is optimistic only in one place: the /assay join is trivial, but ChEMBL was returning 500 for the entire duration of my session, so the plan needs an explicit retry-and-fail-loud policy or the rebuild will silently emit a smaller corpus and the 'regression test that fails if assay_confidence is null' will pass on an empty set. Everything else — dataclass widening, aggregation arithmetic, pchembl_value reuse — is genuinely a day.
critiques.improvement: (1) Move the aggregation rule into META-3's frozen protocol and pick it BEFORE re-running the comparison: specify geometric mean of pchembl_value within endpoint class, with median reported as a sensitivity analysis, and commit the hash first. Then publish whatever number falls out, including if it lands back above the null. (2) Aggregate on full InChIKey (as stated) and additionally emit a stereo_status field per aggregate — single_enantiomer / racemate / undefined — derived from the RDKit stereocentre count corpus.py already computes; refuse to pool records whose stereo_status differs, and surface the physostigmine pair (27.9 vs 9890 nM, both in this file today) as the worked example in the docs. (3) Use the right noise floor for the right endpoint. The proposal attaches Kramer's sigma, which is the Ki figure (PMID 22643060, DOI 10.1021/jm300131x); this corpus is IC50-dominated, so the reference is the mixed-IC50 analysis (PMID 23613770, DOI 10.1371/journal.pone.0061007). Store both, keyed by standard_type, and never let an IC50 aggregate inherit a Ki sigma. (4) Add an enzyme-source field to the endpoint class. Several corpus rows are assigned to CHEMBL220 (human) from assays whose description names eel, bovine or erythrocyte AChE; that is a bigger error source than the amyloid-aggregation record they already caught, and confidence>=9 will not remove it.

critiques.scientific_objection: The substructure results reproduce exactly (RDKit 2026.03.5, PAINS_A/B/C + BRENK + NIH): curcumin -> beta-keto/anhydride, Michael_acceptor_1; baicalein -> catechol_A(92), catechol; donepezil, tacrine, physostigmine -> zero. The readout-collision framing is the right instinct and is a genuine advance over bare PAINS flagging (Baell & Holloway, PMID 20131845, DOI 10.1021/jm901137j; curcumin as PAINS/IMPS, PMID 28074653, DOI 10.1021/acs.jmedchem.6b00975). Two defects. First, catalogue purpose is being conflated. PAINS_A/B/C are frequent-hitter substructures derived from AlphaScreen counterscreens; BRENK and NIH are reactivity and metabolic-liability filters with no interference semantics. I ran the same catalogue over the platform's own clean controls and BRENK flags huperzine A and galantamine on 'isolated_alkene' — two bona fide, non-interfering AChE inhibitors, one of them the platform's headline warhead. The proposal's negative control (physostigmine/tacrine/donepezil clean) passes only because those three happen to lack an alkene; it does not demonstrate what it claims. Second, and decisively for a natural-products corpus: the collision join systematically discards the single most common NP interference mechanism. Colloidal aggregation corrupts essentially every biochemical readout regardless of detection physics, and it is pervasive specifically among traditional-medicine constituents (PMID 25606714, DOI 10.1021/cb5009487; assay methodology PMID 16408018, DOI 10.1038/nchembio718 and PMID 17191086, DOI 10.1038/nprot.2006.77). The proposal lists colloidal_aggregator in the mechanism table but the readout table maps Ellman/DTNB only to {thiol_reactive, chromophore}, so no aggregation collision can ever fire. An aggregator therefore passes the gate labelled clean — the exact failure the module exists to prevent, and it will hit baicalein, curcumin and salvianolic acid B hardest.
critiques.feasibility_objection: None material. Step 5's conjugation heuristic is honestly labelled PREDICTED. The dependency on MEDCHEM-IDEA-2 retaining assay_description is real and correctly stated — the module cannot run at all today because the Activity dataclass discards it.
critiques.improvement: (1) Split the catalogues by purpose in code, not just in the report: run PAINS_A/B/C into the interference layer and BRENK/NIH into a separate reactivity/developability layer that can never emit an evidence downgrade. Add huperzine A and galantamine to the negative-control test with an assertion that neither produces an interference flag — the current control set does not exercise the false-positive mode. (2) Handle aggregation on the assay side rather than the substructure side, because it is not reliably predictable from structure. Parse assay_description for detergent (Triton X-100, Tween, CHAPS) and for carrier protein (BSA), and grade every value from a detergent-free biochemical assay on a high-cLogP, poorly-soluble NP as lower confidence with mechanism 'aggregation not excluded — no detergent control reported'. That is a metadata check, costs nothing, is far better evidenced than any SMARTS, and it applies to the four saponins and two polyphenol conjugates in this catalogue where no PAINS pattern fires at all. (3) Make the chromophore check quantitative enough to be falsifiable: rather than 'extended conjugation with donor substitution', record the compound's reported lambda_max where a source gives one, and only flag a collision when the reported lambda_max falls within a stated window of the readout wavelength. Curcumin's absorbance maximum is in the 420-430 nm region against Ellman's 412 nm read, which is the strongest single case in the catalogue and deserves a measured number rather than a heuristic. (4) Every mechanism-table row already needs a citation per the success criteria — extend that to requiring the citation to establish the mechanism IN the named readout, not merely the reactivity in the abstract.

critiques.scientific_objection: The preflight gate, the decoy AUROC and the paired test against a per-target-median null are all correct and the heavy-atom counts are right. The problem is the calibration set. It is to be built by extending corpus.py's np-cognition-v1 InclusionProtocol, and that protocol is demonstrably not selecting the population it names. I enumerated all 18 admitted AChE compounds: METOCLOPRAMIDE, PRALIDOXIME, RANITIDINE, DONEPEZIL, EDROPHONIUM, TACRINE, VELNACRINE, IPIDACRINE, OCTAAMINOACRIDINE and HUPRINE X are all admitted as NP_DERIVED. Pralidoxime is an oxime reactivator, not an AChE inhibitor, and sits at 340,000 nM; metoclopramide is a benzamide at 20,000 nM; ranitidine at 650 nM. Those three near-inactives create most of the corpus's 7.1-log dynamic range. Any RMSE, Spearman rho or paired-vs-null comparison computed on this set is measuring the broken NP flag, not the model: a predictor that only distinguishes 'potent AChE inhibitor' from 'not an AChE inhibitor at all' will beat the median null handsomely and learn nothing. Scaling to GSK3B, KEAP1, CHRM1 and NOS3 with the same protocol reproduces the defect four more times. Second, missing control: pooled RMSE cannot tell you whether the affinity head has any structural resolution at all. This corpus already contains the decisive cheap test and nobody proposed it — PHYSOSTIGMINE at 14.13-61 nM and (+)-PHYSOSTIGMINE at 9890 nM, an enantiomer pair with a 2.55 log measured gap and identical 2D topology.
critiques.feasibility_objection: 200-300 unattended Boltz-2 runs at the measured 3 min 4 s each is ~10-15 h, which is fine. But 'aim for >=60 pairs spanning >=3 log units and >=4 targets' will not be met by the current protocol if the population is fixed properly: the AChE arm yields 18 admitted compounds today of which 17 have a number, and tightening from ChEMBL's NP flag to a real pharmacology-based inclusion criterion will cut it further. State the expected n per target before running, and be prepared for the honest answer that the corpus is too small for a per-target Spearman.
critiques.improvement: (1) Define the benchmark population by pharmacology, not by ChEMBL's natural_product flag — which the repo already documents as noisy enough to label donepezil and metoclopramide as natural products. Admit compounds with a measured catalytic-inhibition endpoint against the named enzyme, NP tier recorded as an annotation rather than used as the filter, and report the resulting n honestly. The NP framing belongs on the candidate cards, not in the benchmark's inclusion rule. (2) Add a stereochemical resolution arm as a gating precondition: run the affinity head on (-)- vs (+)-physostigmine (2.55 log measured, both already in corpus_ACHE.json) and on (-)- vs (+)-huperzine A. If the head cannot rank enantiomer pairs whose measured gap exceeds 2 log units, no pooled RMSE on the full set is interpretable and that should be reported as the headline finding. This costs 4 extra runs. (3) Report the pooled metric stratified by whether the compound is an actual inhibitor of the target, so the reader can see how much of any apparent skill comes from separating actives from non-binders rather than from ranking actives. (4) The thermo.METHOD_ACCURACY write-back is a good idea but the key must carry its applicability domain in the key itself, not in the note — otherwise a measured AChE-specific, <=128-heavy-atom, single-sequence-mode RMSE will be silently reused for a peptide or a different target class, which is the same category error the module was written to prevent.

critiques.scientific_objection: The ordering discipline — reproduce on crystals, then measure each domain shift separately, then apply a pre-registered threshold — is the right shape, and refusing to transcribe the eLife regression after retrieving two sign-flipped versions is exactly correct. Two objections. First, the four-cell table cannot be filled as specified. Cells 1 and 2 (crystal PP, predicted PP) have a named set. Cells 3 and 4 (crystal peptide, predicted peptide) do not — no protein-peptide structure-plus-affinity benchmark is named anywhere in the proposal, and that is the only arm that bears on the actual question, since all 35 candidates are peptides. Without a named, retrievable set with measured affinities and a stated n, the two cells that matter are aspirational and the pre-registered <=2.0 kcal/mol rule cannot be evaluated at all. Second, a medicinal-chemistry point about what PRODIGY can even see: it is a contact-count regression calibrated on crystal protein-protein interfaces burying on the order of 1500-2000 A^2. A 36-residue amphipathic peptide docked onto AChE is a different interface regime, and — more damagingly for this particular catalogue — contact count is close to a composition-and-size statistic. A polycationic Arg/Trp-rich peptide will generate many interfacial contacts against any acidic surface. So a PRODIGY dG computed on these candidates risks being a rediscovery of net charge, which the platform already reports. The proposal's own decoy logic (from AIML-BENCH-3) is the antidote and is not applied here.
critiques.feasibility_objection: '~1 week' is understated once step 4(a) is taken seriously: co-folding the Kastritis-derived crystal benchmark subset means predicting full protein-protein complexes, which are far larger than the 580-token AChE+peptide systems whose 3 min timing anchors the estimate, and pair-representation cost scales roughly as N^2 on MPS. Time three representative complexes from that benchmark before committing, and be ready to subset.
critiques.improvement: (1) Name the protein-peptide set and its n before starting, and if no set with measured affinities can be assembled on this hardware, say so and report only the two protein-protein cells — a two-cell table with an explicit statement that the peptide transfer is unmeasured is far more useful than a four-cell table with two invented rows. (2) Run PRODIGY on composition-matched scrambles of each candidate against the same receptor (reuse AIML-BENCH-3's generator) and report the design's contact count as a z-score against that null, so it is visible whether the contact count encodes sequence or only composition. (3) Fix the denominator: data/dataset.json's 35 candidates are only 26 distinct sequences — HippoAChE-AlkaPept-X2, BasalAChE-GorgeBlock-B1 and CogAChE-PAS-02 are byte-identical 36-mers, PfcACh-PAM-P1 / MicroTlr4-Antagonist-M3 / CognACh-Mod-06 are one 41-mer, and there are five further duplicate pairs. 'All 35 candidates carry a receptor-bound co-fold' will therefore contain nine redundant rows presented as independent results, and any statistic aggregated over 35 double-counts. Either deduplicate and report 26, or carry an explicit sequence_group id so the redundancy is visible. (4) The constrained-pocket run is correctly labelled circular; keep that discipline and make sure the constrained ipTM cannot be written into any provenance field the UI renders.

critiques.scientific_objection: The framing is the strongest chemistry argument in the whole panel: reporting a dG with a +/-1.9 kcal/mol method error on a molecule that is one of 105 possible chemical species is a category error, and hard-coding the refusal to write an MM-GBSA value is the right enforcement. Three problems. First, the scope arithmetic double-counts. '21 of 35 candidates carry >=4 cysteines' is computed over 35 records that contain only 26 distinct sequences; PfcACh-PAM-P1, MicroTlr4-Antagonist-M3 and CognACh-Mod-06 are the same 41-mer with the same cysteines, so enumerating their isomers separately triples the compute and produces three copies of one finding. Second, and chemically more important, the enumeration is incomplete in a way that understates the problem. Fifteen candidates have an odd cysteine count, which means at least one free thiol — and a free thiol on a 3-11 kDa peptide at pH 7.4 in air does not stay free. It forms intermolecular disulfides: homodimers, mixed disulfides with glutathione, and adducts to albumin Cys34. Those species are not in the intramolecular pairing enumeration at all, so the reported isomer spread is a lower bound on the chemical indeterminacy, and it should be stated as one. Third, the physics filter is biased in a known direction. GBn2 implicit solvent with no explicit ions applied to peptides of net charge up to +8 under-screens electrostatics and over-stabilises salt bridges, so a pass/fail defined as 'interface survives vs dissolves' will systematically return 'survives'. A filter whose failure mode is one-sided is not a filter.
critiques.feasibility_objection: This is the least feasible proposal I can assess. 100-150 isomer systems each requiring a Boltz co-fold plus minimisation plus restrained equilibration plus unrestrained implicit-solvent MD, on a MacBook with no CUDA, is not 1-1.5 weeks. OpenMM's arm64 wheel exposes Reference, CPU and OpenCL — no Metal/CUDA fast path — and OpenCL on Apple Silicon is substantially slower than a CUDA GPU for GB implicit solvent. Also flagged in the proposal itself but worth weighting: the Boltz SG-SG bond constraint is documented only for CCD ligands and canonical residues, and whether intra-chain SG-SG works is unverified. If it does not, the whole enforcement mechanism moves into the relaxation stage and the design changes materially. That verification is a gate on the entire idea, not a step within it.
critiques.improvement: (1) Verify the SG-SG bond constraint against a solved disulfide-rich control FIRST, as a standalone half-day deliverable, and report the verdict to the panel before committing any of the rest. If it fails, the proposal should be re-scoped rather than re-plumbed. (2) Deduplicate to 26 sequences and pick the 4-6 worst distinct offenders, not 8-10 records. Exhaustive enumeration for the 4- and 6-Cys cases (3 and 15 pairings) on distinct sequences is a tractable, complete, publishable result; a bounded sample of the 8-Cys 105 is not, and mixing complete and sampled enumerations in one table invites over-reading. (3) Add the intermolecular species to the written analysis even though they cannot be modelled: for every odd-Cys candidate, state explicitly that the enumerated intramolecular spread excludes disulfide-linked dimer and glutathione/albumin adduct formation, so the reported spread is a floor. That costs nothing and materially strengthens the refusal. (4) Either state the GBn2 one-sided bias in the output of every pass/fail, or replace the MD arm with a cheaper, unbiased geometric check (steric clash and disulfide geometry after minimisation only) and drop the dynamics entirely. The dynamics is the expensive half and it is the half whose verdict cannot currently be trusted in the direction it will fail.

critiques.scientific_objection: Anchoring an error figure between a measured noise ceiling and a trivial-predictor floor is exactly right, and the leakage audit is the correct second mechanism. But the null floor as computed is an artifact of the corpus's broken inclusion rule. I enumerated data/corpus_ACHE.json: 18 compounds, 17 with a numeric value, spanning 0.026 nM (huprine X) to 340,000 nM (pralidoxime) — 7.1 log units. Pralidoxime is an oxime reactivator, not an inhibitor; metoclopramide (20,000 nM) is a benzamide; ranitidine (650 nM) is an H2 antagonist. All three were admitted only because ChEMBL's natural_product flag is set on them, which the repo already documents as noisy. Those three compounds create most of the variance, so the reported predict-the-mean RMSE of 1.644 log is inflated and the null is artificially easy to beat. A model that merely separates 'binds AChE' from 'does not bind AChE' will clear it. Second, the noise ceiling is drawn from the wrong paper for this data. Kramer's sd 0.54 pKi and max attainable R^2 ~0.81 (PMID 22643060, DOI 10.1021/jm300131x) is the Ki figure; corpus_ACHE.json is IC50-dominated, and the corresponding IC50 analysis (PMID 23613770, DOI 10.1371/journal.pone.0061007) gives a materially larger spread. Using a Ki ceiling to judge IC50 predictions understates the irreducible noise and will make the model look worse than the data can resolve.
critiques.feasibility_objection: The 10 h overnight batch and the CPU-side baselines are realistic. The concern is n: after the population is fixed properly, the AChE arm will be well under 60 compounds, and BCa bootstrap CIs resampled over compounds at n~15-20 will be so wide that the hard rule ('not distinguishable from the null model at n=N') fires on essentially everything. That is the honest outcome and the proposal already accommodates it, but the multi-target scale-out is then not optional — it is the only route to a benchmark that can say anything, and it inherits the same population problem at each new target.
critiques.improvement: (1) Redefine the benchmark population by measured pharmacology against the named target, not by ChEMBL's NP flag, and report n before and after. Keep NP tier as an annotation. Then recompute the predict-the-mean null on the corrected set and publish both numbers side by side — the drop from 1.644 is itself an informative result about how much of a benchmark's apparent difficulty can be manufactured by an inclusion criterion. (2) Key sigma_exp to standard_type and use the IC50 reference for IC50 aggregates and the Ki reference for Ki aggregates; never let one inherit the other. (3) Add stereochemistry to the leakage/stratification scheme. Max ECFP4 Tanimoto to the pre-cutoff set is stereo-blind, so an enantiomer of a training compound scores Tanimoto 1.0 and looks like exact memorisation when it may be a 2.5-log-different molecule — this corpus holds (-)- and (+)-physostigmine at 27.9 and 9890 nM as a live example. Record stereo-aware and stereo-blind similarity separately. (4) The 18 replicate pairs giving sigma 0.376 come from a corpus of 18 compounds where 4 compounds supply all the replication; report the per-compound contribution, because a sigma estimated from tacrine's five records plus physostigmine's four is not an 18-pair estimate in any effective sense.

critiques.scientific_objection: The predictor.py ligand-blindness is a real defect and the temporal split is correctly reasoned. Three medicinal-chemistry objections to the design. First, the recall set inflates n: 4EY5, 4EY6 and 4EY7 are the same recombinant human AChE construct, from the same depositing group, all released 2012-10-17 at 2.30-2.40 A. They differ in the ligand, not in the receptor conformation, so they are three ligand poses in one pocket, not three independent recall points, and a Wilson interval computed over them as independent trials is wrong. Second, and specific to this target class: for AChE, symmetry-corrected RMSD <= 2 A is a weak discriminator. The active-site gorge is a narrow ~20 A channel; a ligand placed anywhere inside it is geometrically constrained toward the right answer, so a high RMSD success rate on AChE ligands will overstate the pipeline's pose accuracy on open or shallow sites. The medicinally decisive question is which pharmacophoric contact is reproduced — is the cationic centre stacked on Trp86 at the CAS, or is the ligand at the PAS on Trp286, and is the pyridone/carbonyl hydrogen bond present. I measured those contacts directly on 4EY5 in seconds (N2 to Tyr337-OH 3.01 A, N2 to Trp86 CG 3.49 A), so the check is cheap. Third, species mixing: the holdout query includes P04058 (Torpedo AChE) alongside P22303 (human). Torpedo and human AChE differ in gorge residues and in numbering (the repo's own target_records document the W84->W86, Y121->Y124, W279->W286 mapping), so pooling them into one success proportion mixes two pockets.
critiques.feasibility_objection: posebusters and spyrmsd as pure-Python wheels is credible and the 5-6 h batch is realistic. One real gap: 'fetch the reference entry and ligand instance coordinates from data.rcsb.org' understates the work for multi-copy entries — 4EY5 has HUP in both chain A and chain B, so chain and ligand-instance selection is a decision that must be recorded, not inferred, or the RMSD is against an arbitrary copy.
critiques.improvement: (1) Report the recall set as three ligands in ONE receptor and give it n_receptors=1 alongside n_ligands=3; do not compute a Wilson interval over ligand poses in a single pocket as if they were independent structures. (2) Add a pharmacophore-contact reproduction metric next to RMSD: for each case, extract the reference ligand's protein contacts under 4.0 A and report the Jaccard overlap with the predicted pose's contact set, plus a named pass/fail on the target's canonical interaction (Trp86 stacking and the Tyr337/Tyr124 hydrogen bonds for AChE CAS binders). This is the quantity a medicinal chemist would act on, it is computable with the same code, and it distinguishes 'right pocket, wrong orientation' from 'right pose' — a distinction 2 A RMSD hides in a narrow gorge. (3) Stratify all headline proportions by receptor UniProt and never pool P22303 with P04058. (4) Record the chain and ligand instance used for every reference, since multi-copy entries are the norm in this set. (5) The regression test as written ('18 ligand atoms whose ten nearest protein residues include Trp86, Ser203 and His447') is good and I can confirm the 18-atom count is right for HUP; add Tyr337 and Tyr124 to the assertion, since those are the contacts that distinguish a correct CAS pose from a merely in-gorge one.

critiques.scientific_objection: A permutation null is the correct remedy when no labels exist, and the observation that MW, net charge, pI and GRAVY are order-invariant is arithmetically exact — I confirmed all four are computed by peptide.py as pure composition sums. Two objections. First, the denominator is wrong and it propagates into the statistics. data/dataset.json's 35 candidates are 26 distinct sequences: three codes share the 36-mer KWWKFLRRFWRRLKKYFEELWKKLAEKYFELLKKYG, three share a 41-mer, and there are five further duplicate pairs. The proposed 'ten candidates that carry an explicit receptor' will therefore include perfectly correlated tests, and Holm-Bonferroni across ten when several are byte-identical over-corrects and destroys power against the one thing the experiment is trying to detect. Second, an interpretive overreach that would do real damage if implemented as written: 'order-invariant' is being equated with 'carries no design information'. It does not. Composition IS a design choice, and the composition-derived liability flags — polycationic, amphipathic, KLVFF-containing, odd-cysteine — are currently the most defensible and best-evidenced outputs the platform produces. Tagging them 'composition-determined' and retiring them from the candidate cards would remove honest signal to make room for a scramble-controlled ipTM whose own informativeness the pilot data suggest is nil.
critiques.feasibility_objection: 210 co-folds at roughly the 3 min measured for a 580-token AChE system is 11-14 h in principle, but the receptor sizes vary a lot across the ten targets (AChE 543 aa versus TREM2 Ig-V at 84) and pair-representation cost is superlinear, so the estimate is anchored on one system and should be re-timed per receptor before the batch is committed. K=10 on three DISTINCT sequences as a first pass is the right call.
critiques.improvement: (1) Deduplicate first. Report per distinct sequence with the candidate codes that map to it, run the null once per sequence-receptor pair, and apply Holm-Bonferroni over the number of independent tests actually performed. The deduplication itself is a finding worth publishing: nine of thirty-five 'candidates' are copies. (2) Change the tagging vocabulary from three states to three states that are actually distinguishable: 'order-dependent (scramble-controlled)', 'order-invariant by construction' and 'untested'. Keep order-invariant values on the card with their liability text intact and a one-line note that a composition-matched shuffle reproduces them exactly. That is honest and it does not throw away the platform's best-supported outputs. (3) Add one control the design is missing: a length- and composition-matched shuffle preserves charge and GRAVY but does NOT preserve helical amphipathicity, which is the property most likely to drive nonspecific interface formation for this Arg/Trp-rich class. Include a third control that preserves the hydrophobic moment while scrambling identity (e.g. swap hydrophobics for hydrophobics within the helical face), so the null can separate 'binds because amphipathic' from 'binds because of this specific sequence'. Without it, a design that beats the composition null may still be reporting nothing more than that it is a better amphipath than a random shuffle of the same residues.

critiques.scientific_objection: Replacing a length-triggered boilerplate string with a computed cleavage census is right, using pyteomics' shipped expasy_rules rather than transcribing regexes is right, and forbidding the module from ever printing a t1/2 is exactly the correct discipline. Two objections. First, the sequence census as specified produces a number without knowledge. Tryptic site count is a near-deterministic function of Lys+Arg content, so '215 trypsin-like sites across the catalogue' and '24 trypsin+chymotrypsin sites in 36 residues' are restatements of composition — the same frac_cationic and frac_aromatic peptide.py already reports. Reported alone they add a decimal place, not information. Second, and this is the load-bearing claim of the whole proposal: the assertion that proteolysis of CogAbeta-Clearer-08 and BasalAChE-Abeta-B4 liberates free amyloidogenic Abeta16-35 is asserted, not computed, and the sequence argues against it. The motif quoted in the proposal, KLVFFAEDVGSNKGAIIGLM, contains K16 at position 1 and K28 internally, both tryptic sites; chymotrypsin additionally cuts after F19, F20 and L34. So trypsin and chymotrypsin cut INSIDE the fibril core, and the species released would be fragments, not the intact nucleating segment. Whether an intact amyloidogenic fragment survives depends entirely on which protease and which flanking chemistry — which is exactly what the census can determine and must not pre-empt.
critiques.feasibility_objection: Sound. The sequence half is essentially done; the structural half depends on re-running Boltz with output persistence, which is a shared prerequisite with META-1 and STRUCTBIO-IDEA-1 and should be scheduled once rather than three times. The finding that no mmCIF from the 22 runs survives anywhere in the repo is correct and is a genuine blocker for the structural gating.
critiques.improvement: (1) Report every site count against a composition-matched shuffle null (reuse AIML-BENCH-3's generator), as a z-score, so a reader can see whether the cleavage pattern reflects design or arithmetic. For the linker-cut fraction specifically the null is informative and cheap: GGGGS contains no tryptic or chymotryptic site at all, so a high linker-cut fraction under trypsin would be a real anomaly and a low one is expected — state which. (2) Compute the released-fragment identity rather than asserting it. For each protease and each Abeta-motif-containing candidate, emit the actual fragment list with exact substring cross-reference to motif_provenance, and report explicitly whether any released fragment contains an intact aggregation-competent segment. If the honest answer is that trypsin destroys the core and only a pepsin- or thermolysin-like activity liberates it intact, that is a more precise and more useful hazard statement than the current one. (3) Broaden the protease panel toward CNS- and plasma-relevant activities rather than the classical proteomics set: neprilysin, insulin-degrading enzyme and the aminopeptidases dominate peptide clearance in this compartment, and a panel of trypsin/chymotrypsin/pepsin/thermolysin/proteinase K/Glu-C is a proteomics panel wearing a DMPK label. Where no retrievable specificity rule exists for an enzyme, say so and leave it out — do not substitute a similar one. (4) Deduplicate: the 36-mer with 24 sites is counted three times in the catalogue-level totals.

critiques.scientific_objection: The core insight — that facial segregation, not the amino-acid census, determines lytic potential, so peptide.py's frac_cationic AND frac_aromatic boolean is the wrong trigger — is correct and important. But the specific quantitative claims do not survive checking. (a) modlAMP is not importable in either venv named in the task brief: both /Users/seunghojung/Documents/DeepMind_Bio/.venv/bin/python and .venv312/bin/python return ModuleNotFoundError. The 'verified installed and working on this machine's arm64 Python 3.14 in this session' claim does not reproduce for me, so every downstream number is currently unaudited by any second party. (b) I reimplemented the Eisenberg max-over-18-residue-window moment independently and broadly reproduce the values (six candidate codes at 0.883-0.893), but the max-over-window modality is strongly length-biased and the proposal's headline conclusion inverts once that is corrected. I measured the null: 200 composition-matched shuffles per length give a mean max-window moment of 0.327 at L=26, 0.381 at L=36, 0.401 at L=50, 0.460 at L=75 and 0.491 at L=100. So CogDual-TrkB-PAS-10, the 100-mer presented as the critical false negative, has essentially the same raw moment (0.893) as three 36-mers but a null 0.11 units higher — in z-score terms it is the LEAST amphipathic of the high scorers, not the most alarming. The reference panel compounds it: melittin (26), magainin-2 (23), LL-37 (37) and insulin B-chain (30) all sit in the 23-37 range, so benchmarking a 100-mer against them compares along precisely the biased axis. (c) 'Six candidates score 0.886-0.894' is four distinct sequences — HippoAChE-AlkaPept-X2, BasalAChE-GorgeBlock-B1 and CogAChE-PAS-02 are the identical 36-mer.
critiques.feasibility_objection: The moment and control panel are near-trivial once the dependency question is settled, and the RMT motif census is an exact substring test. HemoPI2 is the risk: it is not verified installed anywhere I can see, it pulls a large ESM/PyTorch download, and its applicability domain against the Hemolytik training distribution will almost certainly exclude the 100-mer and 62-mer — which the proposal anticipates, so the honest outcome may be that the hemolysis arm returns refusals for the molecules of greatest concern. Budget for that outcome rather than for a number.
critiques.improvement: (1) State the environment and get the dependency into a named venv before any number is quoted; run melittin at the stated 0.558 +/- 0.001 as the install check, exactly as proposed. (2) Report the hydrophobic moment as a z-score against 200+ length- and composition-matched shuffles, not as a raw value against a fixed 23-37-residue control panel. This is one function call away from AIML-BENCH-3's generator, it removes the length artifact I measured, and it converts 'moment 0.894' into 'this sequence's facial segregation exceeds 99% of shuffles of its own residues', which is the claim a reader can act on. Report the raw value and the control panel too — they are useful for orientation — but let the z-score drive any liability trigger. (3) Deduplicate to 26 sequences before counting how many candidates are lytic. (4) Keep the BBB section exactly as written; the applicability-domain refusal plus the DOI-carrying RMT shuttle motif census is the strongest and most honest part of the proposal, and it is the part that does not depend on any predictor being installed. (5) Do not retire the frac_cationic/frac_aromatic rule silently — publish the confusion matrix of old rule versus new z-score across the 26 sequences, so the change is auditable rather than asserted to be an improvement.

critiques.scientific_objection: The chemistry is right and the diagnostics are the correct ones: S-S distance, chi3 near +/-90 degrees, and sulfur valence are exactly what distinguishes a real disulfide from a diffusion-model artifact, and the trivalent-sulfur finding is a genuine impossibility that pLDDT cannot see. The cis-Pro false positive against the current Ca-Ca rule is a good catch. One substantive objection, in the emission step. The proposal moves disulfide_connectivity to a PREDICTED ProvenanceValue wherever the predicted S-S set passes distance, chi3 and valence. But the coordinates it reads come from a single unseeded diffusion sample from the same run that produced 1.705 A and 2.552 A S-S distances and chi3 values of -1.1, +156.0, +163.8 and +174.4 degrees. A connectivity read off one draw of a sampler that is demonstrably producing impossible sulfur chemistry elsewhere in the same batch is sampler noise wearing a provenance envelope. Passing the geometric filter shows the draw was self-consistent, not that the connectivity is right — and connectivity is precisely the quantity CBC-CC-3 shows the molecule does not determine. Second, smaller: a 2.5 A Sg-Sg cutoff sits well above the 2.031-2.064 A experimental range measured in 4EY7 and will capture non-bonded thiol pairs in a cysteine-dense 8-Cys peptide, inflating the contact count that then feeds the valence check.
critiques.feasibility_objection: None — this is the most feasible proposal in the set. gemmi is already present as a Boltz dependency, the 22 mmCIFs exist (subject to the /tmp durability bug the proposal correctly identifies as blocker zero), and the analysis runs in under a second. The reference-set download is minutes. Two days is realistic and possibly generous.
critiques.improvement: (1) Gate the emission on reproducibility, not on a single draw: only move disulfide_connectivity out of not_computed where the same pairing is recovered across N>=3 seeds AND it agrees with the parent motif's published pattern (retrievable via motif_provenance). Everything else stays not_computed with the measured geometry attached as the reason — which is a stronger deliverable anyway, because it states what the model produced without granting it the status of a chemical fact. This also makes STRUCTBIO-IDEA-1 and CBC-CC-3 mutually consistent rather than in tension: one says connectivity is undetermined by the molecule, the other must not then assign it from one sample. (2) Report the S-S contact census at two cutoffs (2.3 A and 2.5 A) so the sensitivity of the trivalent-sulfur count to the cutoff is visible; four candidates with a cysteine in two bonds is a strong claim and should be shown to be cutoff-robust. (3) Deduplicate: check whether the four trivalent-sulfur candidates (BasalM1-PAM-B2, BasalSuper-AChE-TrkA-B5, MicroDual-Trem2-Nrf2-M5, MicroNrf2-AntiInflam-M2) are four distinct sequences — nine of the 35 candidate records are duplicates of another, and an artifact count over records rather than molecules will be quoted onward as if it were four independent failures. (4) Calibrate the reference distribution on disulfide-rich structures specifically, not only on the target_records list: 4EY7 and the other AChE entries are cysteine-sparse relative to an 8-Cys 47-mer, so the false-positive rate that matters is the one measured on knottins and EGF-like domains.

critiques.scientific_objection: The criterion-exercise audit is the best general idea in the panel — a criterion with zero rejections over a large denominator is a decorative criterion, and generalising that into a build gate is genuinely novel discipline. I verified the specific failure in source and in data: corpus.py's iter_target_activities reads a.get('confidence_score') from /activity records, and every one of the 18 admitted compounds in data/corpus_ACHE.json carries assay_confidence: null while protocol_summary advertises 'assay confidence >= 8'. The rejected-bucket structure (unparseable / tier_excluded / no_structure / too_large, with 240 of 258 rejected as tier_excluded) confirms no confidence bucket ever existed. Two objections. First, fixing the /assay join solves the plumbing but not the science: for this target, confidence score is the wrong criterion to be arguing about. ChEMBL confidence 9 versus 8 distinguishes direct from homologous single-protein assignment; it does not distinguish an Ellman assay on recombinant human AChE from one on eel or bovine erythrocyte enzyme mapped to CHEMBL220, and the latter is the dominant source of the corpus's log-scale scatter. Raising to 9 will shrink the corpus without removing the real confound. Second, the pre-registration is incomplete in exactly the place the panel is most exposed. The proposal pre-declares a replicate-aggregation rule, correctly. But MEDCHEM-IDEA-2 is simultaneously proposing to re-score the headline benchmark using an aggregation rule (median) chosen after observing that it halves the error and moves the model from worse-than-null to better-than-null. Unless affinity-ache-v1 is frozen BEFORE that re-scoring is published, the pre-specification machinery will be built and then bypassed on its first real use.
critiques.feasibility_objection: Two days for the format, freeze/verify and audit is right. The continuous-validation job is the weak point: ChEMBL's REST API returned HTTP 500 to every request I made this session — direct urllib, curl, and via an MCP client — so a scheduled re-run needs an explicit availability policy. As specified, an outage produces an empty admitted set, which the drift report will render as either 'zero drift' or a spurious total-loss diff. Neither is correct.
critiques.improvement: (1) Make the freeze of affinity-ache-v1 a hard prerequisite for MEDCHEM-IDEA-2's re-scoring, and put the replicate-aggregation rule, the enantiomer-handling rule and the compound population into the frozen YAML before any recomputed huperzine A number is published. The 2.41 -> 1.43 retraction is the first thing this machinery should govern; if it is published first and pre-registered afterwards, the mechanism is theatre. (2) Replace min_assay_confidence as the headline curation criterion with an executable assay-provenance criterion: enzyme source and species parsed from assay_description and bao_label, with a stated rejection count.
