Keep confidence as a secondary filter once the /assay join works. The criterion-exercise audit then has something meaningful to exercise. (3) Add availability handling: record HTTP status and record count per criterion on every scheduled run, and fail loudly rather than emitting a diff when the source is unreachable. A monitored corpus whose monitor cannot distinguish 'nothing changed' from 'the server was down' is not monitored. (4) Extend the audit's zero-rejection rule with its mirror: a criterion that rejects 100% or ~0% of a large denominator both warrant a flag. tier_excluded rejecting 240 of 258 is arithmetically active but is doing the work of a pharmacology filter using ChEMBL's noisy natural_product flag, which this repo already documents as labelling donepezil and metoclopramide natural products — an over-firing criterion is as much a protocol defect as an inert one.

critiques.critic: Human genetics / statistical genetics (PhD, 16 years; therapeutic target validation via human genetics, MR and colocalization). Citations below were retrieved this session via PubMed and NCBI E-utilities; DOIs are given as links. I reviewed GENO-A/B/C in full, plus the proposals whose core is null-model construction, calibration, leakage, measurement error or pre-specification (AIML-STRUCT-1, AIML-STRUCT-2, AIML-BENCH-1, AIML-BENCH-3, CBC-CC-1, MEDCHEM-IDEA-2, META-3). I skipped the structural-chemistry, pose-validity, proteolysis, immunogenicity, membrane-lysis, exit-vector and research-software-packaging proposals (AIML-BENCH-2, CBC-CC-2, CBC-CC-3, STRUCTBIO-1/2/3, MEDCHEM-1/3, DMPK-1/2/3, META-1, META-2) as outside my competence rather than bluff them. Verifications run against the repo this session: platform/cbc/provenance.py audit() confirmed to have no `str` branch; a decimal/integer scan of string fields in data/dataset.json target_records returns 712 numerals across 16 records (NTRK2 49, TREM2 72, NTRK1 61); a claim-shaped scan (numeral adjacent to a unit or %) over candidate prose returns exactly 6, all fabricated effect sizes (+280%, +310%, +240%, +350%, +420%, +45%). A GTEx v10 medianGeneExpression call from this machine did not return within 120 s in this session (possibly transient, but the "seconds" feasibility claim in GENO-C should be re-verified, not assumed). Panel-level observation before the individual reviews: AIML-STRUCT-1, AIML-BENCH-3 and STRUCTBIO-IDEA-3 all propose composition-matched scramble nulls with receptor co-folding, on overlapping candidate sets, with different K and mutually incompatible statistics; AIML-BENCH-1 and CBC-CC-1 are ~70% the same affinity benchmark. Running these separately triples the MPS budget and yields several non-comparable p-values for one question. Merge into one scramble module with one statistic and one affinity benchmark with one ground-truth aggregator before any of them runs.

critiques.scientific_objection: Three defects. (1) The rank/percentile is presented as the missing 'denominator' but it is not a calibration of anything. Minikel et al. 2024 (PMID 38632401, https://doi.org/10.1038/s41586-024-07316-0) report a relative success of 2.6x for mechanisms with genetic support, improving with confidence in the causal gene and largely unaffected by effect size or MAF. Nothing in that result licenses 'rank among the 13,289 genes with any Open Targets association to MONDO_0004975' as a prior on success. Worse, the Open Targets overall score is a weighted aggregate dominated here by the literature and clinical datatypes: the proposal's own table has ACHE at #7 on literature 0.936 and clinical 0.996 with genetic_association absent. The headline deliverable therefore ranks targets by how much has been written about them and whether a drug already exists — the exact circularity the proposal identifies one sentence earlier and then reports anyway. (2) The gnomAD v2-vs-v4 'two live authorities differ 1.8-fold' framing is a misdiagnosis. LOEUF is the upper bound of the 90% CI on the LoF observed/expected ratio (Karczewski et al. 2020, PMID 32461654, https://doi.org/10.1038/s41586-020-2308-7); it contracts toward o/e as the callset grows, so NTRK2 v2 LOEUF 0.219 versus v4 oe 0.0585 / oeUpper 0.123 is estimator precision, not disagreement. Storing both un-merged is correct; calling it a provenance conflict teaches the reader the wrong lesson and invites a cross-version threshold. (3) Constraint is being placed inside a 'genetic evidence layer' where it will be read as indication support. It is an unsigned, indication-agnostic dosage statistic. The curated target records already say this in prose; the schema must enforce it structurally, not restate it.
critiques.feasibility_objection: Two implementation defects that will get the gates switched off. (a) `prose_embedded_number` as a bare numeral regex over string leaves: measured this session, the 16 target records contain 712 numerals in prose, nearly all legitimate (UniProt ranges '295-365', PDB '4EY7', ClinVar counts, residue identifiers). A gate that emits ~700 violations against curated, human-verified narrative will be suppressed within a week, and the stated success criterion 'at least 16 failures' is met by noise rather than by detection. The signal is much sparser than the proposal assumes: a claim-shaped pattern (numeral adjacent to a unit or %) over candidate prose returns exactly 6 hits, and all 6 are the fabricated effect sizes (LTP +280%, +310%, +240%, +350%, +420%, +45%). (b) `check_genetic_drift` as a failing build gate: Open Targets rescores every release by design (new evidence, harmonization and scoring changes). A CI job that goes red whenever an upstream database updates converts a routine event into an alarm and will be disabled, and it repeats the failure the repo already recorded once, where a verifier flagged stale scores as 'wrong'.
critiques.improvement: Split the deliverable in three. (i) Rank on the genetic_association datatype score alone; report the overall-score rank separately and label it 'literature/clinical-driven, includes existing-drug circularity'. (ii) Add a binary genetic_support flag per Minikel's operational definition and attach the published relative success (2.6x) as an explicitly population-level statistic with a note that it is not a per-target probability. (iii) Store constraint as oe with oe_lower, oe_upper and callset n in a `constraint` field family that is structurally excluded from any support score, with a code comment that LOEUF is not comparable across gnomAD versions. Replace the numeral regex with a claim-shaped pattern scoped to candidate-facing prose, and add an explicit `narrative` field type on target records that audit() exempts by construction while requiring the extractable quantities to be migrated to typed Values. Convert check_genetic_drift from a gate into a scheduled report that emits a diff (old value, new value, both release ids) and requires a human pin bump; the only failing gate should be a Value whose source_id lacks a release token. Finally, strengthen the TPP check: an indication_id that merely parses is a schema, not a scientific gate — require that the declared indication is one for which the target has a retrievable release-pinned association record (zero is an acceptable value) and that the primary endpoint matches one used in a registered trial for that indication.

critiques.scientific_objection: The decisive defect is that a plasma pQTL is not an instrument for the quantity a TREM2 agonist modulates, and the sign can be inverted. TREM2 is shed at the H157-S158 bond by ADAM10, and the AD-risk H157Y variant accelerates that cleavage (Thornton et al. 2017, PMID 28855301, https://doi.org/10.15252/emmm.201707673); a Trem2 H157Y knock-in shows elevated soluble TREM2 with a higher soluble:full-length ratio and reduced TREM2 signalling (Qiao et al. 2023, PMID 36721205, https://doi.org/10.1186/s13024-023-00599-3). A UKB-PPP plasma pQTL for TREM2 therefore indexes shed ectodomain, and a variant that raises plasma sTREM2 can simultaneously lower cell-surface receptor available to an agonist. Signal (1) as specified would take that sign at face value and could emit CONCORDANT for a candidate whose direction is wrong. A layer that can be confidently wrong is worse than the current honest absence. Second defect: the four chosen signals will systematically miss the one real directional answer available in this target set. The strongest human directional evidence for TREM2 in AD is the coding allelic series — R47H (Jonsson et al. 2013, PMID 23150908, https://doi.org/10.1056/NEJMoa1211103; Guerreiro et al. 2013, PMID 23150934, https://doi.org/10.1056/NEJMoa1211851) — which is a risk-increasing partial-loss coding variant handled in GWAS and exome studies, not a ClinVar Mendelian record, so signal (4) will not see it and signal (2) returns null exactly as the proposal found. The layer as designed is therefore a guaranteed null-generator that misses its own best case. Third: no Mendelian randomization is actually specified. `betaRatioSignAverage` is a convenience field, not an analysis, and the cis-MR 'extension path' names no LD reference panel, no ancestry, no effect-allele harmonization procedure (the single largest source of sign errors in MR), and no Steiger filtering for reverse causation; at one instrument the exclusion restriction is untestable and no heterogeneity or MR-Egger diagnostic exists.
critiques.feasibility_objection: The API arm at 3-4 days is realistic. The cis-MR arm at 'roughly a week' is not, for the same reason given under GENO-C: it requires AD GWAS summary statistics and QTL summary statistics as bulk downloads with harmonization and, for the EADB component, an access-terms check. Also, the success criterion 'reports UNDETERMINED for at least 34 of 35 candidates' is satisfied by a module that returns UNDETERMINED unconditionally, so it does not demonstrate the layer works; only the fixture test (flipping modality flips the verdict) does, and that test only exercises the concordance rubric, not the retrieval.
critiques.improvement: Add a required `instrument_measures` annotation per QTL (shed_ectodomain | full_length_protein | transcript | splice) and a hard rule that a shed-ectodomain pQTL can never contribute to a directional verdict — it may only produce UNDETERMINED with the shedding mechanism and its citation attached. Add a fifth signal: a hand-curated, versioned, per-row-cited allelic-series table giving each variant's trait direction and its functional classification (hypomorph / GOF / shedding-altering / null), curated exactly like the InclusionProtocol. That is where a legitimate CONCORDANT verdict for a TREM2 agonist would come from, and it turns the layer from a null-generator into something with discriminative power. For the MR path, specify LD panel and ancestry, the harmonization procedure, Steiger filtering, and a printed statement that at n_IV = 1 pleiotropy is untestable. Finally, pre-declare the decision rule and its intended error rates before running, so the directional verdicts are not chosen after seeing the data.

critiques.scientific_objection: The core insight — that a molecular QTL is only a valid instrument if it is measured in the cell type where the drug must act — is the best genetics idea in the packet and I endorse it without reservation. The instrument-provenance arm (step 3) is correct as written. The expression arm is not. `check_region_claim` on bulk GTEx cannot test the claim it names: GTEx has 13 bulk brain regions, no hippocampal subfield and no cell-type resolution, and bulk TPM is a composition-weighted average, so 'CA1 pyramidal neurons' is not testable from that source at all. Worse, the gate as specified ('fails any candidate whose target's peak expression is extra-CNS by more than a stated fold') will fail TREM2 — a myeloid-restricted gene with high spleen, blood and lung expression — which is the one target the proposal itself identifies as genetically supported and which is correctly a brain-microglial target. That is a false positive on the only true positive, and it is exactly the kind of gate that gets a threshold quietly raised until it fires on nothing. Separately, the 'specificity index = brain-region median / whole-body median' is not a specificity statistic: TPM is compositional and within-sample normalized, so cross-tissue ratios are confounded by library composition, and an ad hoc ratio has no denominator — the very complaint GENO-A makes about a bare Open Targets score. The CHRFAM7A paralog caveat for CHRNA7 is correct and should be kept.
critiques.feasibility_objection: Step 2 is materially understated. MetaBrain (de Klein et al. 2023, PMID 36823318, https://doi.org/10.1038/s41588-023-01300-6) and MiGA (Lopes et al. 2022, PMID 34992268, https://doi.org/10.1038/s41588-021-00976-y) publish summary statistics as bulk files, not per-gene APIs, and colocalization additionally requires AD GWAS summary statistics (Bellenguez et al. 2022, PMID 35379992, https://doi.org/10.1038/s41588-022-01024-z), whose EADB component carries controlled-access terms that must be checked before the plan assumes a download. Add liftover to a single build and consistent effect-allele orientation. 'Roughly a week, computation trivial' underestimates the data engineering substantially and skips an access question. Power is also a problem the plan does not acknowledge: MiGA is 255 samples from 100 donors, which for cis-eQTL colocalization at a specific gene is thin — a null there means 'underpowered', not 'no instrument available', and the success criterion as written would record the wrong conclusion. Minor: a GTEx v10 medianGeneExpression call from this machine did not return within 120 s in this session, so the step-1 'seconds' claim should be re-verified.
critiques.improvement: Split the expression arm into two differently named quantities. (a) `peripheral_exposure_index` from GTEx = max non-CNS tissue median / max CNS tissue median, framed and gated purely as an on-target peripheral-toxicity liability for a systemically dosed agent, never as a refutation of a region claim; state the formula, and report the index's distribution across all genes so any single value has a denominator, or use a published specificity measure rather than an ad hoc ratio. (b) `cell_type_expression` from a single-nucleus brain atlas, which is the only source that can address 'CA1 pyramidal neuron' or 'microglia'; region and cell-type claims are checked against that, and anything the atlas cannot resolve is recorded NOT_TESTABLE rather than failed. Keep step 3 exactly as proposed — it is the strongest single check in the whole packet — and add a required power field to every colocalization result (QTL sample size, minimum detectable PP4 given that n) so that 'no colocalization' and 'underpowered to detect one' are distinguishable Values. Before committing to step 2, do a one-day spike: confirm the actual file sizes and the access terms for each summary-statistics source and record them, then re-estimate.

critiques.scientific_objection: The instinct is right and the pilot is the most valuable single result in the packet — a scramble beating the native is exactly the observation that stops a false positive. But the statistic is invalid as specified and the design cannot reach its own success criterion. (1) The empirical p compares a median over 5 native seeds against single-seed decoys. The two arms have different sampling variance — the native median of 5 draws carries roughly 1/sqrt(5) of the seed noise of a single decoy draw — so the reference distribution is not the null distribution of the test statistic. With a reported across-seed sd of 0.133 on a 0-1 metric and decoys ranging 0.308-0.735, that mismatch is not negligible. (2) The scramble null and the off-target-receptor null answer different questions and the proposal treats them as interchangeable. A composition-matched shuffle tests whether residue order carries information; it does not test binding specificity, because a promiscuous cationic amphipath and a genuine designed binder can both beat their own shuffles. Only the off-target panel speaks to specificity, and 5 receptors drawn from an unmatched set of 16 is neither size- nor charge-matched to the cognate receptor.
critiques.feasibility_objection: Arithmetic, not compute. With K = 20 decoys the minimum attainable empirical p is 1/21 = 0.048; after Holm correction across even 10 candidates the smallest achievable adjusted p is about 0.48, and across 35 it is worse. No candidate can be declared sequence-specific at any conventional level, for reasons entirely independent of the biology. Reaching family-wise 0.05 across 35 candidates would need on the order of 700 decoys each, which the stated ~24 h MPS budget cannot support.
critiques.improvement: Match the arms: run decoys at the same seed count as natives and compare median to median, or define the statistic on a single draw in both arms. Then drop the family-wise p-value as the primary readout — it is unreachable at feasible K — and make the primary readout a standardized effect size (native mean minus decoy mean, over decoy sd) with a bootstrap 95% CI, reported per candidate with the full null distribution published. If a p-value is wanted, pre-declare a small primary set of 3-5 candidates at K = 100 and treat the remainder as exploratory with no correction claimed. Finally, name in the protocol which null answers which question — order-information (scramble) versus receptor-specificity (off-target panel) — and size- and pI-match the off-target receptors, otherwise the specificity arm confounds interface score with receptor size.

critiques.scientific_objection: Deduplication is specified on the receptor only (30-40% identity, or mmseqs2). For peptide-protein complexes, leakage runs through the peptide and the interface as much as through the receptor: two entries with dissimilar receptors can present near-identical epitope-peptide pairs, and a post-cutoff entry can be a re-determination of a pre-cutoff interface. Receptor-level dedup will therefore leave residual leakage in a benchmark whose entire purpose is to be leakage-free. Second, the calibration statistics are under-powered for what is being claimed. At N ~ 100 split into reliability bins, per-bin n is ~10-20; a Wilson interval at n = 15 spans roughly +/-0.25 in probability, so the per-bin P(DockQ >= 0.23) will not support the 'stated, defensible ipTM threshold' the success criteria demand, and binned expected calibration error at n = 100 is strongly biased by bin choice.
critiques.feasibility_objection: The proposal is honest that the server-side clustering call returned HTTP 400 and is unvalidated, which is good practice; but the 100-complex target was sized without a power calculation, so the compute estimate is right while the sample size is not. There is no cost barrier to increasing N — the same 1-3 min per complex applies — so the fix is cheap.
critiques.improvement: Dedup on the interface pair, not the receptor: cluster on receptor identity AND peptide/epitope identity, and additionally exclude any post-cutoff entry that is a re-determination of a pre-cutoff complex (same UniProt pair, same ligand peptide). Replace raw binning with a monotone calibration (isotonic or Platt) fitted with a bootstrap band, report the derived threshold as an interval rather than a point, and extend the refusal rule in calibrated_interface_probability: refuse not only outside populated bins but whenever the interval width exceeds a pre-declared maximum. Compute the N required for that maximum width before running, and size the benchmark to it rather than to a round number.

critiques.scientific_objection: The noise-ceiling-plus-null-floor framing is correct and rare, and I endorse the shape. Three statistical defects. (1) sigma_exp from 18 replicate pairs is over-precise and the effective n is wrong: the pairs are not independent draws, because a few compounds contribute several each (TACRINE spans five documents), so the sampling unit is the compound, not the pair, and 0.376 log10 is quoted to three figures on an effective n well below 18. (2) The 'error below experimental uncertainty implies overtraining' inference is only valid if the model predicts the same quantity the replicates measure. If the benchmark's ground truth is a per-compound aggregate over k measurements, its error is sigma_exp/sqrt(k), not sigma_exp, so the attainable floor is lower than stated and the overtraining test would fire spuriously on a legitimately good model. (3) The temporal split boundary — 'the ChEMBL v34 release that Boltz-2 trained on' — is not a leakage boundary. ChEMBL v34 contains activities from documents published decades earlier, and Boltz-2's affinity head also drew on BindingDB, PDBbind and MF-PCBA with their own coverage, so a document-year split does not partition seen from unseen. The exact (compound, target) membership test is the real leakage measurement and should be the primary one.
critiques.feasibility_objection: None material — the ceiling, floor and baselines cost minutes, and the ~10 h MPS batch is realistic at the measured 3 min 4 s per complex. The one scheduling risk is duplication: this proposal and CBC-CC-1 are largely the same experiment with different targets and baselines, and running both spends the overnight budget twice for one answer.
critiques.improvement: Report sigma_exp with a bootstrap CI resampled over compounds and state n_compounds alongside n_pairs. Define the prediction target explicitly (single measurement versus per-compound aggregate) and set the noise floor to the sd of whichever is used. Promote the exact-membership leakage test and the Tanimoto-stratified metrics to primary; demote the temporal split to a labelled sensitivity analysis with its limitation stated in the output file rather than reported side by side as an equal. Merge with CBC-CC-1 into one benchmark with one ground-truth aggregator, one decoy design and one target list, and give the merged protocol a power calculation stating the minimum detectable paired delta against the null at the planned n, so that 'not distinguishable from the null model' is interpretable as a result rather than as an artifact of sample size.

critiques.scientific_objection: The proposal contains one genuinely free and correct win that the neighbouring scramble proposals lack: MW, net charge at pH 7.4, pI and GRAVY are order-invariant by construction, therefore carry exactly zero design information, and can be relabelled 'composition-determined' on every candidate card before a single folding run. That is right, costs nothing, and should be done this week. The rest of the proposal is duplicative of AIML-STRUCT-1 and STRUCTBIO-IDEA-3, with a third and mutually incompatible statistic for the same question, and it inherits the same conceptual gap: a composition-matched shuffle tests order-information, not binding specificity, so 'sequence-specific' is a misleading label for what a positive result would establish.
critiques.feasibility_objection: The stated success criterion is unreachable by construction. At K = 20 the minimum empirical p is 1/21 = 0.048; Holm across the ten candidates gives a smallest achievable adjusted p of about 0.48. The verdict string 'sequence-specific (Holm-corrected p < 0.05)' can therefore never be emitted no matter what the folding shows, which means the study cannot produce its own stated positive outcome. Separately, 210 two-chain runs at 11-14 h is being spent to answer a question two other proposals also intend to answer.
critiques.improvement: Extract the order-invariance relabelling as a standalone one-day change and ship it immediately — it retires four numbers from every candidate card with a proof, not a prediction. Fold everything else into a single merged scramble module (see AIML-STRUCT-1), with one statistic, one seeded RNG scheme, one candidate list and a standardized effect size with bootstrap CI as the primary readout rather than an unreachable corrected p-value. If a significance claim is wanted at all, pre-declare three candidates at K = 100 and treat the rest as exploratory.

critiques.scientific_objection: The per-target-median null is the correct baseline and the refusal-if-you-cannot-beat-it rule is the correct discipline. But two things are mis-specified. (1) The decoy AUROC for affinity_probability_binary does not validate the affinity value; it validates a binary binder-classifier head against unrelated receptors, and AUROC against arbitrary decoys is inflated by any receptor-family or size signal rather than by binding-site complementarity. Reporting it next to the RMSE invites the reader to treat it as evidence about the number. (2) With >=60 pairs spread over >=4 targets, per-target n is ~15. A paired test against a per-target median at n = 15 has low power, so a failure to beat the null is uninterpretable — it cannot distinguish 'the predictor adds nothing' from 'the study could not tell'. Since the pre-declared consequence of failing is to emit no dG anywhere, an underpowered design silently converts into a permanent refusal on statistical grounds rather than scientific ones.
critiques.feasibility_objection: 200-300 unattended MPS runs at the measured ~3 min each is realistic. The scheduling problem is overlap with AIML-BENCH-1, which proposes the same measurement with a different corpus, different baselines and a different aggregator; the two will produce two non-comparable RMSEs for the platform's affinity head.
critiques.improvement: Compute the power of the paired comparison at the planned n and publish the minimum detectable effect in the protocol before running; if the MDE exceeds roughly 0.5 log10 units, either scale the corpus or pre-declare that a null result will be reported as 'underpowered' rather than as 'does not beat the null'. Report the decoy AUROC in a clearly separated section labelled as a binary-classifier property, with size- and family-matched decoys rather than arbitrary ones. When writing the measured RMSE into thermo.METHOD_ACCURACY, make the key carry its applicability domain (target list, heavy-atom range, MSA mode, backend) as structured fields, not prose — otherwise the number will be reused out of domain, which is precisely the failure admet.py's refusal pattern exists to prevent. Merge the ground-truth aggregation with AIML-BENCH-1 and MEDCHEM-IDEA-2 so all three use one aggregator.

critiques.scientific_objection: This is the most important finding in the packet and it should be actioned first: the platform's flagship self-criticism — a 2.41 log10 error on huperzine A — was computed against the second most potent of 23 IC50 values spanning 3.99 log units, so the project's headline honesty result is itself a mis-measurement. Two refinements are needed. (1) Re-scoring against the median replaces one point estimate with another and repeats the defect at lower magnitude. The defensible statement compares the prediction to the distribution: report where 1274 nM falls as a percentile of the 23 measurements, and report the error against the endpoint-class aggregate with a CI that propagates aggregation uncertainty. (2) The aggregator is left open between median and geometric mean while the proposal simultaneously and correctly insists on retaining standard_relation. The geometric mean is undefined on censored values, so the aggregator and the censoring rule must be fixed in advance — pre-declare exclusion of '>' and '<' records from the aggregate with separate reporting as one-sided bounds — or the choice becomes a degree of freedom exercised after the model output is known. Third, minor but worth enforcing: the literature sigma (heterogeneous between-lab public IC50) and the corpus sigma (within-compound across-document, on this corpus) measure different things and must never be pooled; use the corpus figure for this corpus and cite the literature figure only as external context.
critiques.feasibility_objection: None material. One extra ChEMBL /assay call per batch, a dataclass widening and an aggregation step; the endpoint-class table is curation, correctly identified as the real cost. The endpoint-typing insight — that the 5.0 nM record is an AChE-induced amyloid-beta aggregation phenotype and not catalytic inhibition — is the substantive part and is a judgement call that must be written down with a rationale per row.
critiques.improvement: Fix the aggregator and censoring rule in a pre-specified protocol before recomputing anything (this is the natural first instance for META-3's freeze mechanism). Emit each aggregate as n, median, geometric mean of uncensored records, log10 range, IQR in log space, and the count of censored records reported separately. For the retraction, publish the corrected comparison as a percentile against the endpoint-class distribution plus an error-to-noise ratio, not as a second single number; link the retraction to the original 2.41 claim in the ledger. Require every endpoint-class table row to carry a rationale and a citation, and add a test that fails the build if a row lacks one — the same discipline the InclusionProtocol already has.

critiques.scientific_objection: The criterion-exercise audit — a filter that has never rejected a record over N examined is decoration and must fail the gate — is a genuinely novel, generalizable check and the strongest methodological contribution in the packet; it would have caught the assay_confidence bug and will catch its successors. Two objections to the pre-specification half. (1) Hash-locking against a ledger the same agent controls is not pre-registration. Nothing in the design prevents freezing several protocols and reporting the one that came out well; the append-only property proves the timestamp order of a single protocol, not the absence of selective reporting across protocols. That is exactly the failure mode pre-registration exists to prevent, and it is the one this scheme leaves open. (2) The decision rule is pre-specified with blanks: 'MAE 95% CI upper bound below X log units and rho above Y'. A protocol with unset thresholds is not pre-specified; the thresholds are the pre-specification. They also cannot be set by preference — they must be tied to the measurement's own noise floor.
critiques.feasibility_objection: n = 18 for the first instance. A bootstrap CI on MAE at n = 18 will be wide enough that the CI upper bound is likely to exceed any defensible threshold regardless of how the model performs, so the pre-declared 'otherwise NOT_COMPUTED' branch is close to a foregone conclusion driven by sample size rather than by the predictor. Publishing that as a negative result would be a claim about the platform's statistical power dressed as a claim about Boltz-2. The ~18-complex overnight batch itself is fine.
critiques.improvement: Make the protocol registry enumerable and require every frozen protocol to reach a terminal recorded outcome — completed, or abandoned with a stated reason — so the denominator of attempts is visible; that is the checkable analogue of a trial registry and closes the selective-reporting hole. Set the thresholds numerically and tie them to the noise floor from MEDCHEM-IDEA-2 (for example: report as PREDICTED only if the CI upper bound on MAE is below 2 x sigma_exp for the relevant endpoint class). Add a mandatory power section to the protocol template stating the minimum detectable difference against the null at the planned n, computed and frozen before the run; if the MDE at n = 18 is uninformative, either scale the corpus first or pre-declare that the outcome will be reported as 'underpowered', not as a refusal. Ship the criterion-exercise audit independently of the pre-specification machinery — it is valuable on its own and needs none of the freeze infrastructure.

critiques.critic: DMPK / CNS drug delivery (PhD, 17 years industry; preclinical CNS peptides)

critiques.scientific_objection: Three defects. (1) The junction premise is quantitatively overstated. I counted the current data/dataset.json today: only 6/35 sequences contain GGGGS at all, 8/35 contain GGGS, and by the repo's own gg_linker_fraction() regex exactly ONE candidate (CogDual-TrkB-PAS-10) has non-zero linker content. There are also only 26 unique sequences among the 35 candidates (KWWKFLRRFWRRLKKYFEELWKKLAEKYFELLKKYG appears 3x). So 'junctional neo-epitopes manufactured by the GGGGS joins' describes a small minority of the catalogue; the dominant junction class is blunt motif-motif abutment with no linker, which the method text never distinguishes. (2) The SELF/NEO call by exact 9-mer match against UP000005640 errs in both directions. Central tolerance is against peptides actually processed and presented (AIRE-dependent thymic presentation), not against every 9-mer in the proteome, so a self-9-mer match does not establish tolerance; conversely MHC-II registers are degenerate and peptide-flanking residues modulate both processing and TCR contact, so a core differing at a non-anchor position from self is frequently cross-tolerized. An exact-match binary will over-call NEO. (3) Binder count is a weak surrogate for clinical ADA and is being reported without a comparator. Attermann et al., Immunology 2020 (PMID 33010039, doi:10.1111/imm.13274, retrieved this session) show that affinity-trained NetMHCIIpan-3.2 has a materially higher false-positive rate for MAPPs hotspots than an EL/MS-trained model, and position in silico prediction as a complement to MAPPs, not a substitute. Separately, for 3-11 kDa polycationic amphipaths the dominant ADA driver is likely aggregate/particulate and T-cell-independent, and membrane lysis precedes immunogenicity as a liability; ranking this above DMPK-IDEA-3 misorders the stack.
critiques.feasibility_objection: The binary-availability claims do not survive a check of the repo. Neither MHC-II predictor, nor any dependency of one, is present in .venv (Python 3.14.6) or .venv312 — I checked both. NetMHCIIpan-4.3 is licence-gated behind a request form and DTU has historically shipped Darwin builds for x86_64; an arm64 Darwin package should be verified, not assumed. MixMHC2pred-2.0's training data are mono-allelic MS lines heavily weighted to HLA-DR, so an 'allele coverage fraction' reported across DR/DQ/DP will be misleading. Budget the licence wait and the Rosetta fallback as real schedule.
critiques.improvement: Make the primary output a within-construct delta rather than an absolute count: (binder / neo-core burden of the construct) minus (union of burdens of its parent motifs scored separately). motif_provenance already gives 16 exactly attributed motifs with UniProt accessions, so this is computable today and is the only quantity attributable to the design decision rather than to the source biology. Add a control panel of clinically characterised sequences with published ADA rates through the identical pipeline so the count lands on an interpretable scale — the same calibration discipline DMPK-IDEA-3 applies with melittin. Use an EL/MS-trained predictor as primary and report the affinity-trained one only as a sensitivity arm, citing the measured FPR gap. Replace the binary SELF/NEO with three states (exact self match / self match with <=1 non-anchor mismatch / no match) and state in the field note that tolerance is presentation-dependent, not proteome-dependent. Report per unique sequence (n=26), not per candidate (n=35).

critiques.scientific_objection: The protease panel is a proteomics digestion panel, not a clearance panel, and the headline numbers it would produce are numbers without knowledge. Trypsin, chymotrypsin, pepsin pH2.0, thermolysin, proteinase K and Glu-C are laboratory reagents; none is a determinant of plasma or brain-ECF exposure. '215 trypsin-like sites' will always look catastrophic for Arg/Lys-rich peptides while systemic clearance at 3-11 kDa is dominated by glomerular filtration plus exopeptidase trimming (aminopeptidases, DPP-4 at the Xaa-Pro/Xaa-Ala N-terminus, carboxypeptidases), and in brain ECF/CSF by neprilysin, IDE and ACE — a different enzyme set with different specificity. Second, parser.cleave() returns a COMPLETE-digest fragment set, which has no kinetic interpretation and cannot answer the proposal's own headline question ('which bond is cut first'); only the exposure ranking approximates that. Third, the most predictive sequence-level stability determinants are terminal, not internal — free alpha-amino group, identity of residue 2, free C-terminal carboxylate, absence of amidation — and the endoprotease census sees none of them (only 5/35 candidate records mention amidation in any form). Fourth, the structural gate imports the unmeasured error of lone-chain msa=empty Boltz-2 models into a DMPK label; frac_below_70 mitigates but does not calibrate it. The Abeta16-35 liberation analysis is the strongest part, but both Abeta-bearing candidates are already flagged by peptide.py's KLVFF rule, so the increment is fragment identity plus release route, not the hazard itself.
critiques.feasibility_objection: pyteomics, biotite and freesasa are absent from BOTH venvs today (.venv 3.14.6 and .venv312) — the 'verified installed this session' claims do not reproduce against the repo state, which matters in a proposal about traceability. And a stated success criterion will fail on delivery: 'the 12 candidates with non-zero GGGGS/GS linker content (0.06 to 0.29)' does not reproduce — 6/35 sequences contain GGGGS, 8/35 contain GGGS, and by the repo's own gg_linker_fraction() exactly 1 candidate has non-zero linker content.
critiques.improvement: Rescope from a protease census to a structural susceptibility map: rank contiguous segments >=10 residues that are solvent-exposed, non-helical/non-sheet and not disulfide-constrained, per the threading requirement for limited proteolysis. That is protease-agnostic, defensible from coordinates, and makes no enzyme-identity claim. Add a separate deterministic terminal audit — N-terminal residue, P2 identity (DPP-4 motif), C-terminal residue, declared amidation/acetylation — three exact bits per molecule that are more predictive of exposure than the whole endoprotease count. If an endopeptidase arm is kept, restrict it to enzymes with a stated role at the intended site (NEP, IDE, ACE, plasmin, kallikrein), take specificity from a retrieved source (MEROPS) rather than expasy_rules, and label output 'in vitro specificity rule match', never 'stability'. Keep the no-t1/2 rule verbatim — it is the best clause in the batch. Merge the mmCIF persistence work with META-1 step 2 and STRUCTBIO-IDEA-1 step 6 so it is implemented once. Report over 26 unique sequences.

critiques.scientific_objection: The trigger metric is length-biased and the control panel does not calibrate it. (1) mu_H taken as the maximum over 18-residue windows is monotone non-decreasing in length: a 100-mer offers 83 windows to maximise over, a 26-mer offers 9. Comparing CogDual-TrkB-PAS-10 (100 aa, 0.894) with melittin (26 aa, 0.558) is not like-for-like, and the headline finding that the largest construct 'exceeds LL-37' is partly a sampling artifact. (2) The panel itself falsifies the metric's use as a potency trigger: LL-37 is scored at 0.897, above melittin at 0.558, yet melittin is by far the more hemolytic peptide. A descriptor that is non-monotone in the endpoint it is being used to flag cannot be the trigger. (3) Insulin B-chain is a poor negative — it is surface-active and amyloidogenic, and it is not a therapeutic-peptide comparator. (4) mu_H presupposes helix; gating on Boltz-2 SSE from lone-chain msa=empty models imports that pipeline's unquantified error into a safety call. (5) HemoPI2's training distribution (Hemolytik) is dominated by AMPs under ~40 residues; the 100-mer and 62-mer are outside domain, and a two-point melittin/insulin gate is far too weak to license reporting an HC50.
critiques.feasibility_objection: modlAMP is not installed in .venv (3.14.6) or .venv312 — I checked both today, so 'verified installed and working on this machine's arm64 Python 3.14' does not reproduce from the repo state; modlAMP has historically pinned older numpy/scipy, which on 3.14 is a real install risk, not a formality. HemoPI2's ESM/PyTorch download is multi-GB but CPU-feasible.
critiques.improvement: Replace the absolute threshold with a composition-matched null computed per molecule: mu_H(design) versus the distribution over >=200 shuffles of the same residue multiset, reported as percentile and z-score. That controls length and composition at once, makes a 26-mer and a 100-mer comparable, and shares machinery with AIML-BENCH-3. Also report the TOTAL sequence length residing in windows above a stated mu_H — the size of the putative lytic face scales with potency and is not length-biased the same way. Expand the control panel to >=15 peptides with measured HC50 spanning >=2 logs and report Spearman rho between mu_H and measured HC50; if that CI includes zero, do not use mu_H as a trigger at all and publish that — a cheap, decisive negative. Keep the BBB refusal, but note the RMT census is already determinate: 0/35 sequences contain Angiopep-2, T7 (HAIYPRH), RVG29, TAT or ApoE(159-167) as an exact substring, and only 4/35 fall inside B3Pred's 5-30 residue domain (both verified today). A census whose answer is one 'absent' for the whole catalogue belongs in the README as a design finding, not as 35 per-candidate fields. Demote frac_cationic/frac_aromatic to a descriptor and label it composition-determined (it is order-invariant by construction).

critiques.scientific_objection: The veto rests on an unstated premise — that the crystallographic binding mode must be preserved — and that premise is falsified for this exact warhead. Huprine Y and huprine Z are tacrine-huperzine A hybrids in which the huperzine pyridone (the fully buried ring in 4EY5) is replaced by a 4-aminoquinoline, and they are MORE potent inhibitors of human and bovine AChE than either tacrine or (-)-huperzine A (Alcala et al., Neuropharmacology 2003; PMID 12681373, doi:10.1016/s0028-3908(03)00071-6, retrieved this session). AChE also demonstrably accommodates dual-site ligands spanning CAS to PAS. A burial-based rule that would have vetoed huprines needs positive-control validation before it is allowed to fail a candidate, and 'mechanistically void' is the wrong verdict string — the defensible claim is 'incompatible with the pose observed in 4EY5'. Second, one holo structure gives one set of rotamers: the AChE gorge is conformationally labile (Tyr337/Phe338/Tyr341 gate it), so a BFS escape path computed on a single deposited model is not a property of the target. Third, a 1.4 A solvent probe is the wrong probe for a linker — a methylene needs more clearance than a water, so the reported minimum linker lengths will be systematically optimistic.
critiques.feasibility_objection: None material on the compute side: biopython 1.88 is installed in .venv and the RCSB fetch works. The real cost is assembling and curating the positive-control set, which is medicinal-chemistry work not counted in the 2-3 day estimate.
critiques.improvement: 1) Restate every verdict as pose-relative ('conjugation at atom X is incompatible with the pose in <PDB, resolution>') and emit it as an evidence-graded flag, not a validate.py hard failure, until controls exist. 2) Build a positive-control set of conjugates/hybrids known to bind — huprine Y/Z (a fused case the method must be able to distinguish from a tethered one), tacrine homodimers, donepezil-tacrine hybrids, memoquin — and report the method's false-veto rate on it BEFORE it vetoes anything. 3) Compute burial across all deposited holo structures of the target, not one, and report the range with the accession list committed. 4) Run the BFS at two probe radii (1.4 A solvent and ~1.9-2.0 A methylene-scale) and report both path lengths. 5) Separate the steric verdict from the pharmacophore-conflict verdict: losing one H-bond is often tolerable and often recoverable by linker placement, whereas a steric veto is not.

critiques.scientific_objection: The diagnosis is the best-supported finding in the batch; the proposed replacement number is unsafe for two enzymological reasons the proposal names but does not act on. (1) Cheng-Prusoff: for a competitive inhibitor IC50 = Ki(1 + [S]/Km), and Ellman assays across ChEMBL are run from sub-Km to several-fold Km. A material part of huperzine A's 4-log spread is assay design, not measurement noise, so a geometric mean across assays pools two different variance sources and a sigma_exp derived from it is inflated. (2) The largest replicate spreads offered as evidence of noise are carbamates — neostigmine 1.04 log, physostigmine 0.64 log. Carbamates are pseudo-irreversible carbamylating inhibitors whose apparent IC50 depends on pre-incubation time; those records are not replicate measurements of one quantity, so including them in a noise floor is a category error that will make the platform's future error bars too generous. (3) Enzyme source is as important as endpoint: erythrocyte vs recombinant human AChE, and Torpedo/bovine data mapped to CHEMBL220, must be part of the endpoint class alongside standard_type/bao_label. (4) Publishing '~1.4 log' before the endpoint-class table exists repeats the original error with the sign reversed.
critiques.feasibility_objection: Two days is plausible for the /assay join and the dataclass widening, but the endpoint-class curation is harder than stated: [S], Km and pre-incubation time are frequently only in the primary paper and absent from ChEMBL, so a large fraction of records will be unclassifiable. Plan for an explicit 'insufficient metadata' bucket that is excluded from aggregates rather than silently pooled, or the class table will be a fiction.
critiques.improvement: 1) Estimate sigma_exp only from reversible, equilibrium-binding inhibitors with matched substrate and matched [S]/Km; report time-dependent/covalent inhibitors as their own evidence class with their pre-incubation dependence stated, and exclude them from the noise floor. 2) Prefer Ki where ChEMBL supplies it; where only IC50 exists with [S] and Km recorded, apply Cheng-Prusoff and label the result CONVERTED with its own provenance; never pool IC50s across assays with different [S]. 3) Keep the error/sigma_exp ratio printout — that is the right headline. 4) Retract 2.41 and publish the replacement as a RANGE over the defensible reference choices (best-measured, class median, geometric mean of the catalytic-inhibition class) with n for each, so no single choice is again presented as the truth. That is the same discipline the retraction exists to enforce.

critiques.scientific_objection: As specified the join is nearly constant and therefore nearly information-free. The AChE corpus is Ellman-dominated, so the assay side of the join barely varies; the compound side (catechol, Michael acceptor, >=5 phenolic OH) fires on essentially every natural-product polyphenol. A label that is determined by compound class alone adds a flag without adding knowledge, which is precisely the failure mode the panel is guarding against. The proposal's 'no collision, no flag' guard does not help when one side of the join is constant. Second, the artifact direction must be stated per mechanism and one of the two is unfalsifiable from ChEMBL metadata: thiol-reactive electrophiles suppress the 412 nm signal and mimic inhibition (a false-potency artifact), whereas a 412 nm chromophore raises background and its effect depends entirely on whether a compound blank was subtracted — a protocol detail almost never recoverable from ChEMBL. Flagging chromophore interference without knowing the blanking protocol is a label that cannot be checked. Third, conjugation extent from RDKit ring/conjugation perception is not a lambda_max; PREDICTED status is honest but the signal is weak enough that it may not be worth emitting.
critiques.feasibility_objection: None material — RDKit 2026.3.5 with FilterCatalog is installed in .venv and verified. The mechanism and readout tables are curation, correctly identified as the real cost.
critiques.improvement: Convert the output from a downgrade into an orthogonal-evidence retrieval, which is discriminating and checkable: for every flagged compound-target pair, query ChEMBL for a measurement of the SAME pair on a readout in a different physical class (radiometric, LC-MS product quantification, pH-stat, SPR/ITC binding, or a fluorogenic substrate with non-overlapping optics) and report present/absent plus the log-unit concordance where present. A compound whose potency reproduces on an orthogonal readout is exonerated; one with no orthogonal measurement is genuinely lower-confidence. Report the collision rate with its denominator ('k of n compounds, k' of n' activity records') so a universal flag is visible immediately as universal. Add an explicit UNKNOWN_BLANKING state instead of asserting absorbance interference. Keep the requirement that no value is deleted or numerically downweighted.

critiques.scientific_objection: (1) The DeltaG conversion should not be emitted at all for this predictor. The affinity head outputs an assay-blended potency trained on mixed Ki/Kd/IC50; converting with DeltaG=(6-y)*1.364 is arithmetically valid and thermodynamically meaningless, because an IC50 is not an equilibrium dissociation constant (it carries a [S]/Km term) and for time-dependent inhibitors it is not a constant at all. Emit predicted log10 potency only, and gate any DeltaG on inputs that were Kd or Ki from an equilibrium method. (2) The decoy panel is uninformative as designed. Scoring an AChE ligand against NOS3 tests almost nothing; the decoys that carry CNS-safety meaning are near-neighbours — BuChE for AChE (the defining selectivity axis for this chemotype), CHRM2-M5 for CHRM1, GSK3A for GSK3B. An AUROC over unrelated receptors will be flatteringly high and will not license any selectivity statement. (3) Pooling ~60 pairs across 5 targets and reporting a pooled Spearman conflates between-target potency offsets with within-target ranking; at ~12 pairs per target the per-target CI will be too wide for the decision rule to resolve. (4) Training contamination is unmentioned: the affinity head was trained on ChEMBL/BindingDB-derived data and the ground truth here IS ChEMBL, so the measured error is a memorisation-optimistic ceiling, exactly as AIML-BENCH-1 and META-3 state.
critiques.feasibility_objection: The compute estimate is soft. At the measured ~3 min per 543-residue receptor plus ligand, 200-300 runs is 10-15 h of MPS before the MSA arm; adding a paired --use_msa_server arm on >=20 and a 3-decoy panel per ligand pushes this to 20-30 h. That is still an overnight-class job, but '2-4 days wall clock including a day of coding' understates it.
critiques.improvement: Merge with AIML-BENCH-1 into a single benchmark frozen under META-3's prespec mechanism — three overlapping affinity benchmarks is triple the compute for one answer. Make within-target Spearman the primary metric and require n>=20 per target before a target is reported. Replace the unrelated-receptor decoys with pharmacologically informative near-neighbours (BuChE, CHRM subtypes, GSK3A) so the AUROC becomes a selectivity readout that a CNS safety reviewer would actually use. Do not write any DeltaG into thermo.METHOD_ACCURACY or into binding_free_energy from IC50-derived predictions; instead add a key for log10-potency error and state the endpoint heterogeneity in applicability. Inherit AIML-BENCH-1's leakage stratification verbatim.

critiques.scientific_objection: The pre-registered threshold is stated as generous but is effectively unreachable, and the proposal already contains the evidence: the repo's own pilot gives min interface PAE ~17 A for the native candidate-AChE complex, i.e. there is no pose for a contact-count regression to score. Running the four-cell transfer benchmark to establish that is legitimate; running the candidate arm across all 35 is not. Second, the protein-peptide arm needs affinity ground truth from direct methods — the same restriction that collapsed PRODIGY's correlation to r~0.04 on indirectly measured complexes applies to any peptide set assembled, and structure-plus-ITC/SPR protein-peptide data is thin. State the achievable n for that cell before committing a week. Third, a DMPK point the proposal does not make: even a passing DeltaG would not be decision-relevant here. For a 3-11 kDa polycation with no transport mechanism and minutes-scale systemic persistence, the exposure term dominates the affinity term by orders of magnitude; a +/-2 kcal/mol DeltaG changes no decision about these molecules.
critiques.feasibility_objection: prodigy-prot and freesasa are absent from both .venv and .venv312 today — I checked; the 'verified installs cleanly on macOS arm64 this session' claim does not reproduce from the repo state. The install is probably fine, but in a proposal about traceability the verification should be re-runnable.
critiques.improvement: 1) Keep the reproduce-on-crystals wiring check and the four-cell transfer table; cut the candidate DeltaG arm until AIML-STRUCT-1's null shows at least one candidate distinguishable from its scrambles. 2) Exploit the control the catalogue already contains for free: there are only 26 unique sequences among 35 candidates, and one 40-mer (SEAEFRLFRDVWANYCACYPGWLGCDERACPRCHGFWREV) is declared against alpha7 nAChR ECD in PfcACh-PAM-P1 and against TLR4/MD-2 in MicroTlr4-Antagonist-M3, while one 36-mer is declared against AChE in three separate entries. Co-folding one sequence against its several declared receptors is a zero-design-cost specificity control and cuts the co-fold count by 26%. 3) Apply a compartment gate before spending compute: do not co-fold an extracellular peptide against a cytoplasmic target and then report an ipTM as though it meant something — label those compartment-excluded up front.

critiques.scientific_objection: This treats a molecular-definition problem as a conformational-sampling problem. I confirmed 15 of 35 candidates carry an odd cysteine count, so at least one free thiol is unavoidable; in plasma that thiol will form mixed disulfides with albumin Cys34 and with free cysteine/glutathione and will drive covalent dimerisation. The circulating species is then none of the 105 enumerated isomers, so a spread computed over intramolecular pairings is not the uncertainty that matters. Second, the physics filter is not validated for the job: GBn2 implicit solvent systematically over-stabilises salt bridges and under-penalises charge burial for highly charged peptides, and 'interface survives vs dissolves' from short implicit-solvent MD (length unstated) has no calibration proposed — the calibration described is for the Boltz bond constraint, not for the filter. Third, effort allocation: 1-1.5 weeks and 100-150 MD systems spent on the least chemically defined members of an explicitly hypothesis-grade catalogue, several of which are already known to be mechanistically inverted.
critiques.feasibility_objection: openmm and pdbfixer are not installed in either venv today — I checked both, so 'verified this session on this machine' does not reproduce from the repo state. Also, the Boltz SG-SG intra-chain bond constraint is acknowledged as unverified; if it fails, the fallback ('impose connectivity in relaxation') changes the experiment from 'what does the predictor do with this connectivity' to 'what does a forcefield do to a predictor's pose', which is a different and weaker question and should be pre-declared as such.
critiques.improvement: Do the free part first and stop there for now: a deterministic chemical-definition audit emitting, per candidate, Cys count, parity, admissible pairing count, and an explicit 'not a single chemical entity' status that BLOCKS emission of any structure-derived value. Hours, not weeks, and it is the honest deliverable. State the DMPK consequence of the odd-Cys finding explicitly (albumin Cys34 adduction, thiol-disulfide exchange, covalent dimerisation, batch heterogeneity) and frame it as an upstream design defect to be fixed by specifying connectivity or substituting Cys->Ser/alpha-aminobutyrate — not as a downstream quantity to estimate. Defer isomer folding to candidates that survive the receptor-complex null, and cap it at the exhaustive 4- and 6-Cys cases. Keep both enforcement rules (no MM-GBSA path into binding_free_energy; no PREDICTED DeltaG without an attached isomer spread) — those are durable and cost nothing. Note that STRUCTBIO-IDEA-1 reads connectivity off coordinates already on disk; run that first, it may make much of this unnecessary.

critiques.scientific_objection: Commenting only on the ground-truth and noise-ceiling side, which is where I have standing. sigma_exp as constructed will be too large and will therefore license a model error that is actually unacceptable. The 18 replicate pairs mix (a) carbamates, whose apparent IC50 depends on pre-incubation time and so are not replicates of a single quantity, and (b) IC50s measured at different [S]/Km, where the Cheng-Prusoff term contributes real, non-random spread. A noise floor estimated from that mixture is an assay-design variance estimate wearing a measurement-noise label. Second, n is too small for the stated design: 17 compounds with numeric potency cannot support a Murcko scaffold split, and a predict-the-mean RMSE of 1.644 at n=17 carries a CI wide enough to swallow most plausible model errors, so 'Boltz-2 is worse than the null' cannot yet be established or refuted. Third, per-compound geometric-mean aggregation inherits the same [S] problem.
critiques.feasibility_objection: None on hardware — the ceiling, floor and baselines are minutes of CPU as stated, and a ~10 h MPS batch is realistic. The binding constraint is data volume, not compute: reaching the n needed for scaffold and temporal splits requires the multi-target scale-out to happen first, which is not in the 2-3 day estimate.
critiques.improvement: 1) Estimate sigma_exp only from reversible, equilibrium-binding inhibitors with matched substrate and matched [S]/Km; report the carbamate/time-dependent subset separately as an assay-design variance term rather than folding it into the noise floor. 2) Refuse to report scaffold-split metrics below a stated minimum (e.g. >=100 compounds and >=20 scaffolds) — emit 'not evaluable at n=N' instead, which is consistent with the project's own refusal discipline. 3) Make within-target Spearman the primary metric with the between-target offset explicitly removed; keep pooled RMSE as secondary. 4) Merge with CBC-CC-1 and freeze the merged protocol under META-3 rather than building two benchmarks on the same compounds.

critiques.scientific_objection: A Fisher-Yates shuffle over the residue multiset is composition-matched but NOT matched on the property most likely to drive a promiscuous interface score in this chemotype: facial amphipathicity. Shuffling an ideally amphipathic sequence usually lowers its hydrophobic moment, so the null distribution is on average less amphipathic than the design. A design that beats such a null may be winning on amphipathicity rather than on motif identity, and a design that loses to it (as B1 does in the pilot) is condemned even more strongly than stated. Second, the design counts are inflated: there are only 26 unique sequences among the 35 candidates — three entries share KWWKFLRRFWRRLKKYFEELWKKLAEKYFELLKKYG and three share a 40-mer — so K=20 controls per 'candidate' spends roughly a quarter of the compute re-folding identical molecules. Third, the duplication conceals a stronger free control the proposal misses: the same 40-mer is declared against alpha7 nAChR ECD (PfcACh-PAM-P1) and against TLR4/MD-2 (MicroTlr4-Antagonist-M3). One molecule declared against two unrelated receptors is a direct test of declared target specificity requiring no scrambling at all.
critiques.feasibility_objection: None beyond the compute arithmetic, which improves once deduplicated: 26 unique sequences, and only ~10 with an explicit receptor, makes the K=20 design comfortably an overnight-class job.
critiques.improvement: 1) Add a hydrophobic-moment-matched (or helical-wheel-period-preserving) null alongside the plain composition null and report both p-values; the gap between them is itself informative about what the score is keyed on. 2) Deduplicate to unique sequences and add the cross-declaration control described above. 3) Report the design's mu_H percentile within its own shuffle distribution as a zero-compute first-line readout (this is the same statistic DMPK-IDEA-3 needs, so build it once). 4) MW, net charge, pI and GRAVY are provably order-invariant by inspection of platform/cbc/peptide.py — assert that and relabel the cards; do not spend any folding on demonstrating it. 5) Keep the commitment to headline a null result.

critiques.scientific_objection: Commenting only on control design and target selection. The 35 x 26 design contains only 26 unique sequences, so roughly a quarter of the runs re-fold identical molecules under different names. It also includes candidate-receptor pairs that are biologically impossible before any folding: extracellular peptides declared against cytoplasmic targets (GSK-3beta ATP pocket, Keap1 Kelch). Using those as a check on the null's discriminative power is reasonable, but a p-value must never be surfaced for a pair whose target compartment is unreachable — otherwise a passing p on an unreachable target is exactly the kind of number-without-knowledge the rebuild exists to prevent. Separately, the off-target panel drawn from the same 16 receptors repeats CBC-CC-1's decoy weakness: unrelated receptors make an easy null, and a candidate can 'pass' against them while being wholly non-selective among plausible neighbours.
critiques.feasibility_objection: The estimate is credible, and deduplication improves it by ~26%. One caution: the PAE-asymmetry threshold re-derivation is correctly identified as a blocker, but re-deriving it from 'real two-chain output' risks tuning a sanity check on the very predictions it is meant to police — derive it from deposited two-chain crystal structures as well, so the check retains an external anchor.
critiques.improvement: Deduplicate to 26 unique sequences. Add a UniProt subcellular-location compartment gate that runs before any compute and marks impossible pairs compartment-excluded, so no p-value is rendered for them. Add the free cross-declaration control already present in the data (one 40-mer declared against alpha7 nAChR and TLR4/MD-2; one 36-mer declared against AChE three times) — it tests declared specificity with zero new design. Include at least one near-neighbour off-target per candidate alongside the unrelated ones, and report the two decoy classes separately. Derive the PAE-asymmetry threshold from deposited crystal complexes in addition to Boltz-2 output.

critiques.scientific_objection: Scoped to the site-of-action half; I am not assessing the QTL colocalisation methodology. For this catalogue, expression is the second question and the proposal makes it the first. The decisive and far cheaper gate is compartment reachability: an extracellular peptide cannot engage a cytoplasmic target (GSK-3beta, Keap1, and the intracellular scaffold targets) at any regional TPM, and a peptide with no transport mechanism cannot reach any CNS target regardless of where the target is expressed — I verified today that 0/35 sequences carry a documented RMT shuttle motif. GTEx regional specificity is worth having, but it will not catch the mechanistically inverted candidates, whereas a UniProt subcellular-location gate crossed with declared modality will, in minutes, with no API budget. Second, a resolution mismatch runs through the whole expression arm: GTEx bulk brain TPM cannot adjudicate claims stated at cell-type or subcellular resolution ('CA1 cholinergic terminals', 'microglial mitochondria'). Computing a tissue-level specificity index and letting it stand against a subcellular claim substitutes a number for the missing evidence.
critiques.feasibility_objection: Steps 1 and 3 are correctly costed. Step 2 (MiGA/MetaBrain harmonisation to GRCh38 with consistent effect-allele orientation) is routinely underestimated at 'roughly a week' — allele orientation and build harmonisation across 14 datasets is the classic time sink — but it is CPU-only and within the hardware constraints.
critiques.improvement: 1) Add check_compartment as the FIRST gate: UniProt subcellular-location terms for the target versus the candidate's declared modality and route, failing extracellular-agent/cytoplasmic-target pairs before any GTEx call and before any structural compute. 2) Attach a resolution field to every expression value and fail any claim stated at finer resolution than the evidence supporting it, rather than reporting a tissue-level fold-change against a cell-type claim. 3) Keep the CHRFAM7A paralog flag — it is correct, specific, and exactly the kind of measurement-artifact caveat this platform should carry. 4) State the instrument/site-of-action mismatch verdict as a required field, as proposed; that half is sound.

critiques.scientific_objection: Little to object to on the mechanism; the criterion-exercise audit is the highest-leverage item in the batch and the confidence_score defect is real and independently checkable (every activity in data/corpus_ACHE.json carries assay_confidence null, and the rejection buckets contain no low-confidence bucket). Three narrower objections. (a) The decision rule's X and Y must be filled with defended numbers before freezing, and X should be tied to the measured sigma_exp — a model must not be credited with skill inside the data's own noise, nor penalised for failing to beat it — with the sigma_exp construction corrected per MEDCHEM-IDEA-2 (exclude carbamates and unmatched-[S] records). (b) 'A pre-declared aggregation rule for replicates' is not sufficient as stated: for AChE the rule must specify enzyme source, substrate identity, [S] relative to Km, and pre-incubation time, because those determine whether two records are replicates at all. (c) n=18 compounds cannot support MAE-with-CI plus Spearman as decision inputs; freeze the protocol but state the powering explicitly, or scale to multiple targets before freezing.
critiques.feasibility_objection: None material. The freeze/verify commands reuse the existing append-only ledger, the /assay join is one extra call per batch, and 18 complexes on MPS is an overnight job at the measured ~3 min per complex.
critiques.improvement: Fill the decision rule mechanically from the noise floor — e.g. report as PREDICTED only if the MAE 95% CI upper bound is below 2x sigma_exp AND the within-target Spearman CI excludes zero — and record that formula in the frozen YAML so the threshold cannot be renegotiated after the numbers land. Make the criterion-exercise audit report EVERY criterion's rejection count as a required output field, not only the zero-count ones, so a criterion that rejects 1 of 258 is as visible as one that rejects none. Extend the audit to the corpus's assay-metadata criteria (substrate, [S], pre-incubation) once MEDCHEM-IDEA-2's endpoint classes exist, since those are the criteria most likely to be advertised and not enforced next.

critiques.critic:
Metascience / research software engineering (reproducibility, benchmark design, reporting standards; JOSS reviewer).

WHAT I VERIFIED IN THE REPO THIS SESSION (all claims below re-run by me, not taken from the proposals):

1. NOTHING IS UNDER VERSION CONTROL. `git ls-files platform/ data/ memory/ research/ reviews/` returns 0. The only tracked content is the discredited mockup plus .agents/. There is no LICENSE and no CITATION.cff. This is the binding constraint on the entire batch: every success criterion in every proposal that uses the word "committed" is unsatisfiable as literally written. META-1 item 5 is a hard prerequisite for 23 of the 24 proposals, and the panel should sequence accordingly.

2. LEDGER HASH CHECK REPRODUCES EXACTLY. Re-hashing every rec=="ARTIFACT" row across memory/ledger/*.jsonl against the working tree: ok=10, mismatch=4, missing=0. The four mismatches are data/dataset.json, data/real_vs_hardcoded.json, platform/validate.py, reviews/REVIEW_REPORT.md. META-1's central integrity claim is confirmed.

3. TWO PROPOSALS ASSERT A FALSE ABSENCE. META-1 says "searched: no Boltz output directory exists"; DMPK-IDEA-2 says "a filesystem-wide search for *.cif and boltz output directories in the repository returns nothing... the coordinates themselves were discarded". Both are wrong. /tmp/cbc_boltz contains 22 run directories, 22 *.cif, plus confidence_*.json, pae_*.npz and plddt_*.npz per run. STRUCTBIO-IDEA-1 got this right and analysed those exact files. The true defect is narrower and was correctly stated only by STRUCTBIO-IDEA-1: the artifacts live in a macOS-purge-eligible path and no row in data/real_vs_hardcoded.json records a path (I read row 0 — no path field). Consequence: DMPK-IDEA-2 and META-1 both budget compute to re-fold runs whose outputs already exist. Worse, re-folding cannot recover provenance for the *published* numbers, because those runs were unseeded; the surviving files in /tmp are the only physical evidence of what produced data/real_vs_hardcoded.json. Preserving them is urgent, free, and must happen before anything else in this batch. A proposal justified by a false absence is the same epistemic error as the original fabricated data, at smaller scale, and I am marking it as such.

4. THE RECORDED ACCELERATOR IS WRONG. Every row in data/real_vs_hardcoded.json carries "accelerator": "gpu", not "mps". Multiple proposals build arguments on "this was measured on MPS". The provenance field itself disagrees. Nobody caught this — which is exactly META-1's point about unpoliced provenance strings.

5. THE INERT CONFIDENCE FILTER IS CONFIRMED. All 27 activities in data/corpus_ACHE.json carry assay_confidence: null while protocol_summary asserts "assay confidence >= 8", and denominator.rejected has buckets for unparseable/tier_excluded/no_structure/too_large and none for low confidence. META-3 and MEDCHEM-IDEA-2 are both correct.

6. A DENOMINATOR DEFECT NOBODY FOUND, LARGER THAN THE ONE THEY DID. corpus.py:189-201 caps retrieval at limit=1000, page=200, and build_corpus passes max_activities. The emitted "activities_examined: 300 / distinct_molecules_examined: 258" is therefore a client-side truncation cap, not the target's population. corpus.py:185 defines count_target_activities() which fetches ChEMBL's real total_count — and it is not used in the emitted file. So the platform's flagship methodological asset, "an executable InclusionProtocol with a stated denominator", states a denominator that is an artifact of a for-loop bound, over whatever ChEMBL's default ordering returned first. Any aggregation built on this corpus (MEDCHEM-IDEA-2, AIML-BENCH-1, CBC-CC-1, META-3) inherits a selection bias of unknown direction. Fix this before any of them run.

7. provenance.audit() HAS NO str BRANCH. Confirmed at provenance.py:175-192: dict / list / (int,float) only. GENO-A is right that every genetics number embedded in target_records prose ("= 0.124", "pLI 1.000, LOEUF 0.219") is exempt from the repo's own contract. This is the most consequential single defect any proposal found, because it is an unpoliced escape hatch in the guarantee the rebuild exists to provide.

8. CANDIDATE CYSTEINE CENSUS REPRODUCES. Of 35: 21 with >=4 Cys (3x4Cys, 4x5, 4x6, 4x7, 4x8, 2x9), 15 with an odd count. CBC-CC-3's numbers are exact.

9. I COULD NOT VERIFY MEDCHEM-IDEA-2's HEADLINE. The EBI ChEMBL API returned HTTP 500, then timed out, on three independent attempts (direct urllib, and the ChEMBL MCP client) over ~20 minutes. So the claim "25 records, IC50 0.54-5280 nM, median 47 nM, corrected error ~1.43 log" remains unverified by me. I am not calling it wrong — the argument is sound and corpus_ACHE.json does retain exactly one huperzine activity (IC50 5.0 nM, assay CHEMBL643374) — but it means the proposed retraction-with-replacement would today substitute one unverifiable number for another. It is also a live demonstration that every live-fetch design in this batch needs a pinned, archived snapshot and an offline replay path, not a runtime query.

CITATIONS: I add none. I retrieved no external literature this session (the one external service I tried was down), so per the citation contract I cite nothing rather than reconstruct DOIs from memory. Every factual assertion above is from the local working tree and is re-runnable.

CROSS-CUTTING STRUCTURAL PROBLEMS IN THE BATCH:

A. FOUR PROPOSALS INDEPENDENTLY REINVENT THE SAME NULL. AIML-STRUCT-1, AIML-BENCH-3, STRUCTBIO-IDEA-3 and CBC-CC-2 all propose co-folding candidates with receptors and comparing against composition-matched scrambles. Three separate implementations of one statistic will produce three different answers and the panel will then have to adjudicate them. Merge into a single platform/cbc/bench/null.py owned by one proposal (AIML-STRUCT-1 has the best-specified statistic; AIML-BENCH-3 has the best control taxonomy — full shuffle / linker-preserving / motif-block; STRUCTBIO-IDEA-3 has the only epitope-overlap falsification test). Same for the affinity benchmark: AIML-BENCH-1 and CBC-CC-1 are one project, and only AIML-BENCH-1 handles leakage.

B. SEVERAL SUCCESS CRITERIA ARE OUTCOME-CONTINGENT, WHICH IS A PRE-REGISTRATION VIOLATION. AIML-STRUCT-1 requires "at least one candidate reported as indistinguishable (p > 0.05)"; AIML-BENCH-3 requires "if no candidate passes, that null result is the headline"; GENO-B requires "UNDETERMINED for at least 34 of 35". A criterion that can only be met by a particular result is not a criterion, it is a prediction — and it creates pressure to reach that result. Rewrite every one as a process criterion: the table exists, every row carries a verdict produced by a rule frozen before execution, and the rule is sensitive (a fixture flips it). GENO-B's last bullet already does this correctly and should be the template.

C. SEVERAL SUCCESS CRITERIA PIN TO THE AUTHOR'S OWN UNPUBLISHED SESSION. STRUCTBIO-IDEA-1 ("reproduces the numbers measured this session"), MEDCHEM-IDEA-3 ("reproducing the flags listed in E5"), MEDCHEM-IDEA-1 ("98.5% +/- 0.5%"). These are fine as regression pins and worthless as validation — they establish that the code still does what it did, not that what it did was right. Every one must be paired with an independent-reference criterion (false-positive rate on deposited structures; a published benchmark), and the reference must be evaluated BEFORE thresholds are set, or the thresholds are tuned on the test set.

D. UNDERPOWERED DESIGNS PRESENTED AS DECISIVE. AIML-BENCH-3 is the worst case and it is arithmetically fatal: K=20 gives a minimum achievable permutation p of 1/21 = 0.048, so after Holm correction across 10 candidates no candidate can ever reach significance. The design cannot produce a positive result by construction. AIML-STRUCT-1's pilot (3 natives vs 3 decoys) has a minimum achievable p of 0.25 and reports p=1.0 as "decisive". Every proposal that states a p-value or a threshold must state its minimum achievable p and its power, up front.

E. UNCALIBRATED SCALARS SMUGGLED IN AS RESULTS. GENO-C's "specificity index" (brain median / whole-body median, with a threshold "beyond a stated fold") has no reference distribution — it is an ipTM threshold pulled from air, in the exact form the structural proposals correctly attack. DMPK-IDEA-1's n_strong_binders has the same problem: a 15-mer x 25-allele scan at 1% rank yields ~20 hits by construction on a 100-mer. Both are fixed the same cheap way: compute the statistic over a matched null (all protein-coding genes; composition-matched scrambles) and report a percentile, not a raw value.

F. THE MOST VALUABLE OUTPUT IN THE BATCH IS BURIED. META-2 item 5(ii) — a negative-result methods preprint reporting that 19/22 asserted pLDDTs were overstated, that ipTM was 0.00 by construction, and that the affinity error was misstated because ground truth was a single cherry-picked measurement — is publishable metascience independent of everything else here, and it is currently a sub-bullet of a FAIR-packaging proposal. Promote it to its own workstream. But it must not be drafted until AIML-STRUCT-3 has established the seed envelope and MEDCHEM-IDEA-2 has fixed the ground-truth aggregate, or the preprint will republish two numbers this very panel has already shown to be wrong.

RECOMMENDED ORDER (nothing else is interpretable before these): META-1 item 5 (git, LICENSE) and artifact rescue from /tmp -> repo; corpus.py denominator + /assay join; GENO-A's str branch in audit(); META-3's criterion-exercise audit; AIML-STRUCT-3's seeds. Total maybe four days, and it is the difference between a batch of experiments and a batch of anecdotes.

critiques.scientific_objection: The pilot is presented as decisive and is not. With 3 native replicates and 3 decoys, the stated statistic p = (1 + #{decoy >= native_median})/(N+1) has a minimum achievable value of 0.25; reporting 'empirical p = 1.0' as decisive evidence from a design that cannot fall below 0.25 is a power failure dressed as a result. Second, the arms are variance-mismatched by design: natives get 5 seeds, decoys get 1. Given AIML-STRUCT-3's own measurement that a single unseeded run has sd ~0.13 on a 0-1 metric, each decoy draw carries that noise while the native is a 5-seed summary, so comparing the native median against single-draw decoys conflates seed variance with sequence effect and inflates the apparent decoy tail (the 0.735 outlier is exactly what one within-decoy noise draw looks like). Third, a scramble null answers 'is this better than composition' but not 'can this pipeline discriminate anything at all'; without a positive control at identical settings, p > 0.05 is unattributable between 'the design does not bind' and 'the assay is blind'. Fourth, the success criterion 'at least one candidate reported as indistinguishable (p > 0.05)' is outcome-contingent and therefore not a criterion.
critiques.feasibility_objection: The compute estimate is optimistic by roughly 2x. 35 candidates x 26 runs = 910 predictions; at the 3 min 4 s measured elsewhere in this batch for a 543-residue receptor plus peptide, that is ~46 h, not 'roughly 24 h'. The receptor-domain constructs are smaller, which helps, but AChE, TLR4 and TrkA-NGF are not. Also, 'committed table' is currently unsatisfiable: git ls-files over platform/ and data/ returns zero — nothing in this repository is under version control.
critiques.improvement: Give decoys the same seed treatment as natives (>=3 seeds each) and analyse with a statistic that respects the nesting — a permutation test on candidate identity with seed as a within-unit factor, or a mixed model with random intercepts per sequence — rather than comparing a native median against single decoy draws. Pre-register the design with a stated minimum achievable p and a power calculation: to reject at 0.05 you need N >= 19 decoys, and to survive multiplicity across 35 candidates you need N >= 200 or an FDR/effect-size framework instead. Add a positive-control arm at identical settings (2FLU KEAP1+Neh2 16-mer is in the platform's own target_records and is the right size) so a null result is attributable.
