Rewrite the success criteria as process criteria: the table exists, every candidate carries a verdict from a rule frozen before execution, and a fixture with a known-binding pair flips the verdict. Sequence after META-1's git commit, and merge the scramble machinery with AIML-BENCH-3 and STRUCTBIO-IDEA-3 rather than building three of them. The predictor.py:392-398 PAE-asymmetry fix is correct and should be split out as a standalone prerequisite patch — I confirmed the check runs over min(n,60) with a hardcoded 12.0 A threshold that was never derived from two-chain output.

critiques.scientific_objection: The temporal holdout is necessary but not sufficient for leakage control, and the proposal treats it as sufficient. Deduplicating at 30-40% identity WITHIN the benchmark says nothing about each benchmark receptor's similarity to pre-cutoff training entries — a post-2023-06-01 deposition of a well-studied fold is not held out in any meaningful sense. The proposal itself specifies exactly the right control for ligands over in AIML-BENCH-1 (max Tanimoto to pre-cutoff, stratified into bins) and then omits the structural analogue here. Second, N=100 across ~5 ipTM bins gives 15-25 per bin; Wilson intervals at that n have half-widths near +/-0.2 on P(DockQ>=0.23), which cannot support the success criterion 'a stated, defensible ipTM threshold... replaces any borrowed 0.8 heuristic'. The curve will be honest and the threshold will not be defensible. Third, calibration transfer is assumed rather than tested: the benchmark is natural peptide-protein complexes and the deployment set is GGGGS-linked designed chimeras with no homologues; the calibration is only valid if the candidates sit inside the benchmark's feature distribution, which is checkable and unchecked. Fourth, 'Boltz-2's PDB training cutoff is 2023-06-01' is asserted; it should be retrieved from the release and pinned, since the whole design rests on it.
critiques.feasibility_objection: Compute is genuinely modest and the honesty about the unvalidated group_by clustering call (HTTP 400) is exactly right. The real unscoped cost is receptor-level similarity search against the pre-cutoff PDB, which needs a local mmseqs2 database build, not just a dedup pass. Budget a day for that alone.
critiques.improvement: Add a receptor-leakage stratum mirroring the ligand one in AIML-BENCH-1: for each benchmark entry, max sequence identity of the receptor to any pre-2023-06-01 PDB chain, with all headline metrics reported stratified <30% / 30-60% / >60%. Do a precision calculation before choosing N: state the Wilson half-width you need per bin and solve for n (for +/-0.1 at p~0.5 you need ~100 per bin, i.e. ~400-500 complexes, which is still an overnight-scale job at 1-3 min each). Report the candidates' position in the benchmark's feature space (length, charge, composition) so a reader can see whether the calibration transfers; where they fall outside, calibrated_interface_probability should refuse for that reason too, not only for sparse ipTM bins. Pin the training cutoff from the retrieved release manifest and record it in provenance. This proposal, not STRUCTBIO-IDEA-2, should own the calibration curve — STRUCTBIO-IDEA-2's benchmark is entirely pre-cutoff.

critiques.scientific_objection: This is the correct first experiment and the argument is sound; the objections are to two specific claims. (a) 'data/real_vs_hardcoded.json is byte-reproducible on a second execution' is not achievable and should not be a success criterion. Seeding does not confer bitwise determinism on MPS — non-deterministic reduction order and the documented aten::linalg_svd CPU fallback both break it. Promising byte-reproducibility and then quietly relaxing it is how reproducibility criteria get discredited. (b) Item 4 re-runs Huperzine A with an MSA and reports whether the 2.41 log error shrinks. n=1 before and n=1 after is still n=1; a single retest cannot establish that MSA mode improved anything. Worse, MEDCHEM-IDEA-2 argues the 2.41 denominator is itself wrong because the ground truth is one cherry-picked measurement out of many — so this retest, as specified, would publish a delta against a broken reference. (c) The recorded provenance says accelerator: 'gpu' in every existing row, not 'mps' — so the claim that all 22 runs were on MPS is not supported by the repository's own record, and the environment manifest must be reconstructed rather than assumed.
critiques.feasibility_objection: No material objection; this is the cheapest high-value item in the batch and the MSA caching design (16 a3m files, 16 server calls) is proportionate. One caveat: committing ColabFold-derived a3m files means committing third-party-derived data with unstated licensing into a repo that currently has no LICENSE at all.
critiques.improvement: Replace 'byte-reproducible' with: run the same seed twice, measure and publish the observed divergence, and set the reproducibility criterion as agreement within that measured tolerance — the divergence figure is itself a finding worth recording. Defer item 4 until MEDCHEM-IDEA-2 has fixed the ground-truth aggregate, then run it as a paired arm inside AIML-BENCH-1's design (>=20 compounds, both MSA modes) rather than as a one-compound anecdote. Use n>=10 seeds on 2-3 candidates for the variance envelope rather than n=5 on 8 — an sd from 5 draws carries ~35% relative uncertainty, which is not enough to anchor the error bar that every other proposal in this batch wants to inherit. Report the envelope with its own CI. Finally, make the validate.py gate require the accelerator string to come from env introspection (META-1's runtime()), since the existing 'gpu' value proves a hand-set string can be wrong and never noticed.

critiques.scientific_objection: The three-anchor design (noise ceiling, null floor, leakage audit) is the right architecture and I would adopt it as the template for the batch. Three defects. (a) sigma_exp is presented as a band with no uncertainty of its own: 0.376 log from 18 replicate pairs on a single target has roughly 17% relative standard error, and drawing it as a fixed band on the predicted-vs-measured plot repeats exactly the point-estimate error the proposal is written to correct. (b) The temporal split is specified as 'Sheridan on earliest ChEMBL document.year with the boundary at the ChEMBL v34 release Boltz-2 trained on'. Document year is publication year, not the date the record entered ChEMBL — a 2019 paper can be curated into ChEMBL in 2024 and would be misclassified as pre-cutoff. A publication-year split does not implement a training-cutoff split, and conflating them will understate leakage. (c) The leakage audit tests membership in 'the pre-cutoff snapshot', but no snapshot exists in the repository, and I found the live ChEMBL API returning HTTP 500 and then timing out for ~20 minutes today — a live-query leakage audit is neither reproducible nor reliably runnable.
critiques.feasibility_objection: The unscoped item is the pre-cutoff snapshot: it must be an archived ChEMBL release pulled from the EBI FTP and pinned, not a live query. Even restricted to the relevant targets that is a real download-and-index task, not a side effect of an existing function. Also, the ground truth this benchmark aggregates comes from corpus.py, whose retrieval is capped at limit=1000/page=200 — I confirmed the emitted 'activities_examined: 300 / 258 molecules' is a truncation cap, not the target population, and count_target_activities() at corpus.py:185 which would give the real total is defined and unused. Aggregating over a truncated, arbitrarily-ordered slice biases sigma_exp and the compound set in an unknown direction.
critiques.improvement: Report sigma_exp with a bootstrap CI and its n, and draw the band as an interval rather than a line; scale to the stated >=50 pairs across targets before it is used as a ceiling. Replace document.year with the ChEMBL release in which each activity first appeared (retrievable from archived releases); if that cannot be resolved, say so and label the split 'publication-year proxy, not a training-cutoff split'. Pin an archived pre-cutoff ChEMBL release to disk and run the leakage audit offline. Fix the corpus denominator first: call count_target_activities(), record ChEMBL release + retrieval timestamp + verbatim query URLs, and either page to exhaustion or declare the cap and its ordering as a stated sampling frame. The hard rule in item 6 ('when the CI on the paired delta spans zero, the headline is not-distinguishable-from-null, never a bare RMSE') is the single best reporting rule proposed by anyone in this batch and should be lifted into a repo-wide policy, not kept local to this module. Merge CBC-CC-1 into this proposal.

critiques.scientific_objection: Strong proposal, one dominating statistical defect: the effective n is far smaller than the stated n. The 81-entry holdout is selected by mapping to the platform's own 10 UniProt accessions, so it will contain many complexes sharing a receptor (hAChE, BuChE, MAO-B, BACE1) with different ligands. Wilson intervals and AUROC computed over 81 complexes as if they were independent will be too narrow — the independent unit is closer to the number of distinct receptors, which may be under 15. Second, the AUROC criterion 'if the CI includes 0.5, the platform stops displaying that score as a quality indicator' is a good pre-registered rule but needs its inferential asymmetry stated: at n~80 with unbalanced classes the CI half-width is roughly +/-0.12, so failing to exclude 0.5 is likely even for a genuinely useful score. 'Not demonstrated' must not be reported as 'demonstrated absent'. Third, keeping the pre-cutoff recall set separate is exactly right, but the phrase 'measures recall, not prediction' understates it — a model can also fail on its own training data, so a poor recall number is informative while a good one is uninformative; say which direction each result can support.
critiques.feasibility_objection: The dependency chain is longer than stated. PoseBusters redock mode and symmetry-corrected RMSD both require the predictor to emit ligand coordinates, which requires the parse_mmcif rewrite — I confirmed predictor.py:227 discards every atom whose label_atom_id is not 'CA', so the 18 huperzine atoms are dropped before anything downstream runs. That rewrite is shared with STRUCTBIO-IDEA-1's all-atom parser and should be built once. Compute at 3 min x ~100 is fine.
critiques.improvement: Report n_complexes and n_independent_receptors side by side, and compute all intervals with a receptor-level cluster bootstrap (resample receptors, not complexes). Pre-declare the AUROC decision rule with its power: state the AUROC you could detect at this n, and phrase the negative outcome as 'no discrimination demonstrated at n=N (CI a-b)'. Build the all-atom mmCIF parser once, jointly with STRUCTBIO-IDEA-1, rather than twice. Keep the recall/holdout separation and add one sentence per set stating which conclusions each can and cannot support. The 4EY5-versus-existing-model first data point costs no inference and should be done this week — it is the cheapest real measurement anyone proposed.

critiques.scientific_objection: The design cannot produce a positive result. K=20 controls gives a minimum achievable permutation p of 1/(1+20) = 0.048; applying Holm-Bonferroni across 10 candidates requires the smallest p to be below 0.005 to reject anything. No candidate can reach significance under this design regardless of the biology, so the pre-declared verdict string 'sequence-specific (Holm-corrected p < 0.05)' is unreachable by construction and the experiment can only ever return the null. That is not a stringent test, it is a guaranteed outcome, and 210 folding runs would be spent proving an arithmetic property of the design. Second, item 6 proposes to 'demonstrate quantitatively which existing platform outputs are order-invariant' by running peptide.py on designs and scrambles. MW, net charge, pI and GRAVY are sums over the residue multiset — order-invariance is provable in one line of algebra, and the proposal itself says so ('order-invariant by construction', 'tagged composition-determined by construction, before any folding runs'). Generating empirical evidence for a mathematical identity is the definition of adding a number without adding knowledge. Third, this is the third independent implementation of the same composition-matched null in this batch.
critiques.feasibility_objection: 11-14 h of MPS for a design that cannot reject is compute spent to no end. The K=10 pilot is worse: minimum p = 0.091, so even uncorrected it cannot reach 0.05.
critiques.improvement: Either raise K to >=200 per candidate (which makes the compute infeasible at 3 min/run and forces a smaller candidate set), or abandon per-candidate significance and switch to the design this data can actually support: report standardised effect size (design - mean(controls))/sd(controls) per candidate with a bootstrap CI, control the false discovery rate across candidates rather than the family-wise error rate, and pool a shared receptor-specific null across candidates targeting the same receptor to buy back degrees of freedom. State the minimum achievable p in the protocol before running. Drop item 6's folding component entirely and replace it with a one-line proof plus a unit test asserting f(seq) == f(shuffle(seq)) for the four order-invariant descriptors — same conclusion, zero GPU-hours, and it is the stronger evidence. Then merge the remainder into AIML-STRUCT-1, contributing this proposal's genuinely superior control taxonomy (full shuffle / linker-preserving / motif-block permutation), which is the best idea in it and which STRUCT-1 lacks.

critiques.scientific_objection: No leakage handling whatsoever, on the one benchmark where leakage dominates everything else. Boltz-2's affinity head was trained on ChEMBL-derived potency data and this proposal's calibration set is fetched live from ChEMBL by the repo's own corpus.py. Every number it produces is, with high prior probability, a memorisation measurement, and the proposal would write that number into thermo.METHOD_ACCURACY as though it were a method accuracy. AIML-BENCH-1 addresses this properly; this proposal is the same experiment without the control that makes it interpretable. Second, the write-back itself is a reporting hazard: placing an n=60, four-target, plausibly-in-training RMSE in the same dict as literature FEP (1.1) and MM-GBSA (2.5) figures invites readers to compare them as commensurate method-level accuracies. Third, '>=60 pairs... >=4 targets' gives per-target n~15, at which within-target Spearman CIs span most of [-1, 1]; the per-target rho will be uninformative and should not be reported as though it were.
critiques.feasibility_objection: The preflight gate is genuinely good and the heavy-atom census is concrete and checkable (Onjisaponin V at 123 heavy atoms inside the hard cap but at 2.2x the recommended limit is exactly the case that must not silently produce a number). The corpus extension to GSK3B/KEAP1/CHRM1/NOS3 inherits the truncation-cap denominator defect I found in corpus.py and will need that fixed first. 200-300 unattended runs is realistic.
critiques.improvement: Merge into AIML-BENCH-1 and keep three things this proposal has and that one lacks: the RDKit preflight applicability gate with its refusal path, the decoy-receptor AUROC for affinity_probability_binary (that 0.44 is uninterpretable without a decoy distribution is a correct and underappreciated point), and the write-back discipline. For the write-back, use a separate table — measured_in_repo_accuracy — never METHOD_ACCURACY, and require every key in it to carry n, the leakage stratum, the target set and the CI inline, so it cannot be read as a literature-grade method figure. Replace per-target Spearman with a pooled within-target rank correlation with a receptor-level cluster bootstrap. Adopt AIML-BENCH-1's rule that a paired delta whose CI spans zero renders as 'not distinguishable from the per-target-median null at n=N' rather than as an RMSE.

critiques.scientific_objection: This is the best-shaped refusal in the batch — measure the transfer error, pre-register the threshold, publish whichever way it falls — and the two-independent-retrievals-disagree-on-sign anecdote is the strongest available argument for install-don't-reimplement. One real confound in the four-cell table. Step 3 reproduces r ~ -0.73 / RMSE ~1.89 on the eLife benchmark, which is the set the PRODIGY regression was fitted on. That cell is therefore in-sample. The other three cells are out-of-sample. So the reported 'degradation' from crystal-PP to predicted-PP and to peptide conflates two things: the domain shift the experiment is designed to measure, and the ordinary in-sample/out-of-sample gap, which for a small-coefficient regression on 81 complexes is not negligible. As specified, the experiment cannot attribute its own headline number. Second, the pre-registered rule is stated on point-estimate RMSE ('emit only if RMSE <= 2.0 kcal/mol'); at n~20-50 peptide complexes the RMSE CI will be wide enough that the decision is made by sampling noise. Third, the success criterion 'all 35 candidates carry a receptor-bound co-fold' forces a receptor assignment for candidates that may not have a defensible one — I confirmed the targets field is anatomical prose ('CNS -> Brain -> Hippocampus (CA1 Cholinergic Terminals & Synaptic Cleft)'), and for the mechanistically inverted candidates aimed at cytoplasmic targets the honest output is 'no receptor assignable', which this criterion forbids.
critiques.feasibility_objection: A week is optimistic for step 4(a) alone: co-folding the Kastritis benchmark subset means dozens of genuine protein-protein complexes, several of them large, on MPS with unmeasured N^2-N^3 scaling. Time three representative sizes before committing. The registry assembly (step 1) is curation with judgement, not code, and is the item most likely to slip.
critiques.improvement: Add a fourth crystal-PP cell evaluated out-of-sample — hold out a portion of the benchmark from any fitting, or better, use complexes outside the eLife set entirely — so the in-sample/out-of-sample gap can be subtracted from the domain-shift estimate. Restate the pre-registered rule on the interval, not the point: 'emit only if the upper bound of the 95% CI on RMSE is below 2.0 kcal/mol AND the lower bound of the CI on |Spearman rho| excludes 0', and fix n before freezing so the rule is achievable. Change the co-fold criterion to 'every candidate carries either a receptor-bound co-fold with a named UniProt accession and residue range, or an explicit no_receptor_assignable record stating why' — the refusals are data, and for the inverted candidates they are the most informative data in the set. Keep the unconstrained-primary / pocket-constrained-secondary split exactly as written; that is the correct handling of circularity and no other proposal addresses it.

critiques.scientific_objection: The cysteine census reproduces exactly against data/dataset.json (21 candidates with >=4 Cys; 15 with an odd count; 4x8Cys, 4x6Cys, 3x4Cys), and the core insight — that an error bar on a molecule that is one of 105 possible chemical species is a category error — is the most original contribution in the batch. Three objections. (a) The uncertainty arithmetic is smuggled: 'that range... must be combined in quadrature with the method RMSE'. A min/max range over an enumerated hypothesis set and an RMSE are not commensurable, are not independent, and neither is Gaussian; adding them in quadrature produces a number with no distributional meaning. Defining the isomer term as an sd requires a prior over connectivities, which you do not have and cannot get. (b) The OpenMM filter is an uncalibrated binary classifier. 'Interface survives vs dissolves' has no measured false-pass rate on a known-correct complex and no false-fail rate on a known-wrong one, yet it is used to decide which connectivity is real. An unvalidated filter making a chemical assignment is precisely the failure class this repository exists to eliminate. (c) Status misuse: moving disulfide_connectivity to COMPUTED when one connectivity survives is wrong. Nothing was computed from first principles — a neural predictor plus an unvalidated MD filter selected among hypotheses. That is PREDICTED at best.
critiques.feasibility_objection: 1-1.5 weeks understates it if the Boltz SG-SG bond constraint fails, since the fallback ('imposed in the relaxation stage') is a different and much larger piece of work than the primary path — restraint setup, minimisation protocol and equilibration per isomer across 100-150 systems. Scope the fallback explicitly rather than as a one-clause contingency. Verifying the constraint against a conotoxin control first is the right order and should be a hard gate: if it fails, re-plan rather than continue.
critiques.improvement: Report the isomer spread as its own labelled quantity in the same units as the method error, side by side, and state in the schema that they must not be combined — a reader can see max(spread, RMSE) dominates without a false composite. If a composite is required, define it as a stated interval union, not a quadrature sum. Calibrate the OpenMM filter before any candidate touches it: run it on a solved disulfide-rich complex with correct connectivity (should pass) and on the same structure with a deliberately wrong pairing enforced (should fail), and publish both rates; if the filter cannot separate those two, it does not get to adjudicate candidates. Emit surviving connectivities as PREDICTED with the enumeration size, the filter's measured error rates and the parent-motif agreement as separate fields. Keep item 5's two code-level refusals verbatim — 'no code path can write an MM-GBSA value into binding_free_energy' is the kind of criterion that is objectively checkable and cannot be argued around.

critiques.scientific_objection: The best-evidenced proposal in the batch, and the only one that correctly located the existing artifacts — I confirmed 22 run directories under /tmp/cbc_boltz, each with input_model_0.cif, confidence_*.json, pae_*.npz and plddt_*.npz, contradicting the 'coordinates were discarded' claims in META-1 and DMPK-IDEA-2. Three objections. (a) Ordering: the success criterion 'reproduces the numbers measured this session' pins the module to the author's own unpublished run. That is a regression test, not validation, and if thresholds are set from the 22 candidate structures and then the reference set is used to confirm them, the thresholds are tuned on the test. Derive every band from the deposited reference distribution FIRST, freeze it as a data file with provenance, then apply. (b) Disulfide detection by an Sg-Sg radius cutoff is not a bond assignment. 'A cysteine within 2.5 A of two others' is precisely what a distance threshold produces near a cluster; whether that is a trivalent sulfur or a threshold artifact requires a matching rule (maximum-weight matching over the Sg-Sg graph), and the four named candidates are the cases where the distinction decides the finding. (c) Emitting disulfide_connectivity as PREDICTED with 'uncertainty = the measured S-S distance and chi3' conflates a property of the model with an uncertainty about the molecule. Given that 21 of 38 predicted S-S distances fall outside the reference band, the defensible emission for most is not_computed — the proposal applies that only to valence failures, not to chi3 outliers.
critiques.feasibility_objection: None material; two days is credible and gemmi is already installed. Item 6 (move the artifacts out of /tmp and record the path in every row of data/real_vs_hardcoded.json — which I confirmed has no path field) should be hoisted out of this proposal and executed today as a standalone repo-wide action, because four other proposals depend on those files and macOS may purge them at any boot.
critiques.improvement: Split into two commits with an ordering gate between them: (1) rescue the 22 artifacts into a repo path, register each with an ARTIFACT ledger record, and add the path to every row; (2) build the reference distribution over the ~60 deposited structures in target_records.pdb_examples, freeze it as a provenanced data file, and only then run the candidate audit. Replace the radius cutoff with maximum-weight matching over the Sg-Sg graph, and report both the matched assignment and the raw contact list so the trivalent-sulfur calls are auditable. Emit disulfide_connectivity only where distance, chi3 and valence all pass, as PREDICTED with the model's own metrics stored as measurements, not as 'uncertainty'; everything else stays not_computed with the failing check named. Restate the reproduce-this-session criterion explicitly as a regression pin, and make the validation criterion the zero-false-positive rate on deposited structures, which is the one that carries evidential weight. The cis-proline false positive in the current Ca-Ca gate is a genuine, cheap, high-value fix and should land regardless of the rest.

critiques.scientific_objection: The benchmark is entirely inside Boltz-2's training window and the proposal does not say so. 4EY7 and 4EY6 are 2012, 2FLU, 1WWW, 2IFG, 3FXI and 5UN5 are all well pre-2023-06-01, and the 16 curated targets were selected precisely because they are well-characterised — i.e. maximally likely to be memorised. AIML-BENCH-2 gets this exactly right and labels its pre-cutoff arm 'this measures recall, not prediction'; this proposal, running the same class of structures, presents the result as accuracy. That would be tolerable as a positive control, but item 4 then wires the number into the reporting layer as the calibration behind every displayed ipTM: 'no ipTM value anywhere in the platform's output or UI appears without the benchmark N and the measured DockQ distribution attached'. A calibration curve fitted on training-set recall, attached to every displayed confidence, is worse than no calibration, because it is confidently wrong in the flattering direction and it is now institutionalised in the UI. Second, the compute extrapolation is unsound: '26 s per lone chain, essentially independent of length from 26 to 100 residues, so a ~320-token complex is minutes-scale'. Constancy across 26-100 residues shows fixed overhead dominates in that regime; it says nothing about 320-590 tokens where pair-representation cost scales superlinearly. The proposal does then hedge with a timing pilot, which is the right instinct but sits alongside the unsound extrapolation rather than replacing it.
critiques.feasibility_objection: The scoring stack being verified installed is real and useful. The stated hard part — chain mapping and residue-numbering reconciliation — is correctly identified and is genuinely where the days go. 4-6 days is plausible for the monomer arm; the complex arm depends on the timing pilot the proposal itself flags.
critiques.improvement: Relabel the entire proposal as a positive-control / recall suite and say in the artifact, in the README and in every emitted record that every entry predates the model's training cutoff. Its scientific job is then precise and valuable: if the pipeline cannot recover 2FLU's KEAP1-Neh2 interface — a 16-mer in a groove, at 1.5 A, almost certainly in training — then no result on the designed candidates means anything, and that is a genuine, cheap, publishable gate. Move the calibration curve and the ipTM threshold to AIML-STRUCT-2's post-cutoff set; this proposal supplies the floor, that one supplies the scale. Delete the extrapolation sentence and make the timing pilot a precondition rather than a fallback. Keep the AlphaFold-DB cross-check (fetch_alphafold_db already exists) — a free second opinion on the receptor monomers is good value.

critiques.scientific_objection: The distinctive contribution — epitope overlap against the experimentally observed ligand epitope, with contacts defined identically on both sides, validated by reproducing the known 2FLU interface before any prediction is scored — is the only proposal in the batch that offers a coordinate-level falsification route for the mechanistically inverted candidates, and the validate-on-the-known-answer-first ordering is correct. Two objections. (a) pDockQ is a published fitted function. The proposal says 'add pDockQ from interface contact count and interface pLDDT' without saying where the coefficients come from. This repository's governing rule is that no equation may be reconstructed from memory — 32 of 319 retrieved items were explicitly marked must-not-be-implemented for exactly this reason — and a fitted sigmoid with remembered constants is the textbook violation. Either install a retrieved reference implementation and pin it, or drop pDockQ. (b) The proposal gates itself on STRUCTBIO-IDEA-2, whose benchmark I have argued is training-set recall; inheriting that as the 'benchmark context attached' to every displayed interface number propagates the contamination into the UI.
critiques.feasibility_objection: The honesty about the decoy arm is exemplary and rare — naming it as the arm most likely to need a GPU, and pre-committing to a reduced N=10 null rather than dropping the null, is the right trade and the right way to state it. One correction: at N=10 the minimum achievable percentile-based p is 0.091, so the 95th-percentile criterion in the success list is unreachable at reduced N. Say what the reduced-N verdict language will be before running.
critiques.improvement: Retrieve and pin a reference pDockQ implementation, or replace it with quantities you compute yourself from coordinates (buried SASA, contact count, interface pLDDT) reported raw and as decoy percentiles — those carry the same information without importing a remembered fit. Re-anchor the gating dependency on AIML-STRUCT-2's post-cutoff calibration rather than STRUCTBIO-IDEA-2's pre-cutoff set. State the reduced-N (N=10) verdict vocabulary up front, since the 95th-percentile criterion is unreachable there — use effect size plus an explicit 'null too small to support a percentile threshold' label. Merge the decoy-generation and statistics code with AIML-STRUCT-1 and AIML-BENCH-3; keep this proposal's epitope-overlap analysis as its own contribution, since it is the part nobody else has. The three KEAP1-directed candidates carrying a stated Jaccard overlap with the Neh2 epitope, including zero, is a genuinely good and objectively checkable success criterion.

critiques.scientific_objection: Deterministic, cheap, reproducible from an accession, and it falsifies a specific declared coupling chemistry from experimental coordinates rather than from argument — that combination is rare and I rate the idea highly. But the inferential claim overreaches the evidence in a way the success criteria then lock in. A single crystal form of one holo complex establishes that conjugation at N2 is incompatible with the binding mode observed in 4EY5. It does not establish that the conjugate cannot bind: induced fit, an alternative gorge-mouth pose, and the well-populated dual-site AChE inhibitor class (donepezil, the proposal's own positive control) all show the receptor tolerates far larger ligands than huperzine A. 'Mechanistically void' is a stronger claim than one static structure can carry, and validate.py failing a candidate on that basis converts an over-broad inference into an enforced verdict. Second, the grid-BFS 'minimum linker length in Angstroms, and in GGGGS residues' is a new quantitative design parameter with no validation anchor — 3.5 A per extended Gly-Ser residue is a plausible constant, but nothing in the design demonstrates that the computed minimum predicts what actually works. That is a number without knowledge unless anchored.
critiques.feasibility_objection: Genuinely 2-3 days; steps 1-3 are prototyped and the only new algorithmic work is ~80 lines of numpy. No new dependency. The one brittleness: pinning 98.5% +/- 0.5% in a unit test binds the result to a specific Shrake-Rupley parameterisation (n_points, radii set) and will break silently across biopython versions.
critiques.improvement: Narrow every emitted verdict string to the evidence: 'incompatible with the binding mode observed in PDB 4EY5 at 2.30 A' rather than NO_VECTOR as an unqualified property of the molecule, and make the validate.py category name that scope (binding_mode_conflict_observed_structure). Where multiple holo structures of the same warhead exist, run all of them and report the verdict per structure — disagreement between crystal forms is itself the calibration you need. Anchor the linker-length output against a retrieved set of bivalent AChE inhibitors with measured linker-length SAR: if the computed minimum is consistent with the shortest linkers that retain potency, the number has earned its place; if not, report the path length as a geometric measurement and delete the residue-count conversion. Pin the SASA parameters explicitly in the test alongside the tolerance, and record them in provenance.method, so the reproducibility claim survives a library upgrade. Keep the refusal for warheads with no experimental holo structure exactly as written.

critiques.scientific_objection: Highest value-per-day in the batch, and the diagnosis is confirmed in the repository: all 27 activities in data/corpus_ACHE.json carry assay_confidence: null while protocol_summary asserts 'assay confidence >= 8', and corpus_ACHE.json retains exactly one huperzine A activity (IC50 5.0 nM, assay CHEMBL643374, document CHEMBL1129143). Correcting a published error in the self-flagellating direction is a genuine reporting-standards contribution. Three objections. (a) I could not reconfirm the replacement number. The EBI ChEMBL API returned HTTP 500 and then timed out on three attempts over ~20 minutes today, via two independent clients. So '25 records, 0.54-5280 nM, median 47, corrected error ~1.43 log' is currently unverifiable by a third party — and republishing it through the ledger as a retraction-with-replacement would substitute one unverifiable number for another, in a project whose entire premise forbids that. (b) The choice between median (1.43 log) and geometric mean (1.20 log) changes the headline by 0.23 log and would be made after the model output is known. That is a researcher degree of freedom and it belongs in META-3's frozen pre-specification, which this proposal does not reference. (c) It misses the larger denominator defect: corpus.py:189-201 caps retrieval at limit=1000/page=200 and the recorded '258 examined' is that cap, not the population; count_target_activities() at line 185 fetches the real total and is unused. Aggregating within an arbitrarily truncated, default-ordered slice biases the aggregate before any endpoint typing happens.
critiques.feasibility_objection: Two days is right for the code. The endpoint-class table is medicinal-chemistry judgement and is correctly flagged as the heavy item — but it is also an instrument that decides which measurements count, built by one person with no second reader.
critiques.improvement: Do the retraction against a pinned, archived ChEMBL release downloaded to disk, with the release identifier, retrieval timestamp and verbatim query URLs recorded, and make the corrected figure regenerable offline. Do not publish the replacement from a live query. Freeze the aggregation rule (median vs geometric mean, censored-value handling, replicate weighting) in a META-3 prespec BEFORE recomputing, and record the freeze timestamp — this is the single case in the batch where a degree of freedom demonstrably moves the headline. Fix the denominator in the same pass: call count_target_activities(), page to exhaustion or declare the cap as a stated sampling frame with its ordering. Have the endpoint-class table reviewed by a second curator and record both curators in provenance; a table that decides which numbers survive should not be single-sourced. Report the empirical within-compound sigma with its n and a CI, not as a scalar.

critiques.scientific_objection: The mechanism x readout join is a real methodological advance over flag-and-forget PAINS annotation: it makes the flag conditional on whether the proposed interference mechanism can physically operate in the assay that produced the number, and it includes a negative control that must stay unflagged. That is better designed than most published interference filtering. Two objections. (a) Item 5 computes conjugation extent from RDKit perception and flags 'extended conjugation with donor substitution as a candidate 412 nm absorber', labelled PREDICTED. That is an uncalibrated structural classifier with no validation set, sitting inside a module whose purpose is to downgrade other people's measurements. For the handful of compounds actually involved, absorbance maxima are measured, published facts — retrieve them rather than predict them, and the module has no uncalibrated component at all. (b) The mechanism table and the readout table are where every decision lives, they are hand-written by one person, and nothing prevents them being built after the author already knows which compounds they will flag. A curation instrument that determines which evidence is downgraded needs the same pre-specification discipline the panel is demanding of the models.
critiques.feasibility_objection: 1-2 days for the substructure layer is right, RDKit's FilterCatalog ships the SMARTS so nothing is transcribed, and starting with Ellman/DTNB only — refusing to grade readouts not yet in the table rather than defaulting to 'clean' — is the correct scope discipline. The success criterion 'reproducing the flags listed in E5 under test' again pins to the author's own session and is a regression pin, not validation.
critiques.improvement: Replace the conjugation heuristic with retrieved measured absorbance maxima for the specific compounds in the corpus; if a spectrum cannot be retrieved for a compound, emit not_computed rather than a heuristic PREDICTED value — with a corpus this small there is no case for a model. Build and freeze the mechanism and readout tables through META-3's prespec mechanism, hashed and timestamped before the join is run against real compounds, and have a second curator score a sample of rows for agreement. Add an independent validation criterion alongside the E5 regression pin: run the full pipeline over a set of compounds with known-clean orthogonal-readout measurements and report the false-collision rate. Keep item 6 exactly as written — never deleting or numerically downweighting a value, only attaching a labelled evidence_grade with a named mechanism and citation, preserving the raw value — that is the correct handling and it is what makes this proposal safe to run.

critiques.scientific_objection: The audit hole is real and is the most consequential single defect anyone in this batch found. I read provenance.py:175-192 and confirmed audit() branches on dict, list and (int,float) with no str case, and target_records genetic evidence is prose carrying live numerals ('Open Targets direct... = 0.124', 'pLI 1.000, LOEUF 0.219'). The repository's flagship guarantee has an unpoliced escape hatch, and every genetics number in it sits inside that hatch. Fixing this is a half-day and should happen this week independent of the rest of the proposal. Two objections to the rest. (a) The TPP gate is a governance change presented as a computation. Requiring indication_id and failing all 35 without it will be satisfied by someone typing an EFO CURIE; a validated-but-asserted indication adds a field, not knowledge, and the gate then reports green on an unjustified choice. (b) The rank/percentile denominator over-flatters. 13,289 'targets associated with MONDO_0004975' includes text-mined and literature-derived associations, so a rank of #1205 for NTRK1 against that denominator sounds mid-field when against a denominator of genes with any genetic_association evidence it might be nowhere at all. A denominator whose composition is unstated is the same defect the platform criticises elsewhere.
critiques.feasibility_objection: 2-3 days is credible for the API layer; the queries are small JSON over HTTPS. One caution learned the hard way today: I hit HTTP 500 and multi-minute timeouts from EBI ChEMBL this session, so any gate that re-fetches at build time will fail on somebody else's outage. check_genetic_drift as a build-failing check will be disabled within a week of its first false alarm.
critiques.improvement: Ship the audit() str branch as a standalone patch first — regex-scan string leaves for decimal numerals, report prose_embedded_number — and run it before anything else in this proposal; that single change is worth more than the rest combined. Make the TPP gate require the indication AND a provenanced justification (who selected it, on what evidence, with a source), so the field cannot be satisfied by typing. Report rank against two stated denominators: all associated targets, and targets with a non-zero genetic_association datatype, with the composition of each spelled out. Convert check_genetic_drift from a build failure into a scheduled diff report that requires an explicit re-pin to clear, with a cached last-good result so upstream outages cannot break the build. Storing gnomAD v2.1.1 and v4 as two separately labelled Values and forbidding any code path from merging them is exactly right and should be the pattern for every versioned external number in the repo.

critiques.scientific_objection: I am judging the methodological shell rather than the statistical-genetics substance, which is outside my competence. On that shell: the strongest feature is that the honest answer here is UNDETERMINED for nearly everything and the proposal says so rather than manufacturing a verdict, and excluding clinical_precedence from the genetic verdict on circularity grounds is correct and well argued. Two objections. (a) The concordance rubric is where the entire result is decided and it is described only as 'a small explicit rubric comparing the candidate's declared modality against the genetic direction'. An unspecified combination rule over four heterogeneous, partly-missing signals is a free parameter, and writing it after seeing the four signals for all 16 targets means the verdicts are chosen, not computed. (b) The success criterion 'reports UNDETERMINED for at least 34 of 35' is outcome-contingent: if the layer correctly returned UNDETERMINED for 20, the criterion fails even though the layer is right. That inverts what the criterion is for.
critiques.feasibility_objection: 3-4 days for the API layer is credible given the queries already run. The local cis-MR/coloc extension at 'roughly a week' is optimistic in my experience of summary-statistics work, but it is correctly scoped as CPU-only and correctly marked as an extension rather than a dependency, so the main proposal is not hostage to it.
critiques.improvement: Write the concordance rubric out in full — every combination of the four signals mapped to CONCORDANT / DISCORDANT / UNDETERMINED, including all the missing-data cases — freeze it via META-3's prespec with a hash and timestamp before running it on real data, and publish the table itself as the deliverable alongside the verdicts. Replace the '34 of 35' criterion with the process form: every triple carries a verdict produced by the frozen rubric, UNDETERMINED is the default, no silent third state exists, and the fixture test that flips CONCORDANT to DISCORDANT on a modality flip passes. That last bullet is already in the proposal and is the best-designed success criterion of the three genetics items — make it the model for the others. Also add the typed modality enum as an explicit prerequisite with its own gate, since the proposal notes modality is currently only inferable from prose and everything downstream depends on it.

critiques.scientific_objection: The instrument-provenance half is excellent and nearly free: recording which biosample each genetic instrument came from and emitting a cell_type_match verdict turns an invisible assumption into a checkable field, and MISMATCH for plasma/monocyte instruments against brain claims is the kind of finding that changes what the platform may assert. The expression half has an uncalibrated-threshold problem of exactly the kind this panel is attacking elsewhere. 'Specificity index = brain-region median / whole-body median' is an invented statistic with no reference distribution, and check_region_claim fires when peak expression is 'extra-CNS by more than a stated fold' — a number with no empirical basis is an ipTM-0.8-heuristic in different clothing. Whether a ratio of 2 or 20 means anything depends entirely on the distribution of that ratio across all genes, which is computable and is not computed.
critiques.feasibility_objection: Steps 1 and 3 at 2-3 days are realistic and the GTEx CLI is already vendored. Step 2 at 'roughly a week' understates the usual cost of harmonising two consortia's summary statistics to a common build with consistent effect-allele orientation; that is routinely a multi-week task and it is the step most likely to be abandoned half-done, leaving the layer with instrument provenance for some targets and not others. The proposal's own finding that no brain or microglial QTL colocalization was returned for any of the 16 targets suggests the honest outcome for step 2 may be 'no instrument available' across the board, which is worth knowing but is not worth a month.
critiques.improvement: Compute the specificity index for all protein-coding genes in GTEx v10 once, store the empirical distribution as a provenanced data file, and express each target's value as a percentile against it; then check_region_claim's threshold is a stated quantile with a denominator instead of a fold pulled from air. That also makes the CHRNA7 paralog caveat quantitative — you can show where the confounded estimate sits relative to the genome-wide distribution. Split step 2 out as a separate, separately-scheduled proposal with its own go/no-go: first do the cheap query establishing whether any brain or microglial cis-QTL instrument exists for these 16 genes at all, and only build the harmonisation pipeline if the answer is yes for a useful number of them. Ship steps 1 and 3 first — they are days, they are checkable, and the cell_type_match MISMATCH verdict is the single most useful output in the three genetics proposals.

critiques.scientific_objection: The framing is right — immunogenicity is the one major liability of a 3-11 kDa peptide fully determined by primary sequence, needing no structure, no receptor and no MSA, so it is exactly the gap closable honestly on this hardware — and the self-proteome filter is an exact substring test rather than a model, which is the strongest kind of evidence available here. Two objections. (a) n_binders and n_strong_binders are reported raw, with no null. A 100-residue construct yields ~86 15-mers; across a ~25-allele panel at a 1% rank threshold you expect on the order of 20 strong-binder calls by construction, before any biology. Reporting that count as a candidate property, with no expectation under a matched null, is the identical error the structural proposals correctly identify for a bare ipTM — and this batch cannot criticise uncalibrated ipTM in one proposal and ship uncalibrated epitope counts in another. (b) 'SELF' is the wrong label for 'this 9-mer occurs in UP000005640'. Tolerance depends on expression level and thymic presentation, not on presence in a reference proteome; a 9-mer from a testis-restricted protein is present and not tolerized. The field name will be read as a tolerance claim it cannot support.
critiques.feasibility_objection: 2-3 days is credible and the MixMHC2pred fallback genuinely de-risks the NetMHCIIpan licence form. The control gate is too thin: one published positive epitope plus its scramble cannot establish that a binary is correctly installed and configured — a scramble of an immunodominant epitope can itself bind, and a single pass proves nothing about the allele panel or the rank calibration.
critiques.improvement: Report every count against a null: composition-matched scrambles of the same construct (free, CPU-only, and it directly answers 'is this construct worse than its own composition'), plus a reference panel of human proteins of matched length. The junctional attribution then becomes the real finding — junctional neo-cores per junction versus the same rate in non-junctional windows — which is a within-molecule control that needs no external calibration and is the most defensible statistic available. Rename the self filter field to present_in_reference_proteome (UP000005640, release recorded) and state explicitly in the schema that presence is a necessary, not sufficient, condition for tolerance. Replace the single-epitope control gate with a small retrieved benchmark of published binders and non-binders, and report sensitivity and specificity on it before any candidate is scored — the proposal already commits to writing the control result to the ledger before candidate scoring, which is the right discipline, it just needs enough controls to mean something. The zero-numbers-when-no-binary-installed test mirroring the ADMET refusal test is a good, objectively checkable criterion.

critiques.scientific_objection: The proposal's supporting evidence contains a factual error that changes its plan. 'A filesystem-wide search for *.cif and boltz output directories in the repository returns nothing... the coordinates themselves were discarded' is false: /tmp/cbc_boltz holds 22 run directories, each with input_model_0.cif, confidence_*.json, pae_*.npz and plddt_*.npz. STRUCTBIO-IDEA-1 found and analysed those exact files. The real defect is narrower — they sit in a purge-eligible path and no row in data/real_vs_hardcoded.json records a path, which I confirmed. So the 'budget a day of compute to repeat the runs' is unnecessary, and re-folding would in any case not recover provenance for the published numbers, because those runs were unseeded. Second, on substance: the structural gating layer computes SASA and secondary structure on Boltz-2 single-chain models of designed flexible peptides — the one row I inspected has frac_below_70 = 0.19 and these are exactly the sequences where a model is least trustworthy. The 'structurally undetermined' label handles this honestly, but nothing pre-declares what happens if that label covers most sites, in which case the structural half adds nothing over the sequence census while appearing to add rigour. Third, 'does administering CogAbeta-Clearer-08 liberate free Abeta16-35' is an in vivo claim; a static exposure-plus-SSE analysis supports 'the motif is present, flanked by labile linker, and predicted accessible', which is a hypothesis about a released fragment, not its identity.
critiques.feasibility_objection: The sequence census is essentially done and productionising it is under a day — that half should ship immediately. The structural half's stated day of compute is not needed once the existing artifacts are recovered, but the mmCIF-to-SASA-to-SSE plumbing shares the all-atom parser with STRUCTBIO-IDEA-1 and AIML-BENCH-2 and should not be built a third time.
critiques.improvement: Correct the evidence: recover the 22 existing artifacts into the repository, register them in the ledger, and record the path in every row of data/real_vs_hardcoded.json — that is today's work and four proposals depend on it. Then pre-declare the undetermined-fraction rule: if more than a stated fraction of cleavage sites fall in pLDDT<70 regions for a given candidate, report sequence-only for that candidate and say so, rather than reporting a structurally-gated result that is mostly ungated. Reword the Abeta deliverable to a predicted-fragment-identity claim with the prediction chain named, and keep the motif_provenance exact-substring cross-reference, which is objectively checkable. Ship the sequence census now as its own commit — AstroPafr-Block-A4 having zero sites where the polycationic amphipaths have 24 in 36 residues is a real discriminating result that needs no structure at all. The criterion 'no half-life in time units is emitted anywhere; the module must be incapable of printing a t1/2, and a test asserts this' is the best single success criterion in the entire batch: it is a self-limiting, machine-checkable constraint on what the code may claim, and I would like to see that pattern applied to at least five other proposals here.

critiques.scientific_objection: The BBB half is the model for how this whole project should handle an out-of-domain predictor: state the tool's stated applicability domain, count how many candidates it legitimately admits (at most 4 of 35 by length), refuse the rest with the violating property named, and replace the refused prediction with a deterministic, citable substring census. I would hold that up as the reference pattern. The moment half has a coherence problem. The Eisenberg moment at 100 deg/residue presupposes an alpha-helix; step 3 correctly gates on Boltz-2 secondary structure — but those are low-confidence single-chain models of designed flexible peptides, so step 6 then retires a deterministic composition rule and replaces the liability trigger with a quantity whose interpretability depends on a model's uncertain SSE call. The replacement inherits model uncertainty that the old rule, whatever its faults, did not have. Second, the four-peptide control panel calibrates the reader, not the method: four points cannot locate a lytic threshold, and the six candidates scoring 0.886-0.894 'at or above LL-37' is a comparison against a single reference, not a position in a distribution.
critiques.feasibility_objection: About two days is right and the work is largely done. The HemoPI2 arm adds a large one-time model download and — more importantly — a second uncalibrated predictor whose applicability domain over 26-100-residue polycations is asserted rather than measured; the two-control acceptance gate (melittin hemolytic, insulin B-chain not) is far too weak to establish that.
critiques.improvement: Keep both triggers rather than retiring the composition rule: report the deterministic composition flag and the moment side by side, with the moment explicitly labelled conditional on the helicity call and its supporting pLDDT. Replace the four-peptide panel with a rank against a retrieved set of measured peptides with matched assay conditions (a hemolysis database of hundreds gives a percentile instead of an eyeball comparison, and simultaneously supplies HemoPI2's applicability-domain coverage check with real data). Extend the HemoPI2 acceptance gate from 2 controls to a held-out subset of that measured set, and report its measured accuracy on that subset in the provenance of every HemoPI2 value; if it cannot be established, refuse rather than report. Keep verbatim: the melittin 0.558 +/- 0.001 determinism guard, the explicit count of how many of 35 any BBB predictor can legitimately accept, and the per-shuttle DOI requirement. The regression test demonstrating CogDual-TrkB-PAS-10 is now flagged where it previously was not is a good sensitivity criterion.

critiques.scientific_objection: This is my own area and I verified its three central claims independently. The ledger re-hash reproduces exactly (ok=10, mismatch=4, missing=0, the four being data/dataset.json, data/real_vs_hardcoded.json, platform/validate.py, reviews/REVIEW_REPORT.md). git ls-files over platform/, data/, memory/, research/, reviews/ returns zero and there is no LICENSE. The RDKIT_VER literal at build_dataset.py:34 and the getattr fallback at corpus.py:318 are both present as described, and run_boltz's command list at structure.py:191-195 passes no --seed. Three objections. (a) 'searched: no Boltz output directory exists' is wrong — 22 exist under /tmp/cbc_boltz with cif, confidence JSON and pae/plddt npz. This matters operationally: those files are the only physical evidence of what produced the published numbers, re-folding unseeded runs cannot recover their provenance, and preserving them is free and urgent while re-folding is a separate later experiment. (b) A further instance of the very defect the proposal is about, which it missed: every row in data/real_vs_hardcoded.json records accelerator: 'gpu', not 'mps'. A hand-set provenance string is wrong in the shipped data and 215 checks did not notice. Use it as the motivating example for env.runtime(). (c) The noise-envelope rule 'downgrade any delta smaller than 2x that envelope' is built on an sd from three seeds, whose own relative uncertainty is roughly 50%; a reclassification rule driven by a three-draw sd would itself be noise.
critiques.feasibility_objection: 2-3 days plus overnight MPS is right, and the refusal to containerise the neural layer — stating plainly that Docker on macOS has no Metal passthrough and would silently fall back to CPU, and recording that limitation instead of shipping a misleading image — is exactly the correct call and the kind of honesty the rest of the batch should copy. The one real risk is that item 5 (commit everything, add a LICENSE) is listed last in the method while being the prerequisite for essentially every other proposal's success criteria.
critiques.improvement: Reorder: item 5 first, today, plus artifact rescue of the 22 existing runs from /tmp into the repo with ARTIFACT ledger records and a path recorded in every row of data/real_vs_hardcoded.json. Then env.runtime(), then reproduce.py, then re-folding. Correct the artifact-absence claim in the write-up, and add the accelerator:'gpu' discrepancy as the worked example for why introspection must replace literals. Raise the seed envelope to n>=10 on two or three candidates and report it with a CI; replace the '2x the envelope' rule with a distribution-free criterion (the legacy delta must exceed the observed across-seed range) so the reclassification is not driven by a three-point sd. Add to reproduce.py the one gap it does not cover: a check that every provenance.software string, every accelerator string and every seed in the emitted dataset came from env.runtime() rather than a literal, since that is the class of defect that produced both the RDKit literal and the wrong accelerator.

critiques.scientific_objection: The diagnosis is correct and the PROV-O mapping is well chosen — the observation that this project's genuinely novel content is its absences, and that an ordinary tabular export makes a deliberate NOT_COMPUTED indistinguishable from a missing measurement, is the sharpest argument in the proposal and it justifies the formal vocabulary on scientific rather than aesthetic grounds. The objection is sequencing, and it is serious. Exporting a PROV-O/RO-Crate description of a repository that is not under version control, has no licence, and whose own ledger fails its hash check on four artifacts (I reproduced: 4 mismatches) would produce a machine-readable, standards-validating, DOI-bearing description of an irreproducible object. Serialization is not provenance. A crate that validates cleanly while describing a working tree nobody can reconstruct is worse than no crate, because it converts an internal inconsistency into a citable external claim. Second, minting a Zenodo DOI is irreversible; doing it before META-1's reproduce.py exits 0 and before the ledger mismatches are resolved permanently attaches a version identifier to a state the authors will want to disown.
critiques.feasibility_objection: 3-4 days for the code is right and the modelling is the real work, as stated. The IRI resolution criterion is the brittle part and today proved it: EBI returned HTTP 500 and then timed out for ~20 minutes while I was verifying an unrelated claim. A build gate that fails on a third party's outage gets disabled after its second false alarm, and then the check is gone.
critiques.improvement: Hard-sequence after META-1 items 1, 3 and 5, and make it an explicit precondition in the proposal text: no crate, no DOI until reproduce.py exits 0 and the ledger re-hash reports zero mismatches. Make IRI resolution a scheduled report with a cached last-good result and an explicit staleness field, never a per-commit build gate; the per-commit check should be syntactic (is this a well-formed CURIE for a known namespace), which is offline and deterministic. Promote item 5(ii) — the negative-result methods preprint — out of this proposal into its own workstream, since it is the highest-value publishable output the panel has and it is currently a sub-bullet of a packaging task. But gate it: it must not be drafted until AIML-STRUCT-3 has established the seed envelope and MEDCHEM-IDEA-2 has fixed the ground-truth aggregate, or it will publish the 10-unit pLDDT deltas without knowing whether they exceed sampling noise, and the 2.41 log affinity error against a ground truth this panel has already shown to be one cherry-picked measurement out of many. Publishing corrections that are themselves wrong would be the single worst outcome available to this project.

critiques.scientific_objection: The criterion-exercise audit is the best generalisable idea in the batch. It converts 'we stated a protocol' into 'we proved each clause fired', it is cheap, it is mechanical, and it would have caught the confidence-8 bug automatically. I confirmed the bug fires today: 27 of 27 activities in data/corpus_ACHE.json carry assay_confidence: null while protocol_summary asserts 'assay confidence >= 8', and denominator.rejected has no low-confidence bucket at all. Three objections. (a) The audit rule as specified will generate false alarms and then be waived. A criterion can legitimately reject nothing on a given population; 'count == 0 over N >= 50 examined -> NOT_EXERCISED -> fail' conflates 'the guard was never evaluated because the field was always null' — the actual bug — with 'the guard was evaluated 258 times and rejected nobody'. Instrument evaluation attempts, not rejections, and the check becomes both sound and non-annoying. This is precisely the distinction the ChEMBL bug turns on. (b) The freeze mechanism rests on the ledger's append-only guarantee, but the ledger currently fails its own hash check on four artifacts and nothing in this repository is under version control (git ls-files over platform/, data/, memory/ returns zero). A hash-locked pre-specification stored in an untracked directory alongside a mutable ledger is a timestamp the author can rewrite; the tamper test would pass while the guarantee is absent. (c) The decision rule in item 4 has blank thresholds — 'MAE 95% CI upper bound below X and rho exceeds Y'. A pre-specification with unfilled thresholds is not a pre-specification, and filling them after the pilot is the degree of freedom the whole mechanism exists to close.
critiques.feasibility_objection: Two days for the format, the freeze/verify commands and the audit is realistic. The corpus re-fetch with a proper /assay join is the item to watch: I hit HTTP 500 and multi-minute timeouts from EBI today, and the /assay join multiplies request count, so it needs batching, retry-with-backoff and an on-disk cache or it will be flaky. The 18-complex benchmark overnight on MPS is fine.
critiques.improvement: Redefine the audit to count evaluations, not rejections: a criterion is NOT_EXERCISED when the field it claims to read was never non-null across the examined set, and separately report evaluated-but-never-rejected as informational. Declare a hard dependency on META-1 item 5 — the prespec is only binding once the repository is in git and the ledger passes its own hash check — and state that in the proposal rather than assuming it. Fill X and Y before freezing and justify them against AIML-BENCH-1's measured sigma_exp: a threshold tighter than the experimental noise floor is unachievable by construction, and pre-registering an impossible bar is as bad as pre-registering none. Add one criterion the proposal does not have and that I found while verifying it: the executed protocol must record its own retrieval bounds. corpus.py:189-201 caps at limit=1000/page=200, so the recorded 'activities_examined: 300 / 258 distinct molecules' is a client-side truncation cap presented as a population, while count_target_activities() at corpus.py:185 fetches the real total and is unused. A stated denominator that is a for-loop bound is a decorative criterion of exactly the class this proposal exists to detect, and it is currently the platform's headline methodological asset.

refined.expert: PhD in ML for structural biology, 15 years post-PhD; trains and evaluates AlphaFold-class models; reviews for NeurIPS and Nature Methods

revised.title: Fix and measure the inference configuration: determinism, variance decomposition, and MSA as a controlled factor
revised.changed_what: Promoted to strict prerequisite for the other two. Dropped the byte-reproducibility criterion for a measured same-seed divergence tolerance. Renamed the output field from `uncertainty` to `sampling_sd` and added a validate.py rule forbidding it from rendering as an error bar on correctness. Raised seed count to n>=10 on three anchor cases with a bootstrap CI on the sd itself, and now measure the pLDDT envelope separately from the ipTM envelope. Pre-declared the sample-selection rule. Kept a diffusion_samples=1 arm so the 22 legacy deltas stay re-interpretable. WITHDREW the single-compound Huperzine A retest. Added an environment-introspection requirement after confirming the recorded accelerator string is wrong.
conceded: 'data/real_vs_hardcoded.json is byte-reproducible on a second execution' is not achievable and was a bad criterion. Five reviewers said so independently. Seeding fixes the noise draw, not floating-point reduction order on Metal, and the aten::linalg_svd CPU fallback I myself documented is exactly the kind of backend dispatch that breaks bitwise determinism. Promising it and then quietly relaxing it is how reproducibility criteria get discredited.

Writing an across-seed sd into a field named `uncertainty` is the project's own failure mode one level up. A tightly reproducible but systematically wrong prediction would render as high-confidence. Repeatability is not accuracy and must not share a field name with it.

The sd of 0.133 came from n=3. The relative standard error of an sd estimate at n=3 is roughly 50%, so the true value could be 0.07 or 0.20. I let a 3-seed pilot set a platform-wide error bar. That is the same epistemic error as a hardcoded constant, with a sampler behind it instead of a trigonometric expression.

I argued from an ipTM sd to the interpretation of pLDDT deltas. Illegitimate: ipTM is an interface statistic that is often bimodal (docked vs undocked), while mean pLDDT averages over hundreds of residues and will have a much smaller across-seed spread. The pLDDT envelope must be measured on its own before any legacy pLDDT delta is called noise.

The factorial at diffusion_samples=5 produces a statistic that cannot be compared to the legacy diffusion_samples=1 numbers, which is the stated motivation. A top-1-of-5 selection is a max-statistic and is upward-biased relative to a single draw.
The sample-selection rule (top-1 of N by confidence_score vs mean over samples) was never stated, and it changes both the point estimate and the spread. Unspecified.

n=1 before and n=1 after cannot establish that MSA mode improved the Huperzine A prediction, and the 2.41 log denominator is itself contested as a cherry-picked single measurement. I withdraw that item from this proposal.

The recorded provenance says accelerator 'gpu' in every existing row, not 'mps'. My claim that all 22 runs are documented as MPS is not supported by the repository's own record. A hand-set string was wrong and never noticed.
defended: Keeping the peptide chain at msa=empty is correct for the designed chimeras, but I accept the reframing: it is a modelling DECISION, not a fact about the sequences. The motif_provenance records 16 motifs with exact_match true against UniProt, so the parent motifs demonstrably have homologues; what has no homologues is the GGGGS-linked chimera as a whole. I now state it as a decision and add a third MSA arm to make it measured rather than asserted.

This proposal should still run first. One reviewer wanted the production configuration fixed before any calibration, which is precisely this proposal's function, so that objection reinforces the sequencing rather than opposing it.
The 1YCR MSA delta remains confounded with a seed change in the pilot, which is why the factorial exists. I am not quoting it as an effect estimate, and I flagged the confound in the original text.
revised.final_method: Runs before AIML-STRUCT-2 and AIML-STRUCT-1, both of which consume its outputs. (0) Prerequisite, one hour: run the identical job twice at the SAME seed and report whether outputs are bitwise identical; if not, report max per-atom coordinate deviation and |delta ipTM| / |delta pLDDT|. That measured divergence becomes the platform's reproducibility tolerance, and 'MPS is not bitwise deterministic' is recorded in the manifest as a finding. (1) Add seed, use_msa_server, msa_server_url, sampling_steps, step_scale as parameters of run_boltz (platform/cbc/compute/structure.py; the command list at lines 191-195 currently hardcodes out_dir/accelerator/recycling_steps/diffusion_samples/output_format/override and never passes --seed, while boltz/main.py:1102 guards seed_everything(seed) behind 'if seed is not None' with CLI default None). Fix _collect_boltz_outputs (line 220), which keeps only sorted(...)[0] and silently discards every model beyond the top-ranked one, making ensembles impossible. (2) Pre-register the sample-selection rule IN WRITING before any batch runs -- top-1 of N by confidence_score -- and record it in every output row, so all structural batches in this panel share one rule. (3) Environment manifest built by runtime introspection (torch.backends.mps.is_available(), device of the actual tensors), never a hand-set string; validate.py rejects a hand-set accelerator value. (4) Variance design: three anchor cases (one lone helix, one ~600-token complex, one ~1100-token complex) at n>=10 seeds; the remaining five pairs at n=5 and labelled provisional. Report a two-level decomposition, sigma_seed and sigma_sample-given-seed, with a bootstrap CI on each sd, SEPARATELY for mean pLDDT, ipTM, and min interface PAE -- these three do not share a variance. Keep one arm at diffusion_samples=1 so the legacy deltas remain re-interpretable. (5) MSA factorial, three arms: msa=empty both chains; receptor a3m + peptide empty (the production config for candidates); receptor a3m + peptide a3m (added because the motifs do have homologues, so whether a chimera MSA helps or misleads is empirical). 16 receptor a3m files cached under data/msa/ from the ColabFold MMseqs2 server, with an explicit code-level assertion that no candidate sequence is ever transmitted, and a note that the a3m files are third-party-derived data entering a repo with no LICENSE. (6) Emit sampling_sd as a provenance key DISTINCT from uncertainty; leave uncertainty empty until an accuracy-anchored quantity exists from AIML-STRUCT-2. Add a validate.py rule that sampling_sd may never be rendered as an error bar on a value, and a rule that any PREDICTED value lacking seed, software version, sample count, selection rule and sampling_sd is a violation. (7) Document the aten::linalg_svd MPS-to-CPU fallback in boltz/model/loss/diffusionv2.py alongside timings.
final_success_criteria: A same-seed replicate pair is run and the result is published as either 'bitwise identical' or a numeric divergence (max per-atom deviation in A, |delta ipTM|, |delta pLDDT|); the platform reproducibility tolerance is set equal to that measured number, and no criterion anywhere in the project claims byte-reproducibility on MPS.

A table reporting, for three anchor cases at n>=10 seeds, sigma_seed and sigma_sample-given-seed with bootstrap 95% CIs, given SEPARATELY for mean pLDDT, ipTM and min interface PAE. Objective check: nine sd values each with an interval, and no single sd quoted as applying across all three quantities.
The sample-selection rule is written to a file with a timestamp before the first batch executes, and appears verbatim in every output row.

provenance emits `sampling_sd` (never `uncertainty`) for PREDICTED structural values; verify_all.py contains a test that fails if a sampling_sd is rendered as an error bar on correctness, and a test that fails on a PREDICTED value missing seed, version, sample count, or selection rule.

The accelerator field is produced by runtime introspection; a test asserts the recorded string matches the introspected device, and the pre-existing incorrect 'gpu' value in all 22 legacy rows is corrected or explicitly marked unverifiable.
A three-arm MSA comparison table with the seed variance partialled out, reporting the receptor-MSA main effect with a CI, including the peptide-MSA arm and stating whether it changes ipTM materially.

revised.title: Leakage-stratified peptide-protein benchmark serving two functions: confidence calibration AND the power denominator for the candidate screen
revised.changed_what: Rebuilt after confirming from the Boltz-2 appendix that my date filter was wrong. Cutoff moved from >2023-06-01 to >2024-01-01 to escape the authors' checkpoint-selection window. Added cluster-40 leakage stratification against the pre-cutoff PDB, implemented via RCSB's precomputed cluster files after confirming mmseqs2 is unavailable here. n raised from 100 and now sized by a stated precision target. DockQ demoted to secondary for short partners in favour of peptide-backbone RMSD. Refusal logic moved from ipTM-bin occupancy to covariate-space distance. Most importantly, this proposal now ALSO owns the positive-control sensitivity panel that AIML-STRUCT-1 needs, so the two are one machine rather than two.
conceded: The leakage control was wrong and I can now show it verbatim from the paper I cited. Boltz-2's validation set -- the set used to select the released checkpoint -- is defined as 'Initial release date is before 2023-06-01 (exclusive) and 2024-01-01 (inclusive)', n=398. My filter of >2023-06-01 therefore overlapped the model-selection set entirely. Any calibration fit on it would have been optimistic by an unquantified amount. This is the single most common split-design error and it was in my proposal.

Deduplicating the benchmark at 30-40% identity WITHIN itself removes redundancy between benchmark members and does nothing about train-test proximity. The control that matters is each entry's similarity to the pre-2023-06-01 PDB, which I specified for ligands in a sibling proposal and then omitted here. The paper's own filter is 'All the protein sequences of the chains are not present in any training set clusters' at mmseqs --min-seq-id 0.4, and I should have mirrored it.

n=100 cannot support the deliverables. Across ~5 ipTM bins that is 15-25 per bin, Wilson half-widths near +/-0.2, and an AUROC CI around +/-0.10. I committed to a 'stated, defensible ipTM threshold' that the sample size cannot produce. I chose a round number instead of doing a precision calculation.

DockQ >= 0.23 is a CAPRI protein-protein criterion and is the wrong instrument at the short end of a 5-40 residue range. With a handful of interface contacts fnat is unstable and DockQ collapses toward LRMSD. Putting a 5-mer and a 40-mer on one reliability curve mixes two measurement regimes.

Restricting extrapolation to populated ipTM BINS does not address covariate shift. An in-range ipTM computed on an out-of-distribution input still returns a fabricated probability. The applicability guard was on the wrong axis.

The RCSB filter as written will pull crystallisation additives, uncleaved affinity tags, propeptide remnants and symmetry-mate fragments, several of which have no defined correct answer. I budgeted no curation time. Note the confirmation: 2FLU's Kelch entity sequence begins GSSHHHHHHSSGLVPRGSH -- an expression tag sitting in exactly the kind of entry this query returns.

Calibrating in a configuration a sibling proposal shows to be degraded is backwards. AIML-STRUCT-3 now fixes the production configuration first, and this calibration runs once, afterwards, in that frozen configuration.
defended: The temporal-holdout strategy itself stands; only the date was wrong, and the corrected filter still returns 937 entries against the same query, so the fix costs nothing in sample size. Verified this session: >2023-06-01 = 1107, >2024-01-01 = 937, >2024-06-01 = 810.

The unvalidated clustering step is now solved, and not by mmseqs. I re-confirmed that RCSB server-side cluster_id search is disabled ('search is not enabled on [rcsb_cluster_membership.cluster_id]'), and that mmseqs2 has no arm64 wheel and is not installed. But RCSB publishes precomputed cluster files -- clusters-by-entity-30.txt, -40.txt and -70.txt all return HTTP 200 -- and the per-entity Data API returns cluster_membership at 30/50/70/90/95/100. That yields the Boltz-2 0.4 threshold directly, with no local alignment engine, and removes the reviewers' 'budget a day for mmseqs' risk entirely.

One reviewer proposed 2FLU as the seed positive control and separately suggested preferring post-2024 entries; those two requirements conflict for that entry. 2FLU was released 2006-08-15, far pre-cutoff, so it is a recall/competence probe, not a calibration point. I keep it, in the sensitivity panel, explicitly labelled as recall.

I reject the implication that a calibration curve is worthless because the candidates fall outside its domain. Establishing that they fall outside it, and refusing to emit a probability for them on that basis, IS the deliverable. A refusal grounded in a measured domain is knowledge; the current state, which emits nothing and knows nothing, is not.
revised.final_method: Runs after AIML-STRUCT-3, in the frozen production configuration. (1) Benchmark: RCSB query as before but with initial_release_date > 2024-01-01, escaping both the training cutoff and the authors' 398-structure checkpoint-selection window (937 hits available). (2) Leakage stratification, no mmseqs required: download clusters-by-entity-40.txt (verified reachable) plus current holdings with release dates; for each benchmark receptor entity compute whether its 40% cluster contains any pre-2023-06-01 member. Stratify EVERY headline metric by max identity to pre-cutoff -- <30% / 30-70% / >70% -- and never pool. The >70% stratum is the memorisation control and its size is itself a reportable number. Apply the same test to the peptide/epitope, and exclude post-cutoff entries that are re-determinations of a pre-cutoff complex (same UniProt pair, same partner sequence). (3) Curation, with a published count discarded at each filter: require the short entity to carry a UniProt cross-reference, strip/flag expression tags, require buried surface area above a stated threshold, and discard symmetry-mate and additive artefacts. (4) Sizing by precision, not by round number: state the target Wilson half-width per bin (+/-0.10 at p~0.5 implies ~100 per bin) and solve for N; expect 300-500, which at the measured 1-3 min per complex is one weekend of unattended MPS.
