(5) Scoring stratified by partner length: 5-15 residues scored primarily by binding-site-superposed peptide backbone RMSD with 2 A as acceptable, DockQ secondary; 16-40 residues scored by both. Explicit chain mapping recorded. (6) Fit P(correct | ipTM) by isotonic or logistic regression with a bootstrap band rather than binned proportions plus ECE; show binned points only as a visual overlay with per-bin n printed. Do the same for min interface PAE. (7) SENSITIVITY / POWER PANEL, which is the arm AIML-STRUCT-1 depends on: >=10 solved peptide-receptor complexes run through the byte-identical pipeline, each with its own composition-matched scramble set. Report the fraction of genuine binders whose native beats its own scramble distribution. THAT FRACTION IS THE ASSAY'S POWER and becomes the published denominator of every candidate verdict. Include 2FLU (KEAP1 Kelch + Neh2 16-mer AFFAQLQLDEETGEFL, 1.5 A) labelled as pre-cutoff recall, and where a receptor in the candidate set has a solved peptide complex, include that receptor specifically. (8) predictor.calibrated_interface_probability refuses on covariate-space distance, not bin occupancy: fit a domain classifier on partner length, net charge, composition and presence of designed linkers, and return 'out of calibration domain' for inputs outside it. The 26 unique candidates, being GGGGS-linked polycationic chimeras, are expected to fall outside; publishing that refusal is the honest result. (9) Report the local pipeline's success rate next to the Boltz-2 paper's published figures with the gap attributed to MSA mode, MPS backend and peptide-length regime.
final_success_criteria: Every benchmark entry has initial_release_date > 2024-01-01, verifiable per-entry against the RCSB record, and the artefact states the Boltz-2 training cutoff (2023-06-01) and checkpoint-selection window (to 2024-01-01, n=398) with the paper DOI as the source of both.

Every entry carries a `max_identity_to_pre_cutoff` field derived from clusters-by-entity-40.txt, and all headline metrics appear in three strata (<30% / 30-70% / >70%) with per-stratum n. Objective check: no pooled metric is reported anywhere without its stratified breakdown alongside.
A precision calculation is recorded BEFORE the batch runs, stating the target Wilson half-width and the N it implies; the executed N meets it, and every reliability plot prints per-bin n.
Metrics are reported separately for 5-15 and 16-40 residue partners, with peptide-backbone RMSD (<=2 A) primary for the short stratum.

The sensitivity panel reports a single number -- the fraction of >=10 genuine solved binders whose native beats its own scramble distribution -- and that number is printed as the denominator on every AIML-STRUCT-1 verdict. If it is at or near chance, AIML-STRUCT-1's candidate arm is cancelled rather than run, and that cancellation is published.

calibrated_interface_probability returns 'out of calibration domain' for all 26 unique candidates unless a matched-domain calibration set exists; a unit test asserts the refusal fires for a GGGGS-linked polycationic input.
A count of entries discarded at each curation filter is published, so the denominator of the benchmark is auditable.

revised.title: Receptor-complex prediction of the candidate set, gated on demonstrated assay power and scored as an effect size against seed-matched nulls
revised.changed_what: Made strictly conditional on AIML-STRUCT-2's sensitivity panel, without which every result is uninterpretable. Deduplicated 35 records to 26 unique sequences and descoped the primary set to 10. Replaced the family-wise p-value with a standardized effect size and bootstrap CI, and now state plainly that the design is powered to report a negative and is NOT powered to license a positive claim. Seeds matched across arms. Added a moment-preserving second null and a compartment gate. Split the PAE fix out as a standalone prerequisite patch with a principled, measured rule. Compute estimate roughly doubled. Absorbs AIML-BENCH-3 and STRUCTBIO-IDEA-3 rather than duplicating them.
conceded: No positive control. This is fatal as specified and four reviewers landed on it independently. My own pilot number is the evidence against me: min interface PAE 16.84 A native vs 16.45 A scramble, against 0.56 A on a genuine complex, is far better explained by 'this pipeline places no interface at all for a 36-mer on a 543-residue receptor in single-sequence mode' than by 'this design is not sequence-specific'. As designed the experiment cannot separate design failure from method impotence, and I presented it as decisive.

The pilot was not decisive on its own terms either. With 3 natives and 3 decoys the statistic's minimum attainable value is 0.25, so 'empirical p = 1.0' is a power failure dressed as a result. I overstated it.

Variance mismatch. A native median over 5 seeds against single-seed decoys compares a mean with single realisations; the arms are not exchangeable and the permutation logic requires exchangeability. With sd ~0.133 most of the decoy spread is sampler noise, and the 0.735 outlier is exactly what one noise draw looks like.

P-value arithmetic. K=20 gives a floor of 1/21 = 0.048; after Holm across even 10 candidates the smallest reachable adjusted p is ~0.48. No candidate could ever be declared sequence-specific, for reasons independent of the biology. And 'at least one candidate with p > 0.05' is satisfied by estimator resolution rather than by any property of the candidates -- a criterion that cannot fail is not a criterion.

The scramble is not matched in the property that governs this molecule class. MW, charge, pI and GRAVY are order-invariant and preserved, but hydrophobic moment and helical amphipathic periodicity are order-dependent and destroyed by a Fisher-Yates shuffle. So the test as built asks 'does amphipathic helicity matter', not 'is this design sequence-specific'. For an ideally amphipathic Arg/Trp peptide that confound points the wrong way.

35 is not 35. Verified: data/dataset.json holds 35 records but only 26 unique sequences; KWWKFLRRFWRRLKKYFEELWKKLAEKYFELLKKYG appears three times, SEAEFRLFRDVWANY... three times, and five further sequences twice. Reporting them as independent tests triple-counts the exact molecule the pilot ran on.
Compute was out by ~2x. 910 runs at my own measured 168.8 s is 42.7 h, not 'roughly 24 h', and the larger receptors scale worse than linearly.

The PAE sampling window is broken in a way I did not notice. predictor.py:392-398 scans only the top-left min(n,60) x min(n,60) block, so for a 543-residue receptor followed by a 36-mer the check never looks at the interface at all. The threshold was not the only broken part.

Re-deriving the asymmetry threshold from 'real two-chain output' alone would tune the fraud detector on the data it polices. Correct objection; the fix below is derived from a saturation property and scored as a classifier instead.

Scalar ipTM is ambiguous for a two-protein complex. Verified: pair_chains_iptm is asymmetric, [0][1]=0.4396 while [1][0]=0.7136, and the scalar 'iptm' equals the LARGER entry. Reporting it unqualified makes the headline an undocumented max-statistic.
Surfacing a p-value for a pair whose target compartment is unreachable would be a number without knowledge, exactly what the rebuild exists to prevent.
defended: The empirical-null instinct is right and I do not retreat from it. A raw ipTM has no reference distribution, and an isolated 0.735 from a random shuffle would have read as a hit. The fix is a competent assay and a better statistic, not abandoning the null.

Single-sequence mode biases native and decoy identically, so a WITHIN-pipeline contrast survives it even though absolute ipTM does not. What it does not survive is a pipeline with no power at all -- which is why the sensitivity panel, not a configuration change, is the actual remedy.

The PAE-asymmetry threshold can be fixed on a principled basis rather than a tuned one, and I now have the measurement. On the genuine 601x601 two-chain matrix, max asymmetry is 20.30 A over the full matrix and 17.54 A over the sampled 60x60 window, but only 8.02 A where BOTH entries are below 10 A, with median asymmetry 0.710. PAE saturates near 30 A and asymmetry in the saturated region is uninformative; gating the check on both entries being in the confident regime is derived from that property, not fitted to make real complexes pass. It still gets scored as a classifier against regenerated legacy trigonometric matrices.

One candidate is an internal near-positive control that costs nothing. The Keap1-directed sequence DEETGEFLFQLPQLDEETGEWRWYCPWC embeds DEETGEFL, the exact C-terminal degron of the native Neh2 16-mer AFFAQLQLDEETGEFL in 2FLU. If the pipeline has power on Keap1, this is the one candidate where a positive result is expected. Its compartment problem is a delivery objection, not a binding objection, so it should be compartment-flagged and still run as a probe.

The cross-declaration controls already in the data are free and I keep them: one 40-mer declared against both alpha7 nAChR and TLR4/MD-2, and one 36-mer declared against AChE under three different names. These test declared specificity with zero new design.
revised.final_method: GATED: does not run unless AIML-STRUCT-2's sensitivity panel shows the pipeline recovers genuine binders above chance. If it does not, the published output is 'pipeline not demonstrated competent on this receptor class' and the candidate arm is cancelled. (0) PREREQUISITE PATCH, split out and landed first: fix predictor.py:392-398 to sample the explicit inter-chain block rather than the top-left 60x60 corner, and make the rule scale-relative -- flag only when |PAE_ij - PAE_ji| is large relative to 0.5*(PAE_ij+PAE_ji) AND both entries are below ~10 A. Score the new rule as a classifier on genuine two-chain Boltz-2 output AND on regenerated legacy trigonometric matrices, and publish its TPR/FPR rather than a bare cutoff. Separately, parse and record the FULL pair_chains_iptm matrix with an explicit statement of which orientation the headline ipTM reports, plus complex_iplddt and complex_ipde. (1) Deduplicate to 26 unique sequences, mapping candidate codes onto sequences in every output row; descope the primary set to 10. (2) Compartment gate BEFORE any compute: a UniProt subcellular-location check marks extracellular-peptide-versus-cytoplasmic-target pairs compartment-excluded; no effect size or p-value is ever rendered for an excluded pair, though it may still be run as a labelled probe. (3) Seed-matched paired design: native at 3 seeds, each of 8 scrambles at the SAME 3 seeds, each of 3 off-target receptors at the same 3 seeds. 10 candidates x 12 sequences x 3 seeds = 360 runs, ~18-20 h at the measured rate, with the large receptors timed before committing. Analyse per-sequence means with sequence as the unit and seed as the within-unit replicate -- a mixed model with random intercepts per sequence, or a permutation test on candidate identity respecting the nesting -- never a native median against single decoy draws. Report between-sequence and within-sequence sd separately. (4) THREE nulls, each answering a named question, reported separately: (a) Fisher-Yates composition shuffle = does residue ORDER carry information; (b) class-preserving permutation within hydrophobic and within polar residues, preserving heptad periodicity and hydrophobic moment, built with the existing modlAMP machinery = is this design more than 'any amphipathic helix of this composition'; (c) off-target receptor panel, PROMOTED to the primary specificity statistic, size-matched to the cognate receptor within +/-20% residues and including at least one near-neighbour alongside the unrelated ones, with the two off-target classes reported separately. Record Eisenberg hydrophobic moment (18-residue window) as a covariate on every scramble and report ipTM-versus-moment so any positive result can be checked for the amphipathicity confound. (5) PRIMARY READOUT is a standardized effect size -- native mean minus decoy mean over decoy sd -- with a bootstrap 95% CI, per candidate, with the full null distribution published. The family-wise p-value is DROPPED as unreachable at feasible K. Stated in advance: this design is powered to report 'the design lies inside its decoy distribution' and is NOT powered to license a positive sequence-specificity claim; any candidate whose native exceeds all decoys is flagged 'requires a dedicated K>=200 follow-up, not run here' rather than declared specific. (6) Every candidate verdict is printed next to the sensitivity panel's power fraction and next to a same-batch positive control's ipTM and min interface PAE, so a reader can tell a statement about the molecule from a statement about the pipeline. (7) Receptor domains resolved to UniProt accession and residue range from the existing 16 target_records; at least one target run both as domain and full-length to size that modelling choice. All values emitted at status PREDICTED with software 'boltz-2 2.2.1', seed list, selection rule and sampling_sd from AIML-STRUCT-3.
final_success_criteria: The verdict rule is written to a timestamped file BEFORE execution, and every candidate row carries a verdict produced by that frozen rule. A fixture containing a known-binding pair flips the verdict, demonstrating the rule can fire in both directions.

A table of 26 unique sequences (not 35 records) with code-to-sequence mapping, giving for each: native mean +/- sd over 3 matched seeds, each of the three null distributions separately, a standardized effect size with bootstrap 95% CI, and min interface PAE. No family-wise p-value is presented as a primary result.
Every row prints the sensitivity panel's power fraction and a same-batch positive control's scores, so no candidate verdict appears without its denominator.
Compartment-excluded pairs appear in the output with no effect size rendered; a test asserts that rendering one for an excluded pair fails validation.

The PAE-asymmetry check samples the inter-chain block rather than the top-left 60x60 corner, does not fire on the genuine 601x601 two-chain matrix (where full-matrix asymmetry is 20.30 A but confident-region asymmetry is 8.02 A), still fires on regenerated legacy trigonometric matrices, and its TPR/FPR are published.
predictor.py records the full pair_chains_iptm matrix and states which orientation the headline ipTM reports; a test asserts both off-diagonal entries are stored, not just the larger.
Reported wall-clock compute is within a factor of 1.5 of a pre-declared estimate built from a timed large-receptor case, not extrapolated from the smallest one.

Because git ls-files over platform/ and data/ currently returns zero, 'committed' is unsatisfiable today: this proposal is sequenced after the repository is placed under version control, and until then every artefact is published with a content hash.

refined.expert: PhD in ML evaluation and benchmarking, 16 years; publishes on data leakage, split design and reproducibility failures in scientific ML

revised.title: Within-assay affinity benchmark for Boltz-2, with an exact reconstruction of its own ChEMBL training predicate, an interval-valued noise ceiling, and a pose-conditioned error decomposition
revised.changed_what: Four structural changes, three of them larger than any reviewer asked for. (1) THE PRIMARY METRIC CHANGED. I read the Boltz-2 PDF directly this session (jeremywohlwend.com/assets/boltz2.pdf, 55pp, text extracted locally) and found the sentence that invalidates my own headline: the affinity regression head is supervised on assays curated so that models learn 'intra-assay differences in values rather than inter-assay', with hit-to-lead assays required to have >=10 points, average pairwise Tanimoto >=0.25, and non-trivial activity standard deviation. Absolute cross-assay RMSE against a pooled corpus is therefore not the task the head was trained to do. Primary metric is now within-assay Spearman after removing the per-assay median; pooled RMSE survives only as a secondary metric explicitly labelled 'off-task'. This retires my own 2.41-log Huperzine A anchor as motivation — the medchem and structbio critics were right to distrust it, for a reason none of them stated. (2) THE TEMPORAL SPLIT IS DELETED, not demoted. Four reviewers asked me to relabel it a 'publication-year proxy'. The paper shows there is nothing to proxy: the only training cutoff in Boltz-2 is 2023-06-01 and it applies to PDB structures; the affinity corpus from PubChem/ChEMBL/BindingDB carries no stated date boundary. A split that implements nothing must not be reported at all, because a labelled-but-meaningless number still invites comparison. (3) THE LEAKAGE PREDICATE IS NOW EXACT, NOT GUESSED. Verbatim from the paper's Appendix A.2.1: confidence score equal 9; target type restricted to SINGLE PROTEIN; biochemical or functional assays; standard_type in {Ki,Kd,IC50,XC50,EC50,AC50}; unreliable sources excluded; plus a global PAINS filter and discard of ligands with >50 heavy atoms; plus a structural-quality filter dropping assays whose mean ipTM over 10 random binders is <0.75. Sources for the regression head are PubChem, ChEMBL and BindingDB — I correct my own E2 (which said PDBbind and MF-PCBA) and also correct the ML-for-structural-biology reviewer, who repeated the same wrong list; MF-PCBA is a benchmark Boltz-2 is evaluated on, not a regression training source. (4) THE NOISE CEILING IS RE-ESTIMATED AND WIDENED. Recomputed on data/corpus_ACHE.json this session: only 4 of 18 compounds carry replicates (tacrine 5 values, physostigmine 4, neostigmine 2, donepezil 2), so my '18 replicate pairs' were 18 pairs from 4 compounds, with tacrine alone supplying 10. Proper pooled within-compound sd = 0.4206 log10 on df=9, chi-square 95% CI [0.289, 0.768]. Kalliokoski's 0.68 sits inside that interval, so my implicit claim that this corpus is quieter than the public literature is unsupported and withdrawn. Additionally: population fixed by measured pharmacology not ChEMBL's NP flag, and the whole thing merged with CBC-CC-1 and frozen under META-3.
conceded: sigma_exp was over-precise and its effective n was 4 compounds, not 18 pairs. Verified by direct recomputation: pooled within-compound sd 0.4206 log10, df=9, 95% CI [0.289, 0.768]. My 0.376 is withdrawn; the computational chemist's point that the estimator must be written out is accepted (for two independent draws of sd sigma, mean|delta| = 2*sigma/sqrt(pi), so my 0.448 mean |delta| implies 0.397, not 0.376 — and both are superseded by the pooled-variance estimate). The band will be drawn as an interval, never a line, and reported as statistically indistinguishable from the literature value.

The corpus confidence filter is inert and this is a blocking prerequisite, not a side task. Verified: all 27 activities in data/corpus_ACHE.json have assay_confidence null, so `if conf is not None and conf < protocol.min_assay_confidence` at corpus.py never fires, and the emitted protocol_summary string 'assay confidence >= 8' is a claim the code did not enforce. Boltz-2's own predicate needs confidence exactly 9, so the /assay join is required twice over.

The denominator is a truncation cap. 'activities_examined: 300 / 258 molecules' is the limit=1000/page=200 cap, and target_activity_count() at corpus.py:182 is defined and never called. Aggregating sigma_exp over an arbitrarily ordered slice biases it in an unknown direction.

The benchmark population was set by ChEMBL's noisy natural_product flag, and the null floor is partly manufactured by it. Measured: dropping pralidoxime (an oxime reactivator), metoclopramide and ranitidine takes the predict-the-mean RMSE from 1.664 to 1.383 log10 on n=14. The reviewer is directionally right. I record the partial disagreement in 'defended' below.
The temporal split is conceptually void, and I go further than the four reviewers who asked me to relabel it: it is deleted.

'Error below sigma_exp implies overtraining' is only valid if the model predicts the quantity the replicates measure. If ground truth is a k-measurement aggregate the floor is sigma_exp/sqrt(k). The overtraining test as written would have fired spuriously on a legitimately good model.

Ki/Kd/IC50 must not be pooled into one label column. Verified this corpus is 25 IC50 and 2 Ki. Primary analysis restricted to catalytic Ellman IC50; Ki/Kd reported as a labelled secondary set with its own ceiling.

ECFP4 Tanimoto is stereo-blind and this corpus contains the live counterexample the medchem reviewer named: (-)-physostigmine at 27.9 nM and (+)-physostigmine at 9890 nM, ~2.5 log apart, would score Tanimoto 1.0 stereo-blind. Stereo-aware and stereo-blind similarity recorded separately.
n=17 cannot support a Murcko scaffold split; folds of 3-5 are not an estimator. Minimum-n gate goes in code.

Every affinity case must carry the pose record (pocket-aligned ligand RMSD where a holo reference exists, ligand_iptm, complex_plddt) so error decomposes into wrong-pose versus right-pose-wrong-energy. This makes BENCH-1 and BENCH-2 one pipeline rather than two.

The receptor construct is a hidden variable and must be declared: P22303 residues 32-574 (mature chain), monomeric, aglycosyl, no PAS occupant, against reference IC50s measured on native dimeric glycosylated enzyme.
Three teams proposing the same AChE affinity benchmark is a week of wasted MPS time. Merge with CBC-CC-1, freeze under META-3.

A live-query leakage audit is not reproducible, and today it is not even runnable: the ChEMBL REST API returned HTTP 500 to me again this session on both /assay and /activity. Verified alternative: ftp.ebi.ac.uk serves chembl_34_sqlite.tar.gz (4.86 GB) and chembl_37_sqlite.tar.gz (5.76 GB); 6.9 TB free on this disk.
defended: The three junk compounds inflate the null but do not manufacture it. The medchem reviewer said pralidoxime, metoclopramide and ranitidine 'create most of the variance'. Measured: removing all three moves the null RMSE from 1.664 to 1.383 log10, a 17% reduction, because the surviving 14 compounds still span 5.6 log units (huprine X 0.026 nM to velnacrine ~10 uM). The null is not artificially easy; it is genuinely hard because a cholinesterase corpus spans six orders of magnitude. Both numbers get published side by side as the reviewer asked, but the claim that the inclusion rule manufactured the difficulty is quantitatively overstated.

The Kramer 0.54 pKi figure was cited for the principle (models below experimental error are overtrained), not as the numeric ceiling for IC50 data. I already cited Kalliokoski separately as E4 for exactly the IC50 case. The reviewer's remedy — key sigma_exp to standard_type — is right and adopted, but the accusation that I used a Ki ceiling to judge IC50 predictions misreads the original text.

Boltz-2's affinity output convention is confirmed, not assumed, and my risk item can be closed. Verbatim from the paper: values are 'standardized to log 10 scale derived from values measured in uM' and the head is supervised on Ki/Kd/IC50 'all converted to the logarithmic scale using uM as standardized unit'. So affinity_pred_value 0.10516 is 10^0.105 = 1.27 uM, and the 2.41-log error against a measured 5.0 nM is arithmetically right even though it is the wrong metric to headline.

'Underpowered' and 'not better than the null' are different verdicts and I already required the distinction — but the reviewers are right that my pre-declared string collapsed them. Fixed by emitting three mutually exclusive verdicts, not two.
revised.final_method: Merged protocol, frozen and hash-locked under META-3 before any compute. STEP 0 (blocking, no inference). Fix corpus.py: call target_activity_count() and record the true denominator; page to exhaustion or declare the cap and its ordering as a stated sampling frame; join /assay to recover confidence_score, assay_type, assay_organism, substrate and BAO format, since the field does not exist on /activity. Pin retrieval to a local ChEMBL SQLite release from ftp.ebi.ac.uk (chembl_34, 4.86 GB, and chembl_37, 5.76 GB) with release id, file SHA256 and retrieval timestamp committed; the live REST API is 500ing today and is no longer a build-time dependency. STEP 1: LEAKAGE PREDICATE, EXACT. Reimplement Boltz-2's own ChEMBL extraction against the pinned release — confidence_score = 9, target_type = SINGLE PROTEIN, assay_type in (B,F), standard_type in {Ki,Kd,IC50,XC50,EC50,AC50}, unreliable sources excluded, RDKit PAINS catalogue filter, heavy atoms <= 50 — and label every test compound in_boltz_chembl_predicate as true/false/UNKNOWN. Record in_bindingdb and in_pubchem as UNKNOWN unless separately checked; never as false. This buys two genuinely out-of-training strata at zero inference cost, both verified present in this repo: heavy-atom-capped natural products (ginsenoside Rg1 56, salvianolic acid B 52, onjisaponin V 123 heavy atoms, all measured with RDKit this session) and PAINS-flagged compounds (candidates for this stratum include curcumin and baicalein; membership to be established by running the catalogue, not asserted). Also record stereo-aware and stereo-blind max ECFP4 Tanimoto to the predicate set, and note that Boltz-2 also used compound-similarity structure in curation (assays with mean pairwise Tanimoto <0.25 were discarded), so proximity to a training analogue in the same assay matters as much as compound identity. STEP 2: POPULATION. Admit by measured pharmacology against the named target from an Ellman-type catalytic assay on human recombinant enzyme, not by ChEMBL's natural_product flag (which the repo already documents as labelling donepezil and metoclopramide natural products). Report n before and after, and publish the null RMSE on both populations (1.664 -> 1.383 measured today). NP tier is retained as an annotation, never as an inclusion rule. STEP 3: GROUND TRUTH AND CEILING. Landrum-Riniker maximal curation: group by full InChIKey + target + matched assay metadata, aggregate to one pAct per compound-assay. Emit TWO ceilings with their estimators written out: sigma_single for predicting one randomly drawn literature value, and sigma_single/sqrt(k) for predicting a k-replicate aggregate, stating which one each headline metric is scored against. Report the ceiling as median |delta|, a MAD-based robust scale and a compound-resampled bootstrap CI, alongside the pooled-variance point estimate (0.4206, df=9, CI [0.289,0.768], n_compounds=4 today). Carbamates (physostigmine, neostigmine) are reported as a separate time-dependent-inhibition subset, not folded into the noise floor. STEP 4: SPLITS. Random 5-fold (shown only to expose the optimism gap) and Murcko scaffold split, both gated on n. No temporal split. STEP 5: METRICS. Primary: within-assay Spearman rho after per-assay median centring, with a cluster bootstrap resampled over assays. Secondary, labelled off-task: pooled RMSE and MAE against the per-target median null and against 1-NN / similarity-weighted k-NN over the predicate set (the memorisation baseline) and a two-descriptor ridge. All headline figures reported within leakage strata (<0.4 / 0.4-0.7 / >0.7 Tanimoto; in-predicate / out-of-predicate / unknown), never pooled. STEP 6: POSE CONDITIONING. Every affinity case carries ligand_iptm, complex_plddt and, where a holo reference exists, the pocket-aligned symmetry-corrected RMSD from BENCH-2, so affinity error is decomposed by pose quality. STEP 7: SYSTEM UNDER TEST. Boltz-2 v2.2.1 on MPS, both msa=empty and receptor-MSA arms, RDKit preflight gate (>128 heavy atoms hard reject, 56-128 flagged) from CBC-CC-1, top-1 versus top-5 diffusion-sample rule fixed in the protocol before the batch. Budget honestly: two overnight batches, not one, since the MSA arm doubles the run count and is slower per run. STEP 8: POWER AND GATES, IN CODE. Before any compute, compute and publish the minimum detectable within-assay Spearman delta at the planned n given sigma_exp in [0.29,0.77]. No headline metric renders below 50 compounds per target and 20 scaffolds; below that the module emits only the per-compound table and the literal string 'not evaluable at n=N'.
final_success_criteria: data/benchmark_affinity.json contains, for every case, all of: pAct, n_replicates, assay_chembl_id, assay confidence_score (an integer, never null — the build fails if any is null), standard_type, in_boltz_chembl_predicate in {true,false,unknown}, max_tanimoto_stereo_aware, max_tanimoto_stereo_blind, heavy_atoms, pains_flag, and the pose record (ligand_iptm, complex_plddt, pocket_aligned_rmsd or null).
The pinned ChEMBL release id, file SHA256 and retrieval timestamp are committed, and re-running the leakage audit offline with no network reproduces every in_boltz_chembl_predicate label bit-for-bit.
A test asserts the corpus denominator equals target_activity_count() or that a stated sampling frame with its ordering is recorded; the current 'activities_examined: 300' with no frame fails it.

sigma_exp is emitted as {point, ci_low, ci_high, df, n_compounds, n_pairs, estimator_source_code_ref} for each of the two prediction targets, and any plot drawing it as a line rather than a band fails the build.

The headline is one of exactly three mutually exclusive strings: 'within-assay Spearman X.XX (95% CI a-b, n_assays=A, n_compounds=N, stratum=S)', 'not distinguishable from the per-target-median null at n=N (paired-delta CI a-b spans zero)', or 'not evaluable at n=N (below pre-declared minimum of 50 compounds / 20 scaffolds)'. No bare RMSE is renderable anywhere, and the off-task label is attached to every pooled RMSE that is emitted.
The word 'temporal' does not appear as a split name anywhere in the emitted benchmark, and a test asserts no split keyed on document.year exists.
Both null floors (1.664 on the NP-flag population, 1.383 on the pharmacology-defined population, both measured this session) appear in the output with the population definition that produced each.
The output declares the receptor construct verbatim: accession, residue range, oligomeric state modelled, glycosylation state, and the sentence that reference measurements were made on native enzyme.
The pre-registered minimum detectable effect is written into the protocol file before the first inference run and its hash matches the one in the results file.

revised.title: Pocket-aligned pose accuracy, physical validity and pharmacophore-contact reproduction, on three explicitly-labelled sets: recall, congeneric extension, and receptor-disjoint
revised.changed_what: Three changes. (1) SUPERPOSITION: global Kabsch over all matched CA is replaced by pocket-aligned, symmetry-corrected RMSD (align on reference receptor residues with any heavy atom within 10 A of the reference ligand), with global-aligned RMSD and receptor pocket CA RMSD reported as separate columns. Unanimous among the reviewers who commented and correct: for a 543-residue alpha/beta-hydrolase with a 20 A gorge, global fit residual reads out as apparent ligand displacement. (2) THE 'TEMPORAL HOLDOUT' IS RENAMED AND SPLIT IN THREE, because it is not a receptor holdout and I can now say exactly why. Boltz-2's own validation criteria, read from the PDF this session, are: initial release date after 2023-06-01 and on or before 2024-01-01; resolution <4.5 A; ALL protein chains absent from any training cluster at mmseqs --min-seq-id 0.4; and either no small molecule or at least one small molecule with Tanimoto <=0.85 to any training small molecule; yielding 398 structures. Every one of my ten cognition accessions fails their clause 3 by construction — hAChE, BuChE, MAO-A/B, BACE1/2 and TTR all have dense pre-2023 holo coverage. So the 81 entries are a post-cutoff CONGENERIC EXTENSION set, not a holdout, and I now add a genuinely receptor-disjoint arm drawn from the general post-2024 PDB using Boltz-2's own criteria. (3) The AUROC on/off switch is replaced by interval reporting with a minimum-n gate, and all intervals become receptor-level cluster bootstraps.
conceded: Global superposition is wrong for this system. Conceded entirely; pocket-aligned symmetry-corrected RMSD becomes primary.
The 81-entry set is not a holdout. Conceded, and I now have the exact criterion Boltz-2 itself used, which is stronger than any reviewer's version.

The recall set is three ligands in one receptor. Verified: 4EY5, 4EY6 and 4EY7 are the same recombinant hAChE construct from the same group, all released 2012-10-17. A Wilson interval over them as independent trials is wrong; they will be reported as n_ligands=3, n_receptors=1, with no interval.
Effective n is receptor-level throughout. All intervals become cluster bootstraps resampling receptors, and n_complexes and n_independent_receptors are reported side by side.

The AUROC decision rule was an asymmetric-cost decision made without a power calculation: at n~80 with class imbalance, a genuinely useful AUROC of 0.65 routinely yields a CI containing 0.5, so 'stop displaying the score' would discard information with high probability. Replaced by mandatory CI reporting plus the phrase 'no discrimination demonstrated at n=N (CI a-b)', which is not the same as 'demonstrated absent'.

RMSD <=2 A is a weak discriminator inside a 20 A gorge and hides right-pocket-wrong-orientation. The medchem reviewer's pharmacophore-contact metric is the best single addition anyone proposed and is adopted as a co-primary: contacted-residue-set Jaccard at a stated heavy-atom cutoff, plus a named pass/fail on Trp86 stacking and the Tyr337/Tyr124 hydrogen bonds. Their measured 4EY5 contacts (HUP N2 to Tyr337-OH 3.01 A, to Trp86 CG 3.49 A) become the regression assertion, and Tyr337 and Tyr124 are added to my original Trp86/Ser203/His447 test.
Never pool P22303 with P04058. Torpedo and human AChE have different gorge residues and different numbering; all proportions stratify by receptor UniProt.

PoseBusters intermolecular checks run against the co-folded receptor, which has relaxed around its own ligand, so co-folding models clear steric validity more easily than rigid-receptor docking. My comparison to the PoseBusters headline is not apples to apples and the output file will say so.
Reference poses are not automatically ground truth. Filter references on wwPDB ligand-level real-space fit (RSRZ/RSCC and ligand geometry outliers), not only on entry resolution.
Chain and ligand-instance selection must be recorded, not inferred: 4EY5 carries HUP in both chains A and B. Altloc, partial occupancy and crystallographic symmetry mates handled explicitly.
Running the holdout only at msa=empty confounds pose error with receptor-fold degradation on deep-MSA targets. Both arms run.
The all-atom mmCIF parser is built once, jointly with STRUCTBIO-IDEA-1, not twice.
defended: The 2023-06-01..2024-01-01 window is NOT contaminated by Boltz-2 model selection for these targets, and the ML-evaluation reviewer's stated mechanism is wrong. Their validation set required all protein chains to belong to clusters unseen before 2023-06-01 at 0.4 identity; every cognition accession has pre-cutoff training entries, so those chains were excluded from Boltz-2's validation set by the same clause that excludes them from being a real holdout. Their conclusion (this is not a holdout) survives via the training-cluster route, which is stronger. I adopt the tiering anyway because it is nearly free: verified by RCSB Search API today, the cognition set has 81 entries after 2023-06-01 and 63 after 2024-01-01, so dropping the window costs 18 entries.

The predictor.py ligand-blindness is a defect, not a feature request, and it is confirmed: the parse loop skips every row whose label_atom_id is not 'CA', so all 18 HETATM atoms of the huperzine model are discarded before any downstream check runs. This part of the proposal needs no defence but is worth restating because two other proposals depend on the same fix.

Dependency feasibility is now measured, not argued: posebusters 0.6.5 and spyrmsd 0.9.0 (plus rustworkx) installed into the repo venv this session with no compiler, no Boost and no GPU. The AutoDock Vina arm64 failure does not recur.
revised.final_method: Build the all-atom mmCIF parser once (shared with STRUCTBIO-IDEA-1): retain HETATM and non-polymer entities as a Prediction.ligands list with element, altloc and occupancy, add interface_contacts(). New platform/cbc/bench/pose.py. For each case: fetch the reference entry, record the chosen chain and ligand instance explicitly, resolve altlocs by highest occupancy and record the choice, generate symmetry mates and score against the nearest copy; define the pocket as reference receptor residues with any heavy atom within 10 A of the reference ligand; superpose on those residues only; compute symmetry-corrected ligand RMSD with spyrmsd in that local frame, and also report global-aligned ligand RMSD, receptor pocket CA RMSD, predicted-to-reference ligand centroid distance, and Jaccard overlap of the contacted-residue sets at 4.0 A. Run PoseBusters in redock mode, recording every check individually, with a stated caveat that intermolecular checks are evaluated against the co-folded receptor. THREE SETS, NEVER POOLED, EACH WITH A SENTENCE STATING WHICH CONCLUSIONS IT CAN AND CANNOT SUPPORT. (A) RECALL, pre-2023-06-01: 4EY5/4EY6/4EY7 reported as n_ligands=3, n_receptors=1, no interval — a poor result here is informative, a good one is not. (B) CONGENERIC EXTENSION, cognition accessions, two tiers: 2023-06-01..2024-01-01 labelled 'inside Boltz-2's validation window by date, though excluded from their validation set by their new-cluster clause', and >2024-01-01 (63 entries verified today). Every case carries max ECFP4 Tanimoto (stereo-aware and stereo-blind) from the deposited ligand to every ligand co-crystallised pre-cutoff with the SAME UniProt, and both headline proportions stratify at <0.4 / 0.4-0.7 / >0.7. (C) RECEPTOR-DISJOINT, drawn from the 19,260 general post-2024-01-01 holo entries at <=2.5 A verified today, filtered by Boltz-2's own held-out definition: no protein chain in a pre-2023-06-01 mmseqs 0.4 cluster, and ligand Tanimoto <=0.85 to any pre-cutoff ligand. The gap between (B) and (C) is the interpolation premium and is the most interesting number the study can produce. Reference-quality filter on all sets: exclude entries whose ligand is flagged by wwPDB real-space fit. Confidence calibration: record ipTM, ligand_iptm, protein_iptm, complex_plddt, complex_iplddt, complex_ipde against measured RMSD; emit a reliability curve and AUROC with a receptor-level cluster bootstrap CI. Top-1 versus top-5 diffusion-sample rule fixed and recorded before the batch. Both msa=empty and receptor-MSA arms. Budget: two overnight batches, not one.
final_success_criteria: data/benchmark_pose.json carries, per case: pocket_aligned_symcorr_rmsd, global_aligned_rmsd, receptor_pocket_ca_rmsd, ligand_centroid_distance, contact_jaccard_4A, named_pharmacophore_pass, the full per-check PoseBusters table, all six confidence scores, PDB id, chain id, ligand instance id, altloc choice, initial_release_date, wwPDB ligand RSRZ/RSCC, receptor UniProt, and stereo-aware and stereo-blind max Tanimoto to pre-cutoff ligands of the same target.

Headline proportions %(RMSD<=2 A) and %(RMSD<=2 A AND PB-valid) are reported for each of the three sets separately, stratified by receptor UniProt and by Tanimoto bin, with receptor-level cluster-bootstrap intervals and both n_complexes and n_independent_receptors printed; a test fails the build if any two sets are pooled or if P22303 and P04058 appear in one proportion.
The interpolation premium — the difference between set (B) and set (C) proportions, with its interval — is emitted as a named field.
The recall set carries n_receptors=1 and no confidence interval, and a test asserts no interval is computed over it.

AUROC for every confidence score is emitted only with its CI and n; if the CI includes 0.5 the emitted text is 'no discrimination demonstrated at n=N (CI a-b)' and the score keeps rendering with that caveat attached. A minimum n is declared before the batch and no threshold value is ever quoted below it.

A regression test asserts the existing huperzine model parses to 18 ligand atoms whose nearest protein residues include Trp86, Tyr124, Tyr337, Ser203 and His447, and that the named-pharmacophore check passes on it.

The output file states verbatim that PoseBusters intermolecular checks were evaluated against the co-folded receptor rather than a rigid experimental one, and that the comparison to rigid-receptor docking literature is therefore not like-for-like.
The 4EY5-versus-existing-model data point is produced with zero new inference, as the first result.

revised.title: Composition-matched scramble control for the 35 designed candidates — WITHDRAWN as a standalone study
revised.changed_what: Withdrawn. Eight reviewers independently found the same arithmetic defect and they are right: with K=20 controls the smallest attainable empirical permutation p is (1+0)/(1+20) = 0.0476, and Holm-Bonferroni across ten candidates requires the smallest p to be <= 0.005, so the floor on the smallest adjusted p is 0.476. The verdict string 'sequence-specific (Holm-corrected p < 0.05)' is unreachable no matter what the folding shows. At the K=10 pilot the uncorrected minimum p is 0.091, which cannot reach 0.05 either. This is exactly the failure mode this project exists to remediate — a check whose outcome is fixed by its construction rather than by the data — merely inverted from a check that cannot fail into one that cannot fire. Reaching K>=199 for ten candidates is ~2000 co-folds, roughly 100 h of MPS, which is not affordable on this laptop. Compounding it, this was the third independent implementation of the same composition-matched null in one review batch. Withdrawing is the correct outcome and I am not proposing a patched version, because the patched version is AIML-STRUCT-1.
conceded: The design cannot produce its own stated positive result. Conceded without reservation; the arithmetic is not a matter of judgement.

Item 6 proposed to spend folding compute demonstrating a mathematical identity. Conceded, and I did the correct version instead of proposing it: 300 seeded Fisher-Yates shuffles of the 36-mer KWWKFLRRFWRRLKKYFEELWKKLAEKYFELLKKYG through platform/cbc/peptide.py leave EVERY emitted field bit-identical — mol_weight 4942.97, net_charge_ph74 8.93, isoelectric_point 10.95, gravy -1.089, frac_aromatic 0.306, frac_cationic 0.361, n_cysteine 0, cys_pairing, length, and all four liability strings. Zero order-dependent fields survive. That is a unit test, not an experiment, and it ships this week independently of any folding.
Three overlapping scramble proposals on one laptop is the largest single waste in the panel. Merging rather than defending territory.

The candidate count is inflated and I confirmed it: 35 candidates are 26 unique sequences. The 36-mer above appears three times (HippoAChE-AlkaPept-X2, BasalAChE-GorgeBlock-B1, CogAChE-PAS-02); a 41-mer appears three times; five further pairs are duplicated. Holm across ten 'candidates' several of which are byte-identical over-corrects against the one thing the test is trying to detect. Only 10 of 35 carry an explicit target field at all.

A plain composition shuffle is not matched on hydrophobic moment, so a design that beats it may be winning on amphipathicity rather than motif identity — and for the 21 of 35 candidates with >=4 cysteines a shuffle relocates every cysteine and changes fold class, so design-versus-shuffle compares two different folds. Pooling both regimes into one p-value is not interpretable.
No positive control means a universal null cannot be attributed to the designs rather than to Boltz-2 msa=empty having no peptide-docking ability at all.

The 3 min 4 s timing was measured on a receptor plus an 18-heavy-atom ligand, not a 36-residue second protein chain with its own pair representation. The 11-14 h estimate is not supported and would need re-timing.

'Order-invariant' does not mean 'carries no design information'. The medchem reviewer is right and this was the one interpretive error in the proposal that would have done real damage: composition IS a design choice, and the composition-derived liability flags (polycationic, amphipathic, KLVFF-containing, odd-cysteine) are among the platform's best-evidenced outputs. Retiring them from the candidate cards would have removed honest signal to make room for a scramble-controlled ipTM whose informativeness is itself unestablished.
defended: The permutation-null idea is right; only my instantiation was broken. A composition-matched null is the standard remedy when no labels exist, and the underlying observation stands: not one of the 35 candidates has ever been co-folded with its receptor, which is why ipTM was 0.00 for all 22 — they were folded as lone chains and ipTM is undefined for a single chain. That gap should still be closed, in AIML-STRUCT-1.

The three-level control taxonomy is the part of this proposal the alternatives lack and it should survive the withdrawal: a full composition shuffle isolates all order information, a linker-preserving shuffle isolates motif-internal order, and a motif-block permutation isolates the arrangement hypothesis, which is the actual claim these GGGGS-linked concatenations make. Five reviewers said so independently.

One control I proposed nothing about is free and better than any scramble, and I verified it today: the same 41-mer is declared against alpha7 nAChR ECD (CognACh-Mod-06) and against TLR4/MD-2 (MicroTlr4-Antagonist-M3). One molecule asserted against two unrelated receptors is a direct test of declared target specificity requiring no shuffling at all. Credit to the DMPK reviewer; it should go into the merged module.
revised.final_method: No method. The study is withdrawn. Three deliverables are handed over rather than deleted. (1) SHIP IMMEDIATELY, ZERO COMPUTE: a unit test asserting f(seq) == f(shuffle(seq)) over 300 seeded permutations for every field of PeptideReport (run and passing this session), and a three-state tag on every candidate card — 'order-invariant by construction' (value kept, with a one-line note that a composition-matched shuffle reproduces it exactly), 'order-dependent (scramble-controlled)', or 'untested'. Liability flags keep their text; they are composition-determined and still the best-evidenced thing on the card. (2) SHIP IMMEDIATELY, ZERO COMPUTE: the deduplication finding — 35 candidate records are 26 unique sequences — published as a dataset correction, with all per-candidate reporting keyed to distinct sequences and the candidate codes that map to each. Nine of thirty-five 'candidates' are copies, and that is a result. (3) HAND TO AIML-STRUCT-1: the three-level control taxonomy; the cross-declaration specificity control (one 41-mer, two unrelated declared receptors); the requirement for a hydrophobic-moment-matched third null and for stratifying by candidate class (amphipathic-helix versus cystine-rich, with the explicit statement that for the cystine-rich group the shuffle changes fold class and the test is therefore the weaker 'better than a random fold of the same composition'); the per-receptor positive control drawn from solved peptide-receptor complexes; the requirement to re-time a two-protein-chain co-fold before sizing any batch; and the statistical replacement — a seed-matched standardised effect size with a compound-resampled bootstrap CI and a receptor-pooled null, reported with the full null distribution and no dichotomous per-candidate significance claim.
final_success_criteria: verify_all.py contains a test asserting every PeptideReport field is invariant under 300 seeded shuffles, and it passes. (Written and run this session; result: zero order-dependent fields.)

Every candidate card renders each score with one of exactly three tags: order-invariant by construction, order-dependent (scramble-controlled), or untested — and no score is labelled 'carries no design information'.
data/dataset.json reporting is keyed to 26 distinct sequences with the candidate codes mapping to each, and the duplicate count is stated in the README as a dataset correction.
The AIML-BENCH-3 module is absent from the repository and the three handover items appear in the AIML-STRUCT-1 protocol before any folding compute is committed.

No output anywhere in the platform emits a permutation p-value whose achievable minimum, given K and the multiplicity correction, exceeds the threshold it is compared against; a test computes that minimum from K and the correction and fails the build if the verdict string is unreachable.

refined.expert: PhD computational chemist, 19 years; expert in free-energy calculation, docking-score validation and implicit solvent

revised.title: A single merged, leakage-stratified potency benchmark for the Boltz-2 affinity head — emitting log10 potency only, never a binding free energy
revised.changed_what: Four structural changes. (1) The output is no longer a dG. The head emits predicted_potency_log10 in units log10(IC50/uM) and nothing else; the dG conversion is removed from the plan and from the ledger. (2) The decoy arm is rebuilt from the ground up because I found, by reading the Boltz-2 paper this session, that my original decoy design reproduces the model's own training-time negative-generation procedure almost exactly. (3) The benchmark population is defined by pharmacology and by ChEMBL assay confidence 9, not by ChEMBL's natural_product flag, which the repo already documents as noisy and which I confirmed admits pralidoxime, metoclopramide and ranitidine. (4) The applicability gate moves to 50 heavy atoms, the Boltz-2 training filter, verified verbatim in the primary source. This proposal is now explicitly the single merged affinity benchmark with AIML-BENCH-1 and MEDCHEM-IDEA-2 under META-3's prespec mechanism — one protocol, one aggregator, one leakage audit.
conceded: The sign and the label were wrong, and the critique that named it was right. The Boltz docs say verbatim 'You can convert the model's output to pIC50 in kcal/mol by using y --> (6 - y) * 1.364' — pIC50, a positive potency magnitude, not a signed standard-state free energy. At y = -3 (IC50 = 1 nM) the expression returns +12.28 while platform/cbc/thermo.py kd_to_dg(1e-9) returns -12.28. My ledger entry clm_a47c9774148de980 calls this 'dG' and calls it 'internally consistent with the platform's thermodynamics module'. It is sign-inverted relative to thermo.py, and had it been fed to thermo.check() the dG < -18.3 implausibility guard could never have fired. That ledger claim needs a correction record.

IC50 is not Kd and the head is trained on pooled Ki/Kd/IC50/EC50/AC50/XC50, so the output has no defined thermodynamic referent. Emitting it as binding_free_energy is a category error independent of the measured RMSE. Conceded without reservation; no dG is emitted anywhere by this work.

My decoy arm was worse than any critic realised, and I withdraw it in its proposed form on evidence I retrieved myself. The Boltz-2 paper states verbatim that the binary head's negatives were built 'by generating synthetic decoys created by shuffling binders identified in hit-to-lead screens across different targets, while mitigating low false negative rates by ensuring that each decoy has a Tanimoto similarity below 0.3 to all known binders associated with similar proteins' — 1.2M such decoys from ChEMBL and BindingDB (Table 1). Scoring each ligand against three unrelated registry receptors is that exact construction. The AUROC would have measured memorised training behaviour and I would have reported it as discrimination.

The heavy-atom gate was set at the wrong number. The Boltz-2 paper states verbatim that curation involved 'discarding ligands with more than 50 heavy atoms'. The docs' 56 counts heavy atoms plus hydrogens retained by RDKit RemoveHs, which is a different quantity; 50 heavy atoms is the empirical domain edge. Gate moves to 50, which now refuses Ginsenoside Rg1 (56) as well as Onjisaponin V (123).

The calibration population was broken and would have measured the flag, not the model. I enumerated data/corpus_ACHE.json: 18 admitted, all tiered NP_DERIVED, including DONEPEZIL, METOCLOPRAMIDE, PRALIDOXIME (an oxime reactivator, not an inhibitor) and RANITIDINE. Those near-inactives supply most of the corpus's dynamic range.

min_assay_confidence is inert and set to the wrong value. I confirmed every assay_confidence in data/corpus_ACHE.json is None, because confidence_score is an /assay field and platform/cbc/corpus.py:204 reads it off /activity, so the guard at line 206 never fires. Separately, the threshold should be 9, not 8: the Boltz-2 paper says verbatim 'Filter to confidence score equal 9 (maximum confidence)'. The /assay join must be built and verified before any corpus extension, and it is a schedule dependency I did not budget.
Leakage was unaddressed on the one benchmark where it dominates. Conceded in full, and I adopt AIML-BENCH-1's stratification verbatim.

>=60 pairs over >=4 targets gives n~15 per target, at which within-target Spearman CIs span most of [-1,1]. An underpowered null test silently converts into a permanent refusal on statistical rather than scientific grounds. Conceded.

Writing a repo-measured RMSE into thermo.METHOD_ACCURACY next to literature FEP (1.1) and MM-GBSA (2.5) invites a reader to compare a potency error against free-energy errors as commensurate method figures. Conceded; METHOD_ACCURACY is not touched.
'2-4 days wall clock' understated the coding and the /assay repair. Revised to 2-3 weeks with the compute unattended.
defended: I do not drop the binary-classifier arm, only the decoy construction. The docs say verbatim that affinity_probability_binary 'should be used to detect binders from decoys, for example in a hit-discovery stage'. The existing value of 0.44 for Huperzine A against AChE — a 5 nM binder — is uninterpretable without a reference distribution, and that remains the cheapest informative measurement available. The fix is the negative set, not the arm.

I reject the suggestion to replace unrelated-receptor decoys with property-matched decoys alone. Property-matched decoys with no measured activity are still assumed negatives, and natural products are promiscuous. Only ChEMBL records with a measured inactive call on that target are true negatives, and the honest fallback where none exist is to report a bound, not a number.

I defend dropping the natural-product restriction for the benchmark, against the reading that the NP theme should be preserved. The benchmark measures the predictor, not the corpus theme. NP tier is recorded as an annotation and stratified on; it is not an inclusion criterion.
I defend the preflight refusal gate and the write-back discipline as the parts of the original worth keeping, which four critics independently agreed on.

One critique held that a large error on the Huperzine pair is uninformative pending leakage labelling. I partly disagree on direction: AChE is among the most heavily assayed ChEMBL targets and the pair is more likely in-distribution than not, so a 2.41 log10 error on a probably-memorised pair is a strong prior against the head performing well here. That is a hypothesis the benchmark tests, not an assumption it makes, but it should be stated in the prespec so a poor result is not later framed as a surprise.
revised.final_method:
Executed in this order, frozen under META-3 prespec before any run.

STEP 0 — REPAIRS, gating everything downstream. (a) Fix platform/cbc/corpus.py: join /activity to /assay and read confidence_score there; set the protocol threshold to 9; add a low-confidence bucket to the denominator object so rejections are counted. (b) Write a correction record into memory/ledger superseding clm_a47c9774148de980: the Boltz conversion yields pIC50 expressed in kcal/mol, a positive magnitude, sign-inverted relative to thermo.kd_to_dg; the platform emits no dG from this head. (c) Add a verify_all.py check that fails the build if any code path converts affinity_pred_value into binding_free_energy, mirroring the enforcement pattern salvaged from the withdrawn CBC-CC-3.

STEP 1 — POPULATION, defined by pharmacology. For each target, admit ChEMBL v34 records with assay confidence exactly 9, target_type SINGLE PROTEIN, biochemical or functional assay, a catalytic-inhibition or direct-binding endpoint against the named protein, and a numeric IC50/Ki/Kd/EC50/AC50/XC50. NP tier is recorded as an annotation. Publish the achieved n per target BEFORE running; targets with fewer than 20 admitted actives are not reported individually.

STEP 2 — APPLICABILITY PREFLIGHT via platform/cbc/chem.py. Refuse peptides outright. Refuse >50 heavy atoms by default (Boltz-2 training filter) with the refusal recorded, not silently skipped. Publish every dataset natural product's position relative to the 50 line: Huperzine A 18, Baicalein 20, Curcumin 27, Ginkgolide B 30, Asiatic acid 35, Salvianolic acid B 52 (refused), Ginsenoside Rg1 56 (refused), Onjisaponin V 123 (refused).

STEP 3 — LEAKAGE STRATA, assigned before scoring. Stratum A: confidence-9 ChEMBL v34 pairs, labelled in-training-distribution, probably memorised. Stratum B: pairs whose earliest activity document postdates the ChEMBL v34 cut, labelled held-out. All metrics are reported separately by stratum and never pooled across them.

STEP 4 — REGRESSION ARM, actives only. The docs state affinity_pred_value 'should only be used when comparing different active molecules, not inactives', so inactives are excluded from RMSE and Spearman by protocol, not by convenience. Primary metric: within-target Spearman rho with a receptor-level cluster bootstrap. Secondary: pooled RMSE and MAE in log10 units. Decision rule, stated in reference units rather than absolutes: report a potency value only if the head beats the per-target-median null by a paired bootstrap whose 95% CI on the delta excludes zero AND the within-target rho CI excludes zero. Publish the minimum detectable effect at the achieved n before running; if the MDE on rho exceeds 0.5, the null result is reported as 'underpowered at n=N', never as 'does not beat the null'.

STEP 5 — BINARY ARM, three separately labelled negative sets. (a) HARD, primary: same-target ChEMBL measured inactives — standard_relation '>' or value >= 10 uM on the same target and assay class — restricted to compounds with Tanimoto >= 0.3 to at least one known active, which places them deliberately outside the training decoys' <0.3 similarity band. (b) PARALOG: BuChE for AChE, CHRM2-M5 for CHRM1, GSK3A for GSK3B, using ligands with measured selectivity data. (c) SHUFFLE, control only: ligand against unrelated registry receptors, labelled in the output as 'reproduces the training-time synthetic-decoy construction (Boltz-2 paper, Table 1); a high AUROC here is expected and is not evidence of generalisation'. Bootstrap AUROC over LIGANDS, not pairs.

STEP 6 — STEREOCHEMICAL RESOLUTION GATE, 4 runs, run before the bulk. Rank (-)- vs (+)-physostigmine and (-)- vs (+)-huperzine A. Precondition I measured this session and which the proposing critique could not have known: the corpus SMILES cannot be used as-is. PHYSOSTIGMINE is CIP [(11,'S'),(17,'R')] but (+)-PHYSOSTIGMINE is [(11,'R'),(17,'?')] — one stereocentre is UNDEFINED in ChEMBL, so it is not a clean enantiomer but a diastereomer mixture. The SMILES must first be corrected to the true (3aR,8aR) enantiomer by inverting both centres of the (-)-form, recorded as an explicit curation fix with provenance. Both compounds share assay CHEMBL644099, so the comparison is within-assay. If the head cannot rank pairs with a >2 log measured gap, that is reported as the headline finding and no pooled metric is interpreted.

STEP 7 — MSA ARM. --use_msa_server on >=20 paired runs to quantify the single-sequence penalty, shared with the co-fold work.

STEP 8 — WRITE-BACK, to a new table measured_in_repo_accuracy, never to thermo.METHOD_ACCURACY. Each key is a structured record: metric name (log10 potency error, not kcal/mol), point estimate, ci_low, ci_high, n_pairs, n_targets, target list, leakage stratum, heavy-atom range, msa mode, accelerator, boltz version, date. verify_all.py refuses any consumer that reads the point estimate without the interval, and refuses application outside the recorded domain.
final_success_criteria: platform/cbc/corpus.py joins /activity to /assay; a regression test asserts that a known confidence-8 assay is rejected at threshold 9, and that data/corpus_ACHE.json regenerated under the fix has no null assay_confidence.

A ledger correction record supersedes clm_a47c9774148de980, stating that (6-y)*1.364 yields pIC50 in kcal/mol as a positive magnitude, sign-inverted relative to thermo.kd_to_dg, with the worked case y=-3 giving +12.28 vs -12.28.

verify_all.py fails the build if any code path writes an affinity_pred_value-derived quantity into binding_free_energy, and if any record carries a PREDICTED binding_free_energy at all from this pipeline.
n per target is published before any Boltz run; only targets with >=20 admitted actives are reported individually; the minimum detectable Spearman rho at the achieved n is published in the prespec.
Within-target Spearman rho with receptor-level cluster-bootstrap CI, reported separately for leakage stratum A and stratum B, never pooled.

Three AUROCs reported side by side with ligand-level bootstrap CIs and explicit labels: same-target measured inactives (primary), close paralogs, and cross-target shuffle marked as a training-construction control.
The 4-run stereochemistry gate is reported first, with the (+)-physostigmine stereocentre correction recorded as a curation fix and the corrected InChIKey in provenance.
Every refused compound appears in the output with its heavy-atom count and the 50-atom rule cited; Salvianolic acid B, Ginsenoside Rg1 and Onjisaponin V are all refused and visible as refusals.
measured_in_repo_accuracy carries the full structured record; thermo.METHOD_ACCURACY is byte-identical to its pre-project state, asserted by a test.

revised.title: Falsify PRODIGY on this catalogue in an afternoon: measure whether its predicted dG can vary across candidates against a common receptor at all, before spending a week on a transfer benchmark
revised.changed_what: Inverted the order and cut roughly 90% of the compute. The Kastritis co-folding benchmark is withdrawn as under-costed and partly in-sample. In its place I ran the decisive falsification's first half this session and it already returns a number that reframes the whole arm. Installing prodigy-prot 2.4.0 into the Boltz venv and running it on 2FLU (chain X, 285 residues; chain P, a 16-mer peptide) at 25 C gives dG = -8.668 kcal/mol, Kd 4.39e-7 M, with this term decomposition against the installed IC_NIS coefficients: ic_cc -0.568, ic_ca -1.501, ic_pp +0.392, ic_pa -1.814 (interface sum -3.491); nis_a +8.067, nis_c +2.699 (non-interacting-surface sum +10.766); intercept -15.9433. The NIS terms carry 3.1x the magnitude of all four interface terms combined, and prodigy.py line 159 computes SASA on the whole complex, so for a fixed receptor they are a receptor constant. For a 543-residue AChE plus a 36-mer the peptide is 6% of residues and the NIS percentages barely move. The candidate-varying signal is therefore an interface-contact sum whose entire magnitude here (-3.49 kcal/mol) is under two method-RMSEs (1.89), before any question of whether the pose is real.
conceded: Step 3 was mislabelled and I accept the correction from four reviewers. Recovering r = -0.73 / RMSE 1.89 on the eLife 81-complex set reproduces a TRAINING fit, since that is the set the IC-NIS coefficients were regressed on. It is a wiring check and licenses nothing about generalisation.

The 2.0 kcal/mol pre-registered gate is beatable by a predictor with zero information. Protein-peptide affinity sets have sd around 1.3 kcal/mol, so 'predict the set mean' passes a 2.0 threshold. A rule a constant predictor satisfies is not a rule. Replaced with a relative rule.

Step 4(a) was badly under-costed. Co-folding dozens to 144 Kastritis protein-protein complexes, many 300-900 residues, with roughly N^2 pair-representation cost, is multi-day at best on MPS and some may exhaust unified memory. Withdrawn rather than re-timed.

The load-bearing protein-peptide cell named no set and no n. Rather than name one I cannot assemble, I now state the condition: if no set with structures and direct-method (ITC/SPR/stopped-flow) affinities can be built on this hardware, the peptide transfer is reported as unmeasured and binding_free_energy stays not_computed for that stated reason.

My E10 install claim did not reproduce from repo state, and the real situation is worse than the critic found. prodigy-prot 2.4.0 declares numpy>=2; boltz 2.2.1 declares numpy<2.0. Installing prodigy into .venv312 silently upgraded numpy to 2.5.2 and broke the pinned Boltz environment; I restored 1.26.4. They cannot share one venv with satisfied declarations.

The denominator is wrong. I confirmed data/dataset.json holds 35 records but only 26 distinct sequences — 7 duplicate groups, 9 redundant rows. 'All 35 candidates carry a co-fold' would present 9 redundant rows as independent results and double-count any aggregate.

'Every candidate carries a co-fold' forces a receptor assignment on candidates that have no defensible one, including the mechanistically inverted extracellular-peptide-versus-cytoplasmic-target cases. The refusal is the more informative record.

PRODIGY on a low-ipTM model scores the contacts of a wrong pose. With the pilot interface PAE around 17 A on the native candidate-AChE complex, there is no interface for a contact regression to count. Conceded, and it is now the reason the candidate arm is not run rather than a caveat attached to running it.
defended: Install-don't-reimplement is vindicated and I hold it as a general rule. The installed coefficients are IC_NIS = -0.09459*ic_cc -0.10007*ic_ca +0.19577*ic_pp -0.22671*ic_pa +0.18681*nis_a +0.13810*nis_c -15.9433. Two independent retrievals from memory had given mutually sign-flipped forms. Reading it off disk cost one minute and settled it.

I defend the unconstrained-primary / pocket-constrained-secondary discipline verbatim. A pocket-forced score is circular evidence for the mechanism the pocket encoded, and no other proposal in the panel addresses this.

I defend co-folding the candidates with real receptors as necessary work — it is the platform's largest gap — but it is a structure-prediction experiment, not a dG experiment, and I hand it to AIML-STRUCT-1 where the scrambled-sequence null and the across-seed envelope live. Keeping it inside a free-energy proposal was a scoping error on my part.

I reject the framing that a PRODIGY number is worthless merely because DMPK exposure dominates for a polycation with no transport mechanism. That is true and decision-relevant, but the platform's obligation is to state whether a runnable method's error is knowable, and a measured refusal has value independent of whether the molecule is developable.

I decline to add the composition-matched-scramble null as a separate build. Once the receptor-constant NIS result is published, the cheaper and more direct control is a correlation against net charge, which platform/cbc/peptide.py already computes.
revised.final_method:
Two stages, the second conditional on the first.

STAGE A — FALSIFICATION, roughly one afternoon, no Boltz runs.
(A1) Two-venv architecture, forced by the numpy conflict measured above: prodigy-prot lives in its own .venv-prodigy; the interface is a PDB in and a JSON out on disk. Pin prodigy-prot 2.4.0, freesasa 2.2.1 and the numpy version in provenance.software for each venv separately, and add a verify_all.py check that the two are never co-installed.
(A2) Receptor-constancy test. Take a deposited receptor-peptide complex, thread the 26 DISTINCT candidate sequences (not 35 records) onto the peptide chain with a fixed backbone, and run PRODIGY on all 26. Record the min/median/max predicted dG, the interface-term sum and the NIS-term sum separately for each. Decision: if the spread of predicted dG across 26 different peptides is smaller than the method's own 1.89 kcal/mol RMSE, PRODIGY cannot rank this catalogue and the arm closes with a measured refusal.
(A3) Charge-confound test, free. Correlate the 26 predicted dG values against net charge at pH 7.4 from platform/cbc/peptide.py. If |Pearson r| > 0.8, the contact count is rediscovering a property the platform already reports, and that is reported as the finding.
(A4) Seed-stability test on the one class that matters: take the handful of peptide-in-groove complexes this project can actually name, co-fold each at >=3 seeds, and run PRODIGY on crystal and on each model. If the predicted dG scatters across seeds by more than 1.89 kcal/mol on a complex whose answer is known, the pre-registered rule is already failed and no further compute is justified.

STAGE B — TRANSFER BENCHMARK, only if Stage A does not falsify.
Wiring check on the eLife set, explicitly labelled a training-set statistic and never quoted as accuracy. Then a two-cell table, crystal versus Boltz-predicted, on the SAME complexes so the structure shift is isolated cleanly, sized by a pilot on the three largest before any batch is committed. Pre-registered rule restated in reference units and on the interval: emit a peptide binding_free_energy only if PRODIGY-on-models beats the per-set MEAN predictor with a paired bootstrap CI on the RMSE delta excluding zero, AND the upper bound of the 95% CI on RMSE is below the measured spread of the ground truth, AND the CI on |Spearman rho| excludes zero. Primary figure is RMSE and rho as a function of ipTM bin and minimum interface-PAE bin, with n per bin.

DELIVERABLE EITHER WAY. Every candidate's binding_free_energy note is rewritten from 'no calculation has been performed' to a measured statement: either a value with its measured error, or a refusal quoting the specific number that disqualified the method — the isomer-spread-free version of which is the falsification result from Stage A.
final_success_criteria: Two venvs exist; a verify_all.py check fails if prodigy-prot and boltz are importable from the same interpreter, with the conflicting numpy pins (>=2 vs <2.0) recorded in provenance.

The 2FLU decomposition is reproduced by a committed script and recorded in the ledger: dG -8.668, interface-term sum -3.491, NIS-term sum +10.766, intercept -15.9433, with the whole-complex SASA call at prodigy.py:159 cited as the reason NIS is receptor-constant.

The 26-sequence receptor-constancy scan reports min/median/max predicted dG and the interface/NIS split per sequence, over 26 DISTINCT sequences with a sequence_group id making the 9 redundant dataset rows visible.
The predicted-dG versus net-charge Pearson r is reported with its CI, whatever its value.
The eLife reproduction, if run, is labelled 'in-sample training statistic' in the output text itself, not only in a footnote.

The pre-registered rule is expressed on intervals relative to a mean-predictor baseline, is frozen in the ledger before any Stage B run, and is applied mechanically with the outcome recorded either way.

Every candidate carries either a receptor assignment with a named UniProt accession and residue range, or an explicit no_receptor_assignable record stating why — including compartment-excluded for extracellular peptides aimed at cytoplasmic targets.
The candidate co-folding work is formally transferred to AIML-STRUCT-1 in the ledger, with the ipTM=0.00 lone-chain artefact named as the gap it closes.

revised.title: WITHDRAWN — disulfide-isomer folding with an OpenMM implicit-solvent filter; the two enforcement rules and a free chemical-definition audit are relocated to CBC-CC-1
revised.changed_what: Withdrawn. Seven reviewers converged on defects I cannot repair without changing the proposal into something else, and on re-examination the two load-bearing components are both unsound: the uncertainty arithmetic is undefined, and the filter that would adjudicate connectivity has no measurable operating characteristic on this hardware. What survives is roughly item 5 plus a deterministic audit that costs hours, and I have moved those into CBC-CC-1 Step 0 rather than keeping a 1.5-week proposal alive as a wrapper for them.
conceded: The quadrature is invalid and I should not have written it. A min/median/max range over an enumerated set of DISTINCT CHEMICAL SPECIES is a scenario ensemble, not a Gaussian sd of one quantity. Combining it in quadrature with a method RMSE produces a number with no distributional interpretation — the precise failure class this repository exists to eliminate. Defining the isomer term as an sd would require a prior over connectivities that I do not have and cannot obtain.

The OpenMM filter is an uncalibrated binary classifier and 'interface survives vs dissolves' is not a criterion. Worse, its bias is one-sided in a known direction: Amber14/GBn2 with no explicit ions under-screens electrostatics and over-stabilises salt bridges for peptides of net charge up to +8, so it would systematically return 'survives'. A filter whose failure mode runs one way is not a filter.

Moving disulfide_connectivity to COMPUTED was a provenance regression twice over. A connectivity selected by a diffusion model plus an unvalidated MD filter is PREDICTED at best, and gating it on agreement with the parent motif's published pattern makes the published pattern the answer — upgrading a LITERATURE fact to COMPUTED status.

The enumeration undercounted and the denominator double-counted. My own histogram, reconfirmed this session as {0:5, 1:3, 2:4, 3:2, 4:3, 5:4, 6:4, 7:4, 8:4, 9:2}, contains TWO candidates at 9 Cys, which admit 9 x 105 = 945 maximal-pairing topologies — I never enumerated them. And the counts run over 35 records containing only 26 distinct sequences, so the worst offenders would have been folded in triplicate.

The intramolecular enumeration is the wrong uncertainty. Fifteen of 35 records carry an odd cysteine count, so at least one free thiol is unavoidable, and a free thiol on a 3-11 kDa peptide at pH 7.4 in air forms mixed disulfides with glutathione and albumin Cys34 and drives covalent dimerisation. The circulating species is none of the 105 enumerated isomers. This is a molecular-definition problem and an upstream design defect, not a downstream quantity to estimate.

The compute was badly under-priced. OpenMM on this box exposes Reference/CPU/OpenCL only, with no CUDA and no Metal fast path, and 100-150 systems each needing fold plus minimisation plus restrained equilibration plus unrestrained MD is far beyond 1-1.5 weeks. Interface dissociation is a microsecond-to-millisecond process; essentially every isomer would 'survive' any affordable trajectory, so the verdict would carry no information.

The whole plan sat downstream of an unverified gate: the Boltz docs confirm bond constraints for CCD ligands and canonical residues without confirming intra-chain SG-SG. The fallback of imposing connectivity during relaxation is a different and weaker experiment, not a drop-in substitute.

The isomer spread would have been confounded with sampler noise. With across-seed ipTM sd around 0.133, the expected max-minus-min of 15 single-seed draws is roughly 0.45 — comparable to or larger than any plausible connectivity effect. I would have reported seeding as chemistry.
defended: The framing is still correct and I do not retract it: reporting a value with a +/-1.9 kcal/mol method error on a molecule that is one of 105 possible chemical species is a category error, and it is the strongest chemistry point I raised. What is wrong is the machinery I proposed to quantify it, not the observation that it must block emission.

The refusal to let single-trajectory MM-GBSA populate binding_free_energy stands, unanimously endorsed and defended on the merits: these are 26-100 residue polycations forming no congeneric series, and thermo.METHOD_ACCURACY's 2.5 kcal/mol figure is explicitly scoped to relative ranking within a congeneric small-molecule series.

I decline the suggestion to take the parent motif's published pattern as a DATABASE-status primary value. The candidates are GGGGS-linked concatenations, not the parent peptides; a connectivity solved in the parent's structural context is not a property of the chimera, and asserting it would be exactly the kind of borrowed number this project removed.
E16 (the GBn2 citation) remains verified:false. I did not retrieve it this session and it is not cited anywhere as a result of this withdrawal.
revised.final_method:
No experiment. Two artefacts are relocated to CBC-CC-1 Step 0 and cost hours, not weeks.

(1) DETERMINISTIC CHEMICAL-DEFINITION AUDIT, no simulation. For each of the 26 DISTINCT sequences emit: cysteine count, parity, the number of admissible maximal intramolecular pairings (3 for 4 Cys, 15 for 6, 105 for 8, 945 for the two 9-Cys cases), an explicit statement that partial pairing with free thiols is excluded by assumption, and for every odd-Cys sequence an explicit note that the enumeration excludes disulfide-linked homodimers and glutathione and albumin-Cys34 adducts, so any spread computed over it is a FLOOR. Emit a not_a_single_chemical_entity status that BLOCKS emission of any structure-derived value for that candidate, and a sequence_group id so the 9 redundant dataset rows are visible rather than silently triple-counted.

(2) TWO CODE-LEVEL REFUSALS in verify_all.py, both objectively checkable and neither arguable: no code path may write an MM-GBSA value into binding_free_energy; and no candidate carrying not_a_single_chemical_entity may carry a PREDICTED structure-derived value at all.

(3) DESIGN FEEDBACK, written not computed: the odd-Cys finding is reported as an upstream defect to be fixed by specifying connectivity or substituting Cys to Ser or alpha-aminobutyrate, with the DMPK consequences named. That is a catalogue revision, not a calculation.

If anyone later wants the isomer question answered, the correct order is STRUCTBIO-IDEA-1 first — read connectivity off the coordinates already on disk — and only then, if it is still open, an exhaustive scan restricted to the 4- and 6-Cys distinct sequences at >=3 shared seeds, reported as a variance decomposition of sigma_isomer against sigma_seed with an intraclass correlation, never as a min/max range and never combined in quadrature with anything.
final_success_criteria: The audit table covers 26 distinct sequences with sequence_group ids, and the two 9-Cys cases show 945 maximal pairings.
Every odd-Cys sequence carries the explicit intermolecular-species exclusion note and the word 'floor'.
verify_all.py fails the build if an MM-GBSA value reaches binding_free_energy, and fails if a not_a_single_chemical_entity candidate carries any PREDICTED structure-derived value.
No OpenMM system is built, no isomer is folded, and no disulfide_connectivity field changes status as a result of this work.

refined.expert: PhD structural biologist, 21 years; crystallography and cryo-EM; validates deposited structures

revised.title: All-atom physical-validity gate, plus a seed-replication measurement that establishes disulfide connectivity is UNDETERMINED and must stay not_computed
revised.changed_what: The idea survives; two of its three headline claims do not.
