I ran the experiment the panel demanded — 12 fresh Boltz-2 predictions at recorded seeds 1/2/3 on four candidates, 24-25 s each on MPS — and it destroyed my per-candidate findings. (1) 'Four candidates have a trivalent sulfur, chemically impossible' is WITHDRAWN. For BasalM1-PAM-B2, Cys9 has two contacts under 2.5 A in the original draw only; across seeds 1/2/3 it has exactly one (9-34 at 2.054/2.191/2.121 A) while the flipping partner is 1-9 (orig) vs 1-17 (s1, s2) vs absent (s3). For MicroDual-Trem2-Nrf2-M5 the two 'bonds' are 2.328 and 2.438 A — as the crystallographer critic said, that is two thiols packed close, not a disulfide. (2) 'None of this is visible in pLDDT' is WITHDRAWN as factually false; I measured it and the critic was right. The 1.705 A contact in PfcACh-PAM-P1 sits on SG atoms with pLDDT 54.6 and 56.4 in a model of mean pLDDT 59.7 — the model is loudly unconfident, and my claim inverted the evidence. (3) Consequently the EMISSION step is gutted: I no longer propose writing disulfide_connectivity as PREDICTED for the catalogue. (4) The Engh-Huber bond-length/angle arm is dropped. (5) The zero-false-positive success criterion is rewritten, because I verified it would fail as written. What replaces the withdrawn claims is stronger and seed-robust: the deliverable is now a measurement that connectivity is undetermined below pLDDT ~70, and that predicted S-S distances are systematically SHORT.
conceded: The four 'trivalent sulfur' calls were single-draw artifacts. Conceded to all six critics; I ran 3 seeds x 4 candidates and the census is not reproducible at low pLDDT.
'Invisible to pLDDT' was false and the crystallographer had already measured it. Verified: SG pLDDT 54.6/56.4 at the 1.705 A contact.

A 2.5 A Sg-Sg radius cutoff is not a bond assignment. Conceded to the medicinal chemist, the computational chemist and metascience. At 3.5 A the census grows from 38 to 49 contacts; the count is cutoff-driven.

The zero-false-positive criterion on deposited structures fails as written. Verified: 4EY7 chain A has THREE Ca-Ca outliers under the current rule — Tyr105-Pro106 (2.853 A, omega -1.7 deg, genuine cis) plus Pro258->Asn265 (8.627 A, numbering gap 7) and Asp494->Pro498 (6.147 A, gap 4), both unmodelled-loop chain breaks. An omega-aware rule does not catch those; a residue-numbering-continuity precondition is required.

Emitting disulfide_connectivity as PREDICTED from one unseeded draw is sampler noise in a provenance envelope. Conceded to the medicinal chemist and metascience; the emission is now gated on seed reproducibility AND local confidence, which on the current catalogue admits at most one or two structures.

Pinning success criteria to numbers from an unrepeatable /tmp run is a fingerprint, not a regression test. Conceded to the benchmarking critic; artifacts are committed content-addressed first, and the pin is written against the committed files.
Engh-Huber bond lengths and angles are the least informative check on diffusion output. Dropped from the first release.

run_boltz never passes --seed although Boltz-2 exposes it. Verified at platform/cbc/compute/structure.py:191-195: the cmd list has no seed argument. Every one of the 22 structures is therefore an unseeded single draw. This is a real reproducibility bug in my own pipeline and is now fix #2 after the /tmp rescue.
defended: The reference-distribution circularity objection (raised by four critics) is largely wrong for S-S distance, and I now have data. I measured Sg-Sg in ultra-high-resolution depositions where restraint weighting is negligible: 3NIR at 0.48 A gives 2.026/2.037/2.046 A; 1EJG at 0.54 A gives 2.031/2.036/2.047; 2VB1 at 0.65 A gives 2.026-2.038; 1AB1 at 0.89 A gives 2.028-2.043; 4EY7 at 2.35 A gives 2.031-2.073. Over 19 bonds spanning 0.48 to 2.35 A resolution: mean 2.041 A, sd 0.013 A. If the ~2.03 A target were an artifact of the monomer library, the sub-angstrom entries — where the data, not the dictionary, determine the model — would not agree with the 2.35 A entries to 0.013 A. The tight range in 4EY7 is not suspicious; it is what the physics gives. Boltz-2's 1.705-1.90 A values are 10 to 25 sd below anything observed, and that conclusion does not depend on a restraint dictionary.

The short-S-S finding is seed-robust and survives everything the panel threw at connectivity. Even HippoTrk-Saponin-X1, the one candidate whose pairing IS reproducible (identical 4 pairings in 4/4 draws), places them at 1.79/1.876/1.883/1.988 (orig), 1.783/1.962/2.099/2.143 (s2), 1.82/1.895/1.999/2.293 (s3). Systematically short in every draw. This is a property of the model in this configuration, not of the sampler's luck.

The check is not vacuous and does discriminate — 0 D-residues in 22 structures, near-zero non-bonded heavy-atom clashes. A validity gate that flags nothing on backbone stereochemistry and flags a great deal on sulfur chemistry is behaving correctly.

Step 6 (rescue the coordinates out of /tmp) is confirmed urgent and confirmed accurately described. I re-verified this session: /tmp/cbc_boltz holds 22 complete boltz_results trees with input_model_0.cif, confidence JSON and pae/plddt npz. The claims elsewhere in the panel that no Boltz output exists are false.
revised.final_method:
Ordered, with hard gates between stages.

STAGE 0 (today, standalone, blocks four other proposals). Move /tmp/cbc_boltz into the repo under artifacts/boltz/<sha256-prefix>/, register each run in the memory ledger as an ARTIFACT record with sha256, and add mmcif_path + sha256 to every row of data/real_vs_hardcoded.json (verified: it currently has no path field). Add --seed to run_boltz at platform/cbc/compute/structure.py:191 and record the seed in the returned provenance dict; the 22 existing runs are stamped seed=None, unseeded.

STAGE 1. Freeze the reference distribution BEFORE looking at any candidate. Build it from two sets, both stored as a provenanced data file with resolution, n, and retrieval date: (a) a high-resolution arm (<=1.2 A: 3NIR, 1EJG, 2VB1, 1AB1 and additional disulfide-rich entries) for S-S distance and chi3, where restraint weighting is low; (b) a disulfide-rich arm (knottins, EGF-like domains) rather than only the cysteine-sparse target_records entries, since the catalogue contains 8-Cys 47-mers. Report the false-positive rate of every check on this set together with its n and resolution histogram. Bond lengths/angles are not included.

STAGE 2. platform/cbc/structval.py, built on gemmi 0.6.5 (already installed; no new dependency). Checks kept: CA chirality via the N-CA-C-CB improper (4EY7 reference: -122.63 +/- 3.19 deg over 481 residues, zero sign flips); omega with cis/trans/twisted bands; non-bonded heavy-atom clashes via NeighborSearch/ContactSearch; sulfur chemistry. Sulfur is reported in FOUR bands, not two: anomalously short (<1.95 A, as diagnostic as long and the dominant artifact here), bonded (1.95-2.15), ambiguous (2.15-3.00), non-bonded (>3.00). The full histogram is published; counts are quoted at both 2.3 and 2.5 A so cutoff sensitivity is visible. Connectivity is assigned by maximum-weight matching over the Sg-Sg graph, not by radius thresholding, and where a cysteine has competing contacts the verdict is 'connectivity undetermined', never 'trivalent'. Detector validation is external: run the Sg-Sg detector over the reference mmCIFs and report precision and recall against their deposited _struct_conn disulf annotations (verified extractable — 4EY7 yields 69-96, 257-272, 409-529).

STAGE 3. Replace the +/-0.5 A Ca-Ca rule at predictor.py:151-160 with a rule that (i) requires residue-numbering continuity before judging a Ca-Ca distance and classifies discontinuities as chain breaks, and (ii) applies cis and trans bands from omega. Regression cases: 4EY7 Tyr105-Pro106 must be cis-peptide, not outlier; Pro258->Asn265 and Asp494->Pro498 must be chain-break, not outlier; total geometry outliers on 4EY7 chain A must go from 3 to 0.

STAGE 4. The seed-replication measurement, which is now the scientific deliverable. Re-fold all cysteine-containing candidates at seeds 1,2,3 (measured cost 24-25 s each on MPS; the whole catalogue is well under an hour) and report, per candidate, the fraction of draws in which each pairing recurs, plus the S-S distance distribution across seeds. Publish the joint table (violation band) x (local SG pLDDT decile) that the ML critic asked for, so 'confidence does not see this' is quantified rather than asserted — on my measurements it will show the opposite of what I originally claimed, and it should be published that way.

STAGE 5. Emission, deliberately minimal. disulfide_connectivity becomes PREDICTED only where ALL of: identical pairing in >=3/3 seeds; both partners' SG pLDDT >= 70; distance in the bonded band; chi3 outside the eclipsed region. On present evidence that admits HippoTrk-Saponin-X1 and possibly PfcTrk-ErkEnhancer-P2 and AstroEaat2-Up-A2, and nothing else. Every other candidate keeps not_computed with the failing check and the measured geometry recorded as the stated reason. The per-seed agreement fraction is stored as a measurement, not as 'uncertainty'.

STAGE 6. Wire into platform/validate.py as new violation categories and into verify_all.py. Also correct data/real_vs_hardcoded.json, which currently asserts plausible_protein: true for all 22 on the strength of a Ca-Ca check alone.
final_success_criteria: The 22 boltz_results trees live at a repo path, each with a recorded sha256, and every row of data/real_vs_hardcoded.json carries mmcif_path and sha256. Checkable: no row lacks the field; every sha256 recomputes.
run_boltz emits --seed and records it; a test asserts that two runs of the same input at the same seed produce byte-identical mmCIF, and that the 22 legacy runs are stamped seed=null.

On the frozen reference set, the sulfur detector's precision and recall against deposited _struct_conn disulf annotations are both reported and recall is >= 0.95. Chirality and clash checks report a false-positive rate with n and resolution histogram attached.

On 4EY7 chain A the revised Ca-Ca/omega/continuity rule returns zero geometry outliers, classifying Tyr105-Pro106 as cis-peptide and Pro258->Asn265 (gap 7) and Asp494->Pro498 (gap 4) as chain breaks. This is a hard pass/fail on three named residue pairs.

A committed table reports, for every cysteine-containing candidate at seeds 1/2/3: each pairing's recurrence fraction, its distance in each draw, and both partners' SG pLDDT. Pre-registered prediction from this session's pilot: HippoTrk-Saponin-X1 (mean pLDDT 73-79) recovers pairings 1-19, 14-27, 29-38, 43-46 in 3/3; PfcACh-PAM-P1 (mean pLDDT 55-60) recovers no pairing in more than 2/4 draws. If HippoTrk fails to replicate, the confidence-gating hypothesis is wrong and the emission rule is abandoned entirely.

A published joint table of S-S band x local SG pLDDT decile, with the sign and magnitude of the association stated. My prior, from this session's measurement, is that bad geometry concentrates at LOW pLDDT — the opposite of my original proposal's claim, and the table must say so.

Across all seeds and candidates, the fraction of S-S contacts below 1.95 A is reported against the reference distribution (n=19, mean 2.041 A, sd 0.013 A, resolution 0.48-2.35 A). This is the seed-robust finding and it must be stated as a property of Boltz-2 v2.2.1 in msa=empty single-sequence mode, not of the peptides.

data/dataset.json contains at most three PREDICTED disulfide_connectivity values, each satisfying the 3/3-seed and pLDDT>=70 gate, and >=28 entries reading not_computed with a named failing check. A run that fills in more than three is a failed run.
verify_all.py passes with the new checks, and the regression pin is written against the committed content-addressed mmCIFs, not against numbers from an unrepeatable run.

revised.title: Positive-control gate: can this pipeline place a known peptide in a known groove? (Measured this session: yes, DockQ 0.675 in 50 seconds)
revised.changed_what: Every critic said the same thing and every critic was right: this is a pre-cutoff benchmark and I presented recall as accuracy. Boltz-2 trains on PDB releases up to 2023-06-01; 2FLU is 2006, 4EY7 is 2012, and all 16 targets were curated precisely because they are canonical. Three changes. (1) The 16-receptor MONOMER ARM IS WITHDRAWN. A sub-angstrom RMSD on 4EY7 measures memorisation and would invite exactly the wrong inference about a platform whose task is peptide placement. It consumed most of the effort and produced no knowledge. (2) The CALIBRATION DELIVERABLE IS CEDED to AIML-STRUCT-2's post-cutoff, homology-filtered set. I am not competent to build a calibration curve from n=3 and my own success criterion conceded it. (3) The unsound compute extrapolation is deleted and REPLACED WITH MEASUREMENT — and the measurement changes the picture entirely. I ran the flagship: KEAP1 Kelch (285 aa, from 2FLU chain X) + Neh2 16-mer AFFAQLQLDEETGEFL, Boltz-2 v2.2.1, msa=empty, MPS, seed 1, 301 tokens, 49.7 s wall. Scored with DockQ 2.1.3 against the deposited complex: DockQ 0.675 (CAPRI medium), fnat 0.975, iRMSD 1.405 A, LRMSD 8.208 A, clashes 0, against the model's own ipTM 0.921. So the proposal is no longer a plan, it is a result, and what remains is to institutionalise it as a gate.
conceded: The benchmark is entirely inside Boltz-2's training window and I did not say so. Corroborated by search this session: Boltz-2 trains on PDB structures released up to 2023-06-01. Every entry I named predates it by years to decades.

Wiring a recall-derived DockQ distribution behind every displayed ipTM would install an optimistically biased number as the platform's official uncertainty claim — worse than admitting it is uncalibrated. Conceded to the ML and metascience critics; the governance rule is rewritten so that below a stated minimum N the platform prints 'uncalibrated' and no distribution at all.
The 16-receptor monomer arm is close to worthless as calibration. Withdrawn.

'26 s per lone chain, essentially independent of length from 26 to 100 residues, therefore a 320-token complex is minutes-scale' generalised a fixed-overhead regime. The conclusion happened to be right (49.7 s measured) but the reasoning was unsound and is deleted; the timing table is now measured, not inferred.
n=3 complexes cannot support an ipTM threshold. Conceded; no threshold is published from this work.

I named TM-score without naming an implementation. gemmi.calculate_superposition returns RMSD, not TM-score. Since the monomer arm is withdrawn this is moot, but the registry will name US-align and its normalisation length wherever TM-score appears.
defended: The positive-control gate is NOT redundant with AIML-STRUCT-2 and should not be merged out of existence. A large post-cutoff calibration curve tells you the scale of accuracy; it does not tell you that YOUR pipeline, on YOUR receptor, with YOUR msa=empty setting and YOUR chain-mapping code, can place a 16-mer in a groove at all. That is a power measurement, and three critics independently said it was the missing one. It is now measured: DockQ 0.675, fnat 0.975.

msa=empty is not a fatal confound for the complex arm, and I tested the specific worry. The critic argued a six-bladed Kelch propeller in single-sequence mode may not fold, making DockQ uninterpretable. It folded: chain ptm 0.981, iRMSD 1.405 A, zero clashes. The objection was reasonable and the measurement answers it for this case.

The governance rule survives and is the most valuable output. Two critics said so explicitly. Restated: no ipTM is displayed anywhere without its benchmark N; where N is below a stated minimum the platform prints 'uncalibrated' and attaches no distribution.

One datapoint here is genuinely informative even though it is recall: ipTM 0.921 paired with DockQ 0.675 (medium, not high). On a complex the model has almost certainly memorised, ipTM is already optimistic relative to interface quality. That is a legitimate directional statement and it belongs in the record.
revised.final_method:
Reduced to three things, all cheap, none claiming to be a calibration.

(A) POSITIVE-CONTROL PANEL, labelled on its face. data/positive_controls.json, one row per case, each carrying pdb_id, release_date, in_training_window: true, resolution, chain mapping, prediction settings including seed, wall time, and the scores. Anchor case 2FLU is already complete and reproduces from a single command. Extend to the remaining in-registry peptide/protein complexes (1WWW/2IFG TrkA-NGF, 3FXI TLR4-MD-2). Every case is run at >=3 seeds and the DockQ SPREAD is reported, because with n small the seed spread IS the error bar. The artifact header, the README and every emitted record state: all entries predate the 2023-06-01 Boltz-2 training cutoff; measured DockQ bounds recall, not prediction. The gate rule: if the pipeline cannot reach CAPRI-acceptable on 2FLU, no result on any designed candidate means anything, and the platform refuses to display candidate interface numbers.

(B) TARGET/DOMAIN/NUMBERING REGISTRY. The one piece of durable work here that nobody else is doing: for each of the 16 targets, the receptor construct actually used, its domain boundaries, its UniProt-to-deposited numbering offset (e.g. the ACHE 'P22303 minus 31' convention), and the chain correspondence to each deposited entry. This is the prerequisite for every co-folding proposal on the slate and the thing whose absence silently produces wrong answers — demonstrated under Idea 3.

(C) MEASURED TIMING TABLE, replacing the deleted extrapolation. Already begun: 41-residue lone chain 24-25 s; 301-token two-chain complex 49.7 s; both MPS, recycling_steps 3, diffusion_samples 1, msa=empty. Extend across the 26-600 token range before any batch is sized.

Everything that would have been a calibration curve is handed to AIML-STRUCT-2, and this panel's cases are contributed to it as labelled pre-cutoff rows.
final_success_criteria: data/positive_controls.json exists; every row carries release_date and in_training_window, and a validate.py rule fails the build if any row displaying a DockQ lacks those two fields.

The 2FLU case reproduces from one command at >=3 recorded seeds. Pre-registered from this session's seed-1 run: DockQ 0.675, fnat 0.975, iRMSD 1.405 A, LRMSD 8.208 A, ipTM 0.921, 49.7 s. Success is that the seed-1 result reproduces byte-identically and that the 3-seed DockQ spread is reported, whatever it is.

No ipTM appears in any output or UI without its benchmark N; where N is below the stated minimum the string 'uncalibrated' is printed and no distribution is attached. Checkable by grepping the reporting layer and by a verify_all.py rule.

The registry resolves, for all 16 targets, construct boundaries and the deposited-to-UniProt numbering offset, with a unit test per target. Hard test for ACHE: the 4EY7 donepezil epitope extracted at a 4.5 A heavy-atom cutoff contains Trp86, Tyr337 and Phe338 in mature numbering — verified satisfiable this session (full extracted epitope: Tyr72, Asp74, Trp86, Gly120, Gly121, Tyr124, Glu202, Ser203, Trp286, Ser293, Val294, Phe295, Arg296, Phe297, Tyr337, Phe338, Tyr341, His447, Gly448).
A measured timing table spanning at least 40, 300 and 550 tokens exists in the repo; no batch is sized from an extrapolation.
No calibration curve and no ipTM threshold is published from this work. A run that emits one is a failed run.

revised.title: Epitope-overlap forensics: does a candidate's predicted interface sit where the natural ligand actually binds?
revised.changed_what: Narrowed to the one thing nobody else on the slate offers, and stripped of the two parts the panel correctly rejected. (1) pDockQ IS DROPPED ENTIRELY. Five critics independently made the same argument and it is the repository's governing rule: pDockQ is a logistic fit whose coefficients were estimated on AlphaFold2-Multimer interface pLDDT, and reconstructing those constants from memory is precisely the failure the rebuild exists to eliminate — worse, transferring an AF2-Multimer fit to Boltz-2 output is a second error stacked on the first. The module reports the raw quantities it computes itself (interface contact count, mean interface pLDDT, buried SASA) and nothing fitted. (2) THE DECOY-FOLDING ARM IS DROPPED as a deliverable of this proposal; it is the third independent request for the same scrambled-sequence batch, and one batch should serve AIML-STRUCT-1, AIML-BENCH-3 and this. I keep the analysis layer, which is my contribution. Notably, the compute objection I raised against myself is now dissolved: at the measured 49.7 s per complex, 240 decoy predictions is 3.3 hours, not a GPU problem. The duplication objection stands regardless. (3) The gating dependency is re-pointed from my own pre-cutoff panel to AIML-STRUCT-2's post-cutoff calibration, with my 2FLU positive control retained only as the power floor. (4) Numbering reconciliation is promoted from a footnote to a hard precondition, because I demonstrated the failure: the same epitope comparison gives Jaccard 0.000 without offset reconciliation and 0.944 with it.
conceded: pDockQ with remembered coefficients is the exact prohibited act. Dropped, not merely flagged.

Transferring an AF2-Multimer-fitted sigmoid to Boltz-2 confidences is a cross-model regression transfer and I described it as 'a second, published interface score independent of Boltz's own', which it is not. Conceded to the crystallographer.
Bare Jaccard has no scale and no null. Conceded to four critics; replaced by three reported numbers plus two nulls.

Most of this catalogue cannot support side-chain-resolution interface analysis. Median mean-pLDDT over the 22 models is 61.0; the four candidates I re-folded this session run 54-64 mean pLDDT except HippoTrk-Saponin-X1 at 73-79. Buried SASA and hot-spot ranking on such models produce numbers that change with the seed — which I proved for disulfides under Idea 1 and have no reason to think is different for side chains. A confidence precondition is now mandatory.
At N=10 the 95th-percentile criterion is unreachable (minimum achievable percentile p is 0.091) and the criterion was incoherent. Conceded; the reduced-N verdict vocabulary is fixed in advance.

Buried SASA on a co-folded model is not the same quantity as on a crystal complex, because the model relaxes both partners around each other. Reported with the caveat and quantified once against the deposited 2FLU value.
Three separate 20-scramble campaigns on the same candidates is a waste. Conceded; batch generation ceded.
defended: Epitope overlap remains worth building and is the only coordinate-level falsification route on the slate for the mechanistically inverted candidates. Five critics agreed. It converts 'this design is aimed at the wrong site' from argument into measurement.

The validate-on-the-known-answer-first ordering is right, and it now has a passing acceptance test rather than a promise. I extracted the KEAP1 epitope from deposited 2FLU (17 residues at a 4.5 A heavy-atom cutoff) and from my predicted complex (18 residues) using identical contact criteria; after applying the +324 numbering offset, recall of the experimental epitope is 1.000, Jaccard 0.944, with exactly one extra predicted residue (527). The module reproduces a known interface before it is pointed at anything unknown.

The numbering trap is real and severe, not pedantic. The same two residue sets give Jaccard 0.000 raw and 0.944 offset-corrected. Without a reconciliation precondition every epitope-overlap number this module emits would be silently zero and would have been read as 'the design binds nowhere near the site'. That failure mode is now a unit test.
revised.final_method:
platform/cbc/interface.py, three layers, each with a precondition.

PRECONDITION 0 — numbering reconciliation. Before any comparison, resolve deposited-entry numbering to model numbering via Idea 2's registry, assert the offset by sequence alignment, and store it. A comparison with an unresolved offset raises rather than returning a number. Unit test: the 2FLU KEAP1 epitope must reconcile at offset +324 and yield recall 1.000; the 4EY7 donepezil epitope must contain Trp86, Tyr337, Phe338 in mature numbering.

PRECONDITION 1 — confidence floor. Buried SASA, hot-spot ranking and contact chemistry are emitted only where mean interface pLDDT exceeds a stated floor. Below it the module returns not_computed with the measured interface pLDDT as the reason. On the present catalogue this will silence most of it, which is the correct behaviour.

LAYER A — quantities computed from coordinates, nothing fitted: per-residue and total buried SASA via Bio.PDB.SASA.ShrakeRupley (measured at 0.9 s for a 543-residue model), reported both backbone-only and all-atom with probe radius and hydrogen treatment stated; inter-chain residue contact map at a stated heavy-atom cutoff via gemmi NeighborSearch/ContactSearch; contact classification polar/hydrophobic/charged; interface contact count; mean interface pLDDT; fraction of interface residues below pLDDT 70. No pDockQ, no fitted score of any kind.

LAYER B — epitope comparison, three numbers not one: Jaccard, RECALL of the experimental epitope (the fraction of experimentally contacting residues recovered — this is the interface-size-robust number the ML critic asked for), and predicted interface size. Scored separately against every annotated site on the receptor, not collapsed to one — the AChE peripheral anionic site is a second real site and the target record already flags it. Reported for the deposited 2FLU complex alongside its predicted counterpart so the co-folding inflation of interface area is quantified once.

LAYER C — two nulls, both cheap on CPU. (i) Random-patch null: sample K same-size contiguous surface patches on the same receptor and report the candidate's percentile, so a Jaccard of 0.15 can be read against what chance gives on a 543-residue protein. (ii) Composition-matched scramble null, CONSUMED from AIML-STRUCT-1's decoy batch rather than generated here, plus the off-target-receptor null as a second reference. Statistics are seed-matched standardised effect size with a bootstrap CI, not a percentile threshold. Verdict vocabulary is fixed in advance: at N < 20 the module prints the exact rank, the effect size, and the literal label 'null too small to support a percentile threshold'; the 95th-percentile language is used only at N >= 20.

Gating: no interface number reaches the UI without AIML-STRUCT-2's post-cutoff benchmark context attached, plus the 2FLU positive-control result as the power floor.
final_success_criteria: ACCEPTANCE GATE, must pass before the module touches any prediction: run over deposited 2FLU coordinates and the predicted KEAP1+Neh2 complex, the module returns recall of the experimental epitope = 1.000 and Jaccard = 0.944 at a 4.5 A heavy-atom cutoff with offset +324 — reproducing this session's measurement. A second test asserts that the SAME comparison without offset reconciliation raises an error rather than silently returning 0.000.
4EY7 unit test: the extracted donepezil epitope contains Trp86, Tyr337 and Phe338 in mature numbering. Hard pass/fail on three named residues.
No fitted or regression-derived score appears anywhere in platform/cbc/interface.py. Checkable by grep: no pDockQ, no hard-coded logistic coefficients. A verify_all.py rule enforces it.

Every emitted interface metric carries mean interface pLDDT, and any metric emitted where that value falls below the stated floor is a build failure. On the current catalogue this must silence the majority of entries — a run that emits full interface analyses for all 22 has bypassed the precondition.
Every epitope-overlap value carries three numbers (Jaccard, recall, predicted interface size) and its random-patch-null percentile with K stated. No bare Jaccard is published.

The three KEAP1-directed candidates (HippoNrf-KeapDecoy-X3, CogNrf-KeapDis-03, MicroNrf2-AntiInflam-M2) each carry a stated recall against the experimental Neh2 epitope — including 0.000, which is a valid and publishable result — or not_computed with the measured interface pLDDT as the reason.

Where the null has N < 20, the output contains the literal string 'null too small to support a percentile threshold' and reports rank and effect size instead. No percentile threshold is claimed at reduced N.
Zero decoy predictions are generated by this proposal; the scramble batch is consumed from AIML-STRUCT-1 by artifact path and sha256.

refined.expert: Medicinal chemistry (natural products, pharmacophores, assay-interference debunking) — PhD, 20 years

revised.title: Warhead conjugability: a warhead-identity gate that runs on all 35 candidates, plus gorge-depth/linker-span measurement from experimental holo structures (veto withdrawn)
revised.changed_what: The veto is dead and I killed it myself this session. I built the escape-path BFS my critics asked for and ran it. Three things changed. (1) The NO_VECTOR/PHARMACOPHORE_CONFLICT verdict and its validate.py gate are withdrawn entirely — Wong et al. 2003 (PMID 12517147) solved TcAChE complexes of bis(10)- and bis(12)-hupyridone tethered through the exocyclic amine, the exact atom I declared NO_VECTOR, and (-)-bis(10)-hupyridone is >170-fold tighter than (-)-HupA. My gate would have vetoed a validated series. (2) I promoted the med chemist's warhead-identity check to the PRIMARY deliverable, because it runs on all 35 candidates today with no PDB, no SASA and no ChEMBL, whereas the geometry runs on roughly 1 of 25. I verified its three failures myself. (3) What survives of the geometry is a MEASUREMENT, not a verdict — and it passed a real positive control today, so I am not withdrawing it. NEW FINDING OF MY OWN, against my own proposal: the BFS verdict is knife-edge on probe radius. 4EY5 huperzine A N2 gives 17.97 A at probe 1.0, 18.55 A at probe 1.1-1.3, and NO PATH at 1.4 and above (ligand as obstacle). A binary verdict that flips on a 0.1 A change in an arbitrary parameter cannot gate anything. I found this by building the thing, and it independently confirms the critics' conclusion by a route none of them proposed.
conceded: The veto is experimentally falsified. Wong et al., J Am Chem Soc 2003;125(2):363-73, PMID 12517147, DOI 10.1021/ja021111w — retrieved this session — tether alkylene dimers of hupyridone (the HupA fragment) through the amino group, resolve one unit at the anionic subsite adjacent to Trp84 in the same pose as the TcAChE/(-)-HupA complex and the second at Trp279 in the PAS, and report (-)-bis(10)-hupyridone >170-fold tighter than (-)-HupA. The structural biologist is exactly right and this is decisive.

The retained-SASA rule has a false positive inside this repository's own corpus. HUPRINE X is in data/corpus_ACHE.json (CHEMBL208599, assay CHEMBL641012) at Ki 0.026 nM — I confirmed the record directly. RDKit FindMCS against huperzine A returns a shared 17-heavy-atom/16-bond core; huprine X is built by replacing huperzine's alpha-pyridone, and in my 4EY5 calculation the pyridone atoms retain essentially zero SASA. A retained-SASA veto condemns the exact region whose modification produced the most potent AChE inhibitor the platform holds. (One correction to the critic: that corpus record is Ki, not IC50.)

My linker arithmetic was wrong. 3.5 A per Gly-Ser residue is CONTOUR length; a flexible coil's mean end-to-end distance is far below contour, so L/3.5 residues can only span L fully extended, at large entropic cost. The residue-count conversion as I wrote it was a number without knowledge.
'Mechanistically void' overreached one static structure, and validate.py would have converted that overreach into an enforced verdict. The defensible claim is pose-relative.
The object being vetoed is not a defined chemical entity — chemStruct is prose with no SMILES for the conjugate. The computational chemist is right that the gate was testing an underspecified claim.
A 1.4 A solvent probe is the wrong probe for a methylene, as the DMPK critic said — and my sweep shows this is not a small correction: it is the difference between 18.55 A and NO PATH.

Coverage is as bad as the med chemist says: holo complexes exist for maybe 1 of 25 declared warheads, so the geometry module returns NOT_COMPUTED for nearly the whole catalogue while the gate was written as if it covered it.

My numbers are protocol-dependent in a way I did not disclose. Running SASA today WITHOUT stripping waters/cryoprotectants gives 4EY5 HUP 100.00% buried (0.00 A^2 bound) and 4EY7 E20 95.91% buried; the stripped protocol gives 98.47% and 86.62% (the latter independently reproduced by a critic). The stripping manifest is load-bearing and was unstated.
defended: The escape-path BFS itself is sound and I will not withdraw it, because it passed a genuine positive control today. 4EY7 donepezil, whose indanone methoxy sits at the gorge mouth, gives an escape path of 7.36 A at probe 1.4 and 7.10 A at probe 1.9 from C28 (O27 7.39/7.39; C26 7.86/8.19; O25 8.12/8.12) — short and probe-INSENSITIVE. 4EY5 huperzine A N2 gives 18.55 A / sealed. The method therefore discriminates a gorge-mouth binder from a gorge-bottom binder, which is precisely the distinction the platform currently cannot make.

The method reproduces the experimentally validated linker length, which is the anchor the metascientist demanded and said the proposal lacked. My BFS path from the huperzine amine to bulk is 18.55 A, of which 7 A is the bulk-clearance floor (donepezil's surface atom scores 7.1-7.4 A, establishing that floor empirically). The remaining ~11.5 A of gorge traverse sits squarely on the 10-12 methylene spacer (contour ~12.7-15.2 A) that Wong et al. crystallographically resolved spanning CAS to PAS. The number is anchored, not free-floating.

The structural biologist predicted that the BFS 'done correctly, should FIND the gorge — a ~20 A path matching the 10-12 methylene optimum.' It does: 17.97-21.11 A depending on probe. That is a successful pre-registered prediction about my own method and it argues for keeping the measurement while deleting the verdict.

I reject the framing that a NO PATH at methylene-scale probe is simply a method failure. On a rigid crystal the human AChE gorge IS too narrow for a methylene at probe 1.9 A — and Wong et al.'s own abstract stresses that rat/human-type AChE has a narrower gorge than TcAChE, with Tyr337 perpendicular and conformationally rigid via an H-bond to Tyr341, versus TcAChE Phe330. So probe-sensitivity is not just noise; it is the measurement correctly reporting that the tether requires gorge breathing. That is why the right output is the graded VECTOR_REQUIRES_FLEXIBILITY, not a veto and not a clean pass.

I reject one detail of the med chemist's negative-control claim as stated: my burial analysis is not what flags huperzine A and galantamine — that was the BRENK catalogue, which belongs to withdrawn IDEA-3. The exit-vector module never used BRENK.
revised.final_method:
Two modules, strictly ordered, with the gate removed.

A. platform/cbc/warhead.py — PRIMARY, runs on all 35 candidates today, no structure required. Parse the warhead name and declared formula out of each chemStruct string; resolve the name to a PubChem CID and InChIKey; assert declared formula == resolved formula; then assert the declared coupling chemistry has a reactive handle on the resolved structure via RDKit SMARTS (primary/secondary amine, carboxylic acid, thiol, azide, alkyne, aldehyde, halide). Emit through provenance.py with status DATABASE for the resolution and COMPUTED for the handle census. Where a declared coupling has no handle, emit HANDLE_ABSENT — meaning an unstated synthetic step is being smuggled in — never 'impossible'.

B. platform/cbc/exitvector.py — SECONDARY, measurement only, refuses where no experimental holo complex exists.
  1. Ensemble, not one structure: run EVERY deposited holo complex of the warhead plus available apo structures, report the range and commit the accession list.
  2. SASA via Bio.PDB.SASA.ShrakeRupley with n_points, radii set AND the stripped-heteroatom manifest recorded in provenance.method. Report stripped and unstripped values side by side.
  3. Escape-path BFS (prototype saved at /Users/seunghojung/Documents/DeepMind_Bio/research/exitvector_bfs_prototype.py, runs in seconds): 0.8 A cubic grid, Dijkstra over 26-connectivity, bulk solvent defined explicitly as >7.0 A from any protein heavy atom AND outside the protein convex hull (both parameters recorded, not implicit).
  4. MANDATORY PROBE SWEEP over {1.0, 1.2, 1.4, 1.7, 1.9} A, each with ligand-as-obstacle on and off. Any result not stable across the sweep is labelled PROBE_SENSITIVE and is inadmissible as evidence for anything.
  5. Graded, pose-relative verdicts: VIABLE / VECTOR_REQUIRES_FLEXIBILITY / PARENT_BINDING_MODE_NOT_PRESERVABLE_AT_THIS_ATOM_IN_<PDB>_AT_<resolution>. Never NO_VECTOR.
  6. Primary output is the minimum escape-path length in Angstroms. If a residue count is given at all it is a contour-length LOWER BOUND labelled 'cannot be shorter than', plus a separate flexible-chain estimate — never a single 'needs N residues'.
  7. Steric and pharmacophore findings are reported as separate fields, since losing one H-bond is often recoverable by linker placement and a steric block is not.
  8. NO validate.py failure category. Nothing fails a gate. Retained SASA is demoted to a descriptor.

C. A published false-positive audit is a precondition for shipping either module.
final_success_criteria: POSITIVE-CONTROL SUITE, must pass before the module emits anything: (a) 4EY7 donepezil C28 returns an escape path in [6.5, 8.5] A at BOTH probe 1.4 and 1.9 A (measured today: 7.36 and 7.10 A); (b) 4EY5 huperzine A N2 returns a finite path in [15, 25] A for at least one probe in the sweep (measured today: 18.55 A at probe 1.1-1.3). If the huperzine amine — where the tether is crystallographically resolved in PMID 12517147 — returns NO PATH at every swept probe, the method is refuted and must not ship.

Every reported path is a TABLE over probe in {1.0,1.2,1.4,1.7,1.9} x {ligand-as-obstacle on, off}. A unit test pins the observed instability at 4EY5 HUP N2 (finite at <=1.3 A, NO PATH at >=1.4 A with ligand as obstacle) and asserts the module labels it PROBE_SENSITIVE. Any single-probe path length in any output is a build failure.

A published false-positive audit exists in memory/ BEFORE either module ships, containing in writing: (i) the bis-hupyridone case (PMID 12517147) as a false positive of the retired retained-SASA rule, and (ii) huprine X (CHEMBL208599, Ki 0.026 nM, in data/corpus_ACHE.json) as a false positive of the same rule against the huperzine A pose.

SASA regression test pins BOTH the stripped value (4EY5 HUP 98.47% buried, 6.22 A^2, biopython 1.88, ShrakeRupley n_points=960) and the unstripped value (100.00% buried, 0.00 A^2) together with the explicit stripped-heteroatom manifest, so a library upgrade or a protocol drift fails loudly rather than silently.

warhead.py runs on all 35 candidates and reproduces these three verified failures: BasalNgf-TrkA-B3 declares 'Ginsenoside Rg3 Dammarane Core (C36H62O8)' but C36H62O8 resolves to ginsenoside Rh2 (PubChem CID 119307) while Rg3 is C42H72O13 (CID 9918693); HippoAChE-AlkaPept-X2 declares 'Cys-Lys Amide Coupling' on huperzine A, which RDKit shows has 1 primary amine, 0 carboxylic acids, 0 thiols; HippoDual-TrkB-AMPK-X5 declares a 1,2,3-triazole linker on presenegenin, which carries 0 azide and 0 alkyne. Every candidate gets either a resolved CID+InChIKey with a formula verdict, or explicit NOT_COMPUTED.
grep of platform/validate.py returns ZERO failure categories added by either module, and HippoAChE-AlkaPept-X2 does NOT fail any gate as a result of this work.
Every emitted geometric verdict string contains the PDB accession and resolution, and no output anywhere contains the tokens 'NO_VECTOR' or 'mechanistically void'.

The ginkgolide B / bilobalide assignment question (AstroZo1-Protect-A3 vs AstroPafr-Block-A4 appear swapped relative to the PAF-antagonist literature) is surfaced by the warhead-identity table as a flagged discrepancy for human adjudication, not silently corrected.

revised.title: Evidence-grade activity layer: retract the 2.41 log figure as uninterpretable, and rebuild ground truth as a typed, pinned, pre-specified distribution
revised.changed_what: The diagnosis survives intact and is confirmed; the proposed replacement number does not. Four changes. (1) I withdraw the corrected figure, not just the original. Replacing 5.0 nM with a median is a different aggregation over a badly-typed pool, not a truer number. The correct statement — the computational chemist's — is that with measurements spanning ~4 log units the Boltz-2 prediction of 1274 nM falls INSIDE the experimental envelope, so this compound cannot discriminate model accuracy at all. (2) I own a researcher degree of freedom I exercised in the model's favour: I reported both median (1.43) and geometric mean (1.20) and adopted the median AFTER seeing the outcome, and as the med chemist noted this moves Boltz-2 across the predict-the-mean null (1.644 log RMSE) from worse-than-guessing to better-than-guessing. That choice must be frozen before recomputation. (3) The replacement is now unverifiable and I confirmed it: ChEMBL REST returned an error page and the ChEMBL MCP returned HTTP 500 to me throughout this session, exactly as three critics reported. Publishing a retraction-with-replacement from a live query nobody can reproduce would repeat the original sin. The rebuild is therefore blocked on a pinned offline snapshot. (4) Half my own noise-floor evidence was invalid — see conceded.
conceded: The single-compound error figure is uninterpretable and I withdraw BOTH 2.41 and my proposed 1.43/1.20 replacements. No point error goes in its place.

I chose the aggregator after seeing which way it moved the headline. That is exactly the defect class this layer exists to eliminate, and it is worse than cosmetic because it flips the model's verdict relative to the null.

Two of my four noise-floor examples are invalid. Neostigmine and physostigmine are carbamates — pseudo-irreversible carbamylating inhibitors whose apparent IC50 depends on pre-incubation time — so their spreads are not replicate measurements of one quantity. The DMPK critic is right and this cuts my own E4 in half.

The ML-evaluation critic's statistics reproduce exactly on my machine: pooled within-compound sigma = 0.421 log10, df = 9, 95% CI [0.289, 0.768] over four compounds. Kalliokoski's 0.68 sits INSIDE that interval, so my corpus sigma is statistically indistinguishable from the published figure, not smaller than it. Reporting it as a bare scalar reintroduced false precision.

Worse, and this is my own finding: dropping the carbamates leaves sigma = 0.412 log10 but with df = 5 and a 95% CI of [0.257, 1.010]. This corpus cannot constrain its own noise floor at all. Any empirical sigma I quote from it is uninformative and must be reported as such.

The Kalliokoski sigma needed a locator and now has one — I retrieved the open-access full text this session; the verbatim sentence is 'For heterogeneous biochemical pIC50 data, we find a variability with sigma pIC50 = 0.68, MUE pIC50 = 0.55 and MedUE pIC50 = 0.43', in the Abstract and the Summary and Conclusions section.

The sampling frame is broken and I understated it. data/corpus_ACHE.json records activities_examined = 300 as its denominator; target_activity_count() exists at platform/cbc/corpus.py:182 and is not used for it; iter_target_activities() defaults to limit=1000/page=200 with no ORDER BY, no release id and no retrieval timestamp. Every aggregate is over an arbitrary, non-reproducible slice.
Confidence 9, not 8. Confidence 8 is homologous-single-protein; 9 is directly assigned, which is what my prose actually claimed.

Stereochemistry is not an endpoint class and my clustering would have missed it. The corpus already holds PHYSOSTIGMINE at 14.13-61 nM and (+)-PHYSOSTIGMINE at 9890 nM — a 2.55 log eudysmic gap between two rows a reader could pool. Verified in the file today.
Enzyme source (eel/bovine/Torpedo/erythrocyte assays mapped to CHEMBL220) must be part of the endpoint class and confidence >=9 will not remove it.
The geometric mean is undefined on censored values, so aggregator and censoring rule must be fixed together and in advance.

Cheng-Prusoff: part of the spread is assay design ([S]/Km), not measurement noise, so a sigma pooled across assays with different substrate concentrations is inflated. Records lacking [S]/Km need an explicit 'insufficient metadata' bucket excluded from aggregates rather than silently pooled.
defended: The core diagnosis stands and is now confirmed three ways. I re-verified in source and data today: platform/cbc/corpus.py reads a.get('confidence_score') off the /activity payload, the filter is written 'if conf is not None and conf < min' so a None passes through untouched, and all 27 activities in data/corpus_ACHE.json carry assay_confidence: null while protocol_summary advertises 'assay confidence >= 8'. The denominator's rejection buckets (unparseable 0, tier_excluded 240, no_structure 0, too_large 0) contain no low-confidence bucket at all. The advertised filter has never rejected a single record. That is a live false claim in shipped data and it is the right thing to fix first.

The endpoint-typing finding is correct and the structural biologist independently confirmed its mechanistic basis: the 5.0 nM record used as ground truth is inhibition of AChE-INDUCED amyloid-beta aggregation, a peripheral-anionic-site phenomenon at the Trp286/Tyr72/Tyr124 gorge rim, whereas huperzine A is a catalytic-anionic-site binder assayed by Ellman near Trp86/His447. Scoring a CAS-binder prediction against a PAS-phenotype assay is a category error independent of any statistics. This is not curation housekeeping; without it no aggregate means anything.

I reject the suggestion to soften the retraction into a range over 'defensible reference choices'. Offering three numbers and letting the reader pick reproduces the degree of freedom in presentational form. The honest output is the distribution plus where the prediction falls in it, and an explicit statement that this compound cannot discriminate model accuracy.

Sequencing this before AIML-BENCH-1, CBC-CC-1 and META-3 is correct and I hold to it — all three intend to score models against this corpus and would inherit both the inert filter and the untyped endpoints.
revised.final_method:
Order is mandatory: pin, then freeze, then type, then aggregate, then retract.

1. PIN. Obtain a versioned ChEMBL snapshot to local disk and record release id, retrieval UTC timestamp and verbatim query URLs in the emitted corpus. Every downstream figure must be regenerable with the network off. This is now a hard blocker, not a nicety: ChEMBL REST returned an error page and the ChEMBL MCP returned HTTP 500 for the whole of this session, and three other reviewers hit the same outage independently.

2. FREEZE. Before recomputing anything, commit a hashed, timestamped pre-specification (META-3's mechanism) fixing: aggregator = geometric mean of pchembl_value within endpoint class, median reported as sensitivity analysis; censored records ('>' and '<') excluded from aggregates and reported separately as one-sided bounds; replicate weighting; stereo pooling rule; enzyme-source rule. Then publish whatever falls out, including if it lands back above the predict-the-mean null.

3. FIX THE FILTER AND THE FRAME. Batch-join /assay?assay_chembl_id__in=... to attach confidence_score at threshold >=9. Call target_activity_count() and either paginate to exhaustion or declare the cap as an explicit sampling frame with a deterministic ORDER BY. Regenerate protocol.summary() from the filters actually applied. Retain the metadata currently discarded: assay_description, bao_label, bao_format, data_validity_comment, potential_duplicate, pchembl_value, standard_relation, document_year.

4. TYPE. An endpoint class is the tuple (standard_type, bao_label, readout, STRUCTURAL SITE {CAS catalytic / PAS-aggregation / allosteric / unspecified}, ENZYME SOURCE, STEREO_STATUS {single_enantiomer / racemate / undefined}, KINETIC CLASS {reversible-equilibrium / time-dependent-covalent}). Every row carries a rationale and a citation; the build fails on a row lacking either; a second curator scores a sample and both curators are recorded in provenance.

5. AGGREGATE WITHIN CLASS ONLY, emitting n, geometric mean of uncensored records, median, min, max, log10 range, log-space IQR, and censored count separately. Refuse to pool across differing stereo_status. Refuse to print a spread when n < 3. Estimate any noise floor only from reversible equilibrium inhibitors with matched substrate; carbamates and other time-dependent inhibitors form their own evidence class, excluded from the floor.

6. NOISE FLOOR, HONESTLY. Report the corpus sigma with df and 95% CI, keyed by standard_type so an IC50 aggregate never inherits a Ki sigma, alongside the Kalliokoski reference sigma with its verbatim locator. State plainly that the corpus interval contains 0.68 and cannot discriminate.

7. RETRACT. Publish in memory/ as retraction-with-replacement, where the replacement is NOT a number: the measured distribution (n, geometric mean, median, min, max, log10 range), the percentile at which the 1274 nM prediction falls, and the statement that the prediction lies inside the experimental envelope so the comparison cannot discriminate model accuracy. Link the retraction to the original 2.41 claim and update AIML-BENCH-1, CBC-CC-1 and META-3 in the same commit so the retracted anchor does not survive in three proposals. Make the platform structurally incapable of rendering a per-compound model-vs-measurement error without n and log-range beside it.

8. INHERITED FROM WITHDRAWN MEDCHEM-IDEA-3 — two assay-metadata checks that are better evidenced than any substructure rule: (a) parse assay_description for detergent (Triton X-100, Tween, CHAPS) and carrier protein (BSA) and grade every value from a detergent-free biochemical assay on a high-cLogP poorly-soluble natural product as lower confidence with the stated mechanism 'aggregation not excluded — no detergent control reported'; (b) for each compound-target pair, retrieve any measurement on a readout in a different physical class (radiometric, LC-MS, pH-stat, SPR/ITC) and report present/absent plus log-unit concordance. A value reproduced on an orthogonal readout is exonerated; one with no orthogonal measurement is genuinely lower-confidence.
final_success_criteria: The corrected huperzine A analysis regenerates byte-identically with the network disabled, from a snapshot whose ChEMBL release id, retrieval UTC timestamp and verbatim query URLs are committed alongside it. Until that holds, nothing is published — the live-query figures from the original session are hereby marked unverified, because ChEMBL returned HTTP 500 to every attempt this session.

A hashed, timestamped pre-specification of aggregator, censoring rule, replicate weighting, stereo rule and enzyme-source rule exists in the ledger with a freeze timestamp STRICTLY EARLIER than the first commit of any recomputed error figure. A test asserts this ordering.

The ledger contains a retraction of the 2.41 log claim whose replacement contains NO single error figure — it reports n, geometric mean, median, min, max, log10 range, the percentile of the 1274 nM prediction within the distribution, and an explicit statement that the prediction falls inside the experimental envelope. A test greps the retraction record and fails if it contains a lone scalar presented as 'the error'. AIML-BENCH-1, CBC-CC-1 and META-3 are updated in the same commit.

Rebuilt data/corpus_ACHE.json has zero activities with assay_confidence null (today: 27 of 27 are null) at threshold >=9, and the build fails otherwise. protocol.summary() is regenerated from filters actually applied, verified by a mutation test that changes a filter and asserts the emitted string changes.

Huperzine A / CHEMBL220 resolves to at least two endpoint classes with the AChE-induced amyloid-beta-aggregation record (CHEMBL1771986) excluded from the catalytic-inhibition aggregate BY RULE, and every endpoint-class row carries a structural-site assignment, an enzyme source, a kinetic class, a rationale and a citation, with a second curator recorded. Build fails on any row missing any of these.

Every reported sigma carries n, df and a 95% CI. The layer explicitly publishes that the corpus pooled within-compound sigma is 0.421 log10 (df=9, CI [0.289, 0.768]) over all four replicated compounds and 0.412 log10 (df=5, CI [0.257, 1.010]) over reversible inhibitors only, and states that both intervals contain Kalliokoski's 0.68 so the corpus cannot discriminate its own noise floor. Carbamates are reported as a separate time-dependent class and excluded from the floor.

The denominator reports the true target activity count from target_activity_count(), not the retrieval cap. If the frame is capped, the cap and a deterministic ORDER BY are stated in the emitted file. A test fails if activities_examined equals the page/limit cap while total_count is larger.

Aggregation refuses to pool records of differing stereo_status, demonstrated on the worked example already in the file: PHYSOSTIGMINE (CHEMBL94, 14.13-61 nM) and (+)-PHYSOSTIGMINE (CHEMBL76640, 9890 nM), a 2.55 log gap, must land in separate aggregates.
No model-vs-measurement error can be rendered anywhere in the platform without n and log10 range beside it; a test asserts the renderer raises on an attempt.

Every activity carries a detergent/BSA metadata verdict and an orthogonal-readout concordance field (present/absent, and log-unit agreement where present). No raw value is ever deleted or numerically downweighted; only a labelled evidence_grade with a named mechanism is attached.

revised.title: Interference-by-readout: cross-check reactivity substructures against assay detection chemistry — WITHDRAWN
revised.changed_what: Withdrawn. I tested my own negative control this session and it failed in the way the med chemist predicted, only worse. The module's central mechanism — substructure match driving an evidence downgrade — would penalise the best chemistry in the corpus, and its distinctive join can never fire on the interference mechanism that actually matters for natural products. The two components worth keeping are assay-metadata checks, not substructure checks, and they belong in MEDCHEM-IDEA-2, where I have moved them.
conceded: My negative control was worthless and I proved it. Running RDKit 2026.03.5 PAINS_A/B/C + BRENK + NIH today: BRENK flags huperzine A on isolated_alkene, galantamine on isolated_alkene, and — worse than the critic reported — HUPRINE X on isolated_alkene. Huprine X is the most potent compound in data/corpus_ACHE.json at Ki 0.026 nM. Physostigmine, tacrine and donepezil come back clean only because they happen to lack an alkene. My control demonstrated nothing about the false-positive mode.

Catalogue purpose was conflated. PAINS_A/B/C are frequent-hitter substructures from AlphaScreen counterscreens; BRENK and NIH are reactivity/metabolic-liability filters with no interference semantics whatsoever. Feeding them into one interference verdict was a category error.

The join systematically discards the dominant natural-product interference mechanism. I listed colloidal_aggregator in the mechanism table but mapped Ellman/DTNB only to {thiol_reactive, chromophore}, so no aggregation collision can ever fire. An aggregator passes the module labelled clean — the precise failure the module existed to prevent, and it would hit baicalein, curcumin and salvianolic acid B hardest.

The join is near-constant and therefore near information-free: the AChE corpus is Ellman-dominated so the assay side barely varies, while catechol / Michael acceptor / >=5 phenolic OH fires on essentially every NP polyphenol. A label determined by compound class alone adds a flag without adding knowledge.

The module has no measured operating characteristic. Nothing in the design says how often a COLLISION corresponds to a real artefact. 'evidence_grade downgraded' would have been an opinion rendered as a data field, and the validate.py category would have made it a gate.

The 412 nm chromophore step was an uncalibrated structural classifier inside a module whose whole purpose was to downgrade other people's measurements. For a corpus this small, measured lambda_max values should be retrieved, not predicted.

Absorbance interference is unfalsifiable from ChEMBL metadata anyway, because its direction depends on whether a compound blank was subtracted — a protocol detail essentially never recoverable from the record.

Two hand-written curation tables multiplied together have a combined error rate that is neither table's, and both would have been authored by one person who already knew which compounds they wanted to flag.
defended: I still hold that a bare PAINS flag is the wrong artefact and that contextualising interference by detection physics is the right instinct — several reviewers agreed. But being right about the instinct does not rescue this implementation, and I would rather withdraw it than ship a validated-sounding wrapper around an uncalibrated rule.

I defend the two surviving components as genuinely valuable, which is why I am relocating rather than deleting them: the detergent/BSA metadata check is far better evidenced than any SMARTS, costs nothing, and is the only thing here that addresses the four saponins and two polyphenol conjugates where no PAINS pattern fires at all; and orthogonal-readout concordance is the one output in the original design that is discriminating and checkable rather than a labelled opinion.

One correction to a critic's framing: the module was never going to flag physostigmine, tacrine or donepezil, and those flags were correctly reported as clean. The problem is that the clean set was unrepresentative, not that the substructure results were wrong.
revised.final_method: No module is built. platform/cbc/interference.py is not created and no validate.py category is added. The two defensible components move into MEDCHEM-IDEA-2 step 8, where they operate on assay metadata rather than substructures: (a) the detergent/BSA aggregation-not-excluded check, and (b) orthogonal-readout concordance retrieval. Should anyone revive substructure-based interference flagging later, the preconditions established this session are: split catalogues by purpose so BRENK/NIH can never emit an interference downgrade; include huperzine A, galantamine and huprine X in the negative-control set with an assertion that none is flagged; make aggregation fire from assay metadata rather than SMARTS; replace the conjugation heuristic with retrieved measured lambda_max or emit not_computed; and publish a measured false-collision rate against orthogonal-readout-validated compounds before any grade is downgraded.
final_success_criteria: No platform/cbc/interference.py exists and no interference-related failure category appears in platform/validate.py. Verified by grep.
The two relocated checks appear in MEDCHEM-IDEA-2's criteria and are tested there, so the withdrawal loses no defensible capability.

The withdrawal is recorded in the memory/ ledger with the measured reason: RDKit 2026.03.5 BRENK flags huperzine A, galantamine and huprine X (Ki 0.026 nM, CHEMBL208599, the most potent compound in data/corpus_ACHE.json) on isolated_alkene, so the proposed catalogue set penalises the corpus's best chemistry; and the proposed Ellman readout mapping {thiol_reactive, chromophore} structurally excludes colloidal aggregation, the dominant natural-product interference mechanism.

Any future revival must first publish a measured false-collision rate with a CI and an n against a set of compounds having orthogonal-readout-validated potencies; absent that, no evidence grade may be downgraded by substructure.

refined.expert: Human genetics / statistical genetics (PhD, 16 years; therapeutic target validation via human genetics, MR and colocalization)

revised.title: Indication-anchored genetic evidence layer: a genetics-only rank with a computed denominator, release-and-transcript-pinned retrieval, and an executable Target Product Profile as the join key
revised.changed_what:
Four substantive changes, one of which is a retraction of my own evidence item.

(1) RETRACTION OF E-A3. I claimed LOEUF 0.219 was the gnomAD v2.1.1 value and that Open Targets' 0.123 was v4, and I built the 'two live authorities differ 1.8-fold' framing on that. I re-queried both endpoints this session and it is backwards. gnomAD GRCh38 returns NTRK2 oe_lof_upper 0.21881 with obs_lof 13 / exp_lof 94.46 / mis_z 5.632; gnomAD GRCh37 (v2.1.1) returns oe_lof_upper 0.112 with obs_lof 1 / exp_lof 42.42 / mis_z 3.734. So 0.219 is the LARGER-callset value, and the dataset prose that labels it 'gnomAD v4' is correct. My further claim that 'the dataset names no version' is also false: the NTRK2 record reads 'gnomAD v4 constraint is strong (pLI 1.000, LOEUF 0.219, mis_z 5.63, 13 observed vs 94.5 expected LoF)'. I withdraw both statements.

(2) THE RANK IS NOW GENETICS-ONLY, AND THE DENOMINATOR IS COMPUTED, NOT ASSERTED. All three critics said ranking on the Open Targets overall score is circular. They are right, and it is worse than any of us said. I pulled all 13,289 AD-associated targets (27 pages of 500, 24 s wall clock) and ranked locally on the genetic_association datatype score. The inversion is severe: ACHE is overall rank 7 but has genetic_association = 0 (genetics rank 1606, i.e. outside the ranked set entirely); GRIN2B overall 8 -> GA 0; GSK3B overall 28 -> GA 0; TREM2 overall 29 -> GENETICS RANK 3. The headline denominator is no longer 13,289 but 1,603 (targets with any non-zero genetic_association for MONDO_0004975); 963 reach GA >= 0.1 and 120 reach GA >= 0.5. Of the platform's 16 targets, 13 have GA exactly 0; the non-zero three are TREM2 0.858 (rank 3), NOS3 0.195 (rank 744), NTRK2 0.080 (rank 1037).

(3) THE REWEIGHTING SHORTCUT DOES NOT WORK, AND I CHECKED. I tried to obtain the genetics-only ordering server-side by zeroing the non-genetic datasources. First the query 400s because the argument is `datasources`, not `datasourceSettings` (my own stated risk about field renames, realised within one session). With the correct name it returns 200 but does not do the job: ACHE still ranks 5th with only literature 0.936 and clinical 0.996. The harmonic-sum score does not cleanly decompose by reweighting. The rank must therefore be computed client-side from the full row set, which is better anyway because the denominator's composition becomes something the repo computes and can print rather than something it trusts.

(4) THE NUMERAL REGEX AND THE DRIFT GATE ARE BOTH REPLACED. Measured: target_records prose contains 1,298 numerals across 217 string leaves; a bare-decimal detector would emit ~1,300 violations against human-verified narrative and be suppressed within days. Both the statistical-genetics and ML critics predicted this and both were right. Their proposed replacement (claim-shaped numeral + unit) is sharp on candidates -- scoped to exclude the already-quarantined retracted_claims and provenance subtrees it returns exactly 6 live hits, and all 6 are the fabricated LTP effect sizes (+280%, +310%, +240%, +350%, +420%, +45%), independently reproducing the count the critic reported. But it returns only 1 hit on target_records, because the genetics numbers I actually care about carry no unit. So neither proposed pattern is sufficient. I added a third: a named-quantity pattern (pLI|LOEUF|o/e|score|association|h4|CLPP|mis_z followed within 25 characters by a decimal), which returns 64 precise hits in target_records and is the detector that actually finds the genetics-in-prose problem.
conceded: Ranking on the Open Targets overall score is circular, and I reported it anyway one sentence after naming the circularity. Quantified now: ACHE overall #7 with zero genetic evidence versus TREM2 overall #29 at genetics rank 3 of 1,603. Adopted in full.

The '13,289 associated targets' denominator over-flatters and its composition was unstated -- the same defect I criticise elsewhere. Replaced with a computed denominator of 1,603 whose construction rule is printed alongside every percentile.
My evidence item E-A3 was factually backwards on which gnomAD release produces LOEUF 0.219, and my claim that the dataset names no version was false. Both retracted.

The bare-numeral regex would fire ~1,300 times on legitimate curated prose and would be disabled within a week. Withdrawn, and with it the success criterion 'at least 16 prose_embedded_number failures', which I now see was satisfied by noise rather than by detection.

check_genetic_drift as a build-failing gate makes CI a function of an external service's release cadence and will be widened until inert. Demoted to a scheduled job. All three critics said this independently and they are right.
The TPP gate as specified is satisfied by typing an EFO CURIE -- a field, not knowledge. It needed a provenanced justification and a retrievable association record.
Constraint sitting inside a 'genetic evidence layer' will be read as indication support. It is unsigned and indication-agnostic and must be excluded structurally, not by prose caveat.

A percentile without the score distribution's local shape is misleading. Measured: among the 1,603 non-zero targets, GA at rank 100 is 0.517, at rank 500 is 0.349, at rank 1000 is 0.0895, and the non-zero minimum is 0.0304 -- so NTRK2's rank of 1037 sits in a flat tail where hundreds of ranks separate almost no score.
defended: The framing that gnomAD v2-vs-v4 divergence is 'estimator precision, not disagreement -- LOEUF contracts toward o/e as the callset grows' is wrong for this gene, even though my own version attribution was also wrong. Three live values exist today for NTRK2 LoF constraint: Open Targets 26.06 gives oe 0.0585 / oeUpper 0.123 from obs 5 / exp 85.49; gnomAD GRCh38 gives oe 0.1376 / oeUpper 0.2188 from obs 13 / exp 94.46; gnomAD GRCh37 gives oe 0.0236 / oeUpper 0.112 from obs 1 / exp 42.42. The OBSERVED LoF COUNT differs (1, 5, 13) and the point estimate o/e moves 5.8-fold between the smallest and largest. CI contraction cannot move a point estimate. These are different gene models, transcript choices or filtering regimes, and Open Targets matches neither gnomAD endpoint exactly. So 'store both un-merged, never average' is more strongly justified than before, not less -- but I accept the relabel: this is provenance under-specification, not one authority being wrong, and the stored token must pin transcript as well as release.

Keeping the indication as a REQUIRED typed field, even though it will make the portfolio look bad. Minikel 2024 quantifies support per target-indication pair; with no indication the strongest available prior is uncomputable in principle. The critic who called this 'a governance change presented as a computation' is half right -- it is governance -- but a schema that cannot express the join key of the best-quantified prior in target validation is a scientific defect, not a bureaucratic one.

Not attaching Minikel's 2.6x relative success to individual targets. One critic suggested carrying it as a per-target flag with the published statistic attached; I will carry the binary genetic_support flag but will print the 2.6x only as a population-level statistic with an explicit note that it is not a per-target probability, because a 2.6x badge on a target card is exactly how a population figure becomes a fabricated per-asset number.
revised.final_method:
1) platform/cbc/genetics.py, reusing corpus.py's _ssl_context() (bare urllib raises CERTIFICATE_VERIFY_FAILED on this machine -- reproduced again this session before switching to certifi). POSTs to api.platform.opentargets.org/api/v4/graphql, stores meta{apiVersion dataVersion} (26.6.3 / 26.06 today) in every Provenance.source_id as OpenTargets:26.06:<ensembl>:<mondo>.

2) Rank computed CLIENT-SIDE. Page all rows of disease(MONDO_0004975).associatedTargets(enableIndirect:false) with datatypeScores, cache to a provenanced JSON snapshot keyed by dataVersion, then emit for every target THREE fields: genetic_association_score, genetic_rank / 1603 (denominator = count of targets with GA > 0, recomputed from the snapshot and printed with its construction rule), and overall_rank / 13289 carrying a literal label 'literature/clinical-driven; includes existing-drug circularity'. Server-side datasource reweighting is explicitly NOT used -- verified this session that weight=0 does not remove literature/clinical from the ordering.

3) Constraint stored as a `constraint` field family -- oe, oeLower, oeUpper, obs, exp, callset n, release token AND transcript id -- from each authority separately (OpenTargets:26.06, gnomAD:GRCh38, gnomAD:GRCh37/v2.1.1). The family is structurally excluded from any support score by a whitelist in the scoring function, not by comment. A unit test asserts that no code path reads a constraint field into a support computation.

4) TargetProductProfile dataclass with required indication_id validated against the OT disease resolver, PLUS a required `indication_justification` sub-record {selected_by, evidence, source_id} and a required `indication_association` Value holding the release-pinned genetic_association score for that exact target-indication pair -- zero is a permitted and expected value; absent is not. Typing a CURIE alone no longer passes.

5) audit() gains a str branch with TWO scoped detectors and an explicit per-field allowlist: (a) claim-shaped -- signed percentage or numeral+unit -- scoped to candidate-facing prose excluding retracted_claims.* and *.provenance.*; (b) named-quantity -- (pLI|LOEUF|o/e|mis_z|score|association|h4|CLPP) within 25 chars of a decimal -- scoped to target_records. Both report a COUNT that must be non-increasing across commits; only a regression fails the build. Target records gain a `narrative` field type that audit() exempts by construction, with the extractable quantities required to migrate to typed Values.

6) check_genetic_drift is NOT a build gate. It is a scheduled job emitting a dated diff artefact (old value, new value, both release tokens) and opening an issue requiring a human pin bump, with a cached last-good snapshot so an upstream outage cannot break the build. The only failing build gate is the offline invariant: every externally-sourced Value carries a release token, and the stored value equals what the stored snapshot for that token says.
final_success_criteria: Every one of the 16 targets carries genetic_association_score, genetic_rank/1603 and overall_rank/13289, and the README prints the inversion table showing ACHE overall #7 / genetics unranked (GA=0) beside TREM2 overall #29 / genetics #3, with the 1,603 denominator's construction rule stated on the same page.
Re-running the full pagination reproduces the denominator 1,603 and the 13 zero-GA platform targets exactly, from the cached snapshot, offline, with no network access.
A unit test asserts that server-side datasource reweighting is not used for ranking, by checking that the genetics rank of ACHE is unranked-zero rather than the 5th place the reweighted API returns.

pv.audit() on the rebuilt dataset returns zero UNPROVENANCED numeric leaves, and the two prose detectors report counts (currently 6 claim-shaped in live candidate prose, 64 named-quantity in target_records) that a CI check requires to be non-increasing; a commit that raises either count fails.

Every constraint Value carries release token AND transcript id, all three NTRK2 LoF triples (obs 5/exp 85.49, obs 13/exp 94.46, obs 1/exp 42.42) are stored separately and none is merged or averaged; a test asserts no support-scoring code path reads the constraint family.
Constructing a TargetProductProfile with a valid indication_id but no indication_justification or no indication_association Value raises, and a test proves it.
The drift job produces a dated diff artefact on a simulated release bump and does NOT fail the build; the offline token invariant DOES fail the build when a token is stripped from a stored Value.

revised.title: Direction-of-effect layer anchored on the curated human allelic series, with instrument-species annotation that forbids shed-ectodomain pQTLs from producing a directional verdict
revised.changed_what:
The centre of gravity moved from colocalization sign to the coding allelic series, and the MR extension is withdrawn.

(1) THE SHEDDING OBJECTION IS CORRECT AND IS THE BEST POINT ANYONE MADE. I verified both citations: PMID 28855301 (Thornton et al. 2017, EMBO Mol Med, ADAM10/ADAM17 cleave TREM2 at H157-S158 and the AD-risk H157Y variant accelerates shedding) and PMID 36721205 (Qiao et al. 2023, Mol Neurodegener, Trem2 H157Y knock-in: elevated soluble TREM2, higher soluble-to-full-length ratio, reduced TREM2 signalling). A UKB-PPP plasma pQTL for TREM2 indexes the shed ectodomain, and a variant that raises plasma sTREM2 can simultaneously lower the cell-surface receptor an agonist must engage. My signal (1) would have taken that sign at face value and could have emitted CONCORDANT for a candidate whose direction is inverted. A layer that can be confidently wrong is worse than an honest absence, and mine could have been.

(2) THE ALLELIC SERIES IS THE REAL SIGNAL AND MY FOUR SIGNALS MISSED IT -- BUT IT IS ALREADY CURATED IN THIS REPO. The critic is right that R47H is handled in GWAS and exome studies, not ClinVar Mendelian records, so my signals (2) and (4) return null on the one target that has a genuine answer. What I found on reading data/dataset.json is that the curation already exists as prose in the TREM2 target record: Jonsson PMID 23150908 rs75932628-T p.Arg47His OR 2.92 (95% CI 2.09-4.09) P=3.42e-10 Iceland and OR 2.90 P=2.1e-12 combined; Guerreiro PMID 23150934 22 variant alleles in 1092 cases versus 5 in 1107 controls; gnomAD v4 6-41161514-C-T exome AF 0.00286 (AC 4174 / AN 1461812); biallelic loss causing Nasu-Hakola. So the fifth signal is a MIGRATION of existing per-row-cited prose into typed rows, not new curation -- which makes it the cheapest of the five, not the most expensive.

(3) THE MR EXTENSION IS WITHDRAWN. The critic is right that betaRatioSignAverage is a convenience field and not an analysis, and that I named no LD panel, no ancestry, no effect-allele harmonization procedure, and no Steiger filter. I could specify those, but at the instrument count actually available here the exclusion restriction is untestable and no heterogeneity or Egger diagnostic exists. Writing an MR that cannot be diagnosed would be a number without knowledge. It is removed from this proposal entirely.

(4) THE RUBRIC IS FROZEN BEFORE RETRIEVAL AND THE SUCCESS CRITERIA ARE PROCESS-FORM. Two critics independently said the combination rule is where the whole result lives and that writing it after seeing the data means the verdicts are chosen rather than computed. Correct. And the '34 of 35 UNDETERMINED' criterion is satisfied by a stub that returns UNDETERMINED unconditionally -- an outcome-contingent criterion that inverts what a criterion is for. Both fixed.
conceded: A plasma pQTL is not an instrument for the quantity a TREM2 agonist modulates, and the sign can be inverted by the shedding mechanism. Conceded completely; this changes the design, not just the caveats.
The four signals would have missed the coding allelic series -- the one real directional answer in this target set -- making the layer a guaranteed null-generator that misses its own best case.
No Mendelian randomization was actually specified. betaRatioSignAverage is a retrieved field, not an analysis. The MR path is withdrawn rather than patched.
The success criterion 'UNDETERMINED for at least 34 of 35' is satisfiable by an unconditional stub and is outcome-contingent. Withdrawn.
The concordance rubric was an unspecified free parameter over four heterogeneous partly-missing signals. It must be written out exhaustively and hash-frozen before retrieval.
A blanket gate failing 34 of 35 candidates is a constant after its first run and carries information only in the initial census. Replaced with a non-increasing census metric.
TREM2's per-credible-set sign ratios (+1, -1 and 0) must be published as a list with their h4/CLPP and declared not-determined, never majority-voted.
defended: Building the layer at all, despite it returning UNDETERMINED for nearly everything. With the allelic-series signal added it is no longer a null-generator for the target that matters: TREM2 is genetics rank 3 of 1,603 for Alzheimer's (measured this session), so the single target where a directional verdict is both obtainable and consequential is exactly the one the revised design now covers. The blanket-null objection applied to my original four-signal design and I accept it there; it does not apply to the five-signal design.

Keeping clinical_precedence-derived direction stored but excluded from the genetic verdict, rather than dropping it. It is real information about pharmacological precedent and dropping it loses that; the circularity is handled by field separation plus an enforced exclusion in the scoring function, which two critics agreed was correct.

Reporting per-credible-set signs rather than any pooled scalar, against the temptation to produce a single tidy direction field. TREM2's own signs are non-uniform, and a platform that resolves that by averaging would be manufacturing the exact kind of unearned number this rebuild exists to eliminate.
revised.final_method:
A DirectionOfEffect record per (target, indication) built from FIVE independently provenanced signals, none collapsed into a scalar.

(1) ALLELIC SERIES -- now the primary signal. A hand-curated, versioned, per-row-cited table, built by migrating the existing TREM2/NTRK2 target-record prose into typed rows, curated under the same discipline as corpus.py's InclusionProtocol with a stated admission rule and denominator. Each row: variant (rsID + gCoord), trait direction with effect size and CI and P, functional classification from the enum {hypomorph, LoF-null, GOF, shedding-altering, unknown}, biallelic phenotype where known, and a required PMID per row.

(2) COLOCALIZATION SIGN -- demoted, and gated. Every QTL carries a REQUIRED instrument_measures annotation from {shed_ectodomain, full_length_protein, transcript, splice_isoform}. Hard rule enforced in code: instrument_measures == shed_ectodomain can never contribute to a directional verdict; it may only emit UNDETERMINED with the shedding mechanism and PMIDs 28855301 and 36721205 attached. TREM2's UKB-PPP plasma pQTLs are annotated shed_ectodomain and are therefore verdict-inert by construction.

(3) Open Targets directionOnTrait/directionOnTarget with datasourceId retained, clinical_precedence stored in a separate field and excluded from the genetic verdict by an enforced whitelist.

(4) Constraint direction, read only as a bound on how far inhibition can be pushed, never as indication support (shares GENO-A's structurally excluded constraint family).

(5) ClinVar/eva Mendelian series where the source states LoF or GoF.
