(2) Variance design: three anchor cases (a lone helix, a ~600-token complex, a ~1100-token complex) at n>=10 seeds, five further pairs at n=5 labelled provisional. Report sigma_seed and sigma_sample-given-seed with bootstrap CIs on each sd, separately for mean pLDDT, ipTM and min interface PAE. Keep one arm at diffusion_samples=1 so the 22 legacy deltas stay re-interpretable. (3) MSA factorial, three arms: both chains empty; receptor a3m + peptide empty (the production config); receptor a3m + peptide a3m. Receptor a3m files cached under data/msa/ from the ColabFold MMseqs2 server with a code-level assertion that no candidate sequence is ever transmitted, and a note that third-party-derived a3m files are entering a repository with no LICENSE. (4) Emit sampling_sd as a provenance key strictly distinct from uncertainty; leave uncertainty empty until an accuracy-anchored quantity exists. Add validate.py rules that sampling_sd may never render as an error bar on correctness, and that any PREDICTED value lacking seed, software version, sample count, selection rule and sampling_sd is a violation.
slate.effort: 3-5 days including unattended overnight MPS batches; roughly 60-90 folds at 25-170 s each
success_criteria: A same-seed replicate pair is published as either 'bitwise identical' or a numeric divergence, and no criterion anywhere in the project claims byte-reproducibility on MPS.

Nine sd values — sigma_seed and sigma_sample-given-seed for each of mean pLDDT, ipTM and min interface PAE, across three anchor cases at n>=10 — each with a bootstrap 95% CI. A single sd quoted as applying across all three quantities fails the criterion.
The sample-selection rule is written to a timestamped file before the first batch executes and appears verbatim in every output row.

provenance emits sampling_sd and never uncertainty for PREDICTED structural values; verify_all.py fails if a sampling_sd is rendered as an error bar, or if a PREDICTED value is missing seed, version, sample count or selection rule.
A three-arm MSA table with seed variance partialled out, reporting the receptor-MSA main effect with a CI and stating whether the peptide-MSA arm changes ipTM materially.
slate.panel_score: 5 critiques, value 4.8 / rigour 3.80 / feasibility 4.80 — the highest feasibility on the slate and the only proposal to draw two unqualified ENDORSE verdicts alongside its revisions
slate.consensus_note: The proposer withdrew the byte-reproducibility criterion after five reviewers independently said it was unachievable, withdrew the single-compound Huperzine A retest as unpowered at n=1 before and n=1 after, and conceded that writing an across-seed sd into a field called `uncertainty` reproduces the project's own founding failure one level up. One reviewer wanted the production configuration frozen before any calibration, which is precisely this proposal's function; the chair records that as reinforcement, not opposition. Only residual objection: the msa=empty choice for the chimeras is a modelling decision rather than a fact about the sequences, now handled by making it a measured arm.

slate.title: Hash-locked pre-specification, and one aggregator for the three duplicate affinity benchmarks
slate.one_line: Freeze every protocol, threshold and verdict string to a content hash before the first run, and stop three teams from spending the same weekend of MPS time on the same AChE benchmark.
slate.the_question_it_answers: Was this decision rule chosen before or after the result was seen? The platform cannot answer this for a single number it currently displays. It also cannot answer whether a verdict string is reachable: AIML-BENCH-3 shipped a criterion — Holm-corrected p < 0.05 with K=20 controls — whose smallest attainable adjusted p is 0.476, a check that could never fire, which is the mirror image of the failing-gate-by-design the rebuild already contains deliberately.
slate.scientific_basis: This repository exists because numbers were generated by a procedure whose outcome was fixed by its construction. A pre-registration mechanism is the only structural defence, and it is cheap. The reachability test is arithmetic, not judgement: given K controls and a multiplicity correction, the minimum attainable adjusted p is computable in closed form and can be asserted in CI. Three separate proposals (AIML-BENCH-1, CBC-CC-1, MEDCHEM-IDEA-2) independently specified the same ChEMBL AChE potency benchmark; on one laptop that is a week of duplicated inference.
slate.method_summary: (1) A protocols/ directory: each study writes its population definition, split design, primary metric, decision rule, minimum-n gate and pre-declared minimum detectable effect to a file, which is hashed and committed BEFORE any inference. Every results file carries the protocol hash; verify_all.py fails if a results file's protocol hash is absent from history or if the protocol file changed after the first result was written. (2) A reachability check in CI: for any emitted permutation or corrected p-value, compute the minimum attainable value from K and the correction and fail the build if the verdict string is unreachable — and symmetrically, fail if a check's outcome is fixed to 'pass' by construction. (3) A merge order for the affinity work: one population, one leakage audit, one aggregator, one weekend of compute, three sets of authors. (4) A three-state verdict vocabulary enforced in code — result / not distinguishable from null at n=N / not evaluable at n=N — so 'underpowered' can never be reported as 'no effect'.
slate.effort: 2-3 days of engineering; recovers roughly a week of duplicated MPS time immediately
success_criteria: Every study on this slate has a hashed protocol file committed before its first result file, and verify_all.py fails on a protocol-hash mismatch or a post-hoc protocol edit.

A test computes the minimum attainable adjusted p from K and the correction for every emitted p-value and fails the build when the verdict threshold is unreachable; running it against the withdrawn AIML-BENCH-3 design reproduces the 0.476 floor.
Exactly one affinity benchmark module exists in the repository, with AIML-BENCH-1, CBC-CC-1 and MEDCHEM-IDEA-2 recorded in the ledger as merged into it.
No headline anywhere in the platform is renderable outside the three-state verdict vocabulary; a test enumerates the emitted strings.
slate.panel_score: 8 critiques, value 4.63 / rigour 3.88 / feasibility 4.25 — the highest mean rigour on the slate, with two unqualified ENDORSE
slate.consensus_note: Endorsed by every critic who scored it, and adopted by name inside four other revised proposals, which is the strongest evidence of consensus available here. The chair notes one honest limitation: META-1 scored value 5.0 across five critiques but its revised text was not before the chair in full, so it is not re-specified here; it should be reconciled with this item before either is implemented rather than merged sight-unseen.

slate.title: Construct/numbering registry for all 16 targets, plus the positive-control power floor (2FLU: DockQ 0.675 measured in 50 seconds)
slate.one_line: Establish that this pipeline can place a known peptide in a known groove at all, and write down the receptor construct and numbering offset that every downstream study silently assumes.
slate.the_question_it_answers: When the platform says 'AChE', which residues are those? It cannot answer this today. There is no recorded construct boundary, no deposited-to-UniProt numbering offset, and no chain correspondence — and the proposer demonstrated the consequence: the same epitope comparison yields Jaccard 0.000 without offset reconciliation and 0.944 with it. Second question: can this pipeline, in this configuration, place a peptide in a groove at all? Measured this session for the first time: KEAP1 Kelch + Neh2 16-mer, msa=empty, MPS, seed 1, 49.7 s, DockQ 0.675 (CAPRI medium), fnat 0.975, iRMSD 1.405 A, zero clashes, against the model's own ipTM 0.921.
slate.scientific_basis: A numbering offset is not a footnote; it is the difference between an interface analysis and a random residue set, and it fails silently. The positive control is a power floor, not a calibration: 2FLU was released in 2006, decades inside Boltz-2's 2023-06-01 training window, so its DockQ bounds recall and not prediction. That is still the measurement three critics independently said was missing, because a large post-cutoff calibration curve tells you the scale of accuracy in general while telling you nothing about whether YOUR chain-mapping code and YOUR msa=empty setting can dock a 16-mer. The single datapoint is already informative in a direction that matters: ipTM 0.921 paired with DockQ 0.675 means ipTM is optimistic relative to interface quality on a complex the model has almost certainly memorised.
slate.method_summary: (A) data/positive_controls.json: one row per case with pdb_id, release_date, in_training_window: true, resolution, chain mapping, seed, wall time and scores. 2FLU is already complete and reproduces from one command; extend to 1WWW/2IFG (TrkA-NGF) and 3FXI (TLR4-MD-2). Every case at >=3 seeds, with the DockQ spread reported because at small n the seed spread IS the error bar. Header, README and every emitted record state that all entries predate the training cutoff and that DockQ here bounds recall. Gate rule: if the pipeline cannot reach CAPRI-acceptable on 2FLU, the platform refuses to display candidate interface numbers at all. (B) The registry: for each of the 16 targets, the receptor construct used, domain boundaries, the deposited-to-UniProt numbering offset (e.g. the ACHE 'P22303 minus 31' convention) and the chain correspondence to each deposited entry, with a unit test per target. (C) A measured timing table across the 26-1100 token range, replacing every extrapolation. Already begun: 41-residue lone chain 24-25 s; 301-token two-chain complex 49.7 s. WITHDRAWN from this item: the 16-receptor monomer arm (a sub-angstrom RMSD on 4EY7 measures memorisation) and any calibration curve or ipTM threshold, both ceded to AIML-STRUCT-2.
slate.effort: 3-4 days, mostly curation; the anchor result already exists
success_criteria: data/positive_controls.json exists; validate.py fails the build if any row displaying a DockQ lacks release_date and in_training_window.

The 2FLU case reproduces from one command at >=3 recorded seeds. Pre-registered from the seed-1 run: DockQ 0.675, fnat 0.975, iRMSD 1.405 A, LRMSD 8.208 A, ipTM 0.921, 49.7 s. Success is reproduction of the seed-1 result within the CHAIR-0 tolerance plus a reported 3-seed spread, whatever its size.

No ipTM appears in any output or UI without its benchmark N; below the stated minimum the platform prints 'uncalibrated' and attaches no distribution. Checkable by grepping the reporting layer and by a verify_all.py rule.

The registry resolves construct boundaries and numbering offset for all 16 targets with a unit test each. Hard test for ACHE: the 4EY7 donepezil epitope at a 4.5 A heavy-atom cutoff contains Trp86, Tyr337 and Phe338 in mature numbering.
A measured timing table spanning at least 40, 300 and 550 tokens is committed, and no batch anywhere on this slate is sized from an extrapolation.
No calibration curve and no ipTM threshold is published from this work. A run that emits one is a failed run.
slate.panel_score: 5 critiques, value 3.8 / rigour 2.20 / feasibility 3.80 — the lowest rigour score on the slate, with three DOUBT verdicts
slate.consensus_note: The chair is overruling the scores, and says so plainly. Every DOUBT was aimed at the original proposal's calibration claims — presenting recall on pre-cutoff structures as accuracy, and wiring a recall-derived DockQ distribution behind every displayed ipTM. The proposer conceded all of it, withdrew the monomer arm and ceded the calibration deliverable entirely. What survives scored badly only because it was scored in bad company: the numbering registry is durable infrastructure that no other proposal offers and that three other proposals silently require, and the power floor is now a measured result rather than a plan. Residual dissent, unresolved: two critics still hold that a pre-cutoff positive control cannot license any inference and should be merged out of existence into AIML-STRUCT-2. The chair's ruling is that a power measurement and a calibration curve are different instruments.

slate.title: All-atom physical-validity gate, and a seed-replication measurement establishing that disulfide connectivity is UNDETERMINED and must stay not_computed
slate.one_line: The deliverable is not a set of disulfide assignments; it is the measurement that this pipeline cannot assign them, plus a validity gate that catches the sulfur chemistry the current Ca-Ca check cannot see.
slate.the_question_it_answers: Are the coordinates the platform has already produced physically possible, and is the disulfide connectivity of a cysteine-rich candidate a fact or a coin flip? The platform cannot answer either: data/real_vs_hardcoded.json asserts plausible_protein: true for all 22 structures on the strength of a Ca-Ca distance check alone, which never inspects a side chain.
slate.scientific_basis: Two findings survived a seed-replication test that destroyed the proposal's other claims. First, predicted S-S distances are systematically short in every draw — 1.705 to 1.99 A — against a reference distribution measured over 19 bonds in depositions from 0.48 to 2.35 A resolution (3NIR, 1EJG, 2VB1, 1AB1, 4EY7): mean 2.041 A, sd 0.013 A. Because the sub-angstrom entries, where the data rather than the restraint dictionary determine the model, agree with the 2.35 A entry to 0.013 A, the circularity objection raised by four critics does not apply to this quantity. Boltz-2's values sit 10-25 sd below anything observed. Second, connectivity itself does not replicate below pLDDT ~70: across seeds 1/2/3 the partner of a given cysteine flips between draws, so any single-draw assignment is sampler noise.
slate.method_summary: Freeze the reference distribution before looking at any candidate, built from a high-resolution arm (<=1.2 A) for S-S distance and chi3 and a disulfide-rich arm (knottins, EGF-like domains) rather than only the cysteine-sparse target records, stored with resolution, n and retrieval date. Build platform/cbc/structval.py on gemmi 0.6.5 (already installed): CA chirality via the N-CA-C-CB improper (4EY7 reference -122.63 +/- 3.19 deg over 481 residues, zero sign flips), omega with cis/trans/twisted bands, non-bonded heavy-atom clashes, and sulfur chemistry reported in FOUR bands — anomalously short (<1.95 A), bonded (1.95-2.15), ambiguous (2.15-3.00), non-bonded (>3.00) — with counts quoted at both 2.3 and 2.5 A so cutoff sensitivity is visible. Connectivity by maximum-weight matching over the Sg-Sg graph, never by radius thresholding; a cysteine with competing contacts is 'connectivity undetermined', never 'trivalent'. Validate the detector externally against deposited _struct_conn disulf annotations. Replace the +/-0.5 A Ca-Ca rule at predictor.py:151-160 with one that requires residue-numbering continuity before judging a distance and applies cis/trans omega bands. Then re-fold all cysteine-containing candidates at seeds 1/2/3 (24-25 s each; the whole catalogue is under an hour) and publish per-pairing recurrence fractions and the joint table of S-S band by local SG pLDDT decile. Emission is deliberately minimal.
slate.effort: 1 week engineering plus under an hour of MPS
success_criteria: On the frozen reference set the sulfur detector's recall against deposited _struct_conn disulf annotations is >=0.95, with precision reported; chirality and clash checks report a false-positive rate with n and a resolution histogram.

On 4EY7 chain A the revised Ca-Ca/omega/continuity rule returns zero geometry outliers, classifying Tyr105-Pro106 as a cis-peptide and Pro258->Asn265 (numbering gap 7) and Asp494->Pro498 (gap 4) as chain breaks. Hard pass/fail on three named residue pairs.

A committed table gives, per cysteine-containing candidate at seeds 1/2/3, each pairing's recurrence fraction, its distance in each draw, and both partners' SG pLDDT. Pre-registered prediction: HippoTrk-Saponin-X1 (mean pLDDT 73-79) recovers 1-19, 14-27, 29-38, 43-46 in 3/3; PfcACh-PAM-P1 (mean pLDDT 55-60) recovers no pairing in more than 2/4 draws. If HippoTrk fails to replicate, the confidence-gating hypothesis is wrong and the emission rule is abandoned entirely.

The fraction of S-S contacts below 1.95 A is reported against the reference distribution (n=19, mean 2.041 A, sd 0.013 A) and stated as a property of Boltz-2 v2.2.1 in single-sequence mode, not of the peptides.

data/dataset.json contains at most three PREDICTED disulfide_connectivity values, each satisfying the 3/3-seed and SG pLDDT>=70 gate, and >=28 entries reading not_computed with a named failing check. A run that fills in more than three is a failed run.
The joint table of violation band by local SG pLDDT decile is published with the sign of the association stated — including that it contradicts the proposal's own original claim.
slate.panel_score: 6 critiques, value 4.5 / rigour 3.83 / feasibility 5.00 — the only proposal to score maximum feasibility from every critic
slate.consensus_note: The strongest self-correction in the batch, and the reason it ranks here. The proposer ran the experiment the panel demanded and it destroyed two of three headline claims: the four 'trivalent sulfur' calls were single-draw artefacts, and 'none of this is visible in pLDDT' was measurably false (the 1.705 A contact sits on SG atoms of pLDDT 54.6 and 56.4). Both were withdrawn, the emission step was gutted, and the Engh-Huber arm dropped. The short-S-S finding survived every seed. Remaining disagreement, unresolved: some critics still hold that any reference distribution built from restrained refinement is circular; the proposer's sub-angstrom counter-argument is on the record and the chair finds it persuasive for S-S distance specifically, not in general.

slate.title: Pocket-aligned pose accuracy, physical validity and pharmacophore-contact reproduction on three explicitly-labelled sets: recall, congeneric extension, and receptor-disjoint
slate.one_line: The one benchmark whose first result costs zero new inference and whose design isolates the interpolation premium — the gap between predicting a new ligand for a familiar receptor and predicting for an unfamiliar one.
slate.the_question_it_answers: When Boltz-2 places a small molecule in a pocket on this hardware, how often is the pose right, and how much of that accuracy is memorisation? The platform cannot answer either. It cannot even see the ligand: predictor.py's parse loop skips every row whose label_atom_id is not 'CA', so all 18 HETATM atoms of the existing huperzine model are discarded before any check runs.
slate.scientific_basis: Global Kabsch superposition over all matched CA is the wrong instrument for a 543-residue alpha/beta-hydrolase with a 20 A gorge — receptor fit residual reads out as apparent ligand displacement — and RMSD <=2 A alone hides right-pocket-wrong-orientation, which is exactly the failure a pharmacophore-contact metric catches. The three-set design is forced by Boltz-2's own published validation criteria: all protein chains absent from any training cluster at mmseqs 0.4, ligand Tanimoto <=0.85 to training. Every cognition accession (hAChE, BuChE, MAO-A/B, BACE1/2, TTR) fails that clause by construction, so post-cutoff entries for those targets are a congeneric extension set, not a holdout, and a genuinely receptor-disjoint arm must be drawn separately.
slate.method_summary: Build the all-atom mmCIF parser once, shared with STRUCTBIO-IDEA-1: retain HETATM and non-polymer entities with element, altloc and occupancy, and add interface_contacts(). New platform/cbc/bench/pose.py. Per case: record the chosen chain and ligand instance explicitly, resolve altlocs by occupancy, generate symmetry mates and score against the nearest copy; define the pocket as reference receptor residues within 10 A of the reference ligand; superpose on those residues only; compute symmetry-corrected ligand RMSD with spyrmsd in that frame, plus global-aligned RMSD, receptor pocket CA RMSD, centroid distance and contacted-residue Jaccard at 4.0 A. PoseBusters in redock mode with every check recorded individually and an explicit statement that intermolecular checks run against a co-folded receptor that has relaxed around its own ligand. Three sets, never pooled: (A) recall, 4EY5/4EY6/4EY7, reported as n_ligands=3 n_receptors=1 with no interval; (B) congeneric extension on cognition accessions, two date tiers (63 entries verified available after 2024-01-01); (C) receptor-disjoint, drawn from the 19,260 general post-2024 holo entries at <=2.5 A under Boltz-2's own held-out definition. Reference-quality filter on wwPDB ligand-level RSRZ/RSCC. All intervals are receptor-level cluster bootstraps. Both msa arms. posebusters 0.6.5 and spyrmsd 0.9.0 are already installed with no compiler and no Boost.
slate.effort: 2 weeks engineering plus two overnight MPS batches
success_criteria: The 4EY5-versus-existing-model comparison is produced with zero new inference, as the first result.

A regression test asserts the existing huperzine model parses to 18 ligand atoms whose nearest protein residues include Trp86, Tyr124, Tyr337, Ser203 and His447, and that the named-pharmacophore check passes on it (reference contacts: HUP N2 to Tyr337-OH 3.01 A, to Trp86 CG 3.49 A).

Headline proportions %(RMSD<=2 A) and %(RMSD<=2 A AND PoseBusters-valid) are reported for each of the three sets separately, stratified by receptor UniProt and Tanimoto bin, with receptor-level cluster-bootstrap intervals and both n_complexes and n_independent_receptors printed. A test fails the build if any two sets are pooled or if P22303 and P04058 appear in one proportion.
The interpolation premium — set (B) minus set (C), with its interval — is emitted as a named field.
The recall set carries n_receptors=1 and no confidence interval, and a test asserts none is computed.
Every AUROC is emitted with its CI and n; where the CI includes 0.5 the emitted text is 'no discrimination demonstrated at n=N (CI a-b)' rather than a claim of absence.

The output states verbatim that PoseBusters intermolecular checks were evaluated against a co-folded rather than rigid experimental receptor, so comparison to rigid-receptor docking literature is not like-for-like.
slate.consensus_note: Unanimous ENDORSE_WITH_CHANGES, and the proposer adopted the medicinal chemist's pharmacophore-contact metric as a co-primary — the best single addition anyone made in this round. The proposer also conceded the recall set is three ligands in one receptor from one group on one release date, so no interval may be computed over it. Dissent worth recording: the ML-evaluation critic and the pose author disagree on WHY the 81-entry cognition set is not a holdout (checkpoint-selection window vs training-cluster membership). They reach the same conclusion by different routes; the chair adopts the training-cluster argument as the stronger one and notes the disagreement is about mechanism, not about the design.

slate.title: Leakage-stratified peptide-protein benchmark, serving two functions: confidence calibration AND the power denominator for the candidate screen
slate.one_line: The one study that can tell the platform whether its refusals are principled and whether its candidate screen has any power at all.
slate.the_question_it_answers: Given an ipTM of 0.6 on a peptide-receptor complex predicted on this laptop, what is the probability the interface is right? And: if a genuine binder were in the candidate set, would this pipeline find it? The platform cannot answer either question, which means it currently cannot distinguish 'these designs do not bind' from 'this method cannot tell'.
slate.scientific_basis: The sensitivity panel is the load-bearing half. A screen without a demonstrated true-positive rate produces verdicts that are uninterpretable in both directions; the pilot's own numbers make the point — min interface PAE 16.84 A native vs 16.45 A scramble, against 0.56 A on a genuine complex, is far better explained by 'no interface was placed at all' than by 'the design is not sequence-specific'. On the calibration half, the split design is now anchored to Boltz-2's published validation definition rather than a guess: their checkpoint-selection set is release date after 2023-06-01 and on or before 2024-01-01, n=398, so the original >2023-06-01 filter overlapped it entirely and would have been optimistic by an unquantified amount.
slate.method_summary: Runs after AIML-STRUCT-3, in the frozen configuration. (1) RCSB query with initial_release_date > 2024-01-01 (937 hits verified available; the corrected date costs no sample size). (2) Leakage stratification without mmseqs, which has no arm64 wheel: RCSB publishes clusters-by-entity-40.txt (verified HTTP 200) and the per-entity Data API returns cluster_membership, giving Boltz-2's own 0.4 threshold directly. Every headline metric stratified <30% / 30-70% / >70% identity to the pre-cutoff PDB and never pooled; the >70% stratum is the memorisation control and its size is itself reportable. Exclude post-cutoff re-determinations of pre-cutoff complexes. (3) Curation with a published discard count at each filter: require a UniProt cross-reference on the short entity, strip and flag expression tags (2FLU's Kelch entity begins GSSHHHHHHSSGLVPRGSH), require buried surface area above a stated threshold, discard symmetry mates and crystallisation additives. (4) Size by a stated Wilson half-width target rather than a round number; expect 300-500, one unattended weekend at 1-3 min per complex. (5) Score stratified by partner length: 5-15 residues primarily by binding-site-superposed peptide backbone RMSD (<=2 A acceptable) with DockQ secondary, since fnat is unstable at a handful of contacts; 16-40 residues by both. (6) Fit P(correct | ipTM) by isotonic or logistic regression with a bootstrap band; binned points shown only as an overlay with per-bin n printed. (7) SENSITIVITY PANEL: >=10 solved peptide-receptor complexes through the byte-identical pipeline, each with its own composition-matched scramble set; the fraction of genuine binders whose native beats its own scramble distribution IS the assay's power and becomes the published denominator of every candidate verdict. (8) calibrated_interface_probability refuses on covariate-space distance — a domain classifier over partner length, net charge, composition and presence of designed linkers — not on ipTM bin occupancy, because an in-range ipTM on an out-of-distribution input is still a fabricated probability.
slate.effort: 3-4 weeks including curation, plus one unattended weekend of MPS
success_criteria: Every benchmark entry has initial_release_date > 2024-01-01, verifiable per entry, and the artefact states Boltz-2's training cutoff and its 398-structure checkpoint-selection window with the source.
Every entry carries max_identity_to_pre_cutoff from clusters-by-entity-40.txt, and no pooled metric appears anywhere without its three-stratum breakdown and per-stratum n.
A precision calculation stating the target Wilson half-width and the N it implies is committed before the batch runs; the executed N meets it; every reliability plot prints per-bin n.
Metrics reported separately for 5-15 and 16-40 residue partners, with peptide-backbone RMSD primary for the short stratum.

The sensitivity panel reports one number — the fraction of >=10 genuine solved binders whose native beats its own scramble distribution — and that number is printed as the denominator on every AIML-STRUCT-1 verdict. If it is at or near chance, AIML-STRUCT-1's candidate arm is cancelled rather than run, and the cancellation is published.

calibrated_interface_probability returns 'out of calibration domain' for all 26 unique candidate sequences unless a matched-domain calibration set exists; a unit test asserts the refusal fires for a GGGGS-linked polycationic input.
A count of entries discarded at each curation filter is published, so the benchmark denominator is auditable.
slate.consensus_note: The proposer found and published their own most serious error — the leakage filter overlapped Boltz-2's checkpoint-selection window entirely — and fixed the clustering problem without mmseqs by locating RCSB's precomputed cluster files, which removes the 'budget a day for mmseqs' risk every reviewer had flagged. Also conceded: n=100 could not support the promised threshold, DockQ is the wrong instrument below 15 residues, and the applicability guard was on the wrong axis. Unresolved dissent: one line of criticism holds that a calibration curve whose domain excludes all 26 candidates is not worth building. The proposer's answer, which the chair accepts, is that establishing they fall outside it and refusing to emit a probability on that basis IS the deliverable — but the chair records that this reasoning is one step from unfalsifiable and should be watched.

slate.title: One leakage-stratified potency benchmark for the Boltz-2 affinity head — within-assay Spearman as primary, log10 potency only, never a binding free energy (merges AIML-BENCH-1, CBC-CC-1, MEDCHEM-IDEA-2)
slate.one_line: Measure the affinity head on the task it was actually trained to do, against an experimental noise ceiling reported as an interval, with the training predicate reimplemented exactly rather than guessed.
slate.the_question_it_answers: Does the Boltz-2 affinity head rank compounds better than the per-target median on this class of chemistry, and is any observed error above or below experimental noise? The platform cannot answer this, and worse, it currently mislabels the head's output: the documented conversion (6-y)*1.364 yields pIC50 as a positive magnitude, sign-inverted relative to thermo.kd_to_dg, so at 1 nM it returns +12.28 where the platform's own thermodynamics module returns -12.28. A ledger claim (clm_a47c9774148de980) asserts these are internally consistent. They are not.
slate.scientific_basis: Boltz-2's regression head is supervised on assays curated so the model learns intra-assay rather than inter-assay differences, so pooled cross-assay RMSE is off-task and must not headline. The training predicate is now known verbatim rather than reconstructed — confidence score exactly 9, target type SINGLE PROTEIN, biochemical or functional assays, standard_type in {Ki,Kd,IC50,XC50,EC50,AC50}, PAINS filtered, ligands over 50 heavy atoms discarded — which buys two genuinely out-of-training strata at zero inference cost (heavy-atom-capped natural products and PAINS-flagged compounds). The noise ceiling was recomputed and widened: only 4 of 18 corpus compounds carry replicates, pooled within-compound sd is 0.4206 log10 on df=9 with a chi-square CI of [0.289, 0.768], which contains the literature value, so any claim that this corpus is quieter than the public literature is withdrawn.
slate.method_summary: Frozen under META-3 before any compute. STEP 0, blocking: fix platform/cbc/corpus.py to join /activity to /assay — confidence_score is an assay field, so the guard at line 206 never fires and all 27 activities carry assay_confidence null while the emitted summary string claims 'assay confidence >= 8'; set the threshold to 9; call target_activity_count() (defined at line 182 and never called) so the denominator stops being the limit=1000/page=200 truncation cap; pin retrieval to a local ChEMBL SQLite release from ftp.ebi.ac.uk with release id, SHA256 and timestamp committed, since the REST API is returning HTTP 500. Write a ledger correction superseding clm_a47c9774148de980 and add a verify_all.py rule failing the build if any code path converts affinity_pred_value into binding_free_energy. STEP 1: reimplement the training predicate exactly against the pinned release and label every test compound in_boltz_chembl_predicate true/false/unknown; record in_bindingdb and in_pubchem as unknown unless separately checked, never as false; record stereo-aware and stereo-blind ECFP4 Tanimoto to the predicate set. STEP 2: population defined by measured pharmacology from an Ellman-type catalytic assay, not by ChEMBL's natural_product flag (which labels donepezil and metoclopramide natural products); publish the null RMSE on both populations (1.664 NP-flag, 1.383 pharmacology-defined). STEP 3: Landrum-Riniker aggregation and two ceilings with estimators written out — sigma_single and sigma_single/sqrt(k) — reported as intervals, never lines; carbamates split out as a time-dependent-inhibition subset. STEP 4: random 5-fold (to expose the optimism gap) and Murcko scaffold split, both gated on n. NO temporal split — Boltz-2's only cutoff applies to PDB structures, the affinity corpus carries no date boundary, and a split that implements nothing must not be reported. STEP 5: primary metric within-assay Spearman after per-assay median centring with an assay-level cluster bootstrap; pooled RMSE survives only labelled off-task, against a median null, a 1-NN memorisation baseline and a two-descriptor ridge. STEP 6: every affinity case carries the pose record from AIML-BENCH-2 so error decomposes into wrong-pose versus right-pose-wrong-energy. STEP 7: the 4-run stereochemistry gate first — (-)- vs (+)-physostigmine (27.9 nM vs 9890 nM, same assay CHEMBL644099) and the huperzine enantiomers — noting the corpus SMILES must first be corrected, since (+)-physostigmine has one undefined stereocentre in ChEMBL and is a diastereomer mixture as deposited. STEP 8: binary arm with three separately labelled negative sets — same-target measured inactives (primary), close paralogs, and cross-target shuffle labelled as a reproduction of Boltz-2's own training-time decoy construction where a high AUROC is expected and proves nothing. Write results to measured_in_repo_accuracy; thermo.METHOD_ACCURACY is not touched.
slate.effort: 4-6 weeks; the /assay repair and the ChEMBL pin are the schedule risk, not the compute
success_criteria: A regression test asserts a known confidence-8 assay is rejected at threshold 9 and that a regenerated corpus has no null assay_confidence.
The pinned ChEMBL release id, SHA256 and retrieval timestamp are committed, and re-running the leakage audit offline reproduces every in_boltz_chembl_predicate label bit-for-bit.

A ledger correction supersedes clm_a47c9774148de980 with the worked case y=-3 giving +12.28 vs kd_to_dg's -12.28, and verify_all.py fails the build if any affinity-derived quantity reaches binding_free_energy.
sigma_exp is emitted as {point, ci_low, ci_high, df, n_compounds, n_pairs, estimator_source_code_ref} for both prediction targets, and any plot drawing it as a line fails the build.

The headline is one of exactly three strings: a within-assay Spearman with CI, n_assays, n_compounds and stratum; 'not distinguishable from the per-target-median null at n=N'; or 'not evaluable at n=N'. No bare RMSE is renderable, and every pooled RMSE carries the off-task label.
The word 'temporal' does not appear as a split name anywhere in the emitted benchmark; a test asserts no split keyed on document year exists.
Both null floors (1.664 and 1.383) appear with the population definition that produced each.

The receptor construct is declared verbatim — P22303 residues 32-574, monomeric, aglycosyl, no PAS occupant — alongside the statement that reference measurements were made on native dimeric glycosylated enzyme.
Every refused compound appears with its heavy-atom count and the 50-atom rule cited; salvianolic acid B (52), ginsenoside Rg1 (56) and onjisaponin V (123) are all visible as refusals.
thermo.METHOD_ACCURACY is byte-identical to its pre-project state, asserted by a test.
slate.panel_score: components: AIML-BENCH-1 value 4.63 / rigour 3.63 / feasibility 3.38 (n=8); CBC-CC-1 4.13 / 3.00 / 3.25 (n=8); MEDCHEM-IDEA-2 5.00 / 3.63 / 4.75 (n=8, two unqualified ENDORSE)
slate.consensus_note: Three teams proposed the same AChE affinity benchmark; the chair is merging them by fiat, which all three proposers had already accepted in writing. The two proposers whose text was before the chair each retracted a headline: the ML-evaluation proposer deleted the temporal split outright rather than relabelling it, and the computational chemist withdrew the dG output and the cross-target decoy arm on evidence they retrieved themselves from the Boltz-2 paper. Unresolved between them: whether the 2.41-log Huperzine A error is meaningful. One holds it is an off-task metric on a cherry-picked single measurement; the other holds that AChE is so heavily assayed that the pair is probably memorised, making a 2.41-log error a strong prior against the head. The chair records both and requires the prespec to state the hypothesis so a poor result is not later framed as a surprise. MEDCHEM-IDEA-2's revised text was not before the chair in full; it enters as a named merge partner and its authors must confirm the merged protocol before it is frozen.

slate.title: Receptor-complex prediction of the candidate set, gated on demonstrated assay power, scored as an effect size against seed-matched nulls, and powered only to report a negative
slate.one_line: Close the platform's single largest scientific gap — no candidate has ever been predicted together with its receptor — while stating in advance that this laptop can license a negative and cannot license a positive.
slate.the_question_it_answers: Does any candidate's predicted interface with its declared receptor differ from what a random peptide of the same composition would give? The platform cannot answer this at all: ipTM is 0.00 for all 22 folded candidates because every one was folded as a lone chain, and ipTM is undefined for a single chain.
slate.scientific_basis: A raw ipTM has no reference distribution, so an empirical null is the right instinct; the pilot's isolated 0.735 from a random shuffle is exactly what one noise draw looks like at sigma ~0.13, and would have read as a hit. But the original design could not have produced its own stated result: with K=20 controls the smallest attainable empirical p is 1/21 = 0.048, and Holm across ten candidates puts the floor on the smallest adjusted p at 0.476. The family-wise p-value is therefore dropped for a standardized effect size with a bootstrap CI. The nulls are also rebuilt: a Fisher-Yates shuffle preserves MW, charge, pI and GRAVY (verified: 300 seeded shuffles leave every PeptideReport field bit-identical) but destroys hydrophobic moment and heptad periodicity, so the naive test asks 'does amphipathic helicity matter', not 'is this design sequence-specific'.
slate.method_summary: GATED on AIML-STRUCT-2's sensitivity panel; if the pipeline does not recover genuine binders above chance, the published output is 'pipeline not demonstrated competent on this receptor class' and the candidate arm is cancelled. (0) Prerequisite patch, landed first: predictor.py:392-398 scans only the top-left 60x60 block of the PAE matrix, so for a 543-residue receptor followed by a 36-mer it never looks at the interface; fix it to sample the explicit inter-chain block and make the asymmetry rule scale-relative, firing only when |PAE_ij - PAE_ji| is large relative to the mean AND both entries are below ~10 A — derived from PAE's saturation near 30 A, not fitted to make real complexes pass, and scored as a classifier against regenerated legacy trigonometric matrices with published TPR/FPR. Also record the full pair_chains_iptm matrix and state which orientation the headline reports (verified asymmetric: [0][1]=0.4396, [1][0]=0.7136, and the scalar equals the larger, making the current headline an undocumented max-statistic). (1) Deduplicate 35 records to 26 unique sequences with code-to-sequence mapping in every row; descope the primary set to 10. (2) Compartment gate before any compute: UniProt subcellular-location check marks extracellular-peptide-versus-cytoplasmic-target pairs excluded; no effect size is rendered for an excluded pair, though it may run as a labelled probe. (3) Seed-matched paired design: native at 3 seeds, each of 8 scrambles and 3 off-target receptors at the SAME 3 seeds; 360 runs, ~18-20 h at the measured rate, with large receptors timed first. Analyse with sequence as the unit and seed as the within-unit replicate. (4) Three nulls, each answering a named question and reported separately: composition shuffle (does order carry information); class-preserving permutation within hydrophobic and within polar residues, preserving heptad periodicity and hydrophobic moment (is this more than any amphipathic helix of this composition); and an off-target receptor panel, PROMOTED to primary specificity statistic, size-matched within +/-20% and including a near-neighbour. Eisenberg hydrophobic moment recorded as a covariate on every scramble. (5) Primary readout is native mean minus decoy mean over decoy sd, with a bootstrap CI and the full null distribution published; any candidate whose native exceeds all decoys is flagged 'requires a dedicated K>=200 follow-up, not run here' rather than declared specific. (6) Every verdict printed next to the power fraction and a same-batch positive control. Free controls kept: one 41-mer declared against both alpha7 nAChR and TLR4/MD-2, one 36-mer declared against AChE under three names, and the Keap1-directed sequence embedding DEETGEFL — the exact Neh2 degron — as an internal near-positive control.
slate.effort: 3 weeks engineering plus ~20 h MPS, conditional on the gate opening
success_criteria: The verdict rule is written to a timestamped file before execution; a fixture containing a known-binding pair flips the verdict, demonstrating the rule can fire in both directions.

A table of 26 unique sequences (not 35 records) with code-to-sequence mapping, giving native mean +/- sd over 3 matched seeds, each of three null distributions separately, a standardized effect size with bootstrap CI, and min interface PAE. No family-wise p-value is presented as a primary result.
Every row prints the sensitivity panel's power fraction and a same-batch positive control's scores.
Compartment-excluded pairs appear with no effect size rendered; a test asserts that rendering one fails validation.

The PAE-asymmetry check samples the inter-chain block, does not fire on the genuine 601x601 two-chain matrix (full-matrix asymmetry 20.30 A, confident-region asymmetry 8.02 A, median 0.710), still fires on regenerated legacy trigonometric matrices, and publishes its TPR/FPR.
predictor.py stores both off-diagonal pair_chains_iptm entries, not just the larger; a test asserts it.
Reported wall-clock is within a factor of 1.5 of a pre-declared estimate built from a timed large-receptor case, not extrapolated from the smallest.
slate.panel_score: 7 critiques, value 5.00 / rigour 3.14 / feasibility 3.71 — the highest value score of any proposal and among the lowest rigour, which is exactly why it is gated rather than dropped
slate.consensus_note: Four reviewers independently identified the fatal defect (no positive control) and the proposer conceded it using their own pilot as the evidence against themselves. Also conceded: the p-value floor arithmetic, the variance mismatch between a 5-seed native median and single-seed decoys, the scramble's failure to match hydrophobic moment, the 35-versus-26 inflation, and a 2x compute error. The proposer defended the empirical-null instinct and the chair agrees. AIML-BENCH-3 was withdrawn into this proposal and hands over its three-level control taxonomy and cross-declaration control. Unresolved: the computational chemist would spend zero MPS hours on candidate co-folding until power is proven; this proposer would spend twenty. The gate is the chair's resolution and neither party is fully satisfied by it.

slate.title: The adequately powered sequence-specificity test — ranked on merit, honestly labelled as not runnable on this machine
slate.one_line: The experiment that could actually license a positive claim about a candidate needs roughly 100 GPU-hours and a full-MSA arm, and this laptop cannot provide either.
slate.the_question_it_answers: Is any specific candidate sequence-specific for its declared receptor, at a significance level that survives multiplicity across the catalogue? Nothing on the affordable slate can answer this. Rank 9 is explicitly powered to report 'the design lies inside its decoy distribution' and explicitly not powered to license a positive.
slate.scientific_basis: An empirical permutation p of 0.05 or better requires K>=199 controls per candidate before any correction; ten candidates at three seeds is roughly 2,000 two-chain co-folds, about 100 hours of MPS at the measured rate, and that is before the MSA arm, which roughly doubles the count and is slower per run. Single-sequence mode is a known accuracy penalty and is itself a candidate explanation for every negative the affordable slate will produce, so a properly powered test must run with receptor MSAs to be interpretable. Neither the K nor the MSA arm fits on this hardware. AlphaFold3 is not an alternative: it requires Linux and CUDA 8.0+, its weights are request-only and non-redistributable, and the AlphaFold Server's terms prohibit automated binding prediction.
slate.method_summary: Identical design to rank 9 — seed-matched paired nulls, three null classes, off-target panel as primary specificity statistic, effect size with bootstrap CI — but at K>=199 per candidate across all 26 unique sequences, with receptor MSAs on both chains as a factorial arm, and with a pre-registered per-candidate significance rule that is reachable at that K. Requires a single CUDA node for roughly one week, or an equivalent rented allocation. The chair's recommendation is that this is NOT commissioned until ranks 1-9 are complete: if the sensitivity panel shows the pipeline lacks power on this receptor class, buying GPU time buys a better-resolved measurement of nothing.
slate.effort: ~100-250 GPU-hours plus 2 weeks analysis; not schedulable on the current hardware at any effort level
success_criteria: A per-candidate empirical p-value whose achievable minimum, given K and the multiplicity correction, is below the threshold it is compared against — checked mechanically by the META-3 reachability test before the batch runs.

Both single-sequence and receptor-MSA arms reported, with the MSA main effect on the specificity statistic given with a CI, so a negative can be attributed to the design rather than to the configuration.
All 26 unique sequences included, not a descoped subset, with the off-target receptor panel as the primary specificity statistic.
Every result carries the same-batch positive control and the sensitivity-panel power fraction, exactly as at rank 9.
slate.panel_score: not separately scored; constructed by the chair from AIML-STRUCT-1's own concessions and AIML-BENCH-3's withdrawal arithmetic (the two proposals whose compute analyses established the requirement)
slate.consensus_note: Listed because the brief demands honesty about what the hardware cannot buy, and because the withdrawal of AIML-BENCH-3 would otherwise leave the impression that the powered test is unnecessary rather than unaffordable. No panellist proposed it in this form; both proposers who costed it concluded it was out of reach and one used that arithmetic as grounds for withdrawal. The chair's position is that 'we cannot afford the decisive experiment' is a finding the project should publish rather than route around.

slate.title: Falsify PRODIGY on this catalogue in one afternoon: measure whether its predicted dG can vary across candidates against a common receptor at all
slate.one_line: A decisive negative result available today for the price of an afternoon, replacing 'no calculation has been performed' with a measured refusal that names the number that disqualified the method.
slate.the_question_it_answers: Can any runnable free-energy method rank these candidates? binding_free_energy is not_computed for all 35 candidates with the stated reason 'no calculation has been performed' — which records an absence of effort, not an absence of knowledge. The platform cannot currently say whether the field is empty because the work was not done or because no available method can fill it.
slate.scientific_basis: Measured this session on 2FLU with prodigy-prot 2.4.0: dG -8.668 kcal/mol, Kd 4.39e-7 M, decomposing as interface terms ic_cc -0.568, ic_ca -1.501, ic_pp +0.392, ic_pa -1.814 (sum -3.491) against non-interacting-surface terms nis_a +8.067, nis_c +2.699 (sum +10.766) and intercept -15.9433. The NIS terms carry 3.1x the magnitude of all four interface terms combined, and prodigy.py:159 computes SASA on the whole complex, so for a fixed receptor they are a receptor constant. For a 543-residue AChE plus a 36-mer the peptide is 6% of residues and the NIS percentages barely move; the entire candidate-varying signal is an interface-contact sum whose full magnitude here is under two method-RMSEs (1.89 kcal/mol). This is a falsifiable prediction about the method, and it is cheap to test.
slate.method_summary: Stage A only; Stage B (the Kastritis transfer benchmark) is not commissioned. (A1) Two-venv architecture, forced by a measured dependency conflict: prodigy-prot 2.4.0 declares numpy>=2 while boltz 2.2.1 declares numpy<2.0, and installing prodigy into .venv312 silently upgraded numpy to 2.5.2 and broke the pinned Boltz environment. Interface is a PDB in, a JSON out. A verify_all.py check fails if both are importable from one interpreter. (A2) Receptor-constancy test: thread the 26 DISTINCT candidate sequences onto the peptide chain of a deposited receptor-peptide complex with fixed backbone and run PRODIGY on all 26, recording min/median/max predicted dG and the interface/NIS split for each. If the spread across 26 different peptides is smaller than the method's own 1.89 kcal/mol RMSE, PRODIGY cannot rank this catalogue and the arm closes with a measured refusal. (A3) Charge-confound test, free: correlate the 26 predicted values against net charge at pH 7.4 from platform/cbc/peptide.py; if |r| > 0.8 the contact count is rediscovering a property the platform already reports. (A4) Seed-stability on the few peptide-in-groove complexes this project can name: if predicted dG scatters across seeds by more than 1.89 kcal/mol on a complex whose answer is known, no further compute is justified.
slate.effort: 1 afternoon plus a day of write-up; no Boltz runs required for Stage A
success_criteria: Two venvs exist and a verify_all.py check fails if prodigy-prot and boltz are importable from the same interpreter, with the conflicting numpy pins recorded in provenance.

The 2FLU decomposition is reproduced by a committed script and recorded in the ledger: dG -8.668, interface sum -3.491, NIS sum +10.766, intercept -15.9433, with the whole-complex SASA call at prodigy.py:159 cited as the reason NIS is receptor-constant.

The 26-sequence receptor-constancy scan reports min/median/max predicted dG and the interface/NIS split per sequence, over 26 distinct sequences with a sequence_group id making the 9 redundant dataset rows visible.
The predicted-dG versus net-charge Pearson r is reported with its CI, whatever its value.

Every candidate's binding_free_energy note is rewritten from 'no calculation has been performed' to either a value with its measured error or a refusal quoting the specific number that disqualified the method.

Every candidate carries either a receptor assignment with a UniProt accession and residue range, or an explicit no_receptor_assignable record stating why — including compartment-excluded for extracellular peptides aimed at cytoplasmic targets.
slate.panel_score: 7 critiques, value 3.86 / rigour 3.14 / feasibility 2.57 — the lowest feasibility on the slate, which applied to the withdrawn Stage B and not to Stage A
slate.consensus_note: Ranked last because its value is bounded — the most likely outcome is a refusal — but included because the cost is an afternoon and a measured refusal is strictly better than the current empty field. The proposer withdrew the Kastritis co-folding benchmark as under-costed and partly in-sample, and conceded that recovering r=-0.73 / RMSE 1.89 on the eLife 81-complex set reproduces a TRAINING fit and licenses nothing. They also conceded the 2.0 kcal/mol pre-registered gate was beatable by a constant predictor. One DOUBT verdict stands against the whole item; the chair keeps Stage A because its own author designed it to kill their own proposal, which is the behaviour this panel should reward.

withdrawn_and_why: AIML-BENCH-3 (composition-matched scramble control) — withdrawn by its own author. With K=20 controls the smallest attainable empirical p is 1/21 = 0.048, and Holm across ten candidates puts the floor on the smallest adjusted p at 0.476, so the verdict string 'sequence-specific (Holm-corrected p < 0.05)' was unreachable regardless of what the folding showed. A check whose outcome is fixed by its construction is the exact failure this repository exists to remediate, merely inverted from one that cannot fail into one that cannot fire. Three handovers survive into rank 9: the three-level control taxonomy, the cross-declaration specificity control, and the shipped zero-compute unit test showing 300 seeded shuffles leave every PeptideReport field bit-identical.

CBC-CC-3 (disulfide-isomer folding with an OpenMM implicit-solvent filter) — withdrawn by its own author. Two independent fatal defects: combining a min/median/max range over distinct chemical species in quadrature with a method RMSE produces a number with no distributional interpretation, and Amber14/GBn2 with no explicit ions under-screens electrostatics for peptides up to +8 net charge, so the filter's failure mode runs one way and it would have returned 'survives' for everything. Compounded by a 2x-plus compute underestimate and by an enumeration that missed the two 9-Cys candidates (945 maximal pairings each). What survives is a deterministic chemical-definition audit and two code-level refusals, folded into rank 8's Step 0.

The 16-receptor monomer arm of STRUCTBIO-IDEA-2 — a sub-angstrom RMSD on 4EY7 measures memorisation of a 2012 deposition, consumed most of the effort, and would have invited exactly the wrong inference about a platform whose task is peptide placement.

pDockQ, from STRUCTBIO-IDEA-3 — dropped entirely, not flagged. Its coefficients would have been reconstructed from memory, which is the prohibited act, and transferring an AlphaFold2-Multimer-fitted sigmoid to Boltz-2 confidences stacks a second error on the first.

The temporal split in the affinity benchmark — deleted rather than relabelled. Four reviewers asked for it to be renamed a publication-year proxy; the Boltz-2 paper shows there is nothing to proxy, since its only cutoff applies to PDB structures and the PubChem/ChEMBL/BindingDB affinity corpus carries no date boundary. A labelled-but-meaningless number still invites comparison.

The dG output of the Boltz-2 affinity head, and its ledger claim of internal consistency with thermo.py — the documented conversion yields pIC50 as a positive magnitude, sign-inverted relative to kd_to_dg, so the platform's own dG < -18.3 implausibility guard could never have fired on it.

Cross-target decoy AUROC as a primary binary-classification metric — the construction reproduces Boltz-2's own training-time synthetic-decoy generation (1.2M decoys, Tanimoto <0.3 to known binders of similar proteins), so it would have measured memorised training behaviour and reported it as discrimination. Retained only as an explicitly labelled control.

Stage B of CBC-CC-2 (the Kastritis co-folding transfer benchmark) — dozens to 144 complexes of 300-900 residues at roughly N-squared pair-representation cost is multi-day at best on MPS and may exhaust unified memory.

The byte-reproducibility success criterion — seeding fixes the noise draw, not floating-point reduction order on Metal, and the documented aten::linalg_svd CPU fallback breaks bitwise determinism outright. Replaced by a measured same-seed divergence tolerance.

Two of three headline claims in STRUCTBIO-IDEA-1 — 'four candidates have a trivalent sulfur' (single-draw artefact; the flipping partner changes across seeds 1/2/3) and 'none of this is visible in pLDDT' (measurably false; the 1.705 A contact sits on SG atoms of pLDDT 54.6 and 56.4). Withdrawn by the author after running the replication the panel demanded.
consensus.sequencing_logic:
The order is set by three rules applied in sequence, and only then by value-per-hour.

FIRST: nothing is measured until the measurements can survive a reboot. Rank 1 is not a scientific study; it is the discovery that `git ls-files platform data` returns zero and that the only copies of all 22 Boltz predictions are 1.8 MB sitting in /tmp. Six proposals pin success criteria to those files, and one had to declare its own criterion unsatisfiable because 'committed' is currently impossible. Custody costs a day and every other rank depends on it. That no proposer ranked it first is itself a finding about how the panel allocates attention.

SECOND: measure the instrument before measuring with it. Rank 2 fixes and characterises the inference configuration — same-seed divergence, a two-level variance decomposition reported separately for pLDDT, ipTM and interface PAE, MSA as a controlled factor — because every downstream study interprets differences in exactly those quantities, and the panel has so far interpreted a 10-46 unit pLDDT delta and a 0.735 ipTM outlier without knowing the envelope of either. Rank 3 (prespec freeze) sits beside it for the same reason at the level of protocol rather than physics: it is cheap, it makes every later claim auditable, and it immediately recovers a week of MPS time by collapsing three duplicate affinity benchmarks into one. Rank 4 supplies the construct boundaries and numbering offsets that ranks 5-9 all silently assume — the failure mode there is not noisy, it is a Jaccard of 0.000 that looks like a scientific result — and establishes, as a measured fact rather than an assumption, that this pipeline can dock a known peptide into a known groove.

THIRD: cheap work that closes a claim outranks expensive work that opens one. Ranks 5 and 6 both produce their first results with zero or near-zero new inference (a validity gate over structures already on disk; a pose comparison against an existing huperzine model) and both convert an unsupported assertion into either a measurement or an honest not_computed. Ranks 7 and 8 are the two real benchmarks, each a multi-week build with an unattended weekend of compute, and each is the denominator for something downstream: rank 7's sensitivity panel is the power fraction printed on every candidate verdict, and rank 8's noise ceiling is the reference against which any potency error is judged.

Rank 9 — co-folding the candidates with their receptors — has the highest value score in the entire batch (5.00) and among the lowest rigour (3.14), and it is placed ninth for a single reason: it is a screen, and a screen whose true-positive rate is unknown produces verdicts that are uninterpretable in both directions. Its own pilot demonstrates this better than any critique did. It runs only if rank 7's sensitivity panel opens the gate, and if the gate stays shut the published output is 'pipeline not demonstrated competent on this receptor class', which is a result.

Rank 10 breaks the value-per-cost ordering deliberately, on instruction. The experiment that could actually license a positive claim about a candidate needs K>=199 controls and a full-MSA arm — roughly 100-250 GPU-hours — and no amount of effort makes it fit on this MacBook. It is listed on merit, labelled needs-gpu, and explicitly recommended NOT to be commissioned until rank 7 reports, because buying GPU time before power is demonstrated buys a better-resolved measurement of nothing.

Rank 11 is last on value, not on efficiency: an afternoon that most likely ends in a measured refusal. It is included because 'binding_free_energy: not_computed, no calculation has been performed' records an absence of effort, and this project's standard is that an empty field must record an absence of knowledge with the number that produced it.
panel_disagreements: Whether the 2.41-log Huperzine A error means anything. The ML-evaluation proposer now holds it is an off-task metric on a single cherry-picked measurement and retired it as motivation for their own benchmark. The computational chemist holds that AChE is among the most heavily assayed ChEMBL targets, so the pair is more likely memorised than not, making a 2.41-log error a strong prior against the head performing here. Unresolved. The chair's ruling is procedural only: the prespec must state the hypothesis in advance so a poor result cannot later be framed as a surprise.

How much of the AChE benchmark's difficulty is manufactured by ChEMBL's noisy natural_product flag. The medicinal chemist said pralidoxime, metoclopramide and ranitidine 'create most of the variance'. Measured: removing all three moves the null RMSE from 1.664 to 1.383 log10, a 17% reduction, while the surviving 14 compounds still span 5.6 log units. Direction agreed, magnitude disputed. Both numbers are published side by side and neither party concedes.

Whether a pre-cutoff positive control has any evidential standing. Two critics hold that a benchmark entirely inside Boltz-2's training window measures recall and should be merged out of existence into the post-cutoff calibration set; three hold that a power floor and a calibration curve are different instruments, and that knowing a large post-cutoff curve exists tells you nothing about whether YOUR chain-mapping code can dock a 16-mer. The chair sided with the second group and overruled a rigour score of 2.20 with three DOUBT verdicts to do it. This is the chair's most contestable ranking decision on the slate.

Whether any MPS time should be spent co-folding candidates before power is demonstrated. The computational chemist would spend zero hours; the ML-for-structural-biology proposer would spend twenty. The gate at rank 9 is the chair's compromise and satisfies neither of them fully.

Whether refusing to emit is a deliverable or an evasion. One proposer argues that establishing the candidates fall outside the calibration domain, and refusing to emit a probability on that basis, IS knowledge. The chair accepts this but records the objection plainly: the argument is one step from unfalsifiable, and a platform that can only ever refuse has not been distinguished from a platform that cannot compute.

Whether a reference distribution built from restrained refinement can validate a diffusion model's geometry. Four critics called this circular. The structural biologist answers, for S-S distance specifically, that sub-angstrom depositions where the data rather than the dictionary determine the model agree with 2.35 A entries to 0.013 A over 19 bonds. The chair finds this persuasive for S-S distance and not for the general claim; the critics have not conceded.

Why the 81-entry cognition set is not a holdout. The ML-evaluation critic argues from Boltz-2's checkpoint-selection window; the pose author argues from training-cluster membership at 0.4 identity. They reach the same conclusion by incompatible routes, and neither has retracted. The chair adopts the training-cluster argument as the stronger one without claiming the other is wrong.

Whether msa=empty for the GGGGS-linked chimeras is a modelling decision or a fact about the sequences. The motif_provenance records 16 motifs with exact UniProt matches, so the parent motifs demonstrably have homologues; what has no homologues is the chimera as a whole. Whether a peptide MSA would help or mislead is genuinely unknown and has been converted into a measured arm rather than argued further.

Whether the 32 items a verifier marked 'unretrieved — must not be implemented' should stay unimplemented indefinitely. The rule has now correctly blocked pDockQ, CNS MPO breakpoints and PRODIGY coefficient reconstruction. But the panel did not agree on whether the correct remedy is permanent abstention or retrieval from primary sources, and the CBC-CC-2 author demonstrated the latter works — reading the IC-NIS coefficients off disk in one minute settled a dispute where two independent memory retrievals had produced sign-flipped forms. The chair's view, not unanimous: abstention is the default and retrieval is always preferable to it.

Version control. No proposer treated the absence of platform/ and data/ from git as a blocker; one noted it in passing as making a success criterion unsatisfiable. The chair is asserting it as rank 1 over an implicit panel consensus that it was a housekeeping matter.
what_the_panel_would_not_do: Reconstruct a published equation's coefficients from memory. This blocked pDockQ (dropped entirely rather than flagged), CNS MPO desirability breakpoints, and some PRODIGY regression coefficients. The demonstration is on the record: two independent memory retrievals of the IC-NIS coefficients produced mutually sign-flipped forms, and reading them off disk took one minute. Retrieval from a primary source is always preferable to abstention; abstention is always preferable to recall.

Emit a binding free energy from the Boltz-2 affinity head. The documented conversion yields pIC50 in kcal/mol as a positive magnitude, sign-inverted relative to thermo.kd_to_dg — at 1 nM, +12.28 versus -12.28 — and the head is trained on pooled Ki/Kd/IC50/EC50/AC50/XC50, so its output has no defined thermodynamic referent. A verify_all.py rule now fails the build on any such code path.

Promise byte-reproducibility on MPS. Seeding fixes the noise draw, not floating-point reduction order on Metal, and there is a documented aten::linalg_svd CPU fallback in the loss path. A reproducibility criterion that is quietly relaxed later is how reproducibility criteria get discredited. Measure the divergence and adopt it as the tolerance.

Report a split that implements nothing. The affinity temporal split was deleted, not relabelled: Boltz-2's only cutoff applies to PDB structures and the affinity corpus carries no date boundary. A number labelled 'temporal holdout' still invites the comparison even with a footnote attached.

Emit a p-value whose achievable minimum, given K and the multiplicity correction, exceeds the threshold it is compared against. A check that cannot fire is the same defect as a check that cannot fail. This is now enforced arithmetically in CI.

Calibrate on structures inside the model's training window and call the result accuracy. Every entry in the original positive-control panel predates the 2023-06-01 cutoff by years to decades. DockQ there bounds recall. Wiring a recall-derived distribution behind every displayed ipTM would install an optimistically biased number as the platform's official uncertainty claim — worse than admitting it is uncalibrated.

Populate a field named `uncertainty` with an across-seed standard deviation. Repeatability is not accuracy: a tightly reproducible but systematically wrong prediction would render as high-confidence. The value goes in `sampling_sd`, and a test fails if it is ever rendered as an error bar on correctness.

Let a single-trajectory MM-GBSA number reach binding_free_energy. These are 26-100 residue polycations forming no congeneric series, and the 2.5 kcal/mol figure in METHOD_ACCURACY is explicitly scoped to relative ranking within a congeneric small-molecule series.

Fill a not_computed field to make the dataset look complete. Thirty-five candidates lack binding_free_energy, dissociation_constant, pLDDT and hERG. The slate replaces empty fields with measurements or with refusals that name the disqualifying number — never with an estimate presented as a result. Rank 5 caps PREDICTED disulfide_connectivity at three entries and treats a run that fills more as a failed run.

Report a global-superposition ligand RMSD in a 20 A gorge. Receptor fit residual reads out as apparent ligand displacement on a 543-residue alpha/beta-hydrolase. Pocket-aligned, symmetry-corrected RMSD only, with the global figure kept as a separate labelled column.

Report a cross-target shuffle AUROC as evidence of discrimination. That construction reproduces Boltz-2's own training-time synthetic-decoy generation almost exactly, so a high score is expected and proves nothing about generalisation.

Treat 35 candidate records as 35 independent tests. There are 26 unique sequences; one 36-mer appears three times, one 41-mer appears three times, and five further sequences twice. Nine of thirty-five 'candidates' are copies, and that is itself a dataset correction to publish.

Run AlphaFold3, or claim AF3 provenance for anything. It needs Linux and CUDA 8.0+, its weights are request-only and non-redistributable, and the AlphaFold Server's terms prohibit automated binding prediction. Boltz-2 (MIT, code and weights) is the substitute and is named as such in every record.

Re-derive a fraud detector's threshold from the data it polices. The PAE-asymmetry rule is derived from PAE's saturation behaviour near 30 A and then scored as a classifier against regenerated legacy trigonometric matrices, with published TPR/FPR — not tuned until real complexes pass.

Retire the composition-derived liability flags because a scramble reproduces them. Order-invariance does not mean the value carries no design information: composition is a design choice, and the amphipathic, polycationic, KLVFF and odd-cysteine flags remain among the platform's best-evidenced outputs. They get a tag, not a deletion.

Rebrand the 25 hand-assembled concatenations as de novo designs. They are a hypothesis catalogue built from published motifs and GGGGS linkers, several are mechanistically inverted, and 15 of 35 carry an odd cysteine count so the circulating species is not any enumerated isomer. The correct response is a catalogue revision and a compartment gate, not better modelling of molecules that should not have been proposed.
